m satisfies the cited source sample-size condition
ideal exact whitening and calibrated frame
pure input state is normalized to unit norm

claims.statement: For N fixed incident photons measured independently by the Parseval POVM above, the global minimum-Hellinger-distance estimator over unit pure states has uniform expected squared phase-quotient risk at most min{2, 4(m-1)/(N ell_zeta^2)}. Under independent Poisson photon flux tau, the full counts have Y_j~Pois(tau p_j(x)) and pairwise Bhattacharyya coefficient exp[-tau H^2(p_x,p_y)/2] <= exp[-tau ell_zeta^2 d_phi(x,y)^2/2].
assumptions: known calibrated Parseval POVM
unit pure state, identical independent input copies
all m outcomes are retained
ideal no-loss/no-dark-count model for the displayed bound
global minimizer of empirical Hellinger distance is returned
claims.status: internally proved conditional statistical guarantee; no efficient optimization guarantee
claims.source_pointers: Exact multinomial Hellinger expectation bound, triangle inequality, and product-Poisson affinity are derived in the linked report; prior Poisson phase-retrieval controls are listed there.
claims.novelty_boundary: Poisson likelihood, Hellinger geometry, and minimum-distance ideas are standard. Their composition with the whitened O(d)-outcome frame theorem is not priority-cleared. The report makes no algorithmic superiority claim over polynomial-time low-dose methods.
claims.costs: N incident photons exactly, or expected tau incident photons in the Poisson model. Risk is O(m/N) with fixed constants on the good-frame event. claims.falsifier: A counterexample to E H^2(p_hat,p) <= (m-1)/N, the MHD triangle bound, or the exact product-Poisson affinity formula.
claims.next_gate: Construct a polynomial-time estimator with the same uniform risk under low-dose counts; quantify dark-count, gain, and matrix-calibration perturbations.

claims.statement: For Haar-uniform unknown pure states in C^d, any procedure using N copies has expected squared phase-quotient error at least (d-1)/(N+d), because the optimal average fidelity is (N+1)/(N+d) and d_phi^2 >= 1-F pointwise. Hence the O(d/N) risk of the O(d)-outcome Parseval MHD procedure is minimax-rate optimal up to constants for N >= d.
assumptions: Haar prior over normalized pure states in C^d
N identical copies
arbitrary measurement and pure-state estimate permitted in the lower bound
squared quotient loss d_phi^2=2(1-|<x,y>|)
claims.status: established source theorem combined with an internally derived metric comparison

claims.costs: Counts every one of the N input copies and allows the lower-bound comparator arbitrary collective measurements; the upper instrument is a separable single-copy measurement.
claims.falsifier: A failure of the source fidelity theorem under the Haar prior, or an error in d_phi^2 >= 1-F.
claims.next_gate: Specialist review of the risk translation and compare finite-dimensional constants against known covariant POVM estimators.

claims.statement: For d>=2 and nonzero complex sensing rows a_j=t_j u_j with positive lower constant, beta=2 in the unnormalised ell2 metric on raw squared intensities iff the weights p_j=t_j^4/sum_k t_k^4 and directions Pi_j=u_j u_j* form a weighted complex projective 2-design: sum_j p_j Pi_j tensor Pi_j = 2 P_sym/[d(d+1)].
assumptions: complex dimension d>=2
nonzero rows and positive lower phase-retrieval constant
source raw-intensity ell2 interface and nuclear quotient metric
claims.status: internally reconstructed equality characterization from the 2026 source proof and standard design identities; specialist priority review unresolved
claims.source_pointers: Compress to every complex two-plane; equality in the source two-dimensional lower-bound chain forces the quartic maximum to equal its Haar mean on every plane, hence constant on the full sphere; polarization gives the tensor identity. The converse is the projective 2-design moment contraction.
claims.novelty_boundary: Projective 2-design inversion and tight-IC results are prior art; this exact beta iff statement is a short source-specific consequence and is not priority-cleared. The source theorem has a d=1 exception beta=1.
claims.costs: Exact beta=2 needs at least d^2 nonzero rows. In every d, Jasper-Mixon gives an exact design and hence sensing matrix with d^2+O(d^1.525) rows. This deterministic objective charges neither photons nor calibration.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the equality propagation through the source restriction inequalities, the quartic constancy argument, or the complex polarization step.
claims.next_gate: Independent phase-retrieval/frame-theory review and broader exact-source prior-art check.

claims.statement: With F=sum_j p_j Pi_j tensor Pi_j, F0=2P_sym/[d(d+1)], C_d=2(d+2)(d+3)/[d(d+1)], and rho=(beta/2)^2-1, the internally derived one-way bound is ||F-F0||_F^2 <= C_d rho max(1,rho). For m<d^2, rho additionally obeys rho >= (d^2-m)/[C_d m(d+1)^2]; there is no uniform reverse implication from relative moment closeness to beta closeness, as deleting a complete-MUB vector yields beta>=2sqrt(2).
assumptions: complex d>=2
raw unnormalised squared-intensity ell2 phase-retrieval condition number
positive row weights p_j proportional to fourth powers of row norms
claims.status: internally derived theorem candidate with finite sanity checks; proof and priority not independently validated
claims.source_pointers: Haar-average over complex two-planes bounds L_A; the resulting one-sided quartic bound and zero Haar mean control E g^2; a fourth Haar moment contraction controls ||F-F0||_F. Partial transpose yields a trace-one PSD rank-m approximation lower bound.
claims.novelty_boundary: Approximate-design moment metrics and Welch bounds are existing literature. The beta-to-weighted-moment link may be source-specific, but priority is unknown. Lower gaps are not known sharp.
claims.costs: Rows m and weights are counted. No photon likelihood, calibration cost, or algorithmic measurement-design runtime is included.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the two-plane L_A bound, the stated Haar fourth-moment contraction, or the trace-constrained rank approximation argument.
claims.next_gate: Independent algebraic proof review, compare equal-weight constants to current strengthened Welch bounds, and seek sharp examples at fixed (m,d).

claims.statement: A special Bodmann-Haas/Sidon weighted projective 2-design yields an exact beta=2 one-photon POVM with q^2+d outcomes in dimension d when q>=d is an odd prime; two distinct coordinate states have squared Hellinger distance 2/(q+1), so Poisson flux tau requires at least (q+1)/2 log(1/[4 alpha(1-alpha)]) photons for both testing errors <=alpha.
assumptions: d>=2 and odd prime q>=d
the explicit Sidon set and layer-symmetric design
ideal coherent isometry, exact normalization, ideal counters, no loss/background
claims.status: internally derived instrument and testing formulas; floating-point checks d=2..10; no hardware validation
claims.source_pointers: Character projectors sum to (q^2/d)I and coordinate projectors sum to I; square-root design weights therefore normalize to the identity after a common scalar. Coordinate outcome laws differ only on two basis outcomes; use exact Poisson affinity and TV testing lower bound.
claims.novelty_boundary: The Sidon design is published prior art; physical normalization and the coordinate-pair cost comparison are internal construction/audit, with novelty unresolved.
claims.costs: q^2+d output channels and a d-to-(q^2+d) isometry, with two finite-field QFT branches. QFT depth, loss, calibration, and detector costs are unspecified.
claims.falsifier: Failure of the POVM completeness identity, design normalization, coordinate outcome law, or exact affinity lower-bound calculation.
claims.next_gate: Independent circuit/isometry review and compare a physically compiled finite-precision device against Parseval random-frame likelihood performance.

ledger.topic: Efficient Poisson phase retrieval from a Parseval-completed iid sensing block, with dark-count calibration limits
ledger.overall_status: The cited primary source already provides a polynomial-size convex estimator for iid Poisson rows. An exact Parseval completion transfers that theorem to an O(d)-port photon instrument. A common-background/blank-calibration specialization and an unrestricted channel-background nonidentifiability bound are internally derived. Physical synthesis and finite-bit solver robustness remain unknown.

claims.statement: Huang, Li, and Needell (arXiv:2510.00551v1), Theorem 1, report that for iid complex isotropic sub-Gaussian rows with independent entries, E phi=E phi^2=0, E|phi|^2=1, E|phi|^4=1+mu>1, and independent Y_j|phi_j~Pois(|<phi_j,w>|^2), if m>=L d then with probability 1-O(exp(-c d)) a convex PSD least-squares estimator followed by leading-eigenvector extraction has phase-quotient error at most C3 max{K,1/||w||} sqrt(d/m), uniformly over signals. Constants depend on K,mu and are implicit.
assumptions: The row vectors are independent copies with iid entries and stated moments/sub-Gaussian norm.
Conditional count law is independent Poisson with exact means |<phi_j,w>|^2.
The CVX-LS program is globally solved; finite precision/runtime constants for a concrete solver are not part of this statistical theorem.
claims.status: Primary-source-reported theorem; its statement and estimator were checked in arXiv v1, but not independently proof-audited here.
claims.novelty_boundary: Established prior art. No novelty claim.
claims.costs: m iid rows, full Poisson count vector, d-by-d PSD optimization. The paper does not instantiate optical setup work or a solver bit-complexity bound.
claims.falsifier: A mismatch between the cited theorem, estimator, row assumptions, count law, probability, or phase-error statement.

claims.statement: For iid standard complex Gaussian G in C^(m x d), on the event m/4<=lambda_min(G*G)<=lambda_max(G*G)<=4m, let a=1/(4m), R=(I-aG*G)^(1/2), and Btilde=[sqrt(a)G;R]. Then Btilde*Btilde=I. The first m effects are a g_j g_j*, and with uniform known efficiency eta_det and Poissonized launch mean N their counts have means |g_j*w|^2 for w=sqrt(N eta_det a)x. Thus Huang-Li-Needell Theorem 1 applies exactly to that block, while residual, no-click, and loss outcomes remain included in the launch ledger.
assumptions: m is a sufficiently large fixed multiple of d for both source theorem and Gaussian singular-value event.
x has unit norm and eta_det is known, uniform, and state-independent.
The frame is calibrated exactly and a valid fallback instrument is used on the bad-frame event.
Input source is Poissonized with mean launch count N for independent output Poissonization.
claims.status: Internally derived exact POVM and count-law reduction plus standard Gaussian singular-value concentration.
claims.novelty_boundary: Composition of a published estimator theorem with an explicit Parseval completion. It is not the polar-normalized correlated frame and is not a new phase-retrieval estimator.
claims.costs: N launched photons; m+d=O(d) outcomes; md=O(d^2) coefficients; residual/no-click and detector loss charged. Optical synthesis, insertion loss, and calibration exposure remain unquantified.
claims.falsifier: Failure of Parseval completeness, the good-frame probability interval, or the exact Poisson mean identity.

claims.statement: For the completed iid-Gaussian-block POVM, if N eta_det>=max{4m/K^2,16 C3^2 K^2 d/epsilon^2} and 0<epsilon<=1, normalized CVX-LS leading-eigenvector recovery has phase error at most epsilon in the Poissonized model with source-theorem plus bad-frame failure probability. For m=Theta(d), launched-photon scaling is O(d/(eta_det epsilon^2)) with hidden constants. Exactly N launches follow by conditioning the complete source count vector on its Pois(N) total, yielding failure at most 2exp(-c_Gm)+C sqrt(N) exp(-c d).
assumptions: The source theorem and good-frame event hold.
Normalization is used only when the unnormalized phase error is at most half the signal norm; the displayed dose conditions imply this for epsilon<=1.
For the fixed-N statement, all residual and no-click source outcomes are included in the conditioned total; background counts are absent in this version.
claims.status: Internally derived transfer from the primary theorem. Fixed-N conditioning penalty is explicit and may be loose.
claims.novelty_boundary: No claim of photon advantage over an equally informed likelihood estimator or of minimax constants.
claims.costs: All N launched photons including residual/no-click; uniform detector efficiency costs 1/eta_det. CVX-LS variables are d-by-d; numerical precision and compiler costs are additional.
claims.falsifier: A flaw in theorem application, scale normalization, conditioning, or the good-frame event.

claims.statement: If each of the m Gaussian-block channels has the same known dark mean beta per signal exposure, then after subtracting beta the observations satisfy the source paper's heavy-tailed model with iid centered q=4 noise. For complex Gaussian rows, ||xi||_4^4=||w||^2+beta+6||w||^4+6 beta ||w||^2+3 beta^2. For ||w||>=1, Theorem 4 implies normalized phase error at most C[sqrt(d/(N eta_det))+sqrt(beta d m)/(N eta_det)] when normalization is valid. If beta is unknown but common and independent blank counts Z_j~Pois(r beta) are acquired, subtracting Z_j/r adds the explicit term C sqrt(d m)/(N eta_det)[(beta/r^3)^(1/4)+sqrt(beta/r)] and costs m r beta expected blank dark counts.
assumptions: Rows are iid complex Gaussian; dark mean is identical across channels and constant between signal and blank exposures.
Blank counts are independent Poisson with known exposure ratio r>0; row calibration and uniform loss are exact and known.
Use the q=4 high-probability CVX-LS result and satisfy its m>=L d, high-energy, and normalization conditions.
This is a Poissonized input result; exactly fixed source count adds the same O(sqrt(N)) conditioning penalty.
The result is a sufficient subtraction protocol, not an optimal calibration design; pooling the common background or jointly fitting it may reduce calibration cost.
claims.status: Internally derived specialization of Huang-Li-Needell Theorem 4 and exact Poisson fourth moments; not independently proof-audited beyond algebra.
claims.novelty_boundary: Uses the published Huang-Li-Needell Theorem 4; the known per-channel Poisson-background model and low-count ML algorithms already appear in Li-Lange-Fessler (2022). No novelty claim. The new content here is only the stated theorem transfer for common background and independent blank counts.
claims.costs: Signal photons plus m r beta expected blank dark counts and one source-off exposure of relative duration r; exact row calibration and optics remain separately charged.
claims.falsifier: Violation of identical stable background levels, independent blank counts, row-noise iid assumptions, or the displayed fourth moment/error transfer.

claims.statement: For any complete J-outcome POVM with probabilities p_j(x), Poissonized detected source mean S=N eta_det, and unknown additive per-port backgrounds beta_j in [0,beta_bar], if beta_bar>=2S, then any two orthogonal pure states x,y admit nuisance backgrounds beta^(x)_j=S(2-p_j(x)) and beta^(y)_j=S(2-p_j(y)) that make every illuminated detector count exactly Pois(2S) under either hypothesis. Hence there is no uniform single-exposure phase recovery guarantee below epsilon=1/sqrt(2) with success probability exceeding 1/2 over this nuisance class. With an independent blank exposure of relative duration r, the constructed pair has blank-record KL at most 2rS; if rS<=1/16, every equal-prior test has average error at least 3/8. Thus this worst-case class needs r=Omega(1/S) even to distinguish this separated pair.
assumptions: The measurement is a complete POVM, so p(x) and p(y) are probability vectors and 0<=p_j<=1.
Poissonized illumination gives independent channel counts; dark means are arbitrary fixed nuisance values within each world and may differ between candidate worlds.
Dark counts affect registered detector channels; state-independent no-click/loss channels do not help distinguish the pair.
The blank exposure measures the same channel-specific dark means independently at relative duration r.
claims.status: Exact internally derived nonidentifiability and two-point blank-exposure lower bound. The exact no-go is not established for exactly fixed-N multinomial source counts.
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary nuisance-identifiability result under the named interface; no priority claim. It does not imply failure under bounded lower-background, common-background, or multi-exposure models.
claims.costs: Requires the explicit dark-count nuisance class; blank lower bound is relative exposure and at least Omega(J) expected dark events for the constructed worst-case background when rS is constant.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to exact equality of the illuminated laws or to the stated Poisson KL and testing calculation.

open_gates: Direct polynomial CVX-LS transfer for the polar-normalized correlated Parseval Gaussian frame.
Finite-bit solver complexity and optimization-slack stability for the completed-block CVX-LS program.
Quantitative optical compiler precision, insertion-loss cost, and calibration exposure for realizing the Parseval completion.
Finite-sample robust theorem for arbitrary heterogeneous detector backgrounds estimated from blank data.
Exact fixed-N multinomial-plus-dark-count analogue of the nonidentifiability and blank-calibration lower bound.

claims.statement: For a bounded full-rank chart A_B=B V^T with known V in R^{q x r}, if an adaptive sensing algorithm receives m responses from alphabets of size at most 2^b and must answer all post-storage bilinear tasks (a,x) uniformly to error epsilon with failure probability delta, then for p>=q and epsilon<=1/(64 sqrt(r)), mb >= (1-delta)pr log2(1/(32 sqrt(r) epsilon))-h2(delta); transpose the construction for q>p. The lower bound is information-theoretic and permits unbounded computation.
assumptions: rank(A_B)=r; B lies in an operator-norm ball of radius 1/(8 sqrt(r)) around (1/(2 sqrt(r)))[I_r;0] when p>=q
measurement queries are adaptive scalar linear functionals of A; each response has at most b bits
all algorithm randomness is independent of A and included in the retained state
after storage, the decoder simultaneously answers every unit bilinear task a^T A x to epsilon with failure probability delta<1/2
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_candidate; proof in PROOF.md; external correctness, novelty and priority unresolved
claims.novelty_boundary: Adjacent generic exact low-rank recovery and adaptive noisy matrix-recovery results are established prior art. This task-specific finite-bit post-storage bilinear query interface is not claimed novel; priority needs literature/expert review.
claims.costs: Lower counts m calls and b response bits per call; omits query encoding, calibration, physical noise/SNR, and computation. Raw coordinate baseline uses pr calls, b_raw=ceil(log2(4 sqrt(pr)/epsilon)) response bits per call, O(pr) quantization operations, and O(pr+qr) decoder arithmetic.
claims.falsifier: Find a protocol under the stated oracle, task, and uniform error interface that answers all bilinear tasks while using fewer response bits than the packing/Fano bound, or identify a flaw in the operator-norm packing reduction.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof review, then investigate whether a restricted low-entropy task distribution yields a positive acquisition-vs-raw-data result under an equally informed baseline.

claims.statement: For a deterministic adaptive exact-real linear measurement scheme on the same p x r open chart, fewer than pr scalar queries leave locally indistinguishable rank-r factors, so uniform post-storage bilinear accuracy epsilon<R/2 is impossible.
assumptions: p>=q and known V has orthonormal columns
unknown B varies over an open operator-norm ball of radius R=1/(8 sqrt(r)) around a full-rank center
queries are exact scalar linear functionals and are deterministic adaptive functions of prior responses
decoder must answer all unit bilinear tasks uniformly
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_candidate; deterministic scope only; external review and novelty unresolved
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a local dimension/nullspace obstruction adjacent to classical low-rank measurement-count bounds; not claimed as a new general recovery theorem.
claims.costs: Counts scalar exact-real measurement calls; exact precision is an idealized generous interface. Randomized positive-error query-count version not established.
claims.falsifier: Construct a deterministic adaptive scheme with fewer than pr exact scalar linear queries that uniformly answers every bilinear task on the open rank-r chart to epsilon<R/2.
claims.next_gate: Do not extend to randomized positive-error schemes without a separate minimax proof.

ledger.overall_status: internally derived stability theorem and calibration obstruction; prior-art bounded, not externally reviewed or novelty-cleared

claims.statement: For a weighted complex projective 2-design (u_j,p_j) in C^d, d>=2, physical rows a_j=t_j u_j with p_j=t_j^4/S and S=sum_j t_j^4, and raw observations y_j=t_j^2(1+gamma_j)|v_j^*x|^2+eta_j, where ||x||<=R, ||v_j||=1, max_j min_phase||v_j-phase*u_j||<=delta and max_j|gamma_j|<=gamma<1, the nominal dual-frame inverse Xhat=sum_j(t_j^2 y_j/S)[d(d+1)Pi_j-dI] obeys ||Xhat-xx*||_F <= R^2[sqrt(2)gamma+(1+gamma)(2sqrt(d+1)delta+sqrt(d(d+1))delta^2)] + sqrt(d(d+1)/S)||eta||_2.
assumptions: positive p_j sum to one and sum p_j Pi_j tensor Pi_j=(I+F)/[d(d+1)]
p_j=t_j^4/S and S=sum t_j^4
direction error is projective chordal error between unit vectors
gain error is multiplicative intensity gain, not amplitude gain
eta is additive raw-output error
claims.status: internally derived from the exact frame identity; not externally reviewed
claims.source_pointers: Proof is reproduced in the report: weighted design gives F_p(H)=(H+Tr(H)I)/d(d+1) and ||F_p^{-1}A_p^*||=sqrt(d(d+1)); rank-one design moments give sum p z=||x||^2/d and sum p z^2=2||x||^4/[d(d+1)]; row direction perturbations obey ||ztilde-z||_p<=2delta R^2/sqrt(d)+delta^2 R^2.
claims.novelty_boundary: The noiseless projective-design inverse is prior art (Levenshtein/Scott; Balan-Bodmann-Casazza-Edidin). General frame perturbation and phase retrieval total-least-squares under sensing-vector/data errors are also prior art. This is a transparent specialization to the weighted lifted inverse and stated gain/projector/readout interface, not a general new phase retrieval stability theorem.
claims.costs: m scalar intensity channels; raw output precision enters through ||eta||2/sqrt(S); relative intensity gain calibration needs O(epsilon/R^2) accuracy and projective direction accuracy O(epsilon/[R^2 sqrt(d)]) for target lifted Frobenius error epsilon, up to the displayed constants. Calibration-shot counts require an external calibrator/noise model.
claims.falsifier: A weighted 2-design and admissible x, gains, projective row perturbations or eta violating the displayed deterministic inequality; or an algebra error in the canonical inverse norm or projector perturbation estimate.
claims.next_gate: Independent frame-theory derivation review and a finite numerical test on a Jasper-Mixon Sidon/Bodmann-Haas instance against lifted OLS/GLS and rank-one raw least squares.

claims.statement: When physical row amplitudes satisfy t_j^4=Sp_j, the weighted-design inverse is exactly the Moore-Penrose ordinary least-squares estimator for all raw lifted rows A_t(H)_j=t_j^2 Tr(Pi_j H). Its frame operator has scalar eigenvalue S/d and traceless eigenvalue S/[d(d+1)], hence condition number sqrt(d+1). Under independent zero-mean raw-output noise with variances sigma_j^2, its exact Frobenius MSE around its mean is K_d sum_j t_j^4 sigma_j^2/S^2, K_d=d^2(d^2+d-1).
assumptions: same weighted 2-design as WEIGHTED-DESIGN-PERTURBATION
row scaling t_j^4=Sp_j
the lifted Hermitian variable is unrestricted for the OLS comparison
noise coordinates are independent and have finite stated variances for the MSE formula
claims.status: algebraically derived; Gauss-Markov consequence is standard; not externally reviewed
claims.source_pointers: A_t^*A_t=S F_p; the displayed canonical dual formula equals (A_t^*A_t)^-1 A_t^* y. D_j=d(d+1)Pi_j-dI has squared Frobenius norm d^2(d^2+d-1), independent of j.
claims.novelty_boundary: This identifies the closed form with raw-data OLS; it is a control result and not a novelty claim. Heteroskedastic known-noise GLS and rank-one constrained LS are equally informed controls and can improve or use the same data more effectively.
claims.costs: Same m raw scalar readings and the same rows as the closed-form inverse. Generic dense accumulation costs O(md^2); the Jasper-Mixon character structure admits an O(|G| log |G|+d^2) finite-group FFT implementation, assuming group representation/FFT is supplied.
claims.falsifier: A failure of A_t^*A_t=S F_p or a discrepancy between the formula and the raw OLS pseudoinverse on an exact design.
claims.next_gate: Reproduce the identity and covariance formula in a numerical d=2 and a small Sidon construction implementation; separately benchmark GLS under specified heteroskedasticity.

claims.statement: If signal norm is unknown and a common intensity gain g is only known to lie in [1-gamma,1+gamma], then noiseless intensity data cannot uniformly recover X=xx* over ||x||<=R to Frobenius error below gamma R^2/(1+gamma), regardless of the sensing rows or their count.
assumptions: unknown signal norm over the radius-R ball
unknown common intensity gain in [1-gamma,1+gamma]
measurement model y_j=g |a_j^*x|^2
claims.source_pointers: Instances (1-gamma,R^2 vv*) and (1+gamma,[(1-gamma)/(1+gamma)]R^2 vv*) induce identical data and have Frobenius distance 2 gamma R^2/(1+gamma).
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary scale/gain confounding; no novelty claim. Does not apply when signal norm is known exactly or only the normalized direction is a target.
claims.costs: More phase-retrieval samples do not break the ambiguity. An independent gain calibration or known signal norm is necessary.
claims.falsifier: A decoder that distinguishes the two parameter pairs from identical deterministic observations without side information.
claims.next_gate: Include gain-reference acquisition and its uncertainty in any physical experimental protocol.

claims.statement: For the Jasper-Mixon near-minimal Sidon/Bodmann-Haas weighted design with d=|S| and N=|G|, normalized character and coordinate weights are p_chi=d/[N(d+1)] and p_r=1/[d(d+1)], with ratio N/d^2. In their N=d^2+O(d^1.525) regime, max_j|m p_j-1|=O(d^-0.475), so those weights are asymptotically near-uniform.
assumptions: theorem 7 Bodmann-Haas construction in Jasper-Mixon arXiv:2501.14938v1
dense Sidon-set parameter regime yielding N=d^2+O(d^1.525)
m=N+d rows
claims.source_pointers: Theorem 7 proof lines 132-134 gives unnormalized character weights d^2/(2N), coordinate weights 1/2; Theorem 4 and section 3 give the near-minimal cardinality bound.
claims.novelty_boundary: A normalization/cost interpretation of the source construction, not a new design theorem. General sparse-in-group Sidon choices can have a different weight ratio; the claim is specifically about the near-minimal regime.
claims.costs: m=N+d=d^2+O(d^1.525) scalar channels; no sampling or exposure reduction follows from the weights. Equal-scale unit rows with weighted processing have variance K_d sigma^2 sum p_j^2; row-amplitude coding makes the formula raw OLS under homoscedastic raw noise.
claims.falsifier: Recompute the normalized weights or exhibit an allowed near-minimal Sidon parameter sequence with nonvanishing max_j|m p_j-1|.
claims.next_gate: Use the exact finite Sidon parameters in a reproducible weight/noise/FFT simulation; do not infer Poisson dose from additive noise.

cost_ledger.acquisition: m scalar intensity channels; the base theorem assumes all rows measured once; repeated-exposure formula is in CYCLE2_REPORT.md
cost_ledger.response_precision: mb bits for b-bit raw outputs; deterministic quantizer bound and sufficient b are stated in CYCLE2_REPORT.md
cost_ledger.calibration: Sufficient relative-gain/projector precision is quantified; calibration shot counts are UNKNOWN without a reference and noise model
cost_ledger.computation: O(md^2) generic accumulation, or O(|G| log |G|+d^2) with a supplied Jasper-Mixon finite-group FFT representation
cost_ledger.representation: Dense lifted X uses d^2 real values; a rank-one factor uses 2d-1 real values up to global phase, but noisy factorization stability is not established here
cost_ledger.physical_noise: No Poisson/shot-noise or detector exposure model is assumed

prior_art: Levenshtein/Scott reconstruction identity, presented in Balan-Bodmann-Casazza-Edidin Theorem 3.4 and Remark 3.5
Alharbi et al. 2022/2023 quantitative phase-retrieval frame perturbations
Gupta-Dokmanic 2021 Total Least Squares Phase Retrieval handles sensing-vector and measurement errors

finite_checks.scope: d=2, G=Z_3, Sidon set S={0,1}; five-row Jasper-Mixon/Bodmann-Haas weighted design. Moment identity error 1.665e-16; explicit weighted inverse/raw OLS max-entry gap 3.553e-15; one randomized gain/projector/noise fixture had matrix error 0.113801 below theorem bound 0.322494.

ledger.topic: rare-signal detection with false alarms, censoring, heralding, and calibrated nuisance
ledger.overall_status: internally_derived_classical_components; no novelty or external-validation claim

claims.statement: For a binary sequential detector with hypothesis-independent adaptive action and censoring kernels, per-action costs c(a)>0, and finite κ_h=sup_a D(P_h^a||P_(1-h)^a)/c(a), type-I error <= alpha and type-II error <= beta imply κ_1 E_1[C] >= d(1-beta||alpha) and κ_0 E_0[C] >= d(1-alpha||beta).
assumptions: The full stopped transcript, including action, calibration, herald/failure, censoring, and stopping records, is modeled under both hypotheses.
Action-selection and censoring kernels are the same functions of observed history under either hypothesis.
Costs are charged for every attempted measurement, preparation, calibration, control, and readout that the chosen scalar cost includes.
Divergences may be infinite; if so that direction gives no finite lower bound.
claims.status: proof reconstructed directly from KL chain rule and binary data processing; classic ingredients; not a novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Stopped KL inequalities and SPRT optimality are classical. The contribution is explicit charging and scope bookkeeping across adaptive censoring, calibration, and postselection.
claims.costs: Expected total action cost under the named hypothesis. A mean-cost promise does not imply hard spectral support or total thermodynamic cost unless those are explicitly included.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the chain-rule inequality under the stated common action/censoring kernels, or a policy meeting both errors while exceeding the derived bound assumptions without adding information/cost to the transcript.
claims.next_gate: Instantiate the lemma for a measured channel with a complete action/resource vector and compare its attainable KL-per-cost frontier against the strongest policy with the same calibration information.

claims.statement: For fixed exposure T and known b>0,s>0, the randomized upper-count threshold is most powerful at size alpha for Pois(bT) versus Pois((b+s)T); the KL rates per exposure are I1=(b+s)ln(1+s/b)-s and I0=s-b ln(1+s/b), and every test with size alpha and miss beta satisfies T I1>=d(1-beta||alpha), T I0>=d(1-alpha||beta).
assumptions: A homogeneous Poisson background and additive homogeneous signal rate hold over the full exposure.
The background rate and signal rate are known inputs; background calibration cost is not included unless separately charged.
All event counts used by the likelihood are retained.
claims.status: formula derived; known-background threshold/power computed to finite floating-point precision, on/off power reports an explicit tail bound; primary statistical method is classical
claims.novelty_boundary: Neyman-Pearson testing and Poisson signal-background inference predate this work; no new detector or asymptotic exponent is claimed.
claims.costs: Exposure T, with added terms for probe energy, instrument, calibration, control, and computation required by the actual deployment.
claims.falsifier: Observed counts fail the specified Poisson law, b or s are not calibrated/stationary, or the computed randomized threshold does not attain its null size and Neyman-Pearson power for the specified pair.
claims.next_gate: Validate against independent null and signal runs, retaining all marks and charging calibration exposure; include the calibration cost before comparing with a known-b baseline.

claims.statement: For on-count-only observations with unknown background b in an interval of width at least s, the null family Pois(Tb) and signal family Pois(T(b+s)) contain an identical pair of laws. Any uniformly size-alpha test then has power <=alpha at that alternative, so alpha+beta>=1.
assumptions: The only observed data are counts in the signal/on region.
The same background interval is allowed under both hypotheses and its width is at least the signal-rate increment s.
Uniform type-I control is required over the entire null nuisance family.
claims.status: elementary exact impossibility proof; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a direct identifiability obstruction, not a new statistical theorem.
claims.costs: It applies even with unlimited repetitions of the same on-only experiment because the two hypotheses can induce identical laws at every exposure.
claims.falsifier: A valid extra observable or calibration assumption that separates the two distributions; this changes the model and removes the premise.
claims.next_gate: Specify a background-only reference or validated bounded drift/transfer model, then charge its exposure and re-run a uniform-power analysis.

claims.statement: For one attempt with herald probability q_h and conditional success-output law R_h, if the success/failure flag is recorded then D(P1||P0)=d(q1||q0)+q1 D(R1||R0). Repeating physical attempts until a herald succeeds costs c/q_h in expectation under H_h.
assumptions: The attempt outcome is failure with probability 1-q_h or success with probability q_h followed by an output drawn from R_h.
Each attempt costs c, including failed attempts.
When conditioning on success, the success-rate term is omitted from the conditional-output statistic but not from physical exposure.
claims.novelty_boundary: This accounting identity does not invalidate a computational conditional sampler; it distinguishes algorithmic sampling of a conditional law from physical herald preparation.
claims.costs: All failed attempts, conditional-output processing, positive-kernel/model acquisition, representation bits, random bits, and sampler runtime are separate line items.
claims.falsifier: A heralding protocol whose actual one-attempt record law does not factor as the specified success flag and conditional output; update the model to the true outcome space.
claims.next_gate: For any claimed inverse-success-free conditional sampler, independently verify exact zero-event detection, relative rather than additive counting, input representation acquisition, bit complexity, and physical-versus-computational interpretation.

ledger.topic: phase retrieval from physical photon counts with a complete POVM and charged total photon budget
ledger.overall_status: exact count-law derivations proved; conditional random-frame upper and quantum lower match in order; implementation and nuisance robustness unresolved

claims.statement: For a normalized complete POVM with outcome law p(x), N fixed photon copies have counts Multinomial(N,p(x)); a Poissonian source with mean N has independent counts Pois(N p_j(x)). The independent-Poisson total is Pois(N), not N per outcome. Their exact Bhattacharyya affinities are respectively (sum_j sqrt(p_j(x)p_j(y)))^N and exp[-N/2 ||sqrt(p(x))-sqrt(p(y))||_2^2].
assumptions: All outcomes of a complete POVM are recorded, including loss/no-click/herald/failure outcomes when present.
The state x is normalized, so sum_j p_j(x)=1 for every hypothesis.
Fixed-N and Poissonized source models are kept distinct; in the Poissonized case N is expected total input photons.
claims.status: direct exact derivation from multinomial and Poisson mass functions
claims.novelty_boundary: Classical splitting/Poissonization and Hellinger affinity; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: N total incident photons across all outcomes and settings; a setting label is part of the POVM outcome when settings are randomized.
claims.falsifier: A count model in which the stated outcomes are not conditionally independent given a Poisson total or not multinomial given fixed N.

claims.statement: For two known states under a fixed calibrated frame, the Neyman-Pearson statistic uses all recorded counts: under fixed N it is sum_j K_j log(p_j(x1)/p_j(x0)); under independent Poisson counts with means N p_j it is sum_j Y_j log(p_j(x1)/p_j(x0)) because the normalized-state rate correction vanishes. With known additive background c_j the full Poisson log-likelihood ratio instead uses means N p_j(x)+c_j, including the compensator term. A rare prior changes the decision threshold, not the count budget.
assumptions: The two hypotheses and measurement probabilities are known.
All outcomes and setting labels are retained.
Background means, if present, are known for the displayed likelihood; their calibration cost is additional.
claims.status: direct likelihood-ratio derivation; implements the strongest simple-hypothesis test for the same fixed measurement
claims.novelty_boundary: Classical Neyman-Pearson testing; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: N fixed incident photons or expected N photons in the Poissonized experiment, across all outcomes/settings; background calibration exposure is separate.
claims.falsifier: A mismatch between the stated likelihood ratio and the full multinomial or independent-Poisson outcome law.

claims.statement: Let G be an m-by-d complex standard Gaussian matrix, S=G*G, and B=G S^{-1/2}. Conditional on Xia-Xu-Xu's Theorem 4.3 event and their Lemma 4.2 singular-value event, B*B=I and its rank-one POVM E_j=b_j b_j* satisfies || |Bx|-|By| ||_2 >= ell d_phi(x,y) uniformly, with ell >= (1/beta0-delta)/sqrt(1+rho), beta0=sqrt(4/(4-pi)), 0<delta<0.05, 0<rho<1. The event probability is at least 1-4 exp(-c2 delta^2 m)-2 exp(-c1 rho^2 m), provided m is at least the source's implicit constant times max{log(1/delta) delta^-2 d, rho^-2 d}.
assumptions: Complex standard Gaussian entries have real and imaginary variances 1/2.
m >= d so S is invertible almost surely.
d_phi(x,y)=min_|omega|=1 ||x-omega y||_2; magnitude stability is global, including non-unit arguments in the source theorem.
The theorem's universal constants c1,c2 and implicit sample-size constants are not numerically specified.
claims.status: internally derived from primary random-Gaussian magnitude stability plus Gram concentration; no external proof review
claims.novelty_boundary: The Gaussian modulus theorem is published prior work; polar-normalization transfer to a Parseval one-photon POVM is an elementary reconstruction, not priority-cleared novelty.
claims.costs: m detector outcomes, one outcome per incident photon, N photons total; calibration and physical realization of B are unpriced.
claims.falsifier: A flaw in the source lower-modulus event, the polar normalization, or the singular-value transfer inequality.

claims.statement: For a known Parseval POVM with global magnitude lower modulus ell, the global Hellinger minimum-distance fit xhat minimizing ||sqrt(Y/N)-|Bz||_2 over unit z under independent Y_j~Pois(N p_j(x)) satisfies sup_x E_x[d_phi(xhat,x)^2] <= 4m/(N ell^2). For exactly N photons and K~Multinomial(N,p(x)), replacing Y/N by K/N sharpens this to 4(m-1)/(N ell^2).
assumptions: No additive background, detector mismatch, or unmodeled loss; such mechanisms must be included in the full outcome law and the bound rederived.
The frame B and all outcome probabilities are known/calibrated.
The estimator is a global minimum-distance solution; no polynomial-time solver guarantee is asserted.
In the Poisson model N is the expected total count; in the multinomial model N is the fixed total count.
claims.status: internally proved from a coordinate square-root multinomial variance bound, global fit inequality, and modulus
claims.novelty_boundary: Generic Hellinger minimum-distance reasoning is classical; no new statistical estimator class is claimed.
claims.costs: Expected squared phase distance versus N fixed incident photons. A finite epsilon-net implementation is exponential in d; frame generation, calibration, computation, and hardware cost remain separate.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to E( sqrt(Y_j/N)-sqrt(p_j) )^2 <= 1/N for p_j>0, the corresponding multinomial bound E( sqrt(K_j/N)-sqrt(p_j) )^2 <= (1-p_j)/N, the fit triangle inequality, or the assumed ell modulus.

claims.statement: For estimating a Haar-uniform unknown pure d-dimensional state from N identical copies, any measurement-estimator, including arbitrary collective measurements, has average squared phase-distance risk at least (d-1)/(N+d), because optimal average fidelity is (N+1)/(N+d) and d_phi^2=2(1-c)>=1-c^2.
assumptions: The unknown input is genuinely N copies of the same pure d-dimensional state.
Risk is averaged over Haar prior; the resulting lower bound also lower-bounds worst-case risk.
d_phi is the phase-invariant Euclidean distance between normalized pure state vectors.
claims.status: primary theorem translated exactly to the squared phase-distance loss
claims.novelty_boundary: Bruß-Macchiavello 1999 is established quantum state-estimation theory; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: N copies/photons, with no free collective measurement apparatus assumed in physical comparison; theorem gives an information-theoretic bound even allowing collective measurements.
claims.falsifier: An estimator with Haar-average fidelity exceeding (N+1)/(N+d) under the same N-copy pure-state model.

claims.statement: If a family of complex random Parseval POVMs has m=Theta(d) and a uniform lower magnitude modulus ell bounded below by a positive constant, then the global Hellinger estimator has uniform expected squared phase risk O(d/N), while the quantum Haar-average lower bound is Omega(d/N) for N much larger than d. Thus N=Theta(d/epsilon^2) is supported in order for mean-squared phase error epsilon^2 under this ideal model.
assumptions: Fixed positive ell and linear outcome count m=Theta(d); the source theorem has hidden constants in m and failure probability.
Known normalized pure state family, known frame, zero background and no loss.
Expected-risk criterion; Markov conversion to a 1-zeta high-probability guarantee costs an additional 1/zeta factor.
The construction does not imply efficient optimization or physically free frame calibration.
claims.status: conditional order-match proved; finite constants and practical implementation unresolved
claims.novelty_boundary: Order follows from known Gaussian frame stability, a direct Parseval transfer and Hellinger fitting, and known optimal quantum state estimation; not a novelty or hardware-advantage claim.
claims.costs: m output channels and N total photons; also charge all frame calibration, preparation, readout, setting, ancilla, and computation resources in a deployment comparison.
claims.falsifier: Failure of the stipulated modulus event, a corrected MDE upper bound, or a weaker/stronger lower-bound interpretation under the precise loss and prior.

claims.statement: For a unit-row complex projective 2-design of m rows used as the POVM E_j=(d/m)u_j u_j*, the previous raw-intensity lower constant L^2=m/[2d(d+1)] implies ||sqrt(p(x))-sqrt(p(y))||_2 >= ||xx*-yy*||_* / [2 sqrt(2(d+1))], and hence independent-Poisson affinity <= exp[-N ||xx*-yy*||_*^2/(16(d+1))].
assumptions: Equal-weight projective 2-design, normalized pure states, all m outcomes included.
Uses the internally reconstructed raw-intensity law in ../nonlinear_inverse/FINAL_REPORT.md.
No additive background or loss.
claims.status: direct conversion of predecessor result; correct but dimension-looser than random Parseval magnitude stability for state-vector phase distance
claims.novelty_boundary: Classical projective designs plus the predecessor report's condition-number corollary; no new design theorem.
claims.costs: At least d^2 nonzero scalar outcomes are necessary to attain the predecessor's exact complex beta=2 optimum; physical implementation/calibration unpriced.
claims.falsifier: A flaw in the stated raw lower constant, POVM normalization, or amplitude-product inequality.

claims.statement: Dirksen-Krahmer-Romer-Salanevich Theorem 5 proves a real Gaussian-row Poisson spectral recovery guarantee for m>=n log n with relative squared phase error <=2 C_beta(1+C_hat_beta/alpha) log(m) sqrt(log(n)) sqrt(n/m) and success probability >=1-n^-beta-m exp(-c_beta n)-m^-beta, where alpha=||x||^2 and constants are absolute but unspecified. Expected total counts before conditioning on the design equal m alpha.
assumptions: Real x in R^n; independent standard Gaussian sensing vectors a_i.
Independent count observations y_i~Pois(|<a_i,x>|^2), no additive background.
Estimator is the leading eigenvector of m^-1 sum_i y_i a_i a_i^T, scaled to norm squared alpha.
Random unnormalized row model, not one normalized POVM or fixed-total-N multinomial counts.
claims.status: source-reported theorem checked against primary arXiv text; no independent proof audit
claims.novelty_boundary: Published direct Poisson phase-retrieval prior art; not a theorem for the present normalized POVM model.
claims.costs: Charge expected total count m alpha across every row, not alpha per row as if settings were free.
claims.falsifier: Mismatch in the primary theorem statement, model, probability bound, or expected total count calculation.

claims.statement: For independent output counts with known additive background means c_j and signal means N p_j(x), the exact Poisson affinity is exp[-(1/2) sum_j (sqrt(N p_j(x)+c_j)-sqrt(N p_j(y)+c_j))^2].
assumptions: Background means are known and fixed across compared states.
All outcomes are retained and the output counts are independent Poisson variables.
Calibration cost for c_j is not included in this formula and must be charged separately.
claims.status: direct exact derivation; no robustness theorem for estimated backgrounds claimed
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard Poisson Hellinger identity; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: N signal photons plus all background calibration exposure, detector dark-count estimation, and readout cost.
claims.falsifier: A count law not equal to independent Poisson with the stated means.

unknown: Numerical constants for the random-frame sample-size threshold and failure exponent in Xia-Xu-Xu.
Polynomial-time global solution of the Hellinger minimum-distance estimator for the random Parseval frame.
Uniform stability and optimal risk constants with uncertain background, frame calibration error, dark counts, losses, saturation, or heralding.
Whether any one-copy rank-one POVM attains the exact quantum minimax constant for phase retrieval under the stated risk.
Physical optical-network, ancilla, calibration, control, and processor energy needed to implement the random Parseval POVM and its estimator.
Any experimental advantage over the best equally informed calibrated Poisson maximum-likelihood estimator.

ledger.topic: Polynomial-time Poisson phase retrieval with a Parseval-completed iid Gaussian block POVM
ledger.overall_status: Primary high-probability convex estimator theorem identified; exact Poissonized POVM reduction proved; fixed-N guarantee follows by conditioning with an explicit sqrt(N) tail penalty; polar-normalized correlated-frame theorem remains unknown.

claims.statement: For iid complex isotropic sub-Gaussian sensing rows satisfying E phi=E phi^2=0, E|phi|^2=1, E|phi|^4=1+mu>1, and conditionally independent observations Y_j~Pois(|<phi_j,w>|^2), Huang-Li-Needell Theorem 1 states that when m>=L d a convex PSD least-squares estimator followed by top-eigenvector extraction obeys dist(z_*,w)<=C3 max{K,1/||w||} sqrt(d/m), with probability 1-O(exp(-c d)); the source says the guarantee holds simultaneously for all signals. For standard complex Gaussian entries mu=1. L,c,C3 are hidden constants depending on K,mu.
assumptions: Rows have independent entries and are independent across j.
No additive background, saturation, or unmodeled detector noise.
CVX-LS is the global solution of the convex PSD least-squares program; numerical solver precision is an additional implementation issue.
claims.status: Source-reported primary theorem checked against arXiv v1 Theorem 1, Assumptions 1-2, and CVX-LS setup; not independently proof-audited.
claims.novelty_boundary: Published Poisson phase-retrieval result; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: m Poisson rows and their full count data; theorem treats iid row measurements, not a normalized tight frame.
claims.falsifier: Mismatch in the primary theorem assumptions, estimator, rate, probability, or uniformity statement.

claims.statement: On a good singular-value event for iid Gaussian G in C^(m x d), choose a=1/(4m) and R=(I-a G*G)^(1/2). Then Btilde=[sqrt(a)G;R] is Parseval with m+d outputs. With uniform detector efficiency eta_det and Poissonized launch mean N, its first m channel counts are independent Poisson with means N eta_det a |g_j*x|^2=|g_j*w|^2 for deterministic w=sqrt(N eta_det a)x. Thus the iid-row Poisson theorem applies exactly to the Gaussian block; residual and loss/no-click outputs complete the POVM and remain charged in the total launch budget.
assumptions: G has iid standard complex Gaussian entries; m is at least a sufficiently large constant times d.
On the good event lambda_min(G*G)>=m/4 and lambda_max(G*G)<=4m; otherwise a fixed valid fallback POVM is used and this event counts as failure.
x is a unit vector and detector efficiency is uniform and known.
The Poissonized source has expected total N input photons, so all output counts, including residual/no-click, sum to Pois(N).
claims.status: Direct algebraic POVM/count-law reduction plus standard Gaussian singular-value concentration.
claims.novelty_boundary: A measurement-model transfer of a published estimator theorem; this is not the polar-normalized Gaussian Parseval frame.
claims.costs: N launched photons across all m+d output channels and loss/no-click events; m+d=O(d); frame synthesis/calibration remains separately charged.
claims.falsifier: A violation of Parseval completeness, the stated click probability, or the exact Poisson mean identity.

claims.statement: Under the preceding completed-Gaussian-block policy, if N eta_det>=max{4m/K^2,16 C3^2 K^2 d/epsilon^2}, the normalized top-eigenvector CVX-LS estimate has phase error at most epsilon with high probability in the Poissonized experiment. In particular its squared error on the success event is O(d/(N eta_det)); m=Theta(d) gives N eta_det=O(d/epsilon^2) launched-photon scaling with hidden constants.
assumptions: The Huang-Li-Needell source theorem and good-frame event hold.
The estimated signal is normalized to unit norm; the theorem scale is sqrt(N eta_det a).
Ideal exact frame calibration and exact integer counts.
claims.status: Proved reduction from primary theorem; hidden constants and conventional convex-optimization precision caveats retained.
claims.novelty_boundary: Conditional rate transfer only; no hardware energy advantage or minimax-constant claim.
claims.costs: N launched photons; Gaussian-block detection fraction at least eta_det/16 on the good event; all residual/no-click outcomes counted.
claims.falsifier: A flaw in the source CVX-LS theorem, scaling/normalization derivation, or good-frame event.

claims.statement: For exactly N launched photons, the full Parseval POVM output counts are multinomial. The fixed-N law is the all-outcome Pois(N q_i) law conditioned on total count N. For any success event determined by the Gaussian-block counts, its fixed-N failure probability is at most the Poissonized failure probability divided by P(Pois(N)=N), which is O(sqrt(N)) times the Poissonized failure. This yields failure O(sqrt(N) exp(-c d))+P(bad frame), exponentially small for polynomial N in d.
assumptions: All POVM output channels and the no-click/loss category are included in the conditioned total.
The Poissonized success event uses the same estimator and depends only on Gaussian-block counts.
The source failure probability is O(exp(-c d)).
claims.status: Direct conditioning proof; de-Poissonization penalty is explicit and may be loose.
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary Poisson-multinomial conditioning; no new concentration theorem.
claims.costs: Exactly N input photons including all no-click and residual events.
claims.falsifier: A mismatch between the full POVM multinomial law and the conditional independent-Poisson law.

claims.statement: The source theorem permits bounded complex sub-Gaussian entries rather than only Gaussian entries. The distribution P(phi=0)=3/4 and P(phi=2 zeta)=1/16 for each zeta in {1,i,-1,-i} has E phi=E phi^2=0, E|phi|^2=1, E|phi|^4=4 and hence mu=3, so row coefficients can be drawn exactly from {0,+-2,+-2i}.
assumptions: The entries and rows are independent with the stated common distribution.
m/d is large enough for the corresponding sub-Gaussian singular-value bounds and source theorem.
claims.status: Moment calculation proved directly; application of source theorem is conditional on its sub-Gaussian assumptions.
claims.novelty_boundary: An explicit finite-alphabet instance of the published theorem assumptions; no new phase-retrieval theorem.
claims.costs: O(d^2) exact row coefficients plus calibration and synthesis of the residual completion.
claims.falsifier: A moment-calculation error or violation of the theorem assumptions by the stated finite distribution.

unknown: Whether a polynomial-time estimator with this rate is already proved directly for the polar-normalized random Parseval frame B=G(G*G)^(-1/2), whose rows are correlated.
A direct fixed-N multinomial CVX-LS theorem avoiding the O(sqrt(N)) de-Poissonization failure penalty.
Numerical values for the hidden sample ratio L, failure exponent c, and estimator constant C3 in the primary theorem.
Robustness thresholds for finite frame calibration error, residual-completion error, background counts, nonuniform loss, detector quantization, saturation, and approximate SDP solving.
Physical optical network/control energy and calibration-exposure costs for realizing the Parseval completion; no hardware advantage is established.

ledger.statement: For M equal-cost resolvable FOV locations with exactly K detectable-positive locations at arbitrary unknown support, the minimax probability of detecting at least one in b distinct queries is 1 - binom(M-K,b)/binom(M,b). Uniform sampling without replacement attains the value. Under the uniform K-subset prior, adaptive policies using only positive/negative results have the same average success probability.
assumptions: fixed M and K
distinct equal-cost FOVs
perfect binary FOV readout
no side information correlated with target location
ledger.status: exact conditional model theorem; classical and not claimed new
ledger.novelty_boundary: Hypergeometric simple-random-sampling identity and exchangeability argument; no biological sample claim.
ledger.costs: One unit per FOV; real scout, stage, optical resolution, exposure, spectral-channel, storage, and analysis costs are handled separately.
ledger.falsifier: An adaptive strategy using only the stipulated binary outcomes and no location-correlated data exceeds the finite-population worst-case minimax value.
ledger.next_gate: For any proposed advantage, identify and validate the extra spatial prior, proxy, cluster prior, or post-positive follow-up interface.

ledger.statement: If L aggregate channels retain only independent Poisson totals with means given by the L integrated spatial intensity maps, then any two maps with equal per-channel integrals induce identical data laws; spatial organization cannot be tested from these totals alone.
assumptions: only channel totals retained
independent Poisson counts
same integrated intensity in every channel
ledger.novelty_boundary: Identifiability statement for a specified aggregate Poisson interface; known general principle, not a claim about every spectroscopy instrument.
ledger.costs: Spatially resolved readouts or side information are outside the aggregate-only interface and must be charged if used.
ledger.falsifier: An aggregate-only measurement channel distinguishes two maps despite exactly equal complete observed intensity vectors and equal noise laws.
ledger.next_gate: Specify actual instrument outputs and determine whether any retained feature contains spatial labels or nonlinear spatial statistics.

ledger.statement: In the illustrative finite population (M_H,K_H)=(100,10), (M_L,K_L)=(900,1), scout cost 8 high-resolution-FOV equivalents, total budget 28, and minimum one confirmatory FOV per stratum, exact allocation (19,1) gives detection probability 0.8916076 versus 0.2694736 for uniform 28-FOV sampling at equal total cost.
assumptions: illustrative fixed FOV-positive counts
validated stratum map and calibration included in scout cost
equal unit confirmatory field costs
uniform within-stratum sampling without replacement
fixed resolution/noise/classification threshold
ledger.status: exact finite computation from model assumptions; not biological evidence
ledger.novelty_boundary: A transparent conditional design comparison; not a new sampling algorithm or empirical claim.
ledger.costs: Scout, calibration, and scout analysis charged as 8 FOV equivalents; confirmatory acquisition uses the remaining 20.
ledger.falsifier: The exact combinatorial output differs when recomputed from the stated counts and allocations.
ledger.next_gate: Replace known counts with pilot uncertainty intervals and test on held-out specimens at matched end-to-end cost.

ledger.statement: Baker et al. model spatial FOV overdispersion by gamma-Poisson/negative-binomial and regional cell counts by beta-binomial, using pilot-estimated abundance/adjacency parameters; their results are model-conditioned and assume perfect marker-defined cell labels.
assumptions: as specified in cited paper and its datasets
ledger.novelty_boundary: Prior art for overdispersed spatial power analysis; does not supply a universal adaptive guarantee.
ledger.costs: Pilot data and spatial profiling assumptions are inputs; technical classifier error is not modeled as perfect ground truth.
ledger.falsifier: Full-text source contradicts the stated distributions or assumptions.
ledger.next_gate: Fit and validate the chosen overdispersion model on the intended specimen and technology.

ledger.overall_status: internally reconstructed corollary; no external proof review or novelty clearance

claims.statement: For complex dimension d >= 2 and a nondegenerate intensity matrix A with finite phase-retrieval condition number, beta_{Psi_A}^{ell_2}=2 iff the normalized row directions u_j=a_j/||a_j|| with probabilities p_j=||a_j||^4/S, S=sum_j||a_j||^4, form a weighted complex projective 2-design: sum_j p_j Pi_j^{tensor 2}=2 P_sym/[d(d+1)].
assumptions: L_A > 0
standard unnormalized ell_2 norm on raw intensity coordinates
distance ||xx*-yy*||_*
zero rows discarded
claims.status: internally reconstructed, algebraically consistent, awaiting specialist review; not novelty-cleared
claims.source_pointers: Peng-Han-Huang equations (1)-(4), Theorem 3.1, proof of Theorem 3.1 equations (25)-(29), and restriction inequality (17). Sufficiency follows directly by contracting the 2-design moment identity with X and H=(uv*+vu*)/2.
claims.novelty_boundary: Projective 2-design moments are classical. Balan-Bodmann-Casazza-Edidin (2009) give the design inverse; the exact equality characterization for the 2026 global ell_2 phase-retrieval condition number appears to be a short corollary, but priority is unverified.
claims.costs: At least d^2 active intensity rows are necessary for exact equality. This condition number does not charge exposure, shot noise, calibration, or precision.
claims.falsifier: Find a d>=2 matrix with beta=2 whose weighted row-direction fourth moment is not 2P_sym/[d(d+1)], or find a flaw in equality propagation through U^2>=S/3, L<=M, M^2<=S/12 and the two-dimensional restrictions.
claims.next_gate: Independent frame-theory review of equality propagation and polarization, followed by a targeted literature/priority search.

claims.statement: A positive weighted complex projective 2-design in C^d has at least d^2 points. If it has exactly d^2 points, all design probabilities equal 1/d^2 and the directions form a SIC/equiangular tight frame; hence exact beta=2 with exactly d^2 rows forces equal row norms and SIC directions.
assumptions: all design weights positive
projectors are rank-one normalized
claims.status: proof reconstructed from the traceless-Hermitian covariance and checked symbolically by derivation; standard SIC/design connection, not a novelty claim
claims.source_pointers: The rank bound uses covariance rank d^2-1 on traceless Hermitian matrices. The equality case follows from the Gram matrix of sqrt(p_j)(Pi_j-I/d). Balan et al. cite maximal equiangular tight frames as projective 2-designs; Scott identifies SICs as minimal tight rank-one IC POVMs.
claims.novelty_boundary: SICs and the fact that they are minimal tight rank-one designs are classical. This only translates that fact into an exact row-count obstruction for beta=2 under the Peng-Han-Huang objective.
claims.costs: d^2 scalar intensity channels are necessary to exactly attain beta=2; this is quadratic versus O(d) generic injectivity counts in many regimes.
claims.falsifier: An explicit positive weighted 2-design with fewer than d^2 projectors, or a d^2-point weighted design that is nonuniform/non-equiangular.
claims.next_gate: No mathematical gate apparent; check source definitions/normalization and obtain specialist review.

claims.statement: For an equal-weight unit-vector projective 2-design with m rows and exact intensities y_j=|a_j*x|^2, T=sum_j y_j Pi_j gives xx*=(d(d+1)/m)T-(d/m)Tr(T)I.
assumptions: unit-norm row directions
equal weights 1/m
exact noiseless intensity data
claims.status: classical identity; finite d=2 numerical verification passed
claims.source_pointers: Balan et al. Theorem 3.4 (Levenshtein reconstruction formula) and Remark 3.5, pp. 7-8. Their structured implementation is O(md), or O(d^3) for m=Theta(d^2); naive dense matrix accumulation is O(d^4).
claims.novelty_boundary: No novelty claimed; only translated into the current notation and tested on the six Pauli eigenstates in dimension 2.
claims.costs: Specialized known reconstruction is O(md) arithmetic; naive dense accumulation is O(md^2). Requires known/calibrated projectors and exact or estimated intensities.
claims.falsifier: The formula fails the 2-design second-moment identity; finite check currently has max absolute error below 5e-16 in d=2.
claims.next_gate: If noise claims are desired, prove a perturbation bound for approximate designs and specify a count/noise model.

claims.statement: The published theorem's literal phrase 'for any matrix A' cannot include d=1: nonzero scalar rows yield beta=1, so the universal complex lower bound needs d>=2 or an implicit exclusion of the scalar case.
assumptions: at least one nonzero row
same raw ell_2 intensity norm and nuclear-norm quotient distance
claims.status: directly verified counterexample to literal unrestricted wording
claims.source_pointers: Theorem 3.1 says 'For any matrix A'; its proof immediately reduces to two columns. For d=1, Psi_A(x)=(|a_j|^2|x|^2)_j and dist(x,y)=||x|^2-|y|^2|, so L=U=||( |a_j|^2 )_j||_2.
claims.novelty_boundary: A scope/wording caveat, not part of the equality theorem and not an accusation about author intent; the intended domain may be d>=2.
claims.costs: None; one-dimensional exact calculation.
claims.falsifier: A source definition excluding d=1 or an alternate quotient metric changing the displayed scalar calculation.
claims.next_gate: Check full published article text or author clarification if relying on this as an erratum-level issue.

finite_checks.scope: d=2 Pauli X/Y/Z bases; verifies one exact rank-one reconstruction, the tensor 2-design identity, and total intensity normalization; maximum absolute errors 2.24e-16, 4.44e-16, and 8.88e-16.
not_evidence_for: algorithmic complexity beyond cited prior work

ledger.overall_status: internally derived quantitative implication; proof not externally reviewed; construction prior art source-verified

claims.statement: Let d>=2, S=sum_j||a_j||^4>0, p_j=||a_j||^4/S, F=sum_j p_j Pi_j^{tensor 2}, F0=2P_sym/[d(d+1)], rho=(beta_{Psi_A}^{ell_2}/2)^2-1, and C_d=2(d+2)(d+3)/[d(d+1)]. Then ||F-F0||_F^2 <= C_d rho max(1,rho). In particular, if beta<=2(1+epsilon) with 2epsilon+epsilon^2<=1, then ||F-F0||_F <= sqrt(C_d(2epsilon+epsilon^2)).
assumptions: complex sensing space
raw unnormalized ell2 norm on exact intensity coordinates
distance ||xx*-yy*||_*
finite beta and S>0
weights p_j proportional to fourth powers of row norms
claims.status: internally derived using Peng-Han-Huang dimension-two bound, Haar random 2-plane averaging, and exact Haar fourth-moment contraction; Monte Carlo sanity check only; needs independent proof audit
claims.source_pointers: Peng-Han-Huang eq. (17), their complex d=2 estimate M^2<=sum||a_j||^4/12 in eq. (25), and U=||A||_{2->4}^2. The random-plane Beta(2,d-2) projection moment and four-copy Haar permutation contraction are derived in the report.
claims.novelty_boundary: Weighted design/frame-potential identities are classical. Targeted source searches found no direct beta-to-Frobenius stability implication for this phase-retrieval condition number; priority remains uncleared. Castellano et al. (2026), arXiv:2602.13099v3, already use normalized Frobenius moment error as an approximate-design metric and prove stronger fixed-cardinality Welch bounds; no beta-to-moment connection in that model was found.
claims.costs: This is a model theorem and charges no photon exposure, Poisson noise, calibration, or finite precision. Per-row gains needed for nonuniform weights are t_j=p_j^(1/4).
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the random-plane L bound, or a trace-zero Hermitian D supported on Sym^2 for which the stated four-copy contraction fails. The random-D numerical checks currently agree within 0.6% Monte Carlo error for d=2,3,4.
claims.next_gate: Independent symbolic review of the 24-permutation Haar contraction and proof of superoperator/Frobenius identification; then seek a direct prior-art match.

claims.statement: Let N=d(d+1)/2 and C_d=2(d+2)(d+3)/[d(d+1)]. For m nonzero rows and near-optimal rho<=1, rho >= C_d^(-1) max{(sum_j p_j^2-1/N)_+, (d^2-m)_+/[m(d+1)^2]}. If m=o(d^2), then rho >= (1+o(1))/(2m). Consequently beta-2 >= 2(sqrt(1+(1+o(1))/(2m))-1)=Omega(1/m); if additionally m->infinity, beta-2 >= (1+o(1))/(2m).
assumptions: complex d>=2
same phase-retrieval model and normalized row weights as BETA-TO-HAAR-MOMENT
m counts nonzero rows
claims.status: follows from BETA-TO-HAAR-MOMENT plus standard frame-potential and Eckart-Young rank bounds; internal derivation
claims.source_pointers: Weighted frame potential: Tr(F^2)-1/N>=sum p_j^2-1/N. For the second term partially transpose F: it is PSD trace one and rank<=m, while F0^Gamma has spectrum 1/d once and 1/[d(d+1)] with multiplicity d^2-1. The closest trace-one PSD rank-m approximation yields squared error (d^2-m)/[m(d+1)^2].
claims.novelty_boundary: Welch/design equality and approximate-design moment metrics are prior art. Castellano et al. (2026) develop stronger Welch bounds using partial-transpose spectra for fixed-cardinality uniform frames; our beta bridge is distinct, the rank technique is known, the stated weighted bound is elementary, and sharpness is unresolved.
claims.costs: Shows a deterministic row-count/conditioning tradeoff; no physical exposure accounting.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the beta-to-Haar-moment stability law, to the weighted frame-potential inequality, or to the trace-constrained rank-m approximation value for F0^Gamma.
claims.next_gate: Compare the weighted beta-gap bound against sharper fixed-cardinality Welch/approximate-design bounds and determine attainable row-count/weight regimes.

claims.statement: Given Jasper-Mixon's weighted complex projective 2-design weights w_j with sum N=d(d+1)/2 and unit directions u_j, define p_j=w_j/N and intensity rows a_j=p_j^(1/4)u_j. Then sum||a_j||^4=1, the condition-number design weights are exactly p_j, and beta_{Psi_A}^{ell_2}=2. Their construction supplies such designs in every dimension with m<=d^2+O(d^1.525).
assumptions: positive weighted 2-design
unit directions
row amplitudes may be scaled individually
claims.status: Jasper-Mixon design and cardinality are source-reported; row-norm mapping and beta conclusion follow by direct substitution into the reconstructed equality theorem
claims.source_pointers: Jasper-Mixon Theorem 4 gives n(d)<=d^2+O(d^1.525); Theorem 7 and eq. (construction weights) give Bodmann-Haas rows with w_alpha=d^2/(2|G|), w_r=1/2; Corollary 8 gives n(d)<=m(d)+d.
claims.novelty_boundary: The all-d exact near-minimal weighted design is Jasper-Mixon 2025 prior art. Applying fourth-root row scaling to obtain exact phase-retrieval beta=2 is a direct model translation, not a new design construction.
claims.costs: m=d^2+O(d^1.525) intensity channels with unequal row amplitudes p_j^(1/4); explicit row storage is O(md). From the weighted moment identity, exact arithmetic reconstruction up to global phase can be done in O(md) by computing all diagonals and one nonzero row of xx*, while explicitly materializing the full d-by-d matrix costs O(md^2). No finite-precision/noisy implementation benchmark or photon/calibration model is included.
claims.falsifier: An inconsistency in the normalized weights p_j=w_j/N, their sum, or the projective moment identity. The construction has sum w_j=N by taking traces of the Jasper-Mixon identity.
claims.next_gate: If applying physically, specify detector gain/exposure constraints and compare under Poisson Fisher information rather than deterministic beta alone.

claims.statement: The beta-to-Haar-moment stability bound is one-sided and has no dimension-uniform reverse: for complete-MUB designs in prime-power d>=3, deleting one unit row gives relative Frobenius moment error O(1/d) but beta>=2sqrt(2), while the system remains informationally complete.
assumptions: all definitions as above
claims.status: proved conditional on the standard complete-MUB existence theorem in prime-power dimensions; exact algebra recorded in the report; this refutes dimension-uniform reverse stability but says nothing about whether the forward stability constant/order is sharp
claims.source_pointers: Complete MUBs are complex projective 2-designs. Removing one of m0=d(d+1) equal rows gives ||F-F0||_F^2=(1-1/N)/(m0-1)^2 and relative error O(1/d). For u=(w+e)/sqrt(2), v=(w-e)/sqrt(2), the removed squared lower-constant summand is 1/4 and the full sum is 1/2, hence Lprime^2<=1/4; the quartic upper maximum remains Uprime^2=2, so beta>=2sqrt(2). The retained measurements still span all Hermitian matrices.
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a short deletion calculation using standard complete-MUB 2-design facts, not a new frame construction. It only rules out dimension-uniform reverse stability; row count is d(d+1)-1, not sparse.
claims.costs: No new numerical experiment; the finite-row deterministic construction has d(d+1)-1 intensity coordinates and equal row norms. No photon or calibration model is supplied.
claims.falsifier: A violation of the exact design identity, the source formula for L, or a retained-row kernel containing a nonzero rank-at-most-two Hermitian matrix.
claims.next_gate: Determine whether a dimension-dependent reverse estimate can hold under additional regularity or row-count assumptions; separately assess sharpness of the forward beta-to-moment bound.

claims.statement: For every prime-power d>=3, a complete MUB design with one unit row deleted remains informationally complete, has relative ||F-F0||_F error O(1/d), yet beta_{Psi_A}^{ell_2}>=2sqrt(2). Thus moment closeness alone does not imply dimension-uniform beta closeness.

Select orthogonal u=(w+e)/sqrt2, v=(w-e)/sqrt2: the complete lower-square sum is 1/2 and the removed summand is 1/4, while Uprime^2=2. The retained set spans Hermitian matrices because the missing projector is I minus the other projectors in its basis.

With state-independent efficiency eta and an explicit no-click outcome, N attempted single-photon copies and the global count-minimum-Hellinger estimator satisfy uniformly E d_phi(x,xhat)^2<=4r/(N eta kappa_zeta^2), conditional on the frame event.

claims.statement: For a Haar-uniform unknown pure state and N copies, the best achievable mean fidelity, even with collective POVMs, is (N+1)/(N+d). Hence every estimator has mean squared projective error at least (d-1)/(N+d), or (d-1)/(N eta+d) under independent state-blind erasure probability 1-eta. The Parseval-Gaussian estimator therefore achieves the minimax dimension/copy rate O(d/(N eta)) up to constants at fixed stability tolerance; this establishes shot-noise rate, not a quantum advantage.

Squared projective metric d_phi^2=2(1-sqrt(F))

claims.exact_statement: For N=2^d frozen ordered modes X in {1,...,N}, a query t in {1,...,N-1} returns 1{X<=t} passed through an independent BSC(eta), 0<eta<1/2. At worst-case identification error delta in (0,1/4), midpoint adaptive search with r odd and r>=ln(d/delta)/C_eta reads per stage has Q_ad=d*r and error at most delta, where C_eta=-ln(2*sqrt(eta*(1-eta))). Any ex-ante randomized nonadaptive threshold schedule, even with repeated reads, complete outcome retention, and unrestricted decoding, has E[Q_na]>=(N-1)*max{1-2*delta, kl(1-delta||delta)/D_eta}, where D_eta=kl(1-eta||eta). A nonadaptive design that reads every threshold r_na=max{1,ceil(ln((2+delta)/delta)/C_eta)} times and returns the global MLE has error at most delta, so the optimal nonadaptive read count is Theta((N-1)*max{1,ln(1/delta)/D_eta}) up to absolute constants.
assumptions: The hidden mode is fixed throughout measurements.
The ordered labels and all threshold experiments are supplied and known to both policies.
The comparator has fixed known BSC noise eta with conditionally independent reads.
Nonadaptive schedules may be randomized before observations but cannot depend on outcomes; all outputs may be retained.
Each measurement read is charged, and each output is one bit.

claims.exact_statement: Fix spin S in {1/2,1,3/2,...} and fixed J_1,J_2,J_3>0. Constant heats of transport Q_plus and Q_minus in the admitted model.

All between-guard excursions stay in their mode safe sets almost surely, or a separate conditional excursion bound is included.
At each guard event, the conditional post-reset probability of remaining safe is at least 1-p_e for every reachable pre-reset state and allowed reset action.
The number of events of each edge by T is bounded almost surely by M_e.

The exact per-leg deadline success probability is p(t)=e_45^T integral_0^t exp(Q_H s)q_55 ds, identical in the reflected L leg, and M legs all succeed with probability p(t)^M by strong Markov regeneration. With no deadline but safety boundaries, p_infinity=P_45(tau_55<tau_10)=31093519817410066218136533805526688768/31093519817410066218136534504523754857<1; thus infinite safe recurrence has probability zero. claims.statement: For a candidate x at composition c0 with E_x=0 and known zero-energy binary endpoints, if there are M unqueried possible competing polymorphs at c0, exact point-energy queries are the only information source, no lower bounds are supplied, and the algorithm must decide FEASIBLE versus INFEASIBLE, then every zero-error deterministic algorithm needs M competitor queries in the worst case. Any randomized algorithm with error at most delta on the all-zero world and each single-hidden-low-polymorph world requires expected at least M(1-2 delta) competitor queries on the all-zero world for delta<1/2. For equal per-query cost c_E, expected energy-evaluation cost is at least c_E M(1-2 delta).
assumptions: The phase universe includes M distinct competing structures at the candidate composition.
A hidden phase may have energy -(tau+eta), with tau>=0 and eta>0.
The oracle reveals only the queried phase's exact energy.
No sound energy lower bounds, complete phase hull, or structure-search certificate are supplied.
UNKNOWN/abstention counts as failure to decide.
claims.novelty_boundary: A finite-oracle indistinguishability argument specialized to competing polymorphs and energy-above-hull feasibility. No priority claim; the result does not apply when a complete hull or certified lower bounds are supplied.
claims.costs: At least M competitor energy queries worst-case for deterministic zero-error decisions, or expected c_E M(1-2 delta) under the stated randomized guarantee and equal query cost. Structure generation, DFT relaxation cost, target-property evaluation, hull LP cost, training, and experiments are additional.

claims.next_gate: Instrument a phase family with multiple polymorphs and verify that all feasibility labels consume either competitor energies or a documented sound lower-bound/full-hull service.

claims.statement: For a fixed finite phase/composition universe, if every relevant per-atom phase energy changes by at most epsilon in sup norm, then the convex-hull energy at every composition changes by at most epsilon and any candidate-minus-competing-hull gap changes by at most 2 epsilon. A threshold label is invariant when the gap margin exceeds 2 epsilon.
assumptions: The composition-feasible convex-mixture set is fixed under the perturbation.
The energy error bound is simultaneous and uniform over candidate and all competing phases.
The same reference-energy convention and normalization are used for all phase energies.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard convex-mixture stability argument applied to hull-gap classification; no claim of a new general convex-analysis theorem.
claims.costs: Computing hull bounds requires an LP/convex-hull operation over acquired phases. Obtaining uniform simultaneous energy intervals is an upstream data/model-acquisition cost and is not supplied by an average test MAE.
claims.falsifier: A fixed phase universe and uniform sup-norm perturbation with a hull value changing by more than epsilon, or a gap changing by more than 2 epsilon.
claims.next_gate: Measure family-held-out, simultaneous energy bounds and test whether they support the declared hull threshold margins.

claims.statement: Given simultaneous valid intervals L_y<=E_y<=U_y for every phase in a declared finite phase universe, LPs minimizing mixture energy using L and U bound the true competing-phase hull. U_x-H^-_x<=tau is a sufficient robust feasibility condition; L_x-H^+_x>tau is a sufficient robust infeasibility condition; otherwise return UNKNOWN.

All intervals have simultaneous coverage; marginal coverage alone is insufficient without correction.
Composition vectors and energy normalization are consistent.
