claims.falsifier: For any energy realization within all supplied intervals, the computed FEASIBLE/INFEASIBLE classification violates the stated threshold condition.
claims.next_gate: Implement exact small-pool LPs, then compare the query schedule against an equally informed cost-aware point-label BO baseline on held-out phase families.

claims.exact_statement: For q_t + c q_x = 0 on [0,L], with q(0,t)=u(t), nonnegative q0 bounded by Q, an unknown time-constant c in a certified interval [c_-,c_+], and nonnegative zero-order-hold controls of period h bounded by U_max, if the controller knows initial cell integrals, uses the upper envelope for all within-cell profiles consistent with those integrals and Q, and at each sample chooses a command satisfying A_k^+(c,s)+B(c,s)a <= M_max for every admitted c and every elapsed s in [0,h], then total inventory M_c(t)=integral_0^L q(x,t) dx remains at most M_max for all t. The continuous supremum gives the largest command robust over the acquired profile class; the stated speed-time grid with its Lipschitz margin gives a conservative certified implementation.
assumptions: Scalar linear transport with constant-in-time positive speed; c is uncertain only within a fixed certified compact interval.
No diffusion, reaction, recirculation, time-varying coefficient, or unmodeled source.
Initial state is nonnegative and bounded by known Q; cell integrals are acquired with known measurement-error intervals.
Boundary input is nonnegative, bounded, and held constant on each interval of length h.
Initial inventory is certified below M_max; finite-precision evaluations round mass upper bounds upward and commands downward.

The candidate interface is plug-flow total inventory with uncertain fixed speed, acquired initial cell masses, held actuation, and a certified speed-time grid. claims.title: Source-weighted disturbance robustness for common-span endotactic switched inclusions
claims.exact_statement: For a finite family of finite actual exponent-arrow diagrams, each endotactic and all with the same stoichiometric span S, with every rate coefficient in a supplied interval [kappa,K] where 0<kappa<=K<infinity, fix any positive class P=(c+S) intersect R^d_{>0}. Assume the N33 affine-activity witness F_h=min_lambda(r_lambda dot x+b_lambda(h)), H>0, h_P, compact convex plateau K_h, and scale ladder. For every nonneutral active slope r, mode j, let E*_{j,r} be the edges minimizing r dot source among edges with r dot nu nonzero, and Phi_{j,r}(x)=max_{e in E*_{j,r}} x^(source_e); set underlinePhi_r=min_j Phi_{j,r}. Let U(t,x) be a nonempty compact convex multifunction with values in S, measurable in t, upper semicontinuous and locally bounded in x. If, for some 0<=theta<1, every u in U(t,x) obeys r dot u >= -theta*kappa*H*underlinePhi_r(x) for every 0<h<=h_P, x in [h,h^-1]^d, and every active nonneutral slope r of F_h at x, then every maximal absolutely continuous solution of dot x in co(union_j {sum_e a_je*x^(source_je)*nu_je : a_je in [kappa,K]}) + U(t,x) from every x0 in P is global, remains positive, and enters one common compact convex K_P subset P in finite time. K_P and each x0's entry-time bound are independent of rate, mode, mixture, disturbance, and solution selections. A box entry-time bound at scale h is [F_h(c)-min_{x in [h,h^-1]^d}F_h(x)]/[(1-theta)*kappa*H*h^M], where M=max_{j,e}||source_je||_1. There is no entry bound uniform over all x0 in an unbounded P or across different classes.
assumptions: Each mode's actual exponent-arrow diagram is finite and endotactic under the essential-edge definition: for every w, every essential edge at a maximal w-source has w dot nu < 0.
Every mode has exactly the same stoichiometric subspace S; all velocities and disturbances lie in S.
Reaction rates lie in one globally supplied positive interval [kappa,K].

The N33 affine-activity, weighted-source, compact-plateau construction holds for the finite union of mode complexes and this class P; this is internally reconstructed candidate evidence, not externally certified proof.

The disturbance multifunction is nonempty compact convex, t-measurable, upper semicontinuous in state, and locally bounded on the positive orthant; its support satisfies the source-weighted one-sided bound in the exact statement almost everywhere in time.
claims.status: conditional theorem; internally derived differential-inclusion transfer from N33, not externally validated or priority-cleared

This report does not claim either framework as new. The scoped transfer adds a source-tier-specific one-sided disturbance budget to the N33 classwise finite-entry absorber. claims.statement: For a capped protein count N in {0,...,M}, with only unit births of predictable intensity lambda_t <= B and independent per-molecule loss rate gamma, the process is pathwise dominated by the capped immigration-death chain with birth rate B and loss rate gamma. From common initial count, liminf_t P(N_t < h) >= [sum_{n=0}^{h-1} q^n/n!]/[sum_{n=0}^{M} q^n/n!], q=B/gamma.
assumptions: Single-molecule upward jumps only; no bursts or alternate protein-production routes.
Predictable causal birth intensity is uniformly bounded by B across all promoter, resource, and controller states.
The count has a hard ceiling M, with births blocked at M.
Each molecule has independent constant loss rate gamma>0; feedback does not reduce that rate.
The circuit process and comparator start at the same count.
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_model_result; bounded-rate immigration-death domination is established prior art; novelty not claimed
claims.novelty_boundary: Hemberg and Barahona (2007) already use a first-order immigration-death process to dominate bounded Hill/Monod gene-expression propensities and apply it to the toggle switch and repressilator. The finite-cap threshold-tail formula is a direct corollary. The result is a peak-cap screen, not a same-average-cost feedback comparison or a nature claim.

not_charged: growth-mediated dilution unless included in gamma

The present note contributes only the exact finite-error Poisson testing form with total expected raw receptor events charged across all cells and arbitrary downstream stochastic postprocessing. primary_claim.exact_statement: For two binary outputs with independent per-molecule death rate 1, single-unit births, arbitrary full-count causal feedback, and a shared instantaneous aggregate birth-intensity cap B, stationary marginals P(N1=1)=P(N2=1)=1/10 are feasible iff B >= (6-sqrt(34))/(sqrt(34)-5), approximately 0.203439. The lower bound is attained by symmetric state-dependent birth rates described in CYCLE2_REPORT.md.
assumptions: Output state is (N1,N2) in {0,1}^2.
Each occupied output molecule dies independently at rate 1.
A birth adds one molecule to exactly one output; no bursts.
Birth intensity is zero for an output already at its cap 1.
At every state and time, the sum of accepted birth intensities is at most B.
The objective and constraints are stationary long-run occupancy and birth-flow averages.
The controller has access to the full two-output count state.
primary_claim.status: exact model derivation with constructive attainment; novelty unknown
primary_claim.novelty_boundary: The example refutes independent scalar-capacity plus mean-cost checks for the specified shared-cap process. General controlled birth/death average optimization by LP is established queue-control/CTMDP prior art. No priority search has established novelty of the numeric two-output boundary. The model is not a direct biological validation.

secondary_claim.exact_statement: For finite capped species counts with single-unit controlled births, fixed positive linear death rates, and a shared per-state birth-intensity cap, stationary joint-threshold optimization under linear average production or state/action costs is exactly a finite occupation-flow LP. Feasible birth flows z_{x,i} and state masses pi_x obey statewise shared-cap constraints and global balance; conversely u_i(x)=z_{x,i}/pi_x realizes every feasible stationary flow pair.
assumptions: Finite state space product_i {0,...,M_i}.
Births are single-unit and unavailable at each species cap.
Death intensity for species i is gamma_i*N_i with gamma_i>0.
Full count-state feedback is implementable.
Reliability and costs are stationary long-run averages linear in state/action occupation.
Any dynamically evolving resource/controller state that changes rates or costs is included in the state.
secondary_claim.status: proved specialization; general method subsumed by established CTMDP occupation-LP literature
secondary_claim.novelty_boundary: The occupation-flow reduction is standard CTMDP/queue-control mathematics; the specialization is an exact modeling/analysis tool, not a general new optimization principle. Censored observations make the full-state LP an information relaxation; dynamic hidden resources must be added to the state.

literature_status.queue_control: Established prior art. Serfozo 1981 treats controlled birth/death processes and queues under average reward and discusses a linear program; Guo, Huang, and Song 2012 establish equivalent constrained-average CTMDP LPs for history-dependent policies and illustrate with a controlled birth/death system.
literature_status.molecular_feedback: Primary literature already studies antithetic controller architecture and noise reduction under resource competition (Chakravarty, Zhang, Tian 2024), using stochastic simulation/FDT rather than this hard-cap stationary joint-threshold LP.
literature_status.spatial_gene_optimization: Resource-constrained optimization of spatial gene-expression patterns is already studied (Sokolowski et al. 2025, PNAS), with a positional-information objective and production/degradation/resource-utilization constraints; it is distinct from the exact stochastic threshold model here.
literature_status.negative_novelty_claim: No exhaustive novelty search was conducted; absence of this exact formula from the checked sources is not evidence of priority.

Shared peak rate B at every count state and time.
Any explicitly added state-running or state/action controller cost.
not_charged_unless_augmented: Ribosome, RNA polymerase, ATP, or resource-pool dynamics.
Cell growth/dilution changes beyond fixed linear degradation.
Finite-time latency, observation/censoring cost, or switching energy.
Cell-cell transport or multicellular spatial communication.

For biology, augment the state by the limiting resource and controller species, then test whether the threshold LP predicts a measurable reliability tradeoff.

claims.exact_statement: For a capped protein birth-death process N in {0,...,M} with unit births, predictable causal accepted birth intensity 0<=lambda_t<=B, and independent per-molecule loss rate gamma, every controller based on periodic, noisy, delayed, or perfect observations obeys liminf_t Pr(N_t<h)>=Z_(h-1)(B/gamma)/Z_M(B/gamma). The no-observation policy lambda=B below M attains equality. Thus observation rate and precision do not improve the low-tail reliability frontier under a fixed pointwise peak birth cap.
assumptions: Births add exactly one target protein.
Accepted protein birth intensity is predictable and bounded pointwise by B.
The count is capped at M.
Each extant protein is lost independently at constant rate gamma>0.
Observation-based control is causal; sensor errors, delays, and schedules affect only the predictable choice of lambda_t.
The objective is stationary/liminf low-copy probability Pr(N<h), not average energy or another task utility.
claims.novelty_boundary: No novelty claim. Bounded-rate domination is established prior art in gene-regulatory stochastic models. Partially observed and controlled-observation MDPs are established; this application says their sensor choices cannot beat the peak-cap floor for this specific monotone tail objective.

Every LP vertex has prefix support {0,...,K} and at most one strict birth-cap edge within that positive support; therefore some optimizer has all supported birth rates at B except for at most one interior rate, followed by a support cutoff.

Classical RK4 dt=0.02 min, final time 300 min, endpoint rule F<20, ATP>0.5, Pi>5 and alive
claims.evidence: Corrected CellML expression-cost implementation yields 14/13/12 deaths and 108/112/120 balanced endpoints for off durations 30/35/40 min respectively.
claims.scope_boundary: Not validated numerics, not a theorem against all shared policies, uses a distinct genotype from the exact source-reference tube certificate, and F=300 mM is a model stress point rather than an observed yeast state.

claims.statement: The source-model feedback certificate is not a biological breakthrough or a demonstrated advantage over existing startup regulation; large-basin recovery under finite sensing and shared culture actuation remains unresolved.
claims.status: UNKNOWN; no novelty or priority claim
claims.evidence: Prior work includes ATP inhibition, trehalose cycling/T6P, phosphate mobilization, yeast startup thresholds, and recent pathway-transplant regulation. Available FBP, ATP, and Pi measurements do not establish the joint per-cell error/latency interface, and shared glucose fails the whole-tube population guarantee.

claims.next_gate: Calibrate a named strain and actuator, establish separately addressable perfusion and the composite flux error on held-out transitions, then compare against same-information constrained MPC, a prespecified continuous fixed-glucose optimum, and a trehalose/T6P or glucose-withdrawal control.

claims.statement: Under the declared source-accessible measurement interface, the fraction of consumed cellobiose carbon that can become target-available is not narrowed below the stoichiometric outer envelope [0,1] (supremal upper bound 1); the endpoints are not asserted to reproduce every measured intracellular isotope peak.
assumptions: Only the reported intracellular isotope-pool, aggregate ECAR, and target-only cellobiose-response measurements are imposed.
No total cellobiose uptake, species-resolved extracellular isotope balance, or target uptake of cellobiose-derived products is available in the reviewed source materials.
Secreted-product fractions and target capture fractions are constrained only by nonnegativity, capture at most one, and carbon conservation.
claims.novelty_boundary: Novelty UNKNOWN. This is a source-specific inference/identifiability result, not a new tumor-lactate mechanism and not evidence that T cells actually leak carbon.
claims.costs: The mathematical interface result has negligible computation cost. The proposed EL4 design has 240 media samples, including 120 tracer-fed samples; nominal U-13C12-cellobiose use is 42.5 mg at 200 uL/sample or 212.5 mg at 1 mL/sample. Vendor price is quote-only; UCLA FACS rates are published but sorting hours depend on sample yield; LC-MS core quote remains required.
claims.falsifier: The claim would be falsified if the paper or an accessible raw dataset supplied an extracellular isotope balance or a target-cell measurement that quantitatively bounds transfer under the matched coculture conditions.
claims.next_gate: Measure U-13C-cellobiose-derived extracellular products and isotope incorporation in sorted target cells at matched oxygen, pH, and effector:target ratios.

claims.statement: For an initial feed B0 mM cellobiose, carbon conservation gives a strict ceiling of 12*B0 mM carbon atoms and at most 4*B0 mM lactate if all dosed cellobiose is consumed and all of its carbon exits as lactate; the 5 mM source pulse therefore has ceilings 60 mM carbon atoms, 10 mM glucose equivalents, and 20 mM lactate.
assumptions: Cellobiose hydrolysis yields two glucose units.
Each glucose unit contains six carbon atoms and complete lactate fermentation yields two C3 lactates.
The source pulse is treated only as a maximum initial substrate inventory; complete uptake and lactate secretion are not asserted.
claims.novelty_boundary: Stoichiometric bookkeeping only; no novelty or biological occurrence claim.
claims.costs: Exact rational arithmetic; negligible computation. Source-specific 5 mM pulse taken from the dissertation figure legend.
claims.falsifier: An error in pathway stoichiometry, chemical formula, or source pulse condition.
claims.next_gate: Measure uptake fraction and extracellular labeled carbon to replace the conditional ceiling with a confidence interval.

claims.statement: For measured per-effector cellobiose uptake qB, effector:target ratio r, exported lactate-carbon fraction fL, and target capture fraction aL, the maximum carbon-equivalent target flux is 2*r*qB*fL*aL glucose equivalents per target per hour; a material target rescue threshold dT is reachable only if 2*r*qB*fL*aL >= dT.
assumptions: qB is measured in mol cellobiose per viable effector per hour.
fL and aL are measured under the same coculture oxygen, pH, activation, and density conditions.
Glucose-equivalent units compare carbon only and do not assert equal ATP yields.
claims.novelty_boundary: A measurable test criterion; no biological threshold or efficacy is claimed before acquisition.
claims.costs: Requires per-cell uptake, isotope-resolved export/target capture, viable cell counts, target low-glucose titration, and matched oxygen/pH assays.
claims.falsifier: Any measured parameter set violating the claimed equality would indicate unit, stoichiometry, or assay-accounting error.
claims.next_gate: Acquire qB, fL, aL, and dT in EL4-OVA/OT-I, then replicate the decisive condition in human CAR-T/Raji.

claims.statement: The CDT-1/GH1-1 pathway causes consequential glucose, lactate, or other carbon transfer from engineered T cells to the tested tumor targets.
assumptions: Would require cellobiose-derived carbon to be measured in extracellular metabolites and/or target cells.
Would require target functional response attributable to that transfer after accounting for direct CAR-T killing and shared-nutrient effects.
claims.novelty_boundary: The cellobiose T-cell pathway is source-reported and has prior art. Tumor lactate uptake is established in some tumor models. Consequential crossfeeding by these engineered T cells remains unknown.
claims.costs: Proposed first EL4 stage: 240 media samples per four independent blocks before target-pellet, function, and energy wells; 120 are tracer-fed. Nominal labeled cellobiose need is 42.5 mg at 200 uL/sample or 212.5 mg at 1 mL/sample, excluding standards and repeats. Reagent quote required; UCLA FACS rate $71.48-$99.27/hour internal, LC-MS rate unpublished. Human CAR-T/Raji roughly doubles the media base.
claims.falsifier: A well-powered co-culture tracer experiment that places upper bounds below the preregistered materiality threshold on both target isotope uptake and target functional rescue would reject consequential transfer in that declared context.
claims.next_gate: Run the isotope-resolved source-to-target experiment with target-only lactate and glucose calibration arms.

claims.statement: Cellobiose exclusivity does not by itself establish nutrient independence: the source pathway imports one proton per cellobiose and the engineered cells can change shared nutrient demand through activity/expansion, while ATP-equivalent proton-pumping and transgene-expression costs remain unquantified.
assumptions: CDT-1 proton symport and cellobiose-supported effector activity/proliferation are source-reported.
No ATP-per-import or CDT-1/GH1-1 expression energy cost is inferred from the publication.
claims.novelty_boundary: No novel energetic mechanism or cost value claimed; this is an explicit model interface and acquisition gate.
claims.costs: Matched glucose-replete controls, ATP/ADP and respiration assays, proton-flux/pH measurements, plus glutamine/oxygen/amino-acid balance measurements.
claims.falsifier: Matched experiments showing no measurable difference in shared-resource depletion or energy burden over the declared state range would remove the corresponding coupling terms within their detection bounds.
claims.next_gate: Acquire cH and cexpr in matched sorted populations while measuring shared-resource depletion across cellobiose dose and effector:target ratio.

claims.statement: For each PLOS 2021 Table 2 BC and IC genotype, the full source CellML metabolite/growth/dilution model leaves K={1.8<=F<=2.2, 0.585<=A<=1.5, P>=2, A+P<=14} forward invariant under actual-flux feedback U=L-(F-2)+e when |e|<=0.15 mM/min. Since 0.585 mM exceeds each exact CellML ATP-profit threshold, H is nondecreasing there for H>0.
claims.status: conditional theorem; exact rational facet calculation with ln(2)<0.7 over published rounded Table 2 genotype decimals
assumptions: PLOS Table 2 values are treated as exact at their printed decimal precision
CellML fourth-power expression-cost formula and its fixed vatper=5, vatpm=0 growth normalization
Full H-gated source growth law and its metabolite dilution terms
Total actual upper-flux error, including sensing, fitting, delay and actuation, is at most 0.15 mM/min
An independently addressable glucose input realizes the required upper flux below saturation
The CellML algebraic vacuolar-phosphate law with Kvac=250 mM is accepted
claims.evidence: The exact Fraction verifier checks all six inward face margins for both genotypes, the ATP-profit thresholds, and finite glucose inversion. Weakest margins are 0.017232 mM/min (IC ATP upper) and 0.032769 mM/min (IC ATP lower).
claims.novelty_boundary: The result extends the source-reference cell certificate to the paper's simulated BC/IC genotypes. It is not external validation or a biological claim.
claims.costs: One independently addressable feed per controlled cell/state class; F-only staleness limits are 14.02 s (BC) and 15.49 s (IC) only if all other error sources are zero and ATP/Pi are current. Reporter, calibration and throughput costs are unpriced.
claims.falsifier: Measured parameter uncertainty violates an inward face or ATP-profit threshold; or held-out actual flux tracking exceeds 0.15 mM/min.
claims.next_gate: Acquire strain-specific kinetic confidence sets and joint per-cell F/A/P support, then test a finite-bandwidth implementation.

claims.statement: For the PLOS Table 2 source genotypes, no common glucose input can preserve the lower-F face for a BC cell at (F,A,P,H)=(1.8,0.585,7,1) and the upper-F face for an IC cell at (2.2,0.6,2,1), even with ideal zero-error glucose actuation and full source growth dilution.
assumptions: The two source-model genotypes receive the same extracellular glucose concentration at each time
Both state vectors are required to remain in K
The printed Table 2 genotype decimals and CellML rate laws are used
CellML expression costs are recomputed; both witness ATP profits are positive at H=Hmax
claims.evidence: Let z=G/(0.1+G). BC lower-F inwardness requires z>=0.4699966 (G>=0.088678 mM), using the weaker condition that drops positive growth dilution. IC upper-F inwardness allows z<=0.2377541 (G<=0.031191 mM), using ln(2)<0.7 to upper-bound the full source growth term. The gap is 0.2322426 in z.
claims.novelty_boundary: The states are admissible witnesses, not reported simultaneous trajectories. The source paper models genotype coexistence under common glucose, but the exact witness co-occurrence is not established. This refutes a uniform-tube guarantee for the pair, not all shared-feed recovery strategies.
claims.costs: Two distinct glucose feed concentrations are necessary for this exact simultaneous face pair; one additional independent feed channel is the minimum snapshot actuator increase. Dollars and wet-lab mapping of the simulated genotypes are unknown.
claims.falsifier: The model equations or parameter values are wrong, or an experimental claim that the pair occurs is falsified by joint single-cell state data. The mathematical conditional itself is falsified by an arithmetic/source-model error.
claims.next_gate: Measure joint states and kinetic uncertainty in a named strain panel to test whether the disjoint intervals occur in a real population.

claims.statement: At a fixed measured state/genotype, each active state-face condition in the CellML glucose-driven dynamics is a scalar lower or upper bound on z=G/(0.1+G), because upper uptake is affine in z. Intersecting those intervals over cells and uncertainty support is an exact instantaneous common-feed feasibility test; an empty intersection proves no common glucose command works at that instant.
claims.status: exact source-model interface reduction; general application to measured uncertainty support not yet implemented
assumptions: State and genotype uncertainty support is acquired or explicitly bounded
Active safety faces are specified and the source growth/health branch is known or robustly bounded
All independent Pi/health conditions are checked separately
Finite sampling intervals require additional reachable-set bounds
claims.evidence: The PLOS uptake law factorizes as Vmaxup*q(A)*z. F, ATP, and A+P face derivatives are affine in z; Pi and current health derivatives have no direct z term. The BC/IC witness yields disjoint scalar intervals and a minimum of two feed values by interval stabbing.
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a one-dimensional control-feasibility reduction for the specified uptake interface, not a new general barrier-function theory. Population data, uncertainty sets, and finite-horizon guarantees remain unacquired.
claims.costs: O(number of measured cells times active facets) interval aggregation after acquiring state/parameter bounds; data, sensors, and per-lane fluidics dominate and are unpriced.
claims.falsifier: An implementation of the stated equations finds a common z satisfying all certified conflicting active-face constraints.
claims.next_gate: Build a robust interval estimator from live FBP/ATP and a validated Pi assay, then compare one versus two independently perfused state groups.

claims.statement: For the exact BC/IC witness pair, G_BC=0.1 mM and G_IC=0.03 mM make all active local safety-face derivatives point inward under the full source growth/dilution equations: BC is on F and ATP lower faces; IC is on F upper and Pi lower faces.
assumptions: Same source-model state and parameter assumptions as C7-APP-002
The two witness cohorts receive distinct extracellular glucose setpoints
claims.evidence: Exact Fraction lower/upper bounds are BC Fdot>=0.215206 and Adot>=2.790771 mM/min; IC Fdot<=-0.055250 and Pidot>=15.660389 mM/min. Both have Hdot=0 at Hmax.
claims.novelty_boundary: This closes the local two-face obstruction only; it does not prove a forward-invariant two-lane population tube, basin recovery, or long-term survival.
claims.costs: Two independently perfused glucose channels for the two exact witness cells/classes; within-class state heterogeneity may require additional channels.
claims.falsifier: Any active-face derivative has the wrong sign under exact source arithmetic.
claims.next_gate: Test the state-dependent interval controller over sampled trajectories and finite channel response, not only at the two boundary points.

claims.statement: Whether the BC/IC witness pair occurs in a living yeast population, whether the interval rule improves survival/growth over the best fixed-feed or Tps1/T6P control, and whether the current sensor/actuator stack meets the error budget are unknown.
claims.status: UNKNOWN; no biological, novelty, or priority claim
claims.evidence: The BC/IC values are model-selected genotypes; cited dMSCC studies demonstrate dynamic glucose exposure and ATP/FBP-proxy imaging but not a closed-loop per-cell Pi/F/A glucose controller or the required joint error bounds.
claims.novelty_boundary: Known startup regulation by trehalose/T6P and ATP hydrolysis is established prior art; no advantage is claimed.
claims.costs: Acquire strain-specific flux kinetics, ATP/FBP reporters, Pi assays, genotype/state support, separate feed channels, sensor/actuator calibration, and held-out matched controls. Dollars and throughput remain unknown.
claims.falsifier: The witness states do not occur in the acquired support or all measured state intervals share a common feed value; the proposed two-channel intervention fails the held-out endpoint.
claims.next_gate: Run a blinded dMSCC test against best-fixed, same-information shared MPC, and a known trehalose/T6P or glucose-withdrawal comparator.

claims.exact_statement: In the single-cluster hard-step-force model (beta=infinity), before force turns on, the m process is a birth-death chain with lambda_m=(L-m)kon and mu_m=m(ka0+kb0), independent of extracted-antigen count n. Starting at m=1, the probability of hitting mc before zero is [1+sum_{j=1}^{mc-1} product_{r=1}^j mu_r/lambda_r]^-1 for L>=mc and is zero for L<mc.
assumptions: one localized cluster
shared constant association rate kon for fresh binding and rebinding
force-independent prethreshold off-rates
ideal hard step at mmax=mc
absorbing zero before threshold; no tmin restart
finite integer antigen count L
claims.novelty_boundary: A scoped birth-death calculation for a model parameterization, not a new biological law; it does not imply finite-beta thresholding or final-score dose invariance.
costs: requires L, kon, ka0, kb0, and mc to evaluate
does not charge controller sensing or force-generation work
claims.falsifier: An exact pre-force CTMC with these transition rates gives a different threshold-hit probability.
claims.next_gate: Measure force onset versus running maximum under independently controlled antigen count and membrane mobility.

5000 independent trajectories per condition
means use observed score by tmax
no censoring occurred in these local probe conditions
finite differences approximate sensitivities

costs: 5000 simulations per condition
no physical force-displacement work or ATP measured
claims.falsifier: Independent exact source-code replay at these parameters falls outside the Monte Carlo uncertainty for the reported means and ratios.
claims.next_gate: Report the full finite-dose distribution and matched-dose ranking, not only local alphaL.

claims.exact_statement: Within the reconstructed published model, a running-maximum force policy improves affinity ranking under independently drawn, broad dose distributions in these finite scans, but the advantage is prior-dependent and is absent or reversed for affinity pairs matched at the same dose; it is therefore not a universal finite-dose guarantee.
assumptions: source one-cluster model and stopping rules
adaptive source schedule uses F0=800 pN, beta=5
two independently drawn dose scores or same-dose pairs as specified
adaptive threshold chosen from a finite seven-value grid
for independently drawn doses, time-only controller knows the same prior and is screened on 5x7 (F0,tc), with top two schedules validated on a fresh stream

tmax=1800s censor is retained and bounded separately
claims.status: finite computation; scoped refutation of universal-robustness route
claims.novelty_boundary: The qualitative adaptive mechanical proofreading principle is already published in PRX Life (2026); this audit is neither a new mechanism nor a biological validation. Alternative uniform priors are stress tests, not measured in vivo distributions.
costs: 4000-pair fresh validation of top two time schedules and 4000-pair adaptive reference per prior; separate 5000-pair independent/matched reruns
finite parameter grid, not global optimization; adaptive force ceiling held at source 800 pN
AUC MC intervals are approximate normal intervals
barrier-work proxy omits force-displacement work
censored score envelopes can be wide

claims.next_gate: Perform the factorial held-out-dose/mobility experiment in restart_gates/EXPERIMENT.md and optimize the time-only baseline on the same data and true-work constraint.

claims.exact_statement: Antigen-presenting membrane mobility is an experimentally measured confound for a dose-only mechanical-proofreading model: it changes force timing/location/magnitude, antigen extraction speed, and affinity discrimination in B-cell immune synapses.
assumptions: scope limited to the tested primary B cells, DNA-nanostructure NIP antigen and DOPC/DPPC supported bilayers in McArthur et al. 2025
claims.status: established external within the named experiment
claims.novelty_boundary: Source-reported experiment, not new work from this audit and not evidence for mmax force control.

claims.falsifier: A replication under the same substrate/antigen/B-cell conditions finds no reproducible mobility-dependent extraction or force-dynamics effect.
claims.next_gate: Treat measured mobility and accessible antigen pool as blocked factors in the proposed controller comparison.

ledger.overall_verdict: No defensible new immunology principle was established. The attractive mechanism is now published prior art; the best internal result is a scoped audit that identifies dose-prior and matched-dose failure modes plus an experiment that could distinguish mechanism from proxy. Do not present this as a clinical or biological discovery.

claims.exact_statement: For a unital CPTP Hilbert-Schmidt-self-adjoint Phi with a supplied two-output CPTP broadcaster B whose two marginals are Phi, let Gamma=B^*. In a Stinespring dilation of Gamma, the normalized trace of the Schwarz defect for either copy of a Hermitian A is delta(A)=<A,(I-Phi^2)A>_tau, and 0<=delta(A)<=2<A,(I-Phi)A>_tau. The inequality includes negative Hilbert-Schmidt eigenvalues of Phi.
assumptions: Finite-dimensional M_d, d>=2
Phi is CPTP, unital, and Hilbert-Schmidt self-adjoint
B is CPTP and both partial-trace marginals equal Phi
No Hilbert-Schmidt positivity assumption on Phi
claims.novelty_boundary: Direct Stinespring derivation recorded in this branch; no external novelty or priority claim. It does not prove an EB comparator.
claims.costs: Dimension-free exact inequality; finite matrix operations only. No algorithmic rounding is included.
claims.falsifier: An exact admissible example violating the Stinespring compression identity or scalar bound would refute the claim; no such example is known, and the identity follows algebraically.
claims.next_gate: Use the compression certificate only as an input to a proved common-POVM rounding, retaining operator-norm and frame-size costs.

claims.exact_statement: For all Hermitian A,B, ||[A,B]||_{2,tau} <= 3 sqrt(2) (||B||_infty sqrt(e(A)) + ||A||_infty sqrt(e(B))), where e(A)=<A,(I-Phi)A>_tau. Also ||[Phi(A),Phi(B)]||_{2,tau} <= sqrt(2)(||A||_infty sqrt(e(B))+||B||_infty sqrt(e(A))).
assumptions: Finite-dimensional M_d
Phi is unital CPTP and Hilbert-Schmidt self-adjoint
A supplied CPTP two-output broadcaster has both marginals Phi
A and B are Hermitian
claims.novelty_boundary: Independent compression representation for the commutator estimate; not claimed externally novel. Fixed-tuple almost-commuting prior is not a growing-frame result.
claims.costs: Constants are dimension-free, but input operator norms are explicit. For HS-unit directions those norms can be sqrt(d-1), so there is no dimension-free normalized-HS frame bound here.
claims.falsifier: A legal finite-dimensional channel/broadcaster and Hermitian A,B violating (6). Numerical replay covers only three qubit fixtures and does not certify all cases.
claims.next_gate: Prove one canonical POVM controls every positive weighted frame using this estimate with explicit frame-rank, operator-norm, margin, and rounding losses.

claims.exact_statement: For arbitrary A,B in M_d, the marginal satisfies ||Phi(AB)-Phi(A)Phi(B)||_{2,tau} <= min{||A||_infty sqrt(2 e(B)), ||B||_infty sqrt(2 e(A))}, where e(X)=tau(X^*(I-Phi)X).
assumptions: Finite-dimensional M_d
Phi is unital CPTP and Hilbert-Schmidt self-adjoint
A supplied CPTP two-output broadcaster has both marginals Phi
claims.novelty_boundary: The direct broadcaster Stinespring proof is the contribution recorded here; Schwarz-defect and approximate-multiplicativity themes are standard, so no novelty claim is made.
claims.costs: Dimension-free normalized-L2 bound, with explicit operator-norm factors. It gives no operator-norm multiplicativity or finite-dimensional rounding modulus.
claims.falsifier: An exact admissible example violating the compression formula or bound; none known.
claims.next_gate: A theorem must convert this L2 defect to a single measurement/EB Loewner comparison without an uncharged dimension or frame factor.

For the copying Z-dephasing broadcaster, the canonical map induced by the symmetric-subspace coherent POVM has Z-score 3-3 pi/4 < 1, while the target eigenvalue is 1.
assumptions: The named standard symmetric qubit-cloner and copying-dephasing broadcasters
The exact named fixed POVMs, with canonical maps induced through B^*

overall_verdict.status: broad_bounded_holevo_EB_lift_unknown; scoped quantitative advances and interface rejections
overall_verdict.statement: No proof or qualifying bounded-Holevo counterexample for the general approximate-broadcasting-to-EB-lift was obtained. The exact common-channel operator inequality remains open. Composite-spectrum soft clipping is known to fail on a self-compatible qutrit-product example, while the product of factor comparators still works there. An exact non-line-constant d=5 channel also violates the line-peak cover budget, yet has an explicit EB factor-two comparator. A new internally reconstructed qubit subclass proof and a rank-sensitive fermionic completion sharpening are recorded, alongside scoped metrology/control results and boundaries.
overall_verdict.confidence_boundary: Astra W-Z package claims are source-derived and unreviewed unless explicitly attributed to primary published sources. Child calculations, finite diagnostics, and agreement are internal evidence only; no priority claim is made.

claims.exact_statement: For finite-dimensional state-family sequences with uniformly bounded Holevo information, whether a two-output CPTP broadcaster whose two marginals uniformly approach the input family implies a single family-independent EB channel with uniform trace reconstruction error tending to zero, without a dimension/covering condition, remains UNKNOWN in this investigation.

ledger.task: Repeated application of a noncommuting quantum verifier

claims.statement: For any density operator rho and fixed finite sequence of projectors P_1,...,P_m measured sequentially with Lüders updates, if epsilon_i=Tr[(I-P_i)rho] is the rejection probability of test i on the untouched input, then p_all=Tr(P_m...P_1 rho P_1...P_m) >= max(0,1-4 sum_i epsilon_i). The projectors need not commute, the space may include entangled registers, and the bound is dimension-independent.
assumptions: The same initial global state rho is used to define every epsilon_i.
Each test is a binary projective measurement {P_i,I-P_i} with the Lüders accepted branch.
The ordered list P_1,...,P_m is fixed; the theorem does not permit unmodeled intervening prover operations or arbitrary branch-dependent instruments.
claims.novelty_boundary: Published Gao theorem; no novelty claim. It supplies a linear noncommutative union bound, not a product law or a soundness-amplification theorem for arbitrary quantum verifiers.
claims.costs: Uses m supplied rejection bounds epsilon_i. It does not acquire rho or the projectors, estimate epsilon_i, compile tests, or price finite precision. Given dense d-by-d matrices, direct evaluation costs O(m d^3) arithmetic operations and O(d^2) storage; black-box interfaces require separate query accounting.
claims.falsifier: A finite exact counterexample satisfying the projective Lüders assumptions and violating the inequality would refute the claim; the supplied two-projector example only refutes product factorization and is consistent with the bound.
claims.next_gate: For a concrete verifier, extract the actual pass projectors, input-state promise, measurement order, and supplied bounds on Tr[rho(I-P_i)].

claims.statement: For a single effect 0<=E<=I repeatedly measured on the same system with the Lüders instrument, the probability of m consecutive accepts is exactly Tr(E^m rho). If Tr(E rho)=1-epsilon, convexity gives Tr(E^m rho)>=(1-epsilon)^m>=1-m epsilon. If E=P is projective, the repeated-pass probability is exactly Tr(P rho), independent of m.
assumptions: Each accept operation has Kraus operator sqrt(E), with no reset or other operation between repetitions.
The same system and state are reused after each accepted branch.
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary spectral calculus; Gao also notes the same-POVM Jensen bound. No novelty claim.
claims.costs: Requires m instrument applications to the same system; no independent copies are assumed. State/effect acquisition and physical measurement precision are not included.
claims.falsifier: Directly compute Tr(E^m rho) for a specified finite-dimensional effect and Lüders instrument.
claims.next_gate: Use this exact expression whenever the intended verifier is a repeated same-effect Lüders filter; check whether any reset, feedback, or alternative accepted Kraus map changes the instrument.

claims.statement: One-shot pass effects alone do not determine a repeated verifier's all-pass probability. For every 0<epsilon<1 there are two binary instruments on a qubit with noncommuting first-pass effects and one-shot pass probability 1-epsilon on rho=|0><0| for each test, but sequential all-pass probability (1-epsilon)epsilon, which tends to zero as epsilon tends to zero.
assumptions: Verifier 1's accepted CP map has Kraus operators sqrt(1-epsilon)|1><0| and |1><1|, and its rejected Kraus operator is sqrt(epsilon)|0><0|.
Verifier 2 is the Lüders projective test Q=|phi><phi| for |phi>=sqrt(1-epsilon)|0>+sqrt(epsilon)|1>.
Both tests act sequentially on the same qubit; no reset occurs.
claims.novelty_boundary: An exact scope counterexample, not a hardness result. It does not contradict projective Lüders union bounds because verifier 1 uses a non-Lüders accepted instrument.
claims.costs: Two qubit tests; all probabilities and effects are explicit. No state tomography or numerical precision is needed for the symbolic example.
claims.falsifier: Check Kraus completeness, compute both POVM effects and their commutator, and evaluate the two accepted CP maps on |0><0|.
claims.next_gate: Require the complete instrument (accepted and rejected maps, environment retention, reset policy) in any generalized verifier theorem.

claims.statement: For local projective tests on disjoint subsystems, an entangled input can correlate pass events: on |Phi+>=(|00>+|11>)/sqrt(2), the local tests |0><0| on both qubits each pass with probability 1/2, while the joint pass probability is 1/2 rather than 1/4.
assumptions: The input is the stated Bell state, not a product state.
The two local projectors are applied to the same bipartite system.
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary correlation witness. It refutes independent multiplication only; Gao's global sequential-projector bound still applies to this entangled state.
claims.costs: Two qubits and two local measurements; no acquisition or precision costs for the exact state calculation.
claims.falsifier: Evaluate the reduced states and joint projector expectation directly.
claims.next_gate: For any parallel-repetition claim, state the product-input or game-specific entangled-strategy theorem explicitly.

claims.statement: For an adaptive sequence of instruments, if at every reachable history h the conditional rejection probability at round i on the actual postmeasurement state is at most delta_i, then the all-pass probability is at least product_i(1-delta_i), hence at least 1-sum_i delta_i. This is a chain-rule bound and requires no independence or commutation.
assumptions: The conditional bound holds uniformly for every reachable history with positive survival probability.
Each round's accepted/rejected instrument and history update are specified.
The all-pass event retains enough classical history to define the adaptive policy.
claims.novelty_boundary: A chain-rule sufficient condition, not an extension of Gao's theorem from initial-state marginals. No novelty claim.
claims.costs: Bounds are pointwise over reachable histories. Verifying all branches may require sum_i B_i state/test evaluations when B_i histories are reachable at round i; strategy and branch acquisition are unpriced otherwise.
claims.falsifier: Verify survival recursively for a finite instrument tree and check the conditional rejection bounds on each branch.
claims.next_gate: Replace initial-state-only rejection data by conditional bounds for the actual verifier/prover interaction, or prove a specialized parallel-repetition result for the stated game.

claims.statement: For a normalized pure two-form with canonical pair weights w_j>=0, sum_j w_j=1, set a=(1-eta)^2, b=eta^2, u=b/a, P(x)=product_j(1+x w_j), and solve P(x)=1+u. For the N100 sector-faithful convex-Gaussian completion, delta=a(u-x)=T(rho_eta,sigma_eta). If 0<=eta<1/2, delta <= a(1-sum_j w_j^2)[u+(1-u)ln(1-u)]. Its leading small-eta coefficient is e2=(1-sum_j w_j^2)/2, so delta=e2*b^2/a+O(b^3/a^2). Rank-one inputs have delta=0 exactly.
assumptions: Explicit pure two-fermion input and acquired canonical pair amplitudes.
Independent vacuum loss with particle survival probability eta; environment and loss flag discarded.
The bound is asserted only for eta<1/2.
claims.proof_path: REPORT.md, section 'New quantitative sharpening: pair-spectrum-dependent tail'. Use binomial(k,2)e_k=sum_{i<j}w_iw_j e_{k-2}(w_except_i_j)<=e2 and sum_{k>=2}x^k/binomial(k,2)=2[x+(1-x)ln(1-x)].
claims.novelty_boundary: An elementary shape-sensitive sharpening of N100's uniform bound, not a separate N100 headline and not a priority claim. Four-mode convex-Gaussian geometry is established prior art; exhaustive review is open.
costs: Acquire binomial(m,2) two-form coefficients and canonical decomposition.
Compute pair weights and scalar root x with bit precision charged, including log(1/a).
For many blocks, sum per-block errors and separately charge the Gaussian sampler.
claims.falsifier: A nonnegative normalized weight vector and eta<1/2 violating the envelope, or an error in the symmetric-polynomial identity or series sum.
claims.next_gate: Independent specialist proof review followed by a priority check against four-mode trace-distance and robustness results.

claims.statement: For an m-mode code C with k>0 and Majorana distance d_F>=3, n balanced standard lossy four-mode resources rho_eta_i, and deterministic unitary U consisting of Gaussian unitaries and g Tang-model gates exp(i theta_j Q_j) with even Majorana weight(Q_j)<=q, q>=4, the specified codeword fidelity is <=min{A*Theta_gq(C), Theta_gq(C)+Delta}. Here A=product_i(1+R_i) is the N102 robustness factor, Delta=1-product_i(1-delta_i) is the N100 completion distance, and Theta_gq(C) is Tang et al. Theorem 2's bound on (g,q)-doped Gaussian codeword fidelity. Hence fidelity >=1-epsilon requires Theta_gq(C)>=max{(1-epsilon)/A,1-epsilon-Delta}.
assumptions: Independent unobserved vacuum loss; no loss record.
N102 positive Gaussian domination holds for each balanced standard block.
The whole output system, including any Gaussian ancillas, is retained in deterministic unitary preparation; no postselection or measurement discard.
Every non-Gaussian gate exactly matches Tang et al.'s bounded-weight Majorana-product phase-gate model.
The supplied N100/N102 derivations and Tang et al. arXiv:2609.15059v1 Theorem 2 are valid.
claims.proof_path: REPORT.md, section 'Conditional interaction-versus-loss code bound'. Tensor N102 operator domination; each pure Gaussian mixture component after U belongs to Tang's (g,q)-doped family; apply Tang's overlap theorem and N100 trace-distance comparison.
claims.novelty_boundary: N105 uses only Tang's g=0 specialization. This composes the full g-dependent theorem only for deterministic unitary preparation. It does not cover interacting postselection, discarding, arbitrary interactions, or hardware noise. Priority and independent correctness remain open.
costs: Charge g, q, Gaussian circuit description, interaction angle precision, and supplied code parameters m,k,d_F.
Acquire the lossy two-form resource descriptions needed to compute each R_i.
This is a resource inequality, not a code-preparation algorithm or hardware energy estimate.
claims.falsifier: An allowed deterministic circuit and Gaussian component input whose codeword overlap exceeds Tang's stated bound, or a failure of tensor positivity/data processing.
claims.next_gate: Independent audit of Tang's theorem interface and this composition, especially the no-postselection/no-discard boundary.

claims.statement: The four-mode pure Gaussian state (|0000>+|1100>+|0011>+|1111>)/2 is mapped by V=exp(i*pi*n_1*n_3) to (|0000>+|1100>+|0011>-|1111>)/2. The output violates the four-mode Gaussian Plucker relation, so interacting processing need not preserve convex-Gaussianity.
assumptions: Standard four-mode occupation basis.
V is a quartic density-density interaction.
claims.proof_path: REPORT.md, section 'Counterexample and boundaries'. The input is a product of BCS pairs; V phases only |1111>; output Plucker sides are -1/4 and +1/4.
claims.novelty_boundary: Scope counterexample only; it proves neither computational hardness nor a large post-interaction resource lower bound.
costs: One four-mode quartic density-density interaction, charged as a non-Gaussian gate.
claims.falsifier: A correction to the stated Plucker relation or to the action of V on the occupation components.
claims.next_gate: Require an explicit gate-count and output-access model for any stronger interacting simulation claim.

claims.exact_statement: For the one-qubit channel E_(omega,tau)=exp(tau[-i omega[Z,.]+gamma(X(.)X-(.))]), fixed gamma>0 and tau>0, and every local operating point omega0 != 0, the exact finite-cycle channel has Choi rank 4 and Kraus-product span equal to all Hermitian qubit operators. Its local signal tangent is nonzero, so the optimal QFI over Q parallel or arbitrary sequential/adaptive channel uses with noiseless ancillas and parameter-independent controls is Theta(Q).
assumptions: One sensing-qubit channel use lasts exactly tau and the parameter-independent Markovian environment resets between uses.
gamma>0 and tau>0 are fixed as Q grows.
The signal Hamiltonian convention is H=omega Z, matching arXiv:2609.40022.
The local operating point is fixed at omega0 != 0; the parameter is locally estimable there.
Arbitrary ancillas, noiseless controls, recovery, and measurements are allowed between channel uses and are not charged.
claims.novelty_boundary: The asymptotic HNKS criterion and finite-rate QEC setting are established. This report reconstructs the full-rank finite-step mechanism for this transverse-noise channel and extends the exponent conclusion from specified CSS readouts to arbitrary channel strategies. Novelty and priority have not been externally checked.

costs.channel_uses: Q; one use costs tau sensing time, so sequential exposure is Q*tau.
costs.known_or_supplied: gamma, tau, and the local operating point omega0 are treated as calibrated inputs.
costs.controls: Noiseless ancillas, syndrome extraction, recovery, feedback, preparation, and measurement are free in the theorem-level comparison.
costs.coefficient: A finite O(Q) QFI coefficient is obtained by the channel-extension SDP; it was not numerically optimized here.
costs.excluded: Global/Bayesian risk, local-frequency acquisition, control energy, circuit depth, and temporally correlated environments.

claims.falsifier: At any fixed gamma,tau>0 and nonzero omega0, exhibit an exact zero Choi eigenvalue or a nonzero vector orthogonal to the trajectory Kraus span; alternatively exhibit an allowed adaptive strategy with QFI/Q unbounded as Q grows.
claims.next_gate: Write an explicit finite four-Kraus chart, compute the channel-extension SDP coefficient as omega0 approaches zero and tau approaches zero, and compare the result with prior finite-rate QEC papers.

claims.exact_statement: At the same fixed gamma>0,tau>0 but local point omega0=0, every quantum-jump trajectory is proportional to I or X, so S=span_H{I,X}; the trajectory-dilation signal component is H_mod_S=cZ with c=(1-exp(-2 gamma tau))/(2 gamma)>0. The local analytic Choi family admits a differentiable four-Kraus chart through the rank change. The HNKS theorem therefore gives optimal asymptotic QFI lim_(Q->infinity) F_Q(Q)/Q^2=4c^2 for arbitrary noiseless-ancilla parallel strategies, hence Theta(Q^2).
assumptions: Same finite-dimensional one-qubit Markovian channel as claim TRANSVERSE-QEC-FINITE-CYCLE-GENERIC-SQL.
The operating point is exactly omega0=0 and estimation is local at that point.

The analytic one-parameter Choi matrix is factored using local analytic eigenvalue/eigenvector branches; nonnegative vanishing eigenvalue branches have even-order zeros and signed analytic square roots.
Arbitrary ancillas and ideal controls are available; their resource costs are not included.
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_HNKS_application; pointwise rank-change use relies on differentiable fixed-length four-Kraus chart (nonminimal at resonance), a bridge not explicitly discussed in the source theorem and pending independent proof review; global_uniform_estimation_unresolved; priority_unverified
claims.novelty_boundary: The HNKS theorem is established. The resonance rank drop and coefficient c are reconstructed for this channel; no claim is made that the pointwise QFI law gives a uniform minimax or Bayesian advantage over an interval containing nonzero detunings.

costs.asymptotic_qfi_coefficient: 4c^2 per Q^2, with c=(1-exp(-2 gamma tau))/(2 gamma).
costs.unpriced: Growing-code/ancilla size, controls, recovery depth, state preparation, measurement, and operating-point acquisition.

claims.falsifier: Show the gauge-invariant Z component of i sum K_i^dagger partial_omega K_i at zero is not cZ modulo S, or show a smooth local Kraus chart cannot be formed for the analytic Choi family.
claims.next_gate: Construct and publish the explicit smooth four-Kraus chart and analyze the global risk when the prior has nonzero width around resonance.
claims.limitations: The imported theorem is pointwise in the operating parameter and stated in rank-r notation. An analytic Choi factorization gives a differentiable fixed-length chart through the rank change, so we judge the theorem applicable there; the source does not separately formulate a variable-minimal-rank corollary, and the chart bridge has not been externally proof-reviewed.

Instantaneous noiseless recovery every tau and fixed finite code size.
Local frequency operating point and independent repetitions as specified in the paper.

claims.exact_statement: Let X be uniform on [M], encoded into m qubit cells sent through independent amplitude-damping channels A_p with 0 <= p < 1. Let N=sum_i |1><1|_i and let Q=Tr(N rho_bar) be the message-averaged input excitation number, with Q <= mE. For any collective decoder with average error epsilon, d_bin^(2)(1-epsilon || 1/M) <= chi(X:B^m) <= m max_{0<=q<=min(E,1)} F_p(q), where F_p(q)=h_2((1-p)q)-h_2((1+sqrt(1-4p(1-p)q^2))/2). Here h_2 and d_bin^(2) use base-2 logs. This charges cell count, input excitation energy Delta Q, and decoder reliability; it does not bound write work or heat.
assumptions: Independent memoryless qubit amplitude-damping channel with damping probability p over one specified retention interval.
Cell Hamiltonian is Delta |1><1|; Q is averaged over the uniform messages and the stored energy is Delta Q.
Unassisted classical storage code; codewords may be entangled across cells and decoder may be collective.
Uniform M-label source; no side information is supplied to the decoder.
claims.proof_path: work/agents/quantum_physics/thermo_archive/REPORT.md#early-blocker-and-best-scoped-lemma; capacity input is Tang-Zhu-Bai-Wang arXiv:2609.28592v1 Theorem 5.5 and Proposition 5.6; combine its finite-block chi <= sum_i F_p(q_i) with concavity, Jensen, and binary data processing of the correct-decoding event.
claims.novelty_boundary: A model-specific finite-error corollary and reliability accounting for amplitude-damping qubit storage. It does not improve the general OA276 generalized-amplitude-damping archive result, and capacity/Fano composition is standard. The source theorem is a Sep-2026 arXiv v1 preprint and was not independently validated here.

charged: average stored input energy Delta Q

claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the cited finite-block Holevo inequality for an entangled block input, or a code/decoder violating the displayed d_bin^(2) upper bound under the stated channel and average-excitation model.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof audit of the cited finite-block entropy bound, then compare finite-block reliability curves against an explicitly specified generalized-amplitude-damping or device-calibrated memory.

claims.exact_statement: For the same independent amplitude-damping memory and a uniform M-message code with arbitrary m-cell input states rho_x, let Q=(1/M) sum_x Tr(N rho_x) be average total excitation and epsilon average decoding error. For 0<p<1, epsilon >= ((M-1)/M) p^(M Q/(M-1)).
assumptions: Independent amplitude-damping channel with 0<p<1 and ground state |0> fixed by the channel.
Average energy is measured in excitation number over uniform messages; physical energy is Delta Q.
The receiver has a POVM over all output cells and no message-dependent side information.
claims.proof_path: work/agents/quantum_physics/thermo_archive/REPORT.md#early-blocker-and-best-scoped-lemma. For each x, vacuum output probability v_x=Tr(p^N rho_x)>=p^Tr(N rho_x). The vacuum outcome has the same output state for all x; if x_* maximizes v_x, its contribution to average error is >= M^-1 sum_{x != x_*} v_x. Jensen over those M-1 messages and sum_x Tr(N rho_x)=MQ gives the stated lower bound.
claims.novelty_boundary: A direct finite-dimensional amplitude-damping specialization of vacuum/pulse-position reliability reasoning. The M-to-infinity scale Q ~ ln(1/epsilon)/ln(1/p) and sparse pulse-position achievability were already present in prior pure-loss/noisy-archive capital; this is not claimed as a new general result.

not_charged: refresh and lifetime beyond one channel interval

claims.falsifier: A legal code and decoder under the stated model with error below ((M-1)/M) p^(M Q/(M-1)).
claims.next_gate: For a fixed cell-count regime, determine whether a sharper finite-M reliability function is useful beyond this vacuum-event converse and the capacity bound QA-1.

claims.exact_statement: For any integer r>=1 and M>=2, using r banks of M qubits, encode x in [M] by one excitation at position x in each bank. Under independent amplitude damping A_p, decode x if any excitation survives and guess uniformly if all are lost. This has m=rM cells, exactly Q=r input excitations, and average error p^r(1-1/M).
assumptions: Independent amplitude damping on each of the rM qubits.
Occupation-basis preparation and readout are allowed; bank labels and position-to-message map are supplied.
The archive label X is already acquired; the construction is not a measurement protocol.
claims.proof_path: work/agents/quantum_physics/thermo_archive/REPORT.md#early-blocker-and-best-scoped-lemma. There are exactly r excitations; each survives independently with probability 1-p. Any survivor reveals x; all r lost has probability p^r and the uniform-guess conditional error is 1-1/M.
claims.novelty_boundary: Sparse repetition pulse-position coding is standard and overlaps the inherited pure-loss branch. The point here is the explicit cell/energy/reliability accounting for a qubit memory example, not a new coding principle.
claims.falsifier: A violation of the stated error probability under the exact independent-channel model or a hidden resource needed to implement the supplied occupation-basis encoder/decoder beyond the stated cell and excitation counts.
claims.next_gate: Use only as a baseline in a concrete memory-architecture study; do not present it as an advantage until compared with equally informed classical controls under matched energy, cells, error, and timing.

claims.exact_statement: If a physical memory B stores a uniform M-label with decoder error epsilon, then S_2(B) >= chi(X:B) >= d_bin^(2)(1-epsilon || 1/M). For a degenerate memory reset to a fixed pure blank at temperature T, with no side information/correlations available to the resetter, W_reset >= k_B T ln(2) d_bin^(2)(1-epsilon || 1/M).
assumptions: The entire memory register B is reset to a predetermined pure state.
Its Hamiltonian is degenerate during reset and it is coupled to a bath at temperature T.
The resetter receives no side information or correlated systems that can reduce conditional entropy.
The decoded label is uniform on [M] and average error is epsilon.
claims.proof_path: work/agents/quantum_physics/thermo_archive/REPORT.md#thermodynamic-boundary-and-counterexample-to-a-universal-write-cost. Data processing gives d_bin^(2) <= I(X:B) <= S_2(B); degenerate-memory Landauer reset to a pure blank costs at least kBT ln2 S_2(B).
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard Landauer/data-processing consequence under explicit reset assumptions. It prices eventual reset, not measurement write, and can change with nondegenerate Hamiltonians, side information, or correlations.

charged: entropy of the actual archived register
one complete reset to a known pure blank

claims.falsifier: A reset protocol within the stated degenerate-memory, fixed-blank, no-side-information model whose average work is below kBT ln2 S_2(B).
claims.next_gate: Specify a device Hamiltonian and actual reset protocol before translating this conditional work bound into an engineering energy budget.

claims.exact_statement: The measurement-output bit count alone does not fix a universal positive work/heat cost for writing the outcome. In the idealized thermodynamic framework with a pure initialized pointer register, measurement/premeasurement can be implemented as a reversible operation with zero work in principle; the relevant irreversible cost appears when the record is reset or information is otherwise discarded, with work depending on the discarded-information/conditional-entropy and physical memory model.
assumptions: Ideal thermodynamic control model and a pure initialized pointer register.
Measurement outcome is stored reversibly without resetting during the write operation.
No claim about a specific laboratory detector or finite-time implementation.
claims.proof_path: Faist et al. primary paper states the minimum work for logical processes is conditional entropy of discarded information and identifies ideal measurement with a pure register as zero work in principle; Sagawa-Ueda distinguish measurement and erasure costs. See cited works in REPORT.md.
claims.novelty_boundary: Established information-thermodynamics prior art, not a new theorem. It blocks an inference from N18/N32/N62 input-energy costs or archive bit count to an unconditional measurement-work bill.
claims.falsifier: A theorem within the same specified ideal model imposing strictly positive work for every reversible write regardless of initial memory state and discarded information.
claims.next_gate: Avoid scalar write-cost claims; specify an operation channel and its full physical implementation before applying thermodynamic bounds.

ledger.global_verdict: No general physical-acquisition thermodynamic theorem follows from the inspected detection and W-Z archive results. The exact physical memory architecture and acquisition/reset interfaces are decisive. QA-1 is a scoped finite-reliability theorem candidate; QA-2/QA-3 give a self-contained amplitude-damping boundary; QA-4 is a standard conditional reset consequence; QA-5 records an established write-cost counterexample.

claims.exact_statement: For a stationary stochastic process with specified basins A and B, a first-crossing flux Phi_A0 per unit A-occupation and a complete sequential interface family lambda_0,...,lambda_n yield k_AB = Phi_A0 * product_i p_i, where p_i is the conditional probability of reaching lambda_(i+1) before returning to A from the correctly A-history-weighted first-crossing ensemble at lambda_i. The construction samples correctly weighted reactive paths and does not assume a known equilibrium density or Markovian projected coordinate.
assumptions: stochastic dynamics and stationary flux for a scalar rate interpretation
full dynamics state is propagated; interfaces are observable subsets of it
all A-to-B routes meet the interfaces sequentially, with jump overshoots handled consistently
A-side first-crossing flux is measured per physical time spent in A
interface trial starts preserve path-history weights and enough roots are retained to control genealogical dependence

For direct trajectories in a Poisson metastable regime, relative standard error approximately 1/sqrt(k*T). All reaction/force evaluations and model acquisition must be charged.

claims.exact_statement: For any pure-jump CTMC generator Q and c>0, the embedded jump-chain law and all success committors are invariant under Q -> cQ, while physical holding times are divided by c and physical transition frequencies are multiplied by c. Consequently, data consisting only of untimed successful state sequences cannot identify an absolute rate or, with a fixed Eyring prefactor/transmission coefficient, an absolute activation barrier over the family {cQ}.
assumptions: observations retain state sequence and success conditioning only
holding times, physical flux, and external rate-scale calibration are absent
all transition rates are multiplied by the same positive c
claims.status: conditional theorem proved in report; exact rational finite-state witness reproduced; priority/novelty unverified
claims.novelty_boundary: The proof is generator time-rescaling and may be textbook/known. Treat as a task-specific identifiability audit, not a historical-priority claim or breakthrough.
claims.costs: Finite exact witness uses one Python invocation and rational arithmetic; no trajectory, force-field, or experimental acquisition cost. Rate estimation from direct observation additionally requires clock exposure T with k*T on the order of epsilon^-2 for relative standard error epsilon.
claims.falsifier: The embedded transition probabilities change under uniform scaling of all off-diagonal rates, or the scaled process fails X_t^(c) law = X_(c*t) under the CTMC assumptions. Both are algebraically ruled out.
claims.next_gate: Use this as an audit on path-only kinetic claims: explicitly identify where holding times, positive flux, or rate-scale calibration enter the estimator.

full FFS root lineage correlations separately measured or negligible for this illustrative calculation
source benchmark rate is in the model's dimensionless base-rate units k
simulation-step counts are not wall-clock or universal speedup claims

overall_verdict.statement: The source-reported family-113 theorem applies to an explicit unweighted simple graph of monovalent pairing sites and can estimate the count of complete labeled pairings, with exact zero detection. It does not predict thermodynamic assembly yield. A two-vertex mass-action counterexample has identical graph, perfect-matching count, and combinatorial entropy while bound yield varies from about 0.0098 to 0.9901. A separate source-reported entropy inequality survives for saturated pair-additive Gibbs ensembles when marginals are supplied.
overall_verdict.verification_boundary: Family 113 release text and the Lean scope note were inspected; no independent proof review, Lean build, or algorithm replay was done. The molecular mapping and counterexamples are internal mathematical derivations, not an experiment or novelty claim.

claims.claim: For a finite simple undirected graph G=(V,E) with all vertices and edges explicitly listed, family 113 source-reports a classical FPRAS for Z(G), the number of perfect matchings: relative error epsilon with probability at least 1-delta, exact zero output when Z(G)=0, and worst-case bit time polynomial in the full input length, epsilon^-1, and log(delta^-1). Applied conditionally to labeled monovalent molecular sites with a hard binary compatibility graph, it estimates the number of complete one-to-one pairing assignments. On the success event, the combinatorial entropy estimate obeys |kB log(Zhat)-kB log Z| <= kB[-log(1-epsilon)].
assumptions: The graph is explicit, unweighted, simple, finite, and undirected; isolated vertices are listed.
Every site participates in at most one contact and a complete assembly is exactly a perfect matching.
Each edge is a single modeled contact choice; parallel conformations and symmetry quotients are not silently collapsed.
The output is combinatorial count/entropy; physical yield requires separate equilibrium and kinetic assumptions.
claims.proof_path: OpenAI family-113 paper, Theorem 1.1, printed pp. 2-3. The entropy conversion follows by taking logarithms of the claimed relative-error event.
claims.novelty_boundary: No new approximation theorem or experimentally validated molecular result. The theorem covers arbitrary nonbipartite unweighted PM counts, whereas bipartite permanent FPRASes and planar exact methods are prior special-case baselines.

costs.algorithm: Polynomial worst-case bit time in explicit encoding length L, epsilon^-1, and log(delta^-1), according to source; no practical exponent, implementation replay, wall time, or energy figure established here.

Without a supplied sparse generator, constructing compatibilities can require up to binomial(n,2) pair tests, each charged at C_pair; sequence/condition data and measurement costs are outside theorem runtime.
costs.physical: Association constants, concentrations, temperature/salt, copy-number/symmetry model, synthesis, assay time, and instrument/compute energy are not supplied or measured.

claims.claim: Family 113 §10.1 source-reports a simple-graph gadget for counting k-matchings in an explicit host graph G with n vertices and e edges: q=n-2k labeled dummies, each adjacent to all original vertices and with no dummy-dummy edges, give a graph Hk with at most 2n vertices and e+n^2 edges and Z(Hk)=q!|Mk(G)|. Section 10.2 source-reports a feasible-on-every-run TV-tau sampler for uniform perfect matchings using at most 2e counting calls and 2e+1 exact feasibility tests on a graph with e edges.
assumptions: Host graph is finite simple, undirected, unweighted, and explicitly listed.
Target is a labeled set of exactly k disjoint edges; it is not a Boltzmann law over pairings.
claims.proof_path: OpenAI family-113 paper, §10.1 (pp. 41-42), equation (10.2), and §10.2 (pp. 42-43), Lemma 10.2.
claims.novelty_boundary: Useful for fixed-cardinality combinatorial pairing spaces; it does not sum physical energy-weighted states or imply that chemistry samples uniformly.

costs.sampler: At most 2e FPRAS calls and 2e+1 deterministic feasibility tests for direct PM sampling; polynomial worst-case bit time in input length and tau^-1 according to source. For k-matching sampling, apply to Hk and charge its expanded edge count.

claims.claim: The separate family-113 entropy paper source-reports, for feasible edge marginals x of perfect matchings in a loopless labeled multigraph on 2m>=2 vertices, F(x)-(2-2/m)B(x)<=H(x)<=F(x), where H is the maximum Shannon entropy among PM laws, F=-sum_e x_e ln x_e, and B=-sum_e(1-x_e)ln(1-x_e). For a pair-additive Gibbs law p(M) proportional to exp(sum_e theta_e 1[e in M]), its mean x makes it maximum entropy among laws with those marginals; thus the same theorem bounds its conditional saturated-state entropy, and ln Z_weighted=H(x)+sum_e theta_e x_e.
assumptions: Only fully paired perfect-matching states are included.
All state weights factor as a product of edge activities; no cooperative or geometry-dependent multi-edge energy term is omitted.
The graph is loopless and labeled; parallel edges are distinct choices in this entropy theorem.
The theorem assumes feasible edge marginals are supplied; it does not supply an experimental estimator or weighted FPRAS.
claims.proof_path: OpenAI, Entropy and Face Dimension of the Perfect-Matching Polytope, Theorem 1.1 and §6. Gibbs maximum-entropy identity follows from nonnegativity of KL divergence for laws with the same edge means.
claims.novelty_boundary: This yields a conditional entropy/partition-function bracket for a saturated pair-additive model, not total yield, kinetics, or a weighted PM counting algorithm. Prior bipartite entropy/permanent bounds are stronger in that subclass.

costs.calculation: Given exact x and finite theta, evaluating displayed sums is O(|E|) arithmetic; obtaining/calibrating x and theta and propagating measurement uncertainty are external costs. claims.claim: In the ideal dilute mass-action model A+B<->AB with equal total concentrations c, the binary compatibility graph is K2 in every condition, so its perfect-matching count is one and combinatorial entropy is zero. If x=[AB]/c, then x=K_a c(1-x)^2 and x=(sqrt(1+4K_a c)-1)/(sqrt(1+4K_a c)+1). At c=1 micromolar, illustrative K_a=10^4 M^-1 and 10^10 M^-1 produce x approximately 0.009804 and 0.990050 with the same K2 input. Thus graph count/entropy alone does not determine total assembly yield.
assumptions: One ideal equilibrium reaction with no competing species and equal total concentrations.
The listed Ka values are illustrative model parameters, not claimed measurements.
The graph edge encodes allowed contact only; it does not encode association strength.
claims.proof_path: Mass-action conservation: [A]=[B]=c(1-x), [AB]=cx, substitute into Ka=[AB]/([A][B]) and solve the quadratic.
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a counterexample to physical overinterpretation, not a new physical result. It shows omitted thermodynamic parameters matter even for the smallest possible graph.

If opposite-edge pair activities are K,K and the other two are 1, the conditional fully paired law has probabilities K^2/(K^2+1) and 1/(K^2+1); at K=100 its Shannon entropy is about 0.00102 nats while ln Z remains about 0.69315. ledger.title: A3A marked event-kernel control audit
ledger.overall_status: conditional_model_and_assay; novelty_not_established; no_experiment_run

claims.statement: Therapy-induced A3A is reported to promote DSBs and genomic instability in DTPs; A3A loss lowers APOBEC mutations, clusters/SVs, and resistant outgrowth in the cited models.
claims.limitations: Does not establish a specific cluster/SV-to-established-resistance lineage link; models do not provide the complete marked offspring kernel.

claims.statement: A3A manipulation changes DTP colony formation/survival as well as mutation/SV burden and resistant outgrowth, so total resistance differences cannot be attributed to a per-division mutagenesis change without measuring the joint state/offspring process.
claims.limitations: The inference does not identify the direction or size of any direct mutation-specific effect. A3A3B, DNA damage, survival, division, and state changes need separate measurement.

claims.statement: Per-site APOBEC mutation-rate and first-hit delay projections for NSCLC resistance are prior art; the 2025 projection study covers 21 patients and 42 variants and explicitly recognizes a possible indirect persister-reservoir path to APOBEC-independent resistance.
claims.limitations: That paper does not model joint cluster/SV event marks, multitype persister branching, or measured clone-specific establishment.

claims.statement: If complete marked no-escape offspring PGFs are ordered pointwise for every state, then the greater PGF policy has weakly lower eventual escape probability for every initial persister composition under independent branching.
claims.limitations: Sufficient but not necessary; relies on complete kernels, independent lineages, stationary policy and measured event-specific no-establishment weights. The mathematical comparison is standard in spirit; no novelty claim.

claims.statement: In a hypothetical one-event compound resistance model, two event laws with identical 1% per-locus marginals and identical expected total mutations per burst produce 0.796687 versus 0.015872 escape risk from 1000 persister founders under the stated branching parameters, a 50.19-fold difference.
claims.limitations: All event probabilities and establishment probabilities are illustrative assumptions, not cancer measurements. The paired-event route is hypothetical; no clinical inference follows.

claims.statement: The 2023/2025 source findings do not show that A3A-linked joint clusters or structural variants generate an established resistant lineage in the same persister lineage, and do not identify a robust beneficial A3A policy after accounting for divisions, death, damage, A3B, and APOBEC-independent routes.
claims.limitations: This is a scoped literature statement, not proof of global novelty; further primary-art checking is required before any priority claim.

claims.statement: A lineage-resolved assay can discriminate a direct A3A event-kernel change from a mere change in persister reservoir only if it jointly measures state/offspring, divisions/deaths, DNA damage, linked mutation/SV bundles, and genotype-specific rechallenge establishment.
claims.limitations: Experiment unperformed; costs and rare-event power are not yet priced; a failed identifiability or throughput gate yields UNKNOWN.

A3A drives DTP survival, DSBs, mutation clusters/SVs and resistance
generic APOBEC3 persister survival and resistance evolution/transdifferentiation

scalar evolvability trait ODE as new mechanism
