ledger.audit: Independent hostile audit of Spin(9) complex-spinor pure-moment geometry and canonical-EB support
ledger.overall_status: PURE_MOMENT_AND_SUPPORT_CONFIRMED; FULL_COMPARATOR_CONDITIONAL_ON_SEPARATE_STAR_PROOF

claims.claim: Every complex pure ray in the Spin(9) 16-dimensional complex spinor representation is classified for the moment calculation by p=|psi^T psi|^2 and t=||y_7||^2 after phase fixing and Spin(9) reduction; all p,t in [0,1] are attained.
claims.reason: Spin(9) is transitive on the real spinor sphere with point stabilizer Spin(7); the isotropy module splits as 7+8. Spin(7) acts transitively on the spin-8 unit sphere with stabilizer G2, and G2 acts transitively on the standard-7 unit sphere. The p=0 phase ambiguity is resolved by invariant s1=t, independently also by R=sum_i|psi^T Gamma_i psi|^2=1+(1-p)(1-2t). Endpoints are included.

claims.claim: The exact grade scores are s1=p+(1-p)t, s2=(1-p)(1+3t), s3=(1-p)(7-3t), s4=7(1+p)-(1-p)t.
claims.reason: Reconstructed using Hopf-vector grade-one identity, Spin(8) generator frame/Casimir for grade two, exact Fano-triple counts for grade three, and Clifford-basis Parseval for grade four; independently reduced exact symbolic Clifford sums in the 16-dimensional octonion model.

claims.claim: The set of pure-seed grade moment vectors is exactly conv{(1,0,0,14),(0,1,7,7),(1,4,4,6)}.
claims.reason: The moment vector equals p*v0+(1-p)(1-t)*vH+(1-p)t*vV; these are all simplex weights and every point is attained by an explicit representative.

claims.claim: For every nonnegative invariant sector weight alpha, the support over full-domain canonical EB channels equals max{alpha dot v0, alpha dot vH, alpha dot vV}.
claims.reason: The score F_alpha(rho) is convex in rho when alpha>=0, so decomposing any higher-rank normalized effect into pure states upper bounds its score by the pure-seed maximum. A Spin(9) orbit POVM attains each vertex. The formula applies to canonical channels that prepare each effect's normalized state, not unrestricted EB channels with independent preparations.
claims.scope_caveat: Not every canonical EB transfer vector belongs to the pure-seed triangle; the canonical replacer has vector zero. The exact support statement remains valid.

claims.claim: For every pure seed, M(dg)=16 P_g dg and preparation P_g define a full-domain canonical EB channel that is trace preserving, unital, CP, EB, and Hilbert-Schmidt self-adjoint; for invariant weights its score equals the seed score.
claims.reason: Complex irreducibility and Schur averaging give integral P_g dg=I/16. The effects integrate to I; Psi(I)=16 integral P_g dg=I. Each summand is positive rank-one measure-and-prepare with identical effect/preparation state; invariance fixes the score across the orbit.

claims.claim: The three winner cones have 6, 6, and 7 extreme rays and their union is the stated set of ten rays, with ties as listed in REPORT.md.
claims.reason: Independent rational active-normal triple enumeration verifies full-dimensional strict witnesses, rank-three active normals at each extreme ray, exact per-cone lists, and all winning-score ties.

claims.claim: If the full star gap is PSD at the ten union rays on every correct representation block, it is PSD for every nonnegative alpha.
claims.reason: On each winner cone the gap is a linear matrix-valued map; each full-dimensional pointed polyhedral cone is generated by the enumerated extreme rays, so every gap is a nonnegative linear combination of its ray gaps. Shared ties agree in the scalar support term.
claims.not_verified: The parent star matrices, representation reduction, and their exact PSD minors were not independently audited in this task.

claims.claim: The full Spin(9)-covariant common-canonical-EB comparator follows from the candidate star bound plus separation.
claims.reason: This audit establishes the EB support side and cone reduction only. The broadcaster Choi construction, exact three-copy star block identities/PSD certificates, and complete minimax/separation interface must be independently valid in the other proof components.
claims.scope_boundary: No noncovariant all-channel, unrestricted-EB, universal dimension-free, or external novelty claim is supported here.

claims.statement: For the stated periodic scalar PDE with v=0, r(x)=r0+g*cos(kx), source j_s(x)=j0+s*j1*cos(kx), j0>|j1|, and g*j1>0, the spatial mean of R_+(T) strictly exceeds that of R_-(T) for every T>0.

time-independent sinusoidal growth/source fields and periodic domain
zero initial tolerant-state density; no source depletion, reverse switching, saturation, density dependence, competition, or field feedback
orientation changes source phase only; growth field remains fixed

At k=v=r0=1, D=0.1, T=3*pi/2, F=-18.889918547401734, so for sufficiently small positive g the aligned-source arm has lower final mean than the opposed-source arm. At g=0.01, Fourier/RK4 yields -0.188898066076 with grid sizes 32,64,128 agreeing at displayed precision.

At least-one-molecule 95% detection requires M >= 2.996/p under the ideal background-free model.

claims.statement: Let K be self-adjoint on the real Hermitian Hilbert space with K(I)=I. If a trace-preserving EB map Lambda satisfies <A,Lambda(A)>_tau >= <A,K(A)>_tau for every Hermitian A, then Lambda is unital.
assumptions: finite-dimensional M_d
tau=Tr/d
quadratic-form inequality on all Hermitian A
K=K* and K(I)=I
claims.proof: Set T=(Lambda+Lambda*)/2 and P=T-K. Then P>=0 and <I,PI>_tau=0 by TP and Lambda*(I)=I. Positivity gives PI=0, T(I)=I, and Lambda(I)=I.
claims.critical_scope: Testing only traceless A does not yield the identity slack and does not force unitality.
claims.falsifier: A TP EB Lambda and target K meeting the stated full-domain assumptions for which Lambda(I) != I.

claims.statement: Every full-domain feasible TP EB Lambda admits a canonical POVM channel Gamma with Gamma >= (Lambda+Lambda*)/2 >= K. For a Holevo form with r nonzero terms, Gamma uses at most 2r POVM effects.
assumptions: finite-dimensional M_d
same assumptions as C7-CANONICAL-UNITALITY-01
finite Holevo form Lambda(X)=sum_y Tr(M_y X) sigma_y
claims.proof: Unitality makes N_y=Tr(M_y) sigma_y a POVM alongside M_y. With p_y=Tr(M_y)/d, rho_y=M_y/Tr(M_y), u_y=d sqrt(p_y)rho_y, and v_y=d sqrt(p_y)sigma_y, (Gamma_M+Gamma_N)/2-(Lambda+Lambda*)/2=(1/2)sum_y |u_y-v_y><u_y-v_y|_tau >=0. The average is canonical via the union POVM {M_y/2,N_y/2}.
claims.zero_weight_handling: Omit M_y=0 before defining rho_y; PSD trace-zero effects vanish, and the corresponding N_y is zero.
claims.falsifier: An algebraic normalization/factor error in the displayed rank-one decomposition or a failure of either M or N to sum to I.

claims.statement: For K=2 Phi-I with Phi unital, TP, and Hilbert-Schmidt self-adjoint, existence of a full-domain TP EB comparator Lambda with quadratic-form Lambda>=K is equivalent to existence of a canonical comparator. The canonical support inequality for every Q>=0 on traceless Hermitians is necessary and sufficient.
assumptions: finite-dimensional M_d
K=2 Phi-I
canonical set compact convex
support over positive Hilbert-Schmidt Q
claims.proof: The majorant reduction gives the unrestricted-to-canonical direction. Compact-convex separation gives canonical feasibility iff S_d(Q)>=Tr_HS(QK) for every Q>=0. Both K and canonical maps fix I and are self-adjoint, so H0 domination extends to the full Hermitian space.
claims.compactness_repair: Represent all canonical maps by probability measures over density matrices with barycenter I/d and continuous second moments. Rank-one refinement PSD-dominates each canonical map, so supports and existence of a dominator may also be reduced to rank-one maps. The full canonical set is not equal to the rank-one subset.
claims.falsifier: Failure of compactness/convexity of the canonical moment image, the full-domain majorant lemma, or positive-cone separation equivalence.

claims.statement: The identity-slack proof does not extend directly to comparators constrained only on traceless Hermitians. A qubit pure-state replacer is a nonunital TP EB map satisfying the H0 inequality against K=2 Delta-I, where Delta is the completely depolarizing channel.
assumptions: inequality tested only on traceless A
Delta(X)=Tr(X)I/2

claims.exact_statement: For a thin Newtonian slit in the creeping-flow lubrication regime, two aperture layouts with identical fractions of aperture values b and a can have effective conductances G_parallel = W/(12 mu L)*(phi*b^3+(1-phi)*a^3) and G_series = W/(12 mu L)/(phi/b^3+(1-phi)/a^3), respectively. At phi=1/2 and b/a=10, G_parallel/G_series=250.50025; the ratio grows asymptotically as (b/a)^3/4.
assumptions: Thin rectangular slit, aperture much smaller than in-plane lengths.
Newtonian fluid, creeping laminar flow, no-slip walls.
Streamwise layout consists of parallel aperture bands; cross-stream layout forces every route through aperture bands in series.
Negligible side leakage and manifold resistance.

claims.exact_statement: Given a finite passive hydraulic resistor graph with source s and sink t, pairwise edge-disjoint routes P_i whose conservative series conductances are each at least G_*, and conservative additive occlusion costs c_e, define B_cert=sum_i min_{e in P_i} c_e. Any occlusive edge set of total cost below B_cert leaves at least one complete route and therefore leaves effective conductance at least G_* by Rayleigh monotonicity. If the graph consists exactly of the listed disjoint routes and no other bypasses, B_cert is the exact minimum cost to reduce conductance below G_*.
assumptions: The reduced graph and terminal ports are supplied and fixed.
Each surviving edge has a valid post-load conductance lower bound.
Damage only deletes or occludes edges; it does not globally reduce conductance of surviving edges.
Each edge failure has an additive lower-bounded occlusion energy cost.
Fluid transport is passive and the network obeys a linear conductance law over the operating range.
claims.novelty_boundary: The path resistance formula, Rayleigh monotonicity, and edge-disjoint-path reasoning are standard network principles. The contribution is a scoped fracture-energy/post-damage-flow certificate interface; no general continuum theorem or priority claim is made.
costs: Acquire pore/throat graph, edge conductance lower bounds, occlusion/fracture energy lower bounds, and operating pressure range.
Verify listed routes in O(|E|) once a graph and paths are supplied; globally optimizing the architecture is outside the result.
Pore-resolved geometry acquisition and post-damage validation can dominate computation and physical cost.
claims.falsifier: A post-load conductance below G_* before the stated damage-energy budget, despite an independently verified intact route and valid lower bounds for every route edge, falsifies the reduced network assumptions or theorem implementation.
claims.next_gate: Validate edge-level conductance and occlusion-energy lower bounds on a same-batch microfluidic coupon, then test held-out damage sequences.

claims.exact_statement: In a constructed three-corridor network with two identical slit segments per corridor (w=0.5 mm, h=50 micrometre, ell=1 mm, mu=1e-3 Pa s), each segment has model conductance 5.2083e-12 m^3 Pa^-1 s^-1 and each intact corridor has series conductance 2.6042e-12 m^3 Pa^-1 s^-1. For G_*=2.5e-12 m^3 Pa^-1 s^-1, three edge-disjoint corridors with a 1 microjoule cheapest occlusion site each give B_cert=3 microjoule; below this budget one qualifying corridor survives, while at that budget all three can be cut in the exact-union graph.
assumptions: All dimensions and the viscosity are illustrative constructed inputs, not measured material parameters.
Each corridor is a series pair of slits, and the three corridors are parallel with no additional bypasses.
The designated weakest site in each route costs 1 microjoule to occlude; companion sites cost more.

audit.task: Independent scoped audit of Bizeul-Klartag-Lehec arXiv:2610.05474v1, focusing on the high-order tilt-derivative criterion and its Song-Zhang dependency.
audit.status_note: Source-reported means claimed in a current primary preprint. Internally reconstructed means the stated local derivation was checked in this audit. Neither status is external proof validation.

claims.exact_statement: There exists a universal C such that for every n >= 1 and every isotropic log-concave probability measure mu on R^n, the optimal Poincare constant C_P(mu) <= C. By standard Cheeger-Poincare comparison this is a full KLS bound.
assumptions: All dimensions n >= 1.

mu is any isotropic log-concave probability measure; the proof first treats regular measures with a smooth potential satisfying a I <= Hessian V <= b I for measure-dependent 0 < a <= b, then approximates the general case.
The proof uses Letwin's source-reported quadratic-form variance theorem and standard weighted Bochner, regularity, approximation, and Eldan-localization facts.
claims.status: source-reported; load-bearing derivative/cumulant route internally reconstructed, including the fixed-n,m stochastic-integrability endpoint; not externally validated
claims.novelty_boundary: The v1 abstract and theorem state a full KLS proof. Its central new route is a dimension-free all-order cumulant bound derived from the third-cumulant estimate, followed by suspension and the Song-Zhang tilt-derivative criterion. ArXiv submission alone does not establish correctness, acceptance, or priority.
claims.costs: Pure theorem. No algorithmic runtime or data acquisition. The suspension uses an auxiliary isotropic log-concave measure in dimension N n + 1; N is chosen after beta and f so beta ||Hessian f||_infinity / sqrt(N) <= a, then beta tends to infinity. This is not an efficient algorithmic construction.
claims.falsifier: A verified isotropic log-concave counterexample with unbounded C_P falsifies the theorem. A proof-level falsifier for this route would be a counterexample to the uniform cumulant induction, or a demonstrated failure of the localized Itô energy inequality/limit under the stated hypotheses.
claims.next_gate: Independent specialist review of the imported Letwin quadratic-form theorem and the remaining regularity, approximation, and function-domain transitions. The stopped-martingale and infinite-time endpoint is internally closed under compact support and the standard one-dimensional log-concave moment bound; see the follow-up in FINAL_REPORT.md.

claims.exact_statement: For centered regular log-concave mu with Cov(mu) <= I, if one R >= 1 satisfies |T_d f| <= R^d ||f||_2 for every f in L^2(mu) and every integer d >= 1, where T_d f = (1/d!) nabla^d F_f(0) and F_f(z) = E_{mu_z} f, then C_P(mu) <= C R^2 for universal C.
assumptions: mu has a regular strongly log-concave density as defined by BKL, with measure-dependent positive lower Hessian bound.
Cov(mu) <= I and mu is centered.
The tensor norm is Hilbert-Schmidt, and the same R works for all degrees and all L2 functions for the measure.
claims.status: source-reported as Song-Zhang Theorem 5.1 consequence; proof substantially reconstructed by BKL and internally checked in scoped audit
claims.novelty_boundary: The criterion is credited to Song-Zhang v1; BKL restates and reproves it along the same lines rather than treating the earlier full KLS result as a black box. A compressed symmetrization transition can be filled with a triangle/contraction bound and absorbed constants.
claims.costs: No computational costs. This is an analytic implication requiring uniform bounds across every derivative order.
claims.falsifier: A regular centered log-concave measure satisfying the all-orders tensor bound but violating C_P <= C R^2 would falsify the criterion. A proof-level obstruction would be a failure of the eigenfunction/Poisson iteration or Taylor-doubling inequalities under the stated assumptions.
claims.next_gate: Compare the restated theorem and proof against Song-Zhang v1 Theorem 5.1, with attention to exact L2 domains, spectral assumptions, and the symmetrization error constants.

claims.exact_statement: There is a universal K >= 1 such that for every isotropic log-concave mu in every dimension and every integer m >= 2, R_m^mu <= K^(m-1) ((m-1)!)^2 I, where <R_m^mu u,u> = |kappa_m^mu(u,.,...,.)|_HS^2.
assumptions: mu is isotropic and log-concave; compact support is used during stochastic localization and noncompact cases are passed by approximation.
The base order m=3 uses Letwin's quadratic-form inequality Var(X^T M X) <= 8 tr(M^2) for isotropic log-concave X.
Eldan localization is applied with covariance-inverse quadratic variation, and each posterior is affinely normalized before applying the lower-order induction hypothesis.
claims.status: source-reported; cumulant dynamics, covariance-adapted energy drift, factorial convolution bound, and induction coefficient internally reconstructed; fixed-n,m stochastic integrability and the infinite-time endpoint internally closed under compact support; not externally validated
claims.novelty_boundary: The source's key induction relies on the posterior self-similarity of isotropic log-concavity and exact factorial cancellation of the lower-order convolution terms. It is an internal reconstruction, not a proof certification of the imported third-order inequality or stochastic-process technicalities.
claims.costs: No algorithmic acquisition. The auxiliary stochastic process is analytic. Constants grow as K^(m-1)((m-1)!)^2 in cumulant order and are exactly offset by the d! normalization in the suspension.
claims.falsifier: Exhibit an order m and isotropic log-concave posterior violating every dimension-independent bound of the stated factorial form, or identify an incorrect covariance-normalized Itô drift or product estimate that cannot be repaired by constants.
claims.next_gate: Independently verify the imported Letwin base inequality and cited localization existence/approximation facts. The energy martingale is L2 with E bracket infinity <= D^2(8 C_{n,m} C_{n,m+1} + 16(m-1)^2 C_{n,m}^2); E E_m(t) <= C_{n,m} exp(-t) closes the terminal limit for every T tending to infinity. These are fixed-dimension/order justification bounds, not the dimension-free induction estimate.

stochastic_integrability_audit.status: internally closed conditionally on compact support and the standard one-dimensional isotropic log-concave moment bound
stochastic_integrability_audit.quantifiers: For each fixed n>=1 and m>=2, uniformly over t>=0 and compactly supported isotropic log-concave initial laws mu in R^n, E E_m(t)<=C_{n,m}e^{-t}; the martingale quadratic-variation bound is finite for each such mu and depends also on D=diam(supp mu). No uniformity in n,m,D is claimed for these auxiliary bounds.
stochastic_integrability_audit.normalized_moment_bound: For mean-zero variance-one 1D log-concave marginals, Murawski Theorem 1.2 gives ||X_j||_p<=p/2 for p>=2; Lyapunov gives ||X_j||_p<=p for 1<=p<=2. Thus one may take J_m=m^m sum_{pi in Partitions(m)} (|pi|-1)!; coordinate cumulants are bounded by J_m and R_m^nu<=C_{n,m} I with C_{n,m}=n^m J_m^2.
stochastic_integrability_audit.posterior_energy_bound: E_m(t)<=C_{n,m} q_t pathwise, q_t=<A_tu,u>, and E q_t=e^-t.
stochastic_integrability_audit.covariance_localization: For D=diam(supp mu), sum_i H_{i,t}^2 <= 8D^4 I and sum_i ||H_{i,t}||_HS^2 <= 8nD^4, which justifies the covariance SDE martingale and E A_t=e^-t I.
stochastic_integrability_audit.energy_martingale_bound: E bracket(M)_infinity <= D^2(8 C_{n,m} C_{n,m+1} + 16(m-1)^2 C_{n,m}^2), so the local martingale is a true L2 martingale.
stochastic_integrability_audit.endpoint: The direct terminal bound C_{n,m}e^-T tends to zero for every T->infinity; nonnegative energy integrals pass by monotone convergence and the L_m cross term is absolutely integrable by dt tensor dP Cauchy-Schwarz plus the lower-order induction estimate.

claims.statement: For the complex spinor S of Spin(2n+1), dim(S)=d=2^n and End(S)=direct_sum_{k=0}^n Lambda^k R^(2n+1). The output-swap multiplicities are m_{r,±}=#{j=r,...,n : (-1)^((n-j)(n-j+1)/2)=±1}.

The gamma-trace map on spinor-valued j-forms has the standard surjective recursion for 0<=j<=n.

Scaling both rates by s>0 preserves the full equilibrium distribution and sends fixed-time occupancy to zero as s tends to zero.

Initial state U

claims.statement: For a two-state reversible folding model I <-> N started in I, p_N(t)=pi_N(1-exp(-(k_f+k_u)t)). Multiplying k_f and k_u by the same positive factor preserves the Boltzmann equilibrium occupancy pi_N but can make p_N(t) arbitrarily close to zero at any fixed finite t. Hence equilibrium occupancy alone supplies no positive finite-time success guarantee above the initial target occupancy.

Detailed balance with the specified equilibrium ensemble
Initial state is the non-target basin I
A finite fixed assay horizon t

ledger.topic: Full-outcome detector symmetrization with reference-free scalar efficiency and dark-rate acquisition
ledger.overall_status: An exact cyclic M-setting permutation reduces stable heterogeneous detector efficiencies and Poisson dark rates to a common iid row law for the completed Gaussian-block instrument. An independent anytime source-on/source-off pilot selects a fixed main dose from acquired lower/upper confidence bounds. The averaging operation itself is established QKD prior art; exact detector hardware, coefficient calibration, source flux, drift transfer, and fixed-N randomized schedule remain physical gates.

claims.statement: For a complete M-outcome POVM {E_j}, stable detector efficiencies eta_i and independent dark rates b_i, equal-duration cyclic assignment pi_s(j)=j+s mod M over all s=0,...,M-1, and independent Poisson launch flux phi, the aggregate row counts are independent Pois(N eta_bar p_j(x)+beta), where eta_bar=M^{-1}sum_i eta_i, beta=T b_bar, N=phi T, and p_j=x*E_j x. The total source-click count is Pois(N eta_bar) for every unit x. An independent source-off cycle of duration rT gives independent row blanks Pois(r beta). The statement includes all residual outcomes and needs uniform exposure and detector-only scalar response.
assumptions: The frame is a known complete M-outcome POVM and every outcome, including residual ports, is measured during each complete cycle.
Every detector response is a stable scalar efficiency in [0,1] plus an independent Poisson dark process with stable rate.
Source flux and prepared state are constant during each equal-duration cycle; source launches are Poissonized in the reference experiment.
Permutation controls are lossless and do not change state, mode-dependent response, or detector gating; no dead time, afterpulsing, or saturation occurs.
claims.status: Exact internally derived count-law reduction; finite rational fixture checked in symmetrization_check.py. Hardware validity is untested.
claims.novelty_boundary: Detector symmetrization/randomization is prior art in QKD. No novelty claim for permutation averaging; the narrow claim is the exact all-outcome iid Poisson reduction and its use for reference-free scalar acquisition in this completed tomography interface.
claims.costs: M settings per signal cycle and M per row-resolved blank; N expected launched photons, residual/loss events included; source flux monitor, frame coefficients, switch time, blank time, and all dark events are separately charged.
claims.falsifier: State-dependent total source yield under a complete cycle, unequal row backgrounds after blank cycling, or setting-dependent detector response / flux / mode loss outside the model.

claims.statement: For a fixed M-outcome POVM and generic state pair x,y with all outcome probabilities positive, choose any c<=min_j{p_j(x),p_j(y)} and detector efficiencies eta_j=c/p_j(x), eta'_j=c/p_j(y). Both vectors lie in [0,1]^M and make every Poissonized fixed-setting source-channel mean equal Nc under the two different states. Thus arbitrary unknown static per-channel efficiencies obstruct uniform no-reference state recovery even with zero background; cyclic completion removes this specific confound by giving row means eta_bar p_j and a state-independent all-port click total.
assumptions: Every outcome probability of both selected states is strictly positive.
The nuisance class allows world-dependent unknown efficiencies in [0,1]^M.
Source-only Poisson counts are compared under one fixed detector assignment; no independent reference probes are supplied.
claims.status: Exact two-state construction internally derived; it does not cover restricted efficiency ranges or calibrated references.
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary nuisance nonidentifiability, not a new phase-retrieval result. A related arbitrary-channel dark-count obstruction is in the inherited measurement_inverse CYCLE3 report.
claims.costs: No recovery guarantee is possible for this unrestricted nuisance class from the stated fixed-setting source counts alone.
claims.falsifier: An additional restriction/reference that rules out the constructed efficiency vectors or separates source yields.

claims.statement: With calibrated launched flux phi, stable parameters eta_bar>0 and Gamma=sum_i b_i, cumulative independent source-on/off total counts over equal exposure t have rates u=phi eta_bar+Gamma and v=Gamma. Per-look exact Garwood intervals with alpha-spending delta_l=3 alpha/(pi^2(l+1)^2) yield simultaneous time-uniform coverage at least 1-alpha. The stopping conditions eta_L>0, eta_U<=2 eta_L, and Gamma_U<=2 Gamma_L+phi eta_L imply eta_L>=eta_bar/2 and Gamma_U<=2 Gamma+phi eta_bar on the coverage event. The stop is almost surely finite. Pilot launched photons scale, up to constants and a log-log anytime factor, as (phi eta_bar+2Gamma)/(phi eta_bar^2); off exposure of equal duration and M on-settings per cycle are additional costs.
assumptions: The complete source-on detector cycle makes its total source-click mean state-independent.
Source flux phi and the launch denominator are known from independent calibrated flux metrology or heralding; otherwise phi eta_bar is not separated.
Source-on and source-off total counts are independent Poisson processes with rates u and v, and detector parameters remain stable from pilot to main acquisition.
The pilot is independent of fresh main signal and main blank records, and no main-record stopping is used.
claims.status: Confidence sequence and rate calculations internally derived; exact interval construction is standard. Finite-sample physical validation is absent.
claims.novelty_boundary: The state-independent calibration observable and anytime stopping are a composition with established Poisson inference, not detector-efficiency symmetrization prior art itself. Priority for this exact combined protocol remains unknown.
claims.costs: Pilot photons, source-off detector time and dark events, calibrated flux, M on-settings per cycle, one static off setting for scalar dark-rate monitoring, plus a separate fresh main blank.
claims.falsifier: Failure of the total-count state invariance or invalid Poisson/stability/flux assumptions; in particular unknown flux leaves an efficiency-flux gauge.

claims.statement: On the simultaneous pilot coverage event, choosing a fixed fresh main dose N>=C[d/(eta_L epsilon^2)+dm Gamma_U/(M phi eta_L^2 epsilon^2)] and an independent rowwise blank of relative duration r=1 reduces the stable heterogeneous detector model exactly to the Cycle 3 common-background HLN Theorem 4 model on its iid Gaussian block. For m=Theta(d), this suffices at order d/(eta_bar epsilon^2)+d Gamma/(phi eta_bar^2 epsilon^2), including all launched photons and independent blank dark counts. The estimator uses only the first m Gaussian rows; residual rows remain physically measured for symmetrization.
assumptions: Cycle 3 HLN Theorem 4 hypotheses and its hidden constants, oversampling, high-energy and normalization conditions hold.
The detector/flux/frame assumptions of C4-EXACT-CYCLIC-POISSON-REDUCTION hold between pilot, main signal and independent blank.
The dose is selected only from the independent pilot; the main signal dose is fixed before its rows are observed.
The independent blank has the same duration/symmetrization schedule as the main signal and is not reused from pilot data.
claims.status: Internally derived sufficient composition with prior HLN Theorem 4; no end-to-end hardware or numerical solver guarantee.
claims.novelty_boundary: The O(d/epsilon^2) rate and estimator are established prior art. The new interface claim is conditional exact treatment of unknown stable per-detector response plus acquired scalar bounds; detector symmetrization as an idea is prior art.
claims.costs: N main photons plus pilot photons; residual/loss outcomes; independent r=1 blank with expected T Gamma total dark events; M main and M blank settings; O(md)=O(d^2) known frame coefficients and optical synthesis remain separate.
claims.falsifier: Any failure of the iid row law, blank independence/equal mean, pilot-to-main stability, source flux calibration, or the inherited HLN transfer assumptions.

claims.statement: For the M-window Poisson reference with independent launch totals Pois(N/M), conditioning only on their global total N makes window allocations Multinomial(N;1/M,...,1/M), equal to a fixed-N source that assigns each photon an independent uniform setting label and batches by equal-duration windows. Full source click/loss outcomes are multinomial with marginalized detected row probability eta_bar p_j; independent full-window dark processes and an independent blank are unchanged by conditioning. Any aggregate-record failure probability transfers with one factor 1/P(Pois(N)=N)=O(sqrt(N)), independent of M. This does not apply to deterministic balanced per-window quotas.
assumptions: The fixed-N protocol randomizes photon setting labels uniformly; it does not force exactly N/M photons in each setting.
Every detector remains active over fixed equal-duration windows; dark counts are independent of source allocation and do not depend on flux or detector history.
The estimator event depends on aggregated rows and independent blank; all source loss/no-click outcomes are included in the latent global total.
Pilot and main are independent; the fixed-N main dose is selected before its counts.
claims.status: Exact conditioning identity internally derived and finite categorical algebra checked. Randomized timing/flux protocol is not physically validated.
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary Poisson-multinomial conditioning; no new concentration theorem. Deterministic quota schedules and detector gating are outside the proof.
claims.costs: One O(sqrt(N)) tail factor, N fixed launches, M equal-time windows, random source scheduling, continuous detector exposure and deadtime/saturation validation.
claims.falsifier: A mismatch between random-window fixed-N allocations and the conditional Poisson source model, or any coupling of detector dark events/gating to the allocation.

claims.statement: Within a control class that mixes port-permutation matrices with nonnegative exposure weights, exact averaging of arbitrary detector-efficiency and dark-rate vectors at every outcome requires the average assignment matrix J_M/M. Since each permutation has M support entries while J_M/M has M^2 positive entries, at least M distinct permutation settings are necessary; cyclic shifts attain M. For K<M iid random permutations and a fixed eta vector in [0,1]^M, max_j |eta_hat_j-eta_bar| is at most sqrt(log(2M/delta)/(2K)) with probability at least 1-delta by Hoeffding and union bound, but no tomography stability transfer is proved.
assumptions: The hardware control is restricted to pure permutations of M outcome channels and exposure-weighted averaging.
Approximate random-setting bound fixes the detector vector independently of the random schedule; rows may be correlated across settings.
claims.status: Support-count lower bound and Hoeffding diagnostic derived. Approximate recovery with fewer settings remains unknown.
claims.novelty_boundary: Exact worst-case statement is elementary and restricted to permutation-only symmetrization; it is not an optical-design lower bound.
claims.costs: M settings for exact worst-case equalization; K settings give deviations of order sqrt(log(M/delta)/K) but require a missing heterogeneity-robust recovery theorem.
claims.falsifier: An exact averaging decomposition using fewer than M pure permutations or a control outside the stated class.

Transfer of pilot bounds across unbounded detector drift; palindrome cancellation only handles affine drift within one block.

Known flux metrology accuracy, switch insertion loss and settling time, optical frame coefficient calibration, and finite-precision SDP/eigensolver cost.
Experimental validity of independent Poisson dark rates, stable detector-only efficiencies, and common row means after full outcome cycling.

claims.claim: For each finite C, the set of 3-electron spinful noninteracting ground-state ensemble densities generated by real spin-independent local potentials with quotient V-norm at most C is strongly closed in L1 intersect L3.

load_bearing_steps: Strong density convergence and bounded V-norm imply a uniform bound on ensemble kinetic energy through the ground-energy identity and one fixed smooth test determinant.
L1 density convergence gives joint configuration-space tightness for the fixed-N ensembles.
Kinetic boundedness plus tightness gives trace-norm compactness by cutoffs, Rellich compactness, and finite-rank projections.
Weak L^{3/2} and weak-* L-infinity subsequences yield a potential in the same norm ball; variational comparison makes the limiting ensemble a ground ensemble.
known_gaps: Independent hostile audit found no counterexample under the stated interface.
The result is a standard consequence of Lieb's lower-semicontinuous ensemble kinetic functional and closedness of its subdifferential graph; it is not a novelty-cleared advance.

claims.exact_statement: Assume the pinned source Proposition 5.1: its density n has orthonormal spatial orbitals u0=g/sqrt(2), u1=h in H1, n=2|u0|^2+|u1|^2, and the determinant Phi=(u0 up) wedge (u0 down) wedge (u1 up) attains Tens[n]. With P the spatial projection onto span{u0,u1} tensored with spin identity, Q=I-P, and any C>0, the closed one-body form q_NL[psi]=1/2||grad(Q psi)||_2^2+C||Q psi||_2^2 equals free kinetic plus a symmetric nonlocal form perturbation k of relative form bound zero. Its ground space is P H; the three-electron noninteracting determinant Phi is a ground state of dGamma(h_NL), has density n exactly, and retains kinetic expectation Tens[n].

claims.exact_statement: Assume the pinned source's Proposition 4.3, weighted gap (4.23), and Proposition 5.1 for its fixed density n. For the real local function V=Delta g/(2g) in L2_loc, the nonnegative core form q0[f]=1/2 integral |grad f|^2 + integral V|f|^2 on C_c^infty is closable. Under the unitary map f->f/g to L2(g^2 dx), its closure is the weighted Dirichlet form with domain H1(g^2), equivalently D(qbar)={g xi:xi in H1(g^2)}. It contains g,h with qbar[g]=0 and qbar[h]=d. The weighted gap implies the Friedrichs operator has normalized spatial ground orbital g/sqrt(2) at 0 and h at d, with no lower spectrum orthogonal to g. After spin lift, Pauli filling gives a three-electron noninteracting ground determinant (g/sqrt(2) up) wedge (g/sqrt(2) down) wedge (h up), with exact spin-summed density n. This local potential lies outside L3/2+L-infinity by the source's Theorem 6.4.

One-dimensional distributional-potential results are related prior art but do not prove this 3D instance.

ledger.task: bounded-potential closure audit for fixed-N noninteracting ensemble densities

claims.exact_statement: Fix N>=1 and C<infinity. Let X=L1(R3) intersect L3(R3), Y=L3/2(R3)+L-infinity(R3) with its sum norm, and quotient Y by additive constants. Let R_C consist of spin-summed densities of actual ground-state ensembles for the spin-independent N-electron Hamiltonian sum_i[-Delta_i/2+v(x_i)] with real v in Y and quotient sum norm <=C. Then R_C is closed in the strong X norm. The proof uses weak compactness of bounded decompositions v_j=f_j+g_j, strong-X convergence to pass all potential-density pairings, lower semicontinuity and attainment of the ensemble constrained-search kinetic functional, and the variational principle. It does not assume a uniform infinitesimal form bound or operator/form convergence.
claims.status: internally reconstructed proof; theorem is conditional on the stated fixed-N fermionic ensemble interface and standard ensemble constrained-search lower semicontinuity/attainment; no counterexample found
claims.novelty_boundary: The main ingredients are standard Lieb convex density-functional theory and weak compactness; no novelty or priority claim is made. The qualitative bounded-C approximation corollary follows from the pinned source's exact nonrepresentability claim, whose proof is not independently validated here.
claims.costs: Analytic only. The conclusion gives no computable separation radius, and no positive radius uniform over C increasing to infinity.
claims.falsifier: A failure of the ensemble constrained-search lower semicontinuity/attainment step in X, of sequential weak compactness for bounded L-infinity decompositions, or of passing the fixed-N ground-state variational inequality under strong X convergence.
claims.next_gate: Have an independent mathematical reviewer check the constrained-search compactness and the exact topology/interface; if the qualitative barrier is accepted, pursue an explicit lower bound on dist_X(n_star,R_C) for a specified finite C.

claims.exact_statement: The bounded quotient sum norm hypothesis alone does not imply a uniform infinitesimal form bound. For a compactly supported W>=0 and coupling lambda such that -Delta/2-lambda W has a negative bound state, v_epsilon(x)=-lambda epsilon^-2 W(x/epsilon) has constant L3/2 norm, while its normalized one-electron ground density has L3 norm proportional to epsilon^-2 and fails to converge strongly in X as epsilon tends to zero.
claims.status: elementary scaling counterexample to a uniform-form-bound premise; not a counterexample to the closure theorem
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard critical scaling observation, included as a hostile control. It shows why the closure proof must bypass uniform operator-form convergence.
claims.costs: No numerical cost; exact rescaling argument.
claims.falsifier: An error in the dilation scaling of the potential, eigenvalue, orbital, or density norms.
claims.next_gate: Retain this as a limitation/control when presenting the closure proof; do not infer that every bounded-potential sequence has uniformly controlled forms.

claims.statement: For a finite integer-complex endotactic network with rational positive rate bounds and a rational positive stoichiometric-class representative, the internally reconstructed N33 finite-affine-minimum proof yields a compact positive relative polytope with a strict inward margin on every relative facet; a sufficiently narrow collar preserves a positive margin, and the polytope can be rationally perturbed while preserving strictness.
assumptions: N33 affine-minimum and weighted essential-source drift reconstruction is correct
All reaction complexes are integer and nonnegative
Rates range pointwise in a supplied rational box [kappa,K] with kappa>0
The affine class has an exact rational description
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a bridge from the supplied N33 proof artifact to an N35-shaped certificate; it is not external validation, priority, or a useful-size construction bound.
claims.costs: Direct N33 coefficient acquisition has no usable bounds on scale, slopes, offsets, collar widths, or bit heights. Rational enumeration plus exact polynomial verification terminates under strict existence and rational input, but no general verifier was implemented here and no runtime or certificate-size bound is known.
claims.falsifier: A finite endotactic integer network and rational class/rate box for which the N33 active-slope proof holds but no strict relative facet collar exists, or a rational perturbation obstruction despite positive strict margins.
claims.next_gate: Implement and independently audit an exact rational verifier/acquirer for facet-collar inequalities, then submit the domain-erosion bridge and N33 base proof for external mathematical review.

claims.statement: Given an acquired strict rational inward-polytope certificate with margins gamma_i and collar widths ell_i, integer-volume factorial mass-action jumps with predictable bounded controls satisfy Pr(tau_Q<=T) <= sum_i exp(-theta_i V d_i) + 2 m V Lambda T exp(-c_* V), with V>=max(1,max_i ceil(2D_i/gamma_i)), theta_i=min(1/J_i,(gamma_i/2)/(3B_i)), c_*=min_i theta_i ell_i, and the constants defined in FINAL_REPORT.md.
assumptions: Integer nonnegative source complexes and integer stoichiometric jumps
Exact buffered lattice-compatible initial counts inside Q
Predictable rate control remains in the certified admissible set
The strict deterministic collar inequality holds for every allowed instantaneous rate vector
claims.novelty_boundary: Uses an elementary exponential-martingale certificate route consistent with established chemical jump large-deviation and exponential-Lyapunov methods; no optimal large-deviation exponent or all-time safety follows.
claims.costs: Factorial correction D_i/V, overshoot J_i/V, quadratic term B_i, activity Lambda, initial concentration gaps d_i, and horizon work O(V Lambda T) are charged explicitly.
claims.falsifier: An admissible lattice state/control within the stated bounds that violates the generator or stopped-Dynkin inequality, or a missing count-feasibility/factorial correction under the declared propensity convention.
claims.next_gate: External proof review and application-level acquisition of the lattice coset, rate envelope, and buffered start.

claims.statement: The common deterministic absorber and even a strict inward collar do not imply infinite-time molecular-jump safety: for A<->B with total count V and unit constant rates the finite irreducible chain exits [1/10,9/10] almost surely.
assumptions: V is a positive integer
Initial count is an interior state such as N_A=V/2 for even V
Both unimolecular reactions have rate one
claims.novelty_boundary: Refutes only the infinite-time safety implication, not the finite-exponential-horizon N35 bound.
claims.costs: No acquisition cost beyond the finite two-state reaction description and the finite irreducible birth-death chain.
claims.falsifier: Show that a finite irreducible continuous-time Markov chain on {0,...,V} can avoid its endpoint forever with positive probability; this contradicts recurrence of finite irreducible chains.
claims.next_gate: Retain finite-horizon confinement as the claim boundary.

claims.exact_statement: O'Farrell and Raj report that trained primary human macrophages produce gene-specific single-cell RNA-FISH response changes after restimulation, with early trained advantages and later untrained catch-up; the companion source reports measurements across 90,857 cells and 26 donors.
assumptions: limited to source-reported claims and study conditions
no independent cell-level table analysis performed
claims.status: source-reported; not independently validated in this lane
claims.novelty_boundary: Existing 2026 primary-study result; not a C13 discovery.
costs: RNA-FISH across 90,857 measured cells, four genes, and 26 donors according to source
kinetic time course in the shared-data README covers two donors
claims.falsifier: Source-correct reanalysis or a matched independent experiment fails to recover donor-blocked early trained differences and later catch-up.
claims.next_gate: Acquire processed cell rows; estimate independent sample counts; test held-out distribution prediction after covariate and mixture adjustment.

claims.exact_statement: A common donor-specific monotone response-time map across genes is a candidate falsifiable model for the early-trained/late-catch-up pattern; no evidence for this model has been acquired or analyzed.
assumptions: cross-sectional single-cell spot-count distributions are the target
the released-data schema and donor/time availability match Dryad README
time maps and alternative models would be prespecified
claims.status: prospective model contrast only; not a theorem, fitted model, or scientific advance
claims.novelty_boundary: Generic response-time warping is not claimed novel; the potential capability would be a donor-held-out, full-distribution predictive interface if it materially outperforms equally informed static, gene-specific, and mixture baselines.
costs: processed data and scripts not obtained
future analysis must count donors/independent samples rather than cells as replication
imaging, probes, cell counts, time points, and compute must be charged
claims.falsifier: No donor-blocked held-out predictive gain, or the gain disappears after donor/date, density, morphology, and mixture adjustment.
claims.next_gate: Resolve legitimate data access and reconstruct exact sample structure before fitting.

ledger.overall_verdict: C12 is preserved. C13 contains a fresh 2026 primary-source lead and partial data-interface reconstruction only. The processed measurement bytes could not be acquired anonymously; no C13 theorem, biological discovery, prediction, or control capability is established.
No genuinely new protein evolvability or allosteric-design principle established. Nonlinear and censoring repairs do not clear an independent design gate.

claims.statement: For each JUN mutant x bZIP pair with informative replicates, conditioning on the mutant-plus-WT output total gives a binomial likelihood with logit offset log(mutant input / matched WT input) and a common mutant-versus-WT log-enrichment parameter; zero mutant outputs with positive WT outputs remain valid observations without a pseudocount.
assumptions: Output sequencing counts for mutant and WT share a replicate-specific nuisance depth factor that is removed by conditioning.
Observed input counts are treated as fixed offsets.
Replicate pairs with zero input, or with zero total output, carry no information for the conditional likelihood.
claims.status: internally reconstructed; finite synthetic checks pass
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard conditional binomial modeling; no new statistical theorem. It estimates assay-relative selection/enrichment, not binding free energy or kinetics.
claims.costs: Local Python standard-library processing of 30,180 rows; replay takes tens of seconds. Cash cost zero for reanalysis.
claims.falsifier: A correctly reconstructed input/output table yielding a conditional likelihood that does not match the stated count model under a shared-depth selection model, or a synthetic exact-ratio fixture whose MLE/profile set fails the recorded checks.
claims.next_gate: Model biological replicate overdispersion and input-count uncertainty, then validate on an independent selection replicate or orthogonal binding assay before using uncertainty for design decisions.

claims.statement: The released JUN count table has 26,596 non-WT pairs passing the published filter and 3,532 failing; 3,148 failed pairs have a zero mutant output in at least one replicate, 1,887 have an input count at most 10, and 30,128/30,128 non-WT pairs have at least one positive input replicate, with 29,933 having at least four informative replicate pairs.
assumptions: The table and source filter were correctly read from GSE245326 Supplementary Data 3 and the local analysis code.
Rows refer to variant-partner combinations, and WT reference rows are excluded from non-WT counts.
claims.novelty_boundary: Quantifies rows recoverable under an explicit count likelihood; does not show that source-QC filtering is wrong or that every rescued estimate is biologically reliable.
claims.costs: No new assay; local processing only.
claims.falsifier: Independent reconstruction of the released table and filter giving different row counts.
claims.next_gate: Use per-replicate overdispersion and an independent assay to test any claimed rank change among rescued variants.

claims.statement: The best measured single JUN mutant by mean(FOS,FOSB,FOSL1,FOSL2) minus maximum of the 48 other bZIP partners is 1eA; its published-score margin is -0.0612, with family mean +0.2941, family minimum +0.2060, and maximum off-target ATF4 +0.3553. Count-level correction does not change this result because 1eA has all partner rows passing source QC.
assumptions: The target family is predeclared as FOS, FOSB, FOSL1, and FOSL2.
The objective is a four-target mean minus the largest nonfamily partner, not strict worst-case family specificity.
The released score is interpreted as deepPCA relative interaction enrichment under the reported assay conditions.
claims.novelty_boundary: A data-specific negative finding, not a general rule. The margin is post-selection across variants and its count-model uncertainty omits replicate overdispersion.
claims.costs: No new wet-lab experiment; candidate ranking derived from the released 52-partner table.
claims.falsifier: A reproduction using the same target/off-target definitions and accepted rows that finds a different winner or a positive 1eA margin.
claims.next_gate: Do not claim FOS-exclusive or evolutionary accessibility from this single-mutant table; require prospective all-partner validation.

claims.statement: A post hoc additive-energy plus single-residual model nominates JUN 1eA+4aR with predicted family mean +0.4553 and max off-target +0.3172 (mean margin +0.1381), but family minimum +0.3082 gives strict minimum-target-minus-maximum-off-target margin -0.0090; the double is not measured.
assumptions: Published single-mutant energy terms add without energetic coupling in this specific double.
Single-mutant residuals from the nonlinear global map are additive after centering by the WT residual once per mutation.
The 52 partner profiles and the target family reflect the future assay of interest.
claims.status: exploratory prediction only; no double-mutant validation
claims.novelty_boundary: The thermodynamic nonlinearity and energy-addition mechanism are prior art. This is at most a specific, unvalidated mean-preference nomination; it is not a new evolvability principle or strict specificity design.
claims.costs: Prospective panel: 4 genotypes x 52 partners x 6 biological replicates = 1,248 pair-replicate measurements; extended 71-partner control panel = 1,704. Wet-lab cash cost requires facility quotes.
claims.falsifier: Measured double lacks positive simultaneous family-mean margin, has materially different partner ranking, or fails orthogonal direct-binding confirmation.
claims.next_gate: Run a preregistered all-partner panel with WT and both singles in each replicate; report both mean margin and strict min-family margin.

claims.statement: For the nominated double, raw addition of observed single relative scores predicts mean margin +0.145, versus +0.138 for the nonlinear-energy-plus-additive-residual model; the mean-margin difference is about 0.007, and both predict negative strict worst-case margin.
assumptions: Both predictions use the same released single-mutant profiles and same 52-partner scoring objective.
Prediction summaries are point estimates and do not include unmeasured double interaction uncertainty.
claims.status: internally reproduced control comparison; nonlinear advantage not demonstrated
claims.novelty_boundary: A negative baseline result for this candidate. The close point predictions do not establish equal generalization performance, but provide no evidence of useful nonlinear-model lift here.
claims.costs: No additional compute or data beyond the processed table.
claims.falsifier: A prospective multi-double benchmark where frozen nonlinear predictions materially outperform raw-additive and equally informed baselines on held-out measured partner profiles.
claims.next_gate: Test model advantage only on prospective examples where predictions disagree by more than assay uncertainty; otherwise treat the nonlinear model as unvalidated complexity.

claims.statement: The available single-mutant scan cannot establish a beneficial multi-step evolutionary route or exclude viable higher-order bridges; the DHFR-Lov2 two-site comparison also does not isolate sector connectivity from insertion-dependent interface geometry.
assumptions: Only single mutants are measured in the cited DHFR-Lov2 scan.
The two insertion constructs co-vary in insertion site, sector relation, predicted interface area, and apparent thermal response.
claims.status: scope boundary and countermodel internally audited; no biological generalization claimed
claims.novelty_boundary: The limitation is not a breakthrough and does not say the protein has no route; it is an identifiability boundary for these measurements.
claims.costs: A discriminating follow-up requires a crossed multi-site panel, predeclared effect floor and viability criterion, and selected double/compensatory mutants; price depends on library and assay platform.
claims.falsifier: A matched multi-site design showing that sector-derived predictions retain held-out lift after controlling for interface geometry, activity, and abundance, or a directly measured higher-order path in a nominally inaccessible insertion.
claims.next_gate: Do not infer sector causality or multi-mutant accessibility from the existing one-step scan; require the matched-site and higher-order measurement design.

claims.statement: The released DENet KRAS score table is exactly score = 0.3330148018104648 + log10(day14_count/day5_count) for all 3,569 rows, and the released MEK1 score is exactly log10(day15_count) for all 9,351 rows; random genotype splits on these tables therefore assess trajectory-derived abundance targets rather than independent molecular function labels.
assumptions: GEO count tables and public DENet score tables have been correctly crosswalked.
This claim concerns released score-table benchmarks only; separate candidate-screen experiments are outside the analysis.
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact identities from released tables
claims.novelty_boundary: Benchmark-label identifiability result; not a refutation of the paper's separate candidate screens or of sequence models on independent function labels.
claims.costs: Local count/score table matching and arithmetic; no model retraining.
claims.falsifier: A score-table row not satisfying the identity at numerical precision after matching it to the correct deposited counts.
claims.next_gate: Require future-vs-past or independent-line evaluation against an orthogonal function assay before interpreting these score-table correlations as sequence-to-function generalization.

ledger.task: inverse molecular design for catalysts and reaction-selective materials

claims.statement: Let tau pair mirror-image catalysts in a fixed achiral reaction environment, with a signed selectivity target y(tau(c)) = -y(c). If a candidate representation phi identifies the pair, phi(tau(c)) = phi(c), every deterministic predictor of the form f(phi(c)) has mean squared error at least y(c)^2 on the balanced pair, and signed-major-product accuracy is at most 1/2. Randomized predictors obey the same expected-risk bound.
assumptions: the target is signed product selectivity (for example, log(k_R/k_S) or signed ee), not its absolute value
the physical reflection exchanges product labels under a parity-even molecular model
the remaining reaction environment and conditions are achiral and fixed
the representation is exactly invariant across the mirror pair
claims.novelty_boundary: The algebraic obstruction is general and elementary; stereochemistry-aware selectivity prediction is established prior art. No catalyst discovery, chemical novelty, or priority claim is made. The contribution here is the explicit input/target contract and matched-pair discriminator.

costs.representation: Must preserve at least an orientation bit for signed mirror-pair outcomes; the bit does not determine selectivity magnitude.
costs.data: Requires absolute product-configuration labels and exact mirror-pair mapping.
costs.synthesis: Both enantiomeric catalyst identities, verified enantiopurity, and matched catalyst preparation are required; numerical cost is unknown.
costs.assay: Paired fixed-condition measurements of yield and signed ee or initial-rate ratio with replicate uncertainty; exact all-in cost is unknown.
costs.quantum_chemistry: If used, matched competing transition-state/conformer calculations and their spin/solvent/thermal model are additional costs; the theorem itself requires none.

claims.falsifier: The representation premise is falsified by showing phi(c) differs from phi(tau(c)); the physical reflection premise is challenged if verified mirror catalysts in an achiral, fixed environment reproducibly fail to reverse signed selectivity beyond assay uncertainty. A stereo-blind model cannot evade the theorem on fresh, leakage-free mirror pairs.
claims.next_gate: Run a blinded, randomized, replicate matched-enantiomer assay and compare otherwise identical stereo-blind and stereo-aware models on whole held-out pairs and scaffolds.

claims.statement: Under two-channel transition-state theory with equal pathway prefactors, ee = tanh(Delta/(2RT)) for Delta = G_S^‡ - G_R^‡. For a finite candidate set with a uniform estimation error bound |hatDelta_i - Delta_i| <= epsilon, the candidate maximizing hatDelta has regret at most 2 epsilon; hatDelta_selected - epsilon >= 2RT atanh(ee_target) certifies the signed ee threshold.
assumptions: two product channels, irreversible kinetic control, equal transmission/prefactors, fixed temperature
the selected candidate lies in the stated finite set
epsilon is a simultaneous uniform bound over the set, not a test-set mean error
claims.novelty_boundary: The TST conversion and argmax regret bound are standard consequences, not a novel catalyst-design algorithm. The result makes explicit the gap between regression error and a decision certificate.

costs.representation: Requires signed product labels, fixed reaction conditions, and a consistent barrier sign convention.
costs.model: Requires a uniform error guarantee on all candidate scores to certify selection; ordinary MAE/RMSE is insufficient.
costs.assay: Assay confidence bounds must be converted to the same signed Delta scale and combined with model error.
costs.quantum_chemistry: Barrier/conformer costs are task-specific and are not included in the algebraic certificate.

claims.falsifier: The physical conversion fails if measured outcomes are not governed by two irreversible channels with equal prefactors, for example due to different transmission factors, reversibility, product racemization, or changing catalyst speciation. The selection guarantee fails if the claimed uniform error bound does not hold on the finite candidate set.
claims.next_gate: For prospective campaigns, pre-register the signed endpoint and threshold, obtain simultaneous calibration or conservative error bounds, and report selected-candidate regret and hit rate at equal assay/synthesis budgets.

claims.statement: A current source-reported mechanism-aware Ni catalyst-design workflow maps a supplied ligand library into TSRC/intermediate/TSRE templates, computes xTB-refined conformationally informed features, and combines a literature-pretrained model with EDBO+; its prospective benzylic-acetal coupling study reports about 70,000 geometries over 195 ligands in about two weeks and 26 experiments over four rounds at fixed reaction conditions, reaching maximum DeltaDeltaG^‡ = 0.98 kcal/mol (68% ee).
assumptions: statement is attributed to the cited paper and not independently rerun in this track
the reported computational campaign uses supplied reaction/mechanism templates
reaction conditions were not varied in the prospective campaign
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a reconstruction of primary-source reported work, not a new result. It establishes a strong baseline and exposes the supplied-template and fixed-condition boundaries. No equal-total-cost comparison against the strongest alternative acquisition method was independently reproduced here.

costs.candidate_space: 195 chiral N,N ligands; about 47% reported commercially available.
costs.quantum_chemistry: Approximately 70,000 geometries in about two weeks; xTB optimizations/refinement, filtering and clustering, PCM/omegaB97X-3c single points; 756 descriptor summaries per transition state or intermediate.
costs.synthesis: Noncommercial selected ligands require multistep synthesis; exact time, cost, failure, and purification burden are not established in the main article.
costs.assay: 26 prospective experimental screens in four rounds, conditions fixed; exact all-in assay cost and aggregate failure accounting unknown here.
costs.mechanism_template: TSRC/intermediate/TSRE template and reaction-specific mechanism are supplied; acquisition and validation costs must be charged for a new reaction.

claims.falsifier: An exact rerun with the published data/code that fails to reproduce the reported geometry counts, screen sequence, or measured candidate ranking would contradict this reconstruction; a new prospective test that misses the selected-candidate target would falsify transfer to that new task, not the original source report.
claims.next_gate: Benchmark EDBO+ against equally informed random, nearest-neighbor/fingerprint, and simple mechanistic-regression acquisition under identical candidate, literature-data, synthesis-feasibility, and wet-assay budgets; separately include condition optimization.

claims.statement: For a finite controlled CTMC and a projection phi, the projected process is Markov under every point-mass micro-initialization and every piecewise-constant open-loop action schedule iff, for each action, all microstates in each phi-fiber have identical rates into every macrostate.
assumptions: finite microstate space and finite action set
time-homogeneous generator within each piecewise-constant action interval
cell motion, molecular diffusion, and reactions are included as transitions if present
claims.status: established conditional theorem; classical strong lumpability restated in controlled notation; no biological validity claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Exact stochastic lumpability and approximate Markov-chain aggregation are established prior art. No theorem novelty is claimed.
claims.costs: Sparse defect evaluation is O(|A| times |E_Q|); full state enumeration can grow exponentially with cell count and molecular copy cutoffs. Biological parameter acquisition was not done.
claims.falsifier: For a finite proposed model, an action and two microstates in the same macro fiber with different projected rate rows falsify exact faithfulness.
claims.next_gate: Specify a calibrated finite stochastic model and evaluate action-indexed lumpability/defect certificates under measured transport and lineage states.

claims.statement: Under the source-reported BMP Hill response g(b,i)=b/(b+i) at h=1 and Ki=1, pooled mean BMP and inhibitor do not determine the mean pSMAD-production drift: two two-cell states with equal means (1/2,1/2) have drifts 1/2 and 1/4.
assumptions: two equal-volume cell compartments
g(0,0)=0, consistent with absent BMP giving no pSMAD activation
zero initial pSMAD and identical degradation terms
claims.status: exact finite mathematical counterexample within the chosen discretization of a source-reported mechanism; not evidence that the tissue realizes these states
claims.novelty_boundary: Jensen/nonlinear moment non-closure is standard mathematics. The example is a source-specific interface witness, not a priority claim.
claims.costs: Four local (b,i) states are evaluated exactly with rational arithmetic. No experiments, parameter fitting, or stochastic calibration.
claims.falsifier: The arithmetic is directly reproducible; biological relevance would be falsified if within-bin ligand-inhibitor pairing were experimentally fixed by the retained state or if the response were effectively affine over the measured range.
claims.next_gate: Measure paired spatial BMP/inhibitor or pSMAD/antagonist states under matched mean-dose pulse interventions, with cell tracking and lineage readout, to test whether this closure defect is material in the system.

claims.statement: If an action-indexed generator residual is uniformly at most delta in row l1 norm, the prescribed-schedule terminal macro law is within TV delta*T/2 of a candidate coarse CTMC at horizon T.
assumptions: finite state spaces
matched initial macro law
fixed piecewise-constant open-loop intervention schedule
the residual includes every macro transition, including transport and stochastic events
claims.status: proved conditional finite-horizon bound; specialization of standard Markov aggregation error methods; path-distribution and feedback claims not established
claims.novelty_boundary: Formal state-reduction error bounds exist in 2025 prior art; this is a transparent generator-defect specialization for fixed intervention schedules, not a new theorem claim.
claims.costs: Computing the residual requires the finite action-indexed generator; state enumeration may be exponential. The epsilon/T threshold is a design criterion, not an observed biological result.
claims.falsifier: The stated assumptions and proof are mathematical; any use is invalidated if omitted states/transitions make the supplied generator incomplete or rates unbounded after truncation.
claims.next_gate: Establish rate intervals and truncation tails from live signaling, movement, and lineage measurements, then calculate a certified delta for the intervention horizon.

ledger.overall_status: No new biological capability or priority-cleared theorem established. The mathematical non-closure witness is exact; the system-level intervention conclusion remains UNKNOWN.

claims.exact_statement: For a background-subtracted excess field b(x) in a steady front frame satisfying D b'' + v_rel b' - k b = 0 on a source-free tail, with constant D>0, v_rel>0, k>=0, the decaying exponential length is ell=2D/(v_rel+sqrt(v_rel^2+4Dk)); hence ell<=D/v_rel and a requested passive length ell_target is feasible only if v_rel*ell_target<=D.
assumptions: The field is linear and scalar in the tail.
Diffusivity and clearance are constant in space/time and D is the effective lateral diffusivity in the material-cell frame.
The front-relative cell-row speed v_rel is known and positive.
First-order clearance k is nonnegative.
There is no distributed source, positive local amplification, nonlinear saturation, or contact-dependent transport in the fitted tail.
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_exact_conditional_model_lemma; equation is standard moving-frame transport mathematics, not a theorem about tissue
claims.novelty_boundary: No novelty claim for the advection-diffusion calculation. Candidate contribution is its falsifiable application as a reach-speed design boundary for the 2026 Drosophila surface-Fog/mechanical wave; the biological interface is unvalidated.

costs.inputs_supplied_in_this_audit: Cross-paper reported means and profile lengths only.
inputs_not_yet_acquired: same-condition front speed relative to cell rows
surface-associated Fog mobility in that same material frame
first-order active-pool clearance under a matched perturbation
costs.runtime: constant-time evaluation after parameters are measured
costs.experimental_resources: custom reporters/perturbation genotypes, embryo-level live imaging and FCS/pulse-chase; quantitative labor/energy costs not estimated

claims.falsifier: A same-condition background-subtracted passive tail with measured k>=0 but v_rel*ell>D, or systematic failure of predicted ell across held-out doses after uncertainty accounting, falsifies this reduced model.
claims.next_gate: Measure D, k, v_rel, and ell in the same Fog-dose/Gprk2/integrin perturbation series and compare held-out profiles with the no-transport cell-local model.

claims.exact_statement: Using the 2019 reported wave-speed mean 2.2 um/min as a provisional proxy for v_rel and the 2026 FCS means D_slow=1.6 um^2/s and D_fast=55 um^2/s, the zero-clearance lengths D/v are approximately 43.6 um and 1500 um, respectively; across 70 um, estimated Peclet numbers vL/D are 1.60 and 0.047.
assumptions: Cross-paper speed is an acceptable proxy for material-row speed for dimensional screening only.
The measured slow FCS component is a surface-associated mobile pool with effective lateral D_slow.
70 um is used as the spatial comparison span of the 2026 surface-pool profile.
claims.novelty_boundary: Dimensional consistency is not evidence of causality, fit, or priority. Cross-paper numbers are not paired observations.

costs.input_data: Source-reported means; reported plus/minus terms are treated only as corner intervals, not confidence intervals.
costs.computation: Python 3 scalar arithmetic; no tissue simulation, fitting, or raw-data analysis.

claims.falsifier: Matched same-condition D_slow and v_rel produce a materially different scale, or Fogslow is not a mobile surface-associated pool.
claims.next_gate: Repeat the calculation on paired, embryo-level mobility and cell-relative speed estimates with propagated measurement uncertainty.

claims.exact_statement: A single spatial profile P(x) observed under a monotone front can be reproduced by a no-transport cell-age waveform M(a)=P(v_rel*a); in particular, an exponential local waveform produces the same exponential profile with ell=v_rel*tau. Therefore a spatial snapshot alone does not identify moving surface-pool transport.
assumptions: A front maps distance into a response coordinate s=x/v_rel.
A per-cell response waveform has an exponential segment over the measured window.
The currently cited data do not measure same-condition cell trajectories and bound-pool clearance sufficiently to exclude this alternative.
claims.status: constructed_adversarial_model_alias; non-identifiability for the present observations, not a claim that cells use this exact waveform
claims.novelty_boundary: The space-time coordinate identity is elementary. Its purpose is to prevent interpreting a front-frame profile as proof of lateral ligand transport.

costs.required_measurements: cell-linked MyoII time course, first vitelline-contact time, cell-row-relative front speed, surface-Fog mobility/clearance, and embryo-level profile
costs.runtime: profile reconstruction and held-out error comparison after data acquisition

claims.falsifier: The alternative is rejected only if the measured per-cell waveform fails to predict spatial profiles across perturbations while the transport model predicts held-out conditions.
claims.next_gate: Fit both reduced models to a subset of perturbations; hold out one Fog/Gprk2 dose and one integrin condition.

claims.exact_statement: In the reported 2026 experimental conditions, primordium-only G-alpha restoration and source-confined membrane-tethered Fog do not sustain WT-like MyoII wave propagation, and increasing Fog/Gprk2 signaling range is reported to slow the invagination wave; the complete relay therefore includes propagation-zone GPCR/Fog and adhesion/de-adhesion effects.

claims.exact_statement: In the discrete serial no-bypass relay with per-cell detachment reserve Delta_i = alpha*(M0 + Gamma*O_i*I_i/(K+I_i))*sin(theta_i) - beta*B_i and the constitutive rule that cell i detaches iff Delta_i>0, propagation through N rows occurs if and only if min_i Delta_i>0.
assumptions: Cells are arranged in a serial propagation path with no bypass or long-range recruitment around a stalled row.
Detachment occurs exactly when quasi-static normal de-adhesion force exceeds adhesion load.
Force closures F_deadh=alpha*M and F_adh=beta*B hold over the modeled regime.
O, I, B, theta and coefficients are well-defined state variables; no mapping from published fluorescence proxies to these quantities is assumed.
claims.status: internally_proved_exact_conditional_discrete_model_result; not validated as the embryo force law
claims.novelty_boundary: The induction is elementary and exact only for the named serial force-threshold model. The biological roles of integrin, MyoII, contact and detachment are source-reported prior findings; no literature priority claim is made for weakest-link propagation generally.

claims.exact_statement: Under B=I and fixed O, theta with Delta(I)=alpha*sin(theta)*(M0+Gamma*O*I/(K+I))-beta*I, the marginal effect of integrin changes sign exactly at O_c=beta*(K+I)^2/(alpha*Gamma*K*sin(theta)); for fixed O, an interior reserve maximizer is I*=sqrt(alpha*Gamma*O*K*sin(theta)/beta)-K when positive.
assumptions: Integrin state I has both a saturating cofactor effect on contractility and an adhesive load proportional to I.
MyoII-to-deadhesion force and adhesion-load coefficients are locally constant.
Receptor input O and detachment angle theta are held fixed while I is titrated.
alpha, beta, Gamma, K and active I/O units are positive and calibrated.

claims.exact_statement: If N cell reserves are iid Normal(mu,sigma^2) under the serial criterion, the probability of propagation is Phi(mu/sigma)^N, and target failure probability epsilon requires mu/sigma >= Phi^{-1}((1-epsilon)^(1/N)); at epsilon=0.05 this is 2.4421108 for N=7 and 2.7992115 for N=20.
assumptions: Per-cell force reserves are identically distributed Gaussian with common mean and variance.
Cell reserves are independent.
The deterministic serial criterion C9-M1 applies.

claims.exact_statement: A single front-relative exponential profile does not identify active-pool transport: for constant v, the same profile P(d)=b+(A-b)exp(-d/ell) is generated by a no-lateral-transport contact-age waveform M(a)=b+(A-b)exp(-(Delta-a)/tau) with a=Delta-d/v and tau=ell/v. Therefore profile length and cross-paper D/v values alone cannot identify a biological Fog-dose, mobility, or clearance threshold.
assumptions: The front-relative profile is observed over a finite range with monotone distance-to-contact-age mapping.
A local contact-age response may vary across the observed age window.
The published summaries do not pair calibrated active-pool mobility, clearance, cell-age history, force state and speed in the same condition.
claims.novelty_boundary: Coordinate reparameterization is elementary. Its value is a bounded inference warning and restart gate, not a novel theorem about all source observations.

claims.exact_statement: The pinned 2025 skull-wave simulator initializes a shallow phenotype tail q0=0.005333 per micron, versus qstar=0.061637 per micron under a homogeneous A-homeostatic scalar KPP reduction. The released output replay gives 21.7353 microns/hour for the interpolated phi-half line and 10.8082 microns/hour after local drift removal. In that scalar comparator, a single adjusted speed cannot identify alpha when q is unknown: multiple positive (q,alpha) pairs reconstruct the same speed.
assumptions: Scalar reduction assumes constant leading-edge density and uniform advection; it is not the full nonlinear source PDE.
The replay analyzes released Mathematica output CSVs and does not rerun or converge the solver.
The speed-to-alpha counterexample is conditional on the standard shallow-tail Fisher-KPP branch.

failures_and_unknowns.statement: No source-derived numerical Fog-dose, receptor-clearance, mobility, integrin, or force threshold is identifiable from profile lengths and cross-paper parameter proxies.

The measured slow Fog FCS component is presumed membrane/receptor-associated but is not chemically established as the active signal, and its D is not established as active-state material-frame mobility.

The two-gate law assumes a quasi-static peel threshold, linear force closures, a saturating integrin cofactor, and a serial no-bypass relay; biology may require viscoelasticity, stochastic bond rupture, multiple mechanical paths, distributed forcing, or a different constitutive law.
The iid Gaussian reliability values are illustrative conditional calculations, not estimates of embryo reliability; cell-level correlations and non-Gaussian tails are unknown.
No empirical integrin sign-switch has been observed; the local derivative changes sign only within the proposed dual-role closure and requires matched receptor input, angle, and calibrated force.

The scalar skull-wave reduction is not the full moving-density force-balanced PDE; its shallow-tail speed match is a finite model-output diagnostic only, while nature-level q, alpha, and propagation remain unknown.

The released phi-half OLS trajectory is 21.7353 microns/hour; after subtracting the sampled model tissue velocity and adding the local density-gradient correction, the relative speed is 10.8082 microns/hour.

failures_and_unknowns.statement: The scalar KPP reduction is not the full source nonlinear moving-tissue PDE; density, flow, pressure and proliferation are dynamically coupled.

The biological initial exponent q, matched material-frame advection, held-out front speed, and BAPN live-speed response are unavailable in the reviewed source package; alpha and propagation law for nature remain UNKNOWN.

The published SI Fisher velocity equations and alpha inversion have a factor/sign/units concern under visual reading; an independent hostile auditor is checking this, so this report does not assert a corrected source verdict.
The 15-micron spatial grid cannot resolve the 16.2-micron scalar pulled-threshold length, and the exact PDE was not rerun or subjected to grid/time convergence checks.

Active migration, non-Fickian relative cell motion, contact-age kinetics and mechanical relay remain equally informed alternatives to a scalar propagation interpretation; the primary source acknowledges migration versus displacement limitations.

claims.statement: For the one-dimensional inertial phi^4 field with kappa, lambda, v, rho > 0, E[phi]=integral[kappa/2 phi_x^2+lambda/4(phi^2-v^2)^2]dx, and far fields -v,+v, the exact static kink phi_K=v tanh((x-x0)/ell), ell=sqrt(2kappa/(lambda v^2)), supports a translation eigenmode E=0, one shape eigenmode E=3, and continuum [4,infinity) for the dimensionless linearized Hessian H=-d_y^2+4-6sech^2(y), where E=2 rho omega^2/(lambda v^2). Thus omega_shape/omega_bulk_edge=sqrt(3)/2. This is a theorem for the stated field model only.
assumptions: one scalar order parameter and the stated quartic-gradient energy
inertial dynamics rho phi_tt=-delta E/delta phi, with no damping in the spectral theorem
infinite line and topological far-field phases; finite-boundary effects excluded
the order parameter's dynamic Hessian is the static energy Hessian; not implied by the recent static metamaterial paper
claims.novelty_boundary: The 2026 source supplies strain-programmed static walls but explicitly treats space as pseudo-time, not physical time; the phi^4 kink Hessian spectrum and reflectionless Pöschl-Teller scattering are classical. No priority claim is made for applying the result to an architected material.
claims.costs: Static profile/energy fitting must acquire kappa, lambda, v and ell; inertial mass density rho requires dynamic calibration. Losses, nonlocal modes, geometric coupling to translations, specimen length, cell resolution, and finite-bit estimation costs are not measured or charged numerically.

claims.next_gate: On a finite coupon, measure a static single-wall profile and local tangent Hessian, then use laser vibrometry/DIC under a weak chirp to compare a wall specimen with a uniform-phase control.
