claims.statement: For H=-d_y^2+4-6sech^2(y) plus any bounded self-adjoint additive multiplication perturbation W with norm delta<1/2, the Riesz spectral projection on the radius-1/2 circle around E=3 retains rank one. Hence exactly one simple mode remains in that circle, its E lies in [3-delta,3+delta], and the spectrum is otherwise contained in the delta-neighborhood of {0} union [4,infinity). The shape mode remains separated from the bulk continuum by at least 1-2delta in E units.
assumptions: the perturbation acts additively on the dimensionless squared-frequency Hessian
gradient coefficient, inertia, domain, and scalar-field interface remain fixed
real self-adjoint perturbation with operator norm less than 1/2
claims.novelty_boundary: This uses standard bounded self-adjoint perturbation and Riesz projection theory; the material-specific conversion of manufacturing variation into a measured Hessian norm is absent. No novelty or fabrication certificate is claimed.
claims.costs: Must bound the full local tangent-Hessian perturbation in operator norm after loading. A geometric tolerance alone is insufficient. The condition does not cover gradient/inertia disorder or viscoelastic loss; finite-device boundary and pinning costs remain unmodeled.
claims.falsifier: If the calibrated additive Hessian perturbation reaches delta>=1/2, this quantitative certificate no longer applies. If a mode disappears or falls outside the certified interval while the assumptions are verified, the proof/interface implementation is wrong.
claims.next_gate: Map local tangent stiffness under the programmed wall, convert it to a dimensionless sup-norm bound, and independently measure mode frequencies before using the certificate.

claims.statement: For rates k0=(1,1,4,0), k1=(0,4,1,1) and jump marks 1,2,3,4, both constant-source count processes have per-volume drift 15 and variance rate 41; after centering and scaling by sqrt(V), both converge to sqrt(41) times Brownian motion on fixed horizons. Interpreting marks as zero-order reactions ∅→jP, the rate contrast (-1,3,-3,1) annihilates the generator moments of orders 0, 1, and 2 and is an explicit scalar CLE collision of the type in Faul-Hoessly-Xia Remark 3.5/Theorem 3.3.
assumptions: Independent Poisson reaction channels at constant source concentration
Volume V tends to infinity with a fixed physical horizon
The jump set is bounded and the rate vectors are supplied
claims.proof_path: PROOF.md sections 2 and 3; generator-level relation is verified by the explicit mark-moment sums.
claims.novelty_boundary: The CLE generator collision is covered by the published reaction-SDE identifiability framework. This work studies exact sampled endpoint counts beyond that diffusion limit; no priority claim is made.
claims.costs: Requires stable source replenishment and a known volume/rate scale; no experimental cost is measured.
claims.falsifier: A measured process with a different drift, second jump cumulant, non-Poisson dependence, depletion, or refractory period violates the bridge.
claims.next_gate: Validate the constant-source mechanism independently in a physical assay.

claims.statement: For every mu>0, P0(Y=1)=mu exp(-6mu)>0 while P1(Y=1)=0, so D(P0||P1)=infinity although P1 is absolutely continuous with respect to P0. The event has product probability at most n mu exp(-6mu), which vanishes when n/mu is bounded and mu tends to infinity.
assumptions: Exact unmarked endpoint increments
No measurement error
The stated rate vectors and event-rate scale are exact
claims.novelty_boundary: A model-specific support calculation; it invalidates a symmetric finite-KL statement but is not a general theorem.
claims.costs: The exact likelihood must preserve the zero-probability event; discarding it changes finite-sample decisions.
claims.falsifier: Any mechanism-1 reaction path that can yield a total increment of one removes the support singularity.
claims.next_gate: Keep the singular event in finite exact likelihoods; use TV-equivalent regularization only for the critical asymptotic limit.

claims.statement: For the exact pair, chi-square(P1||P0)=6/(41^3 mu)+o(mu^-1), full squared Hellinger distance=3/(2*41^3 mu)+o(mu^-1), and D(P1||P0)=3/(41^3 mu)+o(mu^-1); D(P0||P1)=infinity because P0(Y=1)>0=P1(Y=1).
assumptions: The stated bounded-mark compound-Poisson pair with known rates and exact integer increment readout
Span-one local lattice Edgeworth expansion on a moderate-deviation window
Pair-specific L2 tails controlled by the compact saddle exponent F=I0-2I1 and explicit low/high count bounds
claims.proof_path: PROOF.md section 3; exact recurrence diagnostics in exact_cp_audit.py and high_precision_cp_check.py
claims.novelty_boundary: Local Edgeworth methods and broad cadence information loss are prior art. The pair-specific coefficient and directional support correction are reconstructed here; priority remains unknown.

claims.falsifier: A rigorous saddlepoint/local expansion or interval-certified recurrence yielding a different coefficient, or a failure of the stated source model, refutes the claim.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof review of the moderate-deviation local expansion and three-region tail split; theorem-by-theorem comparison with Duval (2014).

claims.statement: After conditioning model 0 on Y!=1, if mu,n tend to infinity and n/mu tends to lambda, the binary log likelihood converges to a Gaussian shift with I=6 lambda/41^3 and equal-prior optimal error Phi(-sqrt(3 lambda/(2*41^3))). At fixed physical horizon T, lambda is asymptotic to T/(V Delta^2), so the pair-specific nontrivial cadence scale is Delta proportional to V^-1/2.
assumptions: Exact endpoint counts from independent stationary compound-Poisson increments
Known supplied rate shapes and no unmodeled channel effects
The pair-specific one-step chi-square expansion and moderate-window remainder in PROOF.md section 3
The conditioning error n*mu*exp(-6mu) tends to zero
claims.novelty_boundary: Duval (2014) establishes the broad square-root macroscopic-sampling boundary and Gaussian equivalence in compound-Poisson inference; no novelty claim for the exponent. Exact-pair constant and support treatment priority are unknown.
claims.costs: The asymptotic 5% equal-prior target requires T/(V Delta^2) about 124313, or about 353*sqrt(TV) intervals for one path. Finite affinity and score bounds at this target are not tight enough to certify 5%.
claims.falsifier: A calibrated exact-count experiment whose error curve fails to approach the stated curve as a function of T/(V Delta^2) falsifies the ideal channel prediction.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof audit, then a preregistered source/readout experiment with measured volume, intensity, and detector effects.

claims.statement: For finite bounded positive-integer mark supports with a shared lattice span, positive rates, equal cumulants M1 through Mk for k>=2, common M2=m2>0, and first difference delta at M(k+1), the full squared Hellinger distance is asymptotic to delta^2/[4*(k+1)!*m2^(k+1)]*mu^-(k-1). Product affinity changes at scale n/mu^(k-1), giving fixed-T cadence exponent V^(-(k-1)/k). This claim is Hellinger/affinity only; it does not assert generic chi-square, KL, or LAN.
assumptions: Fixed k>=2 and finite positive integer mark supports
Same lattice span, so the additive semigroups have common eventual support
Common positive second cumulant and cumulant match through k
Uniform local lattice Edgeworth expansion; Chernoff tails for the marginal Hellinger remainder
No nuisance parameter changes the stated cumulant contrast
claims.proof_path: PROOF.md section 5; k=3 finite recurrence diagnostic in generic_k_falsifier.py and generic_k_falsifier.json
claims.novelty_boundary: Duval-Hoffmann (2011) discusses arbitrary discrete compound-law extensions if expansions are available, but does not state this first-differing-cumulant test exponent. The derivation is a classical Edgeworth consequence under stated support conditions; priority is unverified.
claims.costs: For fixed T and path count, read count scales as V^((k-1)/k); constants depend on delta and m2. Physical replication and endpoint-read costs are not measured.
claims.falsifier: The span-mismatch example in PROOF.md shows the lattice condition is necessary. The mark-7 example there refutes any automatic extension from this Hellinger statement to global chi-square/LAN.
claims.next_gate: Independent formalization of the general-k local Edgeworth remainder and systematic prior-art search; retain no general KL/LAN claim without a separate tail condition.

claims.statement: When the two rate shapes are known but one common intensity multiplier is unknown, estimating it as sample_mean/15 has absolute error O_P(1) at n/mu->lambda>0; plugging it into the H3 score changes that score by O_P(1). Independent mechanism-common iid mean-zero endpoint read errors with fixed finite sixth moment also perturb the H3 score by O_P(1) after differencing. Since the score scale is sqrt(n), the score test retains the pair-specific leading Gaussian power.
assumptions: Known rate shapes; only one shared scalar intensity multiplier is unknown
The two candidate classes remain separated by their stated third-cumulant contrast
Independent endpoint errors common to both mechanisms, mean zero, fixed distribution, finite sixth moment
Critical regime n/mu tends to a finite positive constant
claims.novelty_boundary: This establishes a score robustness result, not arbitrary composite LAN, a profile-likelihood theorem for unknown mark proportions, or an exact likelihood for dependent noisy increments.
claims.costs: The same sample estimates the common effective scale; physical volume and a common source multiplier remain confounded. Independent physical calibration is needed to plan a cadence in volume units.
claims.falsifier: A scale nuisance that closes the third-cumulant gap, detector error growing at the count-noise scale, or nonstationary/dependent read error can alter or remove the result.
claims.next_gate: Test the score under a measured endpoint error kernel and expand nuisance classes only with an explicit separation margin.

claims.statement: The PGF coefficient recurrence evaluates the truncated exact increment PMFs, affinity, reverse KL, and finite affinity-based error bounds. At mu=1000 a separate 50-digit recurrence reproduces the asymptotic constants to the displayed precision; at mu=100 and n/mu about 124288, affinity-based equal-prior error bounds are only about [0.017,0.129].
assumptions: Finite floating-point recurrence and Chernoff tail truncation
No interval-certified arithmetic
k=3 check uses rates built from the fourth finite-difference contrast
claims.novelty_boundary: These numbers validate implementation and attempt to falsify coefficients; they do not prove asymptotics or provide a certified finite error guarantee.
claims.costs: Panjer recurrence is O(J*m_max) time and O(m_max) memory; current arithmetic is not interval-certified and the finite test bounds do not certify 5% power.
claims.falsifier: Independent high-precision recurrence or interval arithmetic disagreeing with the output would refute the finite audit.
claims.next_gate: Use interval arithmetic or analytically bounded rounding error before treating recurrence output as a finite planner certificate.

claims.statement: Bounded finite positive mark support, common span, and matching low-order cumulants do not guarantee finite global chi-square: the mark-7 pair in PROOF.md has chi-square(P_B||P_A)=infinity for every mu>0.
assumptions: Finite positive integer mark support
The rate vectors specified in PROOF.md section 5 with 0<epsilon<1/45

claims.exact_statement: For every n>=4 and every graphical labeled degree vector d, let Omega_d be the simple undirected graphs on the fixed labeled vertex set [n] with degree vector d. The lazy chain holds with probability 1/2, otherwise chooses a four-set uniformly and one of six ordered pairs of distinct perfect matchings uniformly, and switches when the first matching is present and the second absent. The release paper states t_mix(d)<=2 n^8 in worst-case total variation distance 1/4. If |Omega_d|>1 it states spectral gap >=1/(24 n^2 binom(n,4)); if |Omega_d|=1 the mixing time is zero.
assumptions: Simple undirected unweighted graphs
Complete host: every vertex pair is eligible
Vertex labels and each labeled vertex degree are fixed
The degree vector is graphical and explicitly supplied
claims.status: source-reported theorem; exact statement reconstructed from pinned release PDF; source proof not independently verified
claims.novelty_boundary: The release paper claims the all-graphical-sequence simple-undirected Kannan-Tetali-Vempala result. No correctness, proof verification, external review, or priority claim is made in this audit.

costs.mixing: At most 2 n^8 lazy proposal steps for TV distance 1/4; each step samples a four-vertex set and checks at most four edges
costs.exact_sampler: Source states expected polynomial bit running time in the explicit degree-vector length and almost-sure termination; a rare correction branch enumerates up to 2^binom(n,2) adjacency bitstrings

claims.falsifier: A graphical labeled degree vector and starting graph for which the specified chain remains farther than 1/4 in total variation after 2 n^8 steps, or a source-proof defect invalidating its transition or gap argument.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof audit or small-state exact enumeration against the transition matrix; keep source-reported status until then.

claims.exact_statement: For n=2m with m>=5, split labeled cell vertices into two distant groups A and B and give each group a 4-regular circulant graph with cycle edges at distances 1 and 2. The observed disjoint union is a simple 4-regular graph with zero A-B contacts. Under the uniform degree-only law on all simple 4-regular graphs on 2m labels, permutation symmetry gives expected crossing-edge count 4m^2/(2m-1). Since the count is at most 4m, the stationary probability of at least m crossing edges is >=(2m+1)/(6m-3)>1/3. Conditional on the source mixing theorem, after 2(2m)^8 steps this event has probability >1/12 from any start, although all such cross-compartment contacts are physically impossible.
assumptions: Two compartments contain m labeled cells each and no physical cross-compartment contact is possible
Each compartment has an observed simple 4-regular contact graph
The proposed null fixes only the labeled degree vector and samples on the complete graph
Family 131's TV statement is assumed for the conditional probability consequence; its proof is not independently verified here
claims.status: internally derived exact counterexample to biological interpretation beyond the degree-only null
claims.novelty_boundary: This does not refute the chain theorem or the degree-only null as a mathematical distribution. It refutes interpreting that null as a spatially valid contact-generating model without geometry constraints.

costs.null_mixing: 2(2m)^8 proposal steps for the source TV threshold
empirical_observables: contact distance or shared boundary length

claims.falsifier: The example's physical premise fails if cross-compartment edges are in fact feasible, or its null calculation fails if the sample space is not the complete-host uniform 4-regular graph law.
claims.next_gate: On a named cell-contact dataset, compare the degree-only null to a spatially constrained null while preserving the same labeled cells; report distance, cross-region, and cell-type mixing distributions.

claims.exact_statement: Corollary 1.2 states an exact uniform sampler over Omega_d using unbiased random bits, almost-sure termination, and expected polynomial bit running time in the binary encoding length of d. The correction branch has probability delta=2^-(4 binom(n,2)+10) and can enumerate the graph universe, so the source gives no polynomial bound on every execution.
assumptions: Input is any finite graphical labeled degree vector
Output is an exact uniform graph from the complete-host simple-undirected realization set
Expected, not worst-case per-execution, bit runtime
claims.status: source-reported corollary and caveat reconstructed from release PDF; proof not verified
claims.novelty_boundary: Exact output law and expected-time guarantee are distinct from a worst-case polynomial sampler and from the finite-time Markov chain alone.

costs.typical_branch: O(n^8) chain steps under the source mixing scale
costs.rare_branch: Enumerates up to 2^binom(n,2) adjacency bitstrings and tabulates the finite-time law
costs.execution_tail: Almost-sure termination with unbounded execution-time tail

claims.falsifier: The source algorithm fails to terminate almost surely, has a nonuniform output law, or its expected bit cost is not polynomial in the stated input length.

claims.exact_statement: Fix a labeled partition of vertices into compartments C_1,...,C_s and a within-compartment degree vector. Under H0^strat, draw each compartment graph independently and uniformly from its simple-undirected complete-host realization set with the same labeled degrees; cross-compartment edges are forbidden. For a statistic T preregistered before randomization, draw B independent null graphs G_1,...,G_B and compute p_MC=(1+#{b:T(G_b)>=T(G_0)})/(B+1). If the observed graph G_0 is itself uniform under this conditional null, G_0,...,G_B are exchangeable and p_MC is super-uniform, so rejection at p_MC<=alpha has conditional type-I error at most alpha. This is a conditional statistical application, not a new network-science theorem.
assumptions: Compartment partition, labeled degrees, node covariates, statistic, and tail direction are fixed before inspecting the observed edge pattern, or selection is otherwise accounted for
Under the null, conditional on these variables, the observed graph is uniform on the product of within-compartment degree-sequence realization sets
Each compartment host is complete within the stratum; cross-stratum edges are structurally impossible
Exact sampler outputs independent exact-uniform draws, or approximate chains are assigned an explicit joint TV error budget
claims.status: internally derived finite-sample randomization-test guarantee conditional on an explicit exchangeability null; source proof for the sampler/mixing result remains unverified
claims.novelty_boundary: The validity proof is the standard exchangeability rank argument. Family 131 supplies a source-reported sampler/mixing tool only for complete-host degree-sequence sets; it does not establish that biological observations are exchangeable or that the null generated the tissue.

costs.exact_sampler: B independent draws per compartment; expected polynomial bit cost per source corollary, but an exponentially rare correction branch and unbounded run-time tails prevent a worst-case polynomial execution guarantee
costs.approximate_switch_chain: With s strata and n_j vertices in stratum j, choose per-chain epsilon_j=eta/(B s); source t_mix(1/4)<=2 n_j^8 plus standard TV amplification gives at most 2 B ceil(log2(B s/eta)) sum_j n_j^8 proposals and type-I error at most alpha+eta; cutoff alpha-eta for eta<alpha restores at-most-alpha control
costs.Monte_Carlo_resolution: Minimum p-value 1/(B+1); B>=log(2/beta)/(2 epsilon^2) gives Hoeffding error epsilon for the fixed-threshold exceedance probability with confidence 1-beta

claims.falsifier: The test's biological calibration fails if, conditional on the asserted degrees/strata/covariates, edge opportunities remain nonexchangeable due to distance, boundaries, local density, cell type, detection, or post-hoc stratum selection; this falsifies the model interpretation, not the exchangeability lemma.
claims.next_gate: On a named dataset, preregister the compartments and molecular/contact statistic; compare complete-host, compartment-preserving, and geometry-aware local-coordinate controls, and report the spatial covariates that would falsify within-stratum exchangeability.

claims.claim: Verma et al. report four 500 K DFT barrier comparisons in which molecular-H2-assisted hydrogenation barriers are below the corresponding atomic-H barriers.
claims.qualification: The complete detailed numeric reconstruction used the primary preprint and the published dataset; do not represent the preprint as the version of record.

claims.claim: Under mean-field TST with matched substrate coverage, effective site molecularity, and prefactor, the molecular-H2 path beats the atomic-H path exactly when theta_H2*/theta_H* exceeds exp(-(B_H-B_H2)/kBT). At source-predicted 500 K coverages, the four conditional ratios are approximately 45916, 10.80, 1.34, and 443.
claims.source_data: Materials Cloud DOI 10.24435/materialscloud:94-1n, Source File/Main Figures/Fig 4/Fig 4c/Automated Reactions/500/coverage.dat
claims.qualification: Coverages are model outputs, not measurements; no prefactor equality or physical mechanism is established. The formula is a direct TST rearrangement, not a novelty claim.

claims.claim: At 500 K, a 0.13 eV barrier shift gives an e^(0.13/kBT) approximately 20.4-fold single-rate change, and opposite shifts in two competing barriers change their ratio by approximately 418-fold.
claims.qualification: The source's 0.13 eV test MAE is not a per-edge uncertainty bound or confidence interval. This calculation only shows why mean error cannot certify all 9237 added elementary reactions.

claims.claim: Zhang et al. report 660 mg gcat^-1 h^-1 methanol STY for 40 wt% Cu/Al2O3 DAR versus about 100 mg gcat^-1 h^-1 fixed-bed, and about 5% versus 60% CO selectivity.
claims.qualification: Three independent measurement error bars are reported. The difference is observed in different reactor geometries; this cycle does not refute the performance result.

claims.claim: Interpreting 360 mL/min as STP flow for 3:1 H2:CO2 at 452 m/s yields 0.342 W gas kinetic power, reproducing the paper's approximately 0.34 W.
claims.qualification: The flow reference basis is inferred from the reported power and must be confirmed. This is kinetic power in the feed stream, not total measured reactor power and not an additional load to add on top of compression.

claims.claim: On the inferred standard-flow basis, reversible isothermal ideal-gas compression from 1 to 20 bar is approximately 1.99 W and feed sensible heating 298 to 573 K is approximately 2.28 W per 1 g-catalyst flow condition.
claims.qualification: Ideal gas, inlet/outlet reference conditions, heat capacity, pressure recovery, and heat recovery assumptions. These are not measured power draws. Actual load and pressure drop are UNKNOWN.

claims.claim: The SI's 20 nm diameter by 100 nm length cylinder at 4 g/cm3 and 40 wt% Cu contains approximately 476357 Cu atoms, 36.64 times the reported approximately 13000. Under the SI's half-energy absorption and one-third affected assumptions, source-reported kinetic energy gives approximately 0.00579 eV per affected Cu, about 29 times below the cited 0.17 eV/atom DFT structural excess.
claims.qualification: This identifies an internal mismatch under the printed geometry and assumptions, not a demonstrated failure of the real catalyst. Actual localization of impact energy into a small active-atom fraction is unmeasured. DFT energy is not measured operating free energy.

claims.claim: Network thermodynamic consistency via independent pathway constraints is already treated in a 2025 primary paper; this cycle does not claim a new closure theorem or projection algorithm.

unknowns: Operando H2* and H* coverages on the experimental Cu/SiO2 catalyst.
H/D surface scrambling and isotope transfer time scales under the published 50 bar conditions.
Transition-state prefactor and site-molecularity ratios for the molecular-H2 and atomic-H routes on experimental catalyst states.
Whether the published large-network mechanism satisfies local detailed balance on every reversible reaction cycle; no assertion either way is made here.
Real DAR compressor power, pressure drop, furnace duty, heat recovery, air-hammer duty, feed basis, and full product/feed balance.
The actual number of active Cu atoms receiving collision energy and the impact-localization mechanism.
Costs, acquisition times, power, and replication requirements for the proposed isotopic and operando tests.

verification.result: Passed; source coverage row parsed and all deterministic calculations reproduced.
verification.scope_limit: No DFT, microkinetic solver, experiment, or external validation performed by this cycle.

ledger.scope: Independent audit of c8 sparse rational-rate endotactic recognition complexity; no edits to c8 parent artifacts.

claims.statement: For the essential-source predicate on explicit sparse positive rational generalized-polynomial channels with dimension included in the input, NON-ENDOTACTIC is NP-complete and ENDOTACTIC is coNP-complete, provided the z>0 UNSAT converse explicitly handles neutral clauses by averaging their three literal values.
assumptions: Finite nonempty numerator and denominator supports with rational exponents and strictly positive rational coefficients.
Rational reaction vectors are explicitly encoded; direction w ranges over real vectors.
Neutral channels are removed before the maximum, and every exact active top tie is checked.
Dimension varies as part of the input.
3SAT source clauses use three distinct variables for coefficient-one hardness.
claims.novelty_boundary: The reduction and sparse quotient-support complexity statement were not found in the scoped primary search; historical priority remains unknown and no external proof review is claimed.
claims.costs: The map uses n+1 dimensions, 3n+m+1 channels, and O(n+m) listed terms; full dense coordinate serialization remains polynomial. Dimension-fixed XP algorithms are not ruled out.
claims.falsifier: A counterdirection for an UNSAT formula, a satisfiable formula whose assignment direction lacks an outward active top tie, a non-polynomial witness-bit counterexample, or a failure of exact support formulas under positive coefficient aggregation.
claims.next_gate: External proof review of the all-directions UNSAT converse and rational LP witness-bit lemma; comprehensive scoped priority search.

claims.statement: The c8 top-level PROOF.md omits a necessary z>0 subcase in its stated UNSAT argument: neutral clauses are not constrained by target being an active top. The missing implication is repaired because S_C=0 gives average literal value z, hence some literal is at least z. The child HARDNESS.md contains this repair. The satisfying-witness sentence claiming both guards score -1 is an arithmetic typo; their scores are -1 and -3.
assumptions: Clause has three literal occurrences and S_C is the sum of sigma*u_i-z over occurrences.
All nonzero active channel scores are compared exactly; neutral clauses are excluded before maximizing.
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a proof-document correction, not a refutation of the theorem: the other report supplies the omitted average argument.
claims.costs: The repair adds one line of exact arithmetic; the guard-score correction changes no inequality needed by the reduction.
claims.falsifier: An example with S_C=0 and all three literal values less than z, or a truth assignment direction with either guard score not in {-1,-3}.
claims.next_gate: Update the primary proof file with the neutral-clause average and correct guard-score sentence.

claims.statement: The 3SAT reduction does not prove coNP-hardness for standard strong endotacticity. Standard GMS strong endotacticity requires an inward reaction at the global maximum over all sources, retaining neutral sources; the all-eight-clauses UNSAT instance at (0,0,0,-1) has only neutral guards at global score 2.
assumptions: Strong endotacticity is the GMS Definition 3.14(4) all-reactant source-maximum condition.
The fixture has all eight sign patterns of one 3-variable, 3-literal clause.
claims.novelty_boundary: No lower bound for strong-endotactic recognition is claimed. The auxiliary essential-top-face label in child_hardness/HARDNESS.md is nonstandard and its added condition, as written, collapses to ordinary endotacticity.
claims.costs: The exact Fraction replay is finite and fixture-specific; it only blocks the claimed transfer and does not settle complexity of the standard strong property.
claims.falsifier: An inward reaction at global source score 2 in the listed direction, or a different source definition that expressly excludes neutral sources (which would no longer be standard GMS strong endotacticity).
claims.next_gate: If strong hardness is pursued, construct a separate reduction controlling all-source neutral maxima.

claims.statement: The reduction uses positive rational rates that can be unbounded or singular at the boundary, including Xi/Z^2 and 1/(Xi Z^2); it does not establish hardness for globally bounded rational laws, canonical Hill/Michaelis-Menten syntax, or other restricted biochemical kinetics.
assumptions: The formal input promises positivity only on the open positive orthant through positive numerator and denominator coefficients.
No boundary regularity, global boundedness, or rate/source-complex compatibility is imposed in the sparse quotient encoding.
claims.novelty_boundary: The broad class includes rational/tropical neighboring work, but the reduction has not been mapped into canonical Hill/MM or globally bounded subfamilies; their complexity is unknown here.
claims.costs: The common-denominator lift can be exponentially larger than the sparse quotient input; exact explicit mass-action diagram costs are not poly-bounded by this reduction.
claims.falsifier: An explicit polynomial-size transformation of this reduction into the named restricted kinetic syntax, or a separate proof establishing such restricted hardness.
claims.next_gate: Either prove a restricted-syntax embedding with full size accounting or design a specialized algorithm for that subclass.

claims.statement: Scoped primary sources establish finite explicit reaction-diagram endotactic/strong recognition and rational/polynomial tropical-equilibration methods, but no exact collision for sparse rational quotient-support endotactic recognition or its complexity was identified; priority remains unknown.
assumptions: The comparison is limited to the primary sources listed in PRIMARY_SOURCES.md and targeted searches recorded there.
claims.novelty_boundary: No exhaustive search or first-of-kind claim is made.
claims.costs: JPD's explicit graph input can be exponentially larger after denominator expansion; Samal et al.'s tropical equilibration endpoint differs from universal endotactic recognition.
claims.falsifier: A primary source defining the same sparse quotient input and proving or algorithmically resolving the same universal active-source predicate.
claims.next_gate: Search citations and computational-complexity literature around endotactic recognition, succinctly encoded reaction networks, and tropical support-order predicates.

claims.statement: For a fixed mass-action reaction network under the Langevin approximation, full-SDE rate identifiability is equivalent to linear independence, source by source, of the lifted reaction signatures (nu, nu nu^T).
assumptions: Fixed known reaction graph and species set
Mass-action kinetics with strictly positive rates on reactions present
Ideal structural knowledge of the complete drift/diffusion generator and state variables
SDE law comparison is local on bounded open subsets of the positive orthant where the martingale problem is well posed
claims.status: source-reported theorem: Theorem 3.3(1), with coefficient interface in Remark 3.5
claims.novelty_boundary: The lifted-signature identifiability criterion is published. It concerns ideal full-state Langevin-law identifiability on a fixed known network; it does not supply a finite noisy-data sample-complexity result or identify unknown reaction graphs from partial observations.

costs.input: Complete species list, candidate reaction graphs, and exact generator coefficients are assumed known/supplied.
costs.computation: Per-source linear-independence/rank check; the paper provides a Julia implementation. No finite noisy-data acquisition cost follows from the theorem.
costs.data: Ideal full-state law/generator; no measurement precision or trajectory count is supplied by the structural theorem.

claims.falsifier: A fixed network with linearly dependent lifted signatures but an injective ideal full-SDE rate map would contradict the source-reported criterion.
claims.next_gate: Use a finite-state counterexample to examine information discarded when the full CTMC is reduced to its first two jump signatures.

claims.statement: For the two one-source catalytic networks defined in FINAL_REPORT.md, the mass-action ODE drift, Langevin covariance, and waiting-time law agree, but their single-turnover CTMC product-yield laws differ at the third jump moment. Five independent preformed-complex assays and the exact likelihood-ratio rule give type-I and type-II errors 181/7776 each, with combined error 181/3888 < 0.05 under the stated fixed rates and exact readout assumptions.
assumptions: Species order (C,E,S,P), with C representing a bound intermediate E:S4
Network A rates by yields k=1,2,3,4 are (1,1,4,0); Network B rates are (0,4,1,1)
First-order stochastic propensity kappa_k C for each present channel
Each assay starts from exactly C=1,E=S=P=0 and stops after its one event; every completed channel produces P>0
Five independent assays, known fixed candidate rates, and exact integer product-yield readout
claims.status: internally reconstructed candidate plus finite exact rational calculation; no external chemical validation or novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: The construction is a direct finite-difference witness for the published first-two-moment interface. Novelty is unknown and likely illustrative rather than a new identifiability theorem. It does not establish a real enzyme mechanism.

costs.input: Five correctly prepared C=E:S4 complexes; each yields one product-count measurement. Complex preparation, purity, and concentration calibration are not priced.
costs.measurement: Resolve k in {1,2,3,4}; assume zero classification error. Waiting-time measurements carry no distinguishing information because both total rates equal 6. At a fixed horizon T, the probability any of five assays is right-censored is at most 5 exp(-6T); T >= log(500)/6 gives a 1% batch bound.
costs.computation: Four-category exact likelihood ratio; O(N) count updates for N=5, with exact finite multinomial error summation.
costs.resources: Five single-turnover reactions; enzyme is released, but each trial needs a newly prepared bound complex. Parallel completion time has expectation H_5/6 = 137/360 time units.

claims.falsifier: Observing both a k=1 and k=4 endpoint in the same ideal assay batch has zero probability under either closed candidate; calibrated yield frequencies inconsistent with either multinomial law also reject the two-model set.
claims.next_gate: Establish chemical feasibility and availability of C=E:S4; measure detector confusion and preparation yield; recompute the optimal sample count under the resulting observation channel.

claims.statement: On the fixed eight-channel mass-action graph with source complexes C and 2C, the two strictly positive rate vectors r_A=(2,1,4,1), q_A=(4,1,10,1) and r_B=(1,4,1,2), q_B=(1,10,1,4) induce identical full CLE drift and covariance fields for every state x.
assumptions: Species order is (C,E,S,P); C=E:S4
For k=1,2,3,4 the channels are C→E+(4-k)S+kP and 2C→2E+(8-k)S+kP
Factorial-normalized source monomials are x_C and x_C^2/2
Both parameter vectors are strictly positive on the same eight-reaction graph
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact algebra; finite-checked with rational arithmetic
claims.novelty_boundary: The source-wise lifted signature criterion is source-reported in Faul-Hoessly-Xia Theorem 3.3(1). This finite witness instantiates its known moment-nullspace mechanism at two source monomials; no general theorem or priority claim is made.

costs.input: Known graph, species list, source normalization, and two exact rate vectors are supplied.
costs.computation: Exact moment and matrix comparison; Python standard-library script runs in under one second locally.
costs.data: No data are needed for the structural coefficient identity.

claims.falsifier: Any source-wise difference in M0, M1, or M2, or any inequality between the printed polynomial drift/covariance matrices, invalidates the claimed CLE collision.
claims.next_gate: Obtain an independent mathematical review of the derivation and verify that the factorial-normalized CLE convention matches the intended finite-volume chemical model.

claims.statement: For the finite CTMC initialized at (C,E,S,P)=(2,0,0,0), the complete product-jump path law differs between the two CLE-equivalent rate vectors. The exact CTMC likelihood-ratio test needs five independent runs for sum of type-I and type-II errors at most 0.05; endpoint product counts alone need sixteen runs for that criterion.
assumptions: Finite-copy propensities are r_k C for source C and q_k binom(C,2) for source 2C
Assays are independent and observed to completion
Only product-count jump sizes in {1,2,3,4} are observed; no reaction-source label is available
The two candidate rate vectors are known simple hypotheses
Readout has zero error and there are no background reactions
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact path and endpoint laws; likelihood errors and adjacent minimum counts finite-tested by exact integer/rational dynamic programming
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a two-source, state-dependent finite CTMC construction and a fixed-pair acquisition result, not an empirical discovery or a new general identifiability theorem. It does not include detector noise, rate-calibration cost, or finite-sample nuisance-rate estimation.

costs.marked_path: Five-run sum-error target uses ten prepared C intermediates, at most ten product-jump records (expected 7.5), and five completion checks if depletion is not directly observable. Four runs give equal conditional errors 0.0395544 each; five give 0.0249843 each.
costs.endpoint_only: Sixteen independent C=2 runs are needed for sum-error ≤0.05, each with one final product count in {1,...,8}; eleven runs suffice for equal-prior Bayes error ≤0.05.
costs.measurement: Resolve every event product-yield increment exactly as an integer 1 through 4 and run to completion; a calibrated analog readout rounded to the nearest integer needs absolute error below 0.5 molecule-equivalent. No practical detector noise model is supplied. Event timestamps carry no information for the fixed A-vs-B comparison.
costs.runtime: One run has expected completion time 3/32 time units. A fixed horizon T≥ln(500)/8 gives a union-bound batch censoring probability at most 1% for five runs.

claims.falsifier: An event yield outside 1..4, more than two events, persistence of C beyond the model's completion tail, or violation of C+E=2 or 4C+S+P=8 falsifies the closed pair. A larger batch with poor likelihood under both hypotheses rejects the pair rather than favoring one.
claims.next_gate: Validate the cooperative 2C chemistry, calibrate the product-jump observation channel and preparation state, then recompute the exact LRT with measured confusion and rate uncertainty.

claims.statement: For the fixed two-source graph and exact completed product-marked event-time law from a controlled C=2 initialization, all eight positive source rates are structurally identifiable even though their CLE rate map is not injective.
assumptions: The graph is known and source reactions follow the stated first- and second-order propensities
The output records event times, ordered product-yield increments, and completion/path length, but not chemical source or internal state
Rates are strictly positive and the event-time law is observed ideally
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact structural inversion; no finite-sample confidence or noisy acquisition result
claims.novelty_boundary: The result is specific to this small controlled hidden-source CTMC. It does not establish generic partial-observation identifiability for reaction networks.

costs.input: Controlled C=2 initial count and fixed reaction graph.
costs.observation: First waiting time identifies H=2R+Q; second gap on two-event paths identifies R; Q=H-2R; conditional marks identify normalized rates r/R and q/Q.
costs.limitation: If waiting times are discarded, common positive scaling of all rates leaves the marked-path law unchanged.

claims.falsifier: Two distinct positive (r,q) pairs producing the same ideal marked-time law would contradict the stated inversion; an exact symbolic counterexample is the decisive audit.
claims.next_gate: Derive finite-sample intervals or an optimal nuisance-rate acquisition policy under a calibrated noisy observation channel.

claims.statement: For a centered compound-Poisson process with unknown intensity and jump density observed on a coarse mesh Δ_T→∞ with T/Δ_T→∞ and T/Δ_T^2=o((log(T/Δ_T))^{-1/4}), Duval Theorem 2 gives a strictly positive local asymptotic minimax lower bound in the loss ||(λ,f)||_{2,P}=||λf||_2, so consistent estimation of (λ,f) is impossible when Δ_T is of order T^α for 1/2<α<1.
assumptions: The compound-Poisson jump law is centered, has finite variance, and is an unknown density f
The parameter r=(λ,f) lies in the paper's class P and r0 has finite stated L2,P norm
Observations are floor(T/Δ_T) independent increments over horizon T
Δ_T→∞, T/Δ_T→∞, and the paper's logarithmic condition holds
claims.status: source-reported primary theorem reconstructed from the author manuscript
claims.novelty_boundary: The result concerns asymptotic coarse-time sampling of stationary independent increments. It is not a finite-volume state-dependent CRN result and is distinct from the exact finite-count assay above.

costs.data: floor(T/Δ_T) coarsely spaced increments over [0,T].
costs.statistical: A fixed local parameter neighborhood has positive asymptotic minimax risk; the theorem is not a sample count for the catalytic pair.

claims.falsifier: A uniformly consistent estimator over one of the theorem's stated local neighborhoods under its mesh conditions would contradict the source-reported lower bound.
claims.next_gate: No new application is claimed; retain as a novelty-boundary reference only.
