ledger.task: Reverse-transfer release family 115 to a conditional randomization model for single-cell gene-by-cell counts, correcting the Poisson-uniformity boundary

claims.statement: The pinned family-115 source states that for nonnegative integer row and column margins with equal total, with complete support and no supplied cell caps, there is an exact uniform sampler terminating almost surely with expected bit cost polynomial in both dimensions and log of the total. It separately states a worst-case polynomial-bit sampler within 2^-k total variation, polynomial in dimensions, log total, and k.
assumptions: Complete cell support; no input forbidden positions or individual caps.
Margins are binary-encoded nonnegative integers with equal total.
Unbiased random bits and bit-operation cost model.
claims.status: source-reported theorem statement; relevant PDF statements/sections read, proof not independently verified, no implementation replay or external review
claims.novelty_boundary: Historical priority, correctness, and practical advantage are not independently established. Exact expected-time sampling has restricted-class primary antecedents, including Miller-Harrison and sparse-margin Arman-Gao-Wormald results.
claims.costs: Expected polynomial bit time in dimensions and log total; separate bounded-time sampler polynomial in accuracy bits k. The paper itself notes a rare exhaustive correction branch and deliberately large polynomial exponents. Dense table output costs at least one write per cell.
claims.falsifier: A proof error or an exhaustive small-instance check showing output support/probabilities disagree with uniformity; algorithmic cost claim requires independent proof review or reproducible implementation accounting.
claims.next_gate: Obtain independent proof review and implementation; benchmark on realistic single-cell dimensions without upgrading the source claim from its current status.

claims.statement: The pinned family-115 bounded-table source states an all-execution polynomial-bit FPRAS for counting nonnegative integer tables with arbitrary binary-encoded margins and individual upper bounds, including zero bounds/structural zeros. Its conditional-count self-reduction gives a sampler within TV tau of uniform, reports infeasibility exactly, and has all-execution polynomial-bit cost in input length and tau^-1. It does not claim exact sampling for arbitrary capped fibers.
assumptions: Margins and all cell upper bounds are explicit binary-encoded integers.
The feasible fiber may be empty; zero upper bounds encode forbidden positions.
FPRAS accuracy inputs epsilon, delta; sampling TV input tau.
claims.status: source-reported theorem statement; proof not independently verified
claims.novelty_boundary: Prior FPRAS results cover important special cases such as binary tables, fixed row dimension, and tight-capacity settings. Family 115 unrestricted correctness and priority remain unverified here.
claims.costs: Counting cost polynomial in total binary input length L, epsilon^-1, and log(delta^-1); approximate sampling cost polynomial in L and tau^-1 on every execution. A dense per-cell bound/mask requires O(rows times columns) input entries unless a supported sparse encoding is established.
claims.falsifier: A feasible bounded fiber where estimated count guarantee or self-reduction sampling guarantee fails; exact proof review needed beyond the stated theorem and inspected source sections.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof/code audit and realistic dense/sparse data benchmarks.

claims.statement: For independent Poisson cell counts with means lambda_gc=a_g b_c, conditioned on row and column margins and any fixed support/bounds, table probability is proportional to the product over cells of 1/x_gc!. It is uniform on a particular fiber if and only if the product of all cell factorials is constant on that fiber. Non-factorized means leave interaction weights as well.
assumptions: Independent Poisson variables on allowed cells.
Fixed row and column totals; fixed, data-independent support and cell bounds.
Factorized means lambda_gc=a_g b_c for the simple factorial-weighted formula.
claims.status: proved directly by conditioning the joint Poisson pmf; no external theorem needed
claims.novelty_boundary: Classical conditional-table calculation; no novelty claimed. It corrects the overbroad inference that Poisson conditioning gives uniform tables.
claims.costs: Constant-size symbolic derivation; no data acquisition. Using this law for inference requires a sampler for the factorial-weighted target if it is not the intended uniform microcanonical null.
claims.falsifier: An algebraic error in the conditional pmf; the exact 2x2 case in the linked script is a reproducible check of the nonuniformity claim.
claims.next_gate: If the scientific null is Poisson, compare/use its factorial-weighted conditional law rather than substituting the uniform sampler.

claims.statement: If independent nonnegative geometric cell counts have pmf (1-q_gc)q_gc^k with q_gc=a_g b_c in (0,1), conditioning on any fixed row/column margins gives the uniform law over the feasible tables. The result continues to hold on any fixed bounded/structural-zero fiber for appropriately truncated geometric variables. This is NB shape 1 and is overdispersed: variance equals mean plus mean squared.
assumptions: Independent cell counts with a fixed common geometric shape 1.
Geometric odds factor as a_g b_c on the allowed support.
Support and cell bounds are fixed independently of the observed random zeros; each q_gc is below one.
claims.status: proved by direct factorization on the fiber; model-scoped conditional-uniform bridge, not a novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: The conditioning identity is standard exponential-family reasoning. The specific application is a clearly stated overdispersed gene-by-cell null; empirical fit and biological usefulness are UNKNOWN.
claims.costs: No estimation of a_g or b_c is required after conditioning. Unbounded complete-support sampling uses the family-115 exact sampler at source-reported expected polynomial cost; bounded/structural-zero sampling is only approximate via the separate family-115 bounded interface.
claims.falsifier: Two feasible tables with unequal conditional mass under the stated independent geometric/separable-odds model; direct factorization rules this out unless support or parameter assumptions fail.
claims.next_gate: Evaluate calibration on blinded negative controls and compare to Poisson and NB alternatives with the same margins.

claims.statement: For 2x2 margins (2,2)/(2,2), the fiber has three tables. Under factorized independent Poisson means their conditional probabilities are (1/6,2/3,1/6); under factorized independent NB shape 2 odds they are (9/34,16/34,9/34); under geometric/NB shape 1 they are (1/3,1/3,1/3).
assumptions: Three-table fiber described in the report.
Poisson or negative-binomial odds factor by row and column.
NB shape is common across cells.
claims.status: exact finite-rational check passed; proof follows from the conditional weights
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary counterexample; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: Three feasible tables; exact rational arithmetic only.
claims.falsifier: The saved script asserts the fiber and all three probability vectors using fractions; changing a conditional law or margin is needed to produce a different result.
claims.next_gate: Use this as the minimal regression check when implementing a conditional sampler.

claims.statement: Under the independent geometric shape-1 model with gene-by-cell odds q_gc=a_g b_c, a raw gene-by-cell count table is uniform conditional on its gene totals and cell library totals. A prespecified gene-set versus cell-group association statistic can therefore be tested by exact fixed-margin randomization on the uncapped complete-support fiber; the plus-one Monte Carlo p-value is finite-sample superuniform. For caps/structural zeros, use only the bounded approximate sampler, with sampling-law error charged.
assumptions: Raw integer counts, fixed prespecified gene set and cell group, and no post-selection of support/masks from the tested zeros.
Independent geometric shape-1 counts with multiplicatively separable cell odds.
For the exact family-115 sampler: full support and no supplied cell caps; for capped fibers: source-reported bounded TV sampler only.
claims.status: conditional statistical validity proved under stated model; biological fit and actual dataset validation not performed
claims.novelty_boundary: A model-specific use of established fixed-margin randomization; no biological validation, causal interpretation, or novelty claim.
claims.costs: For M exact uncapped samples, expected source-theorem runtime is M times a polynomial in dimensions and log total, plus M statistic calculations; the statistic reads the gene-by-cell matrix. Additive Monte Carlo error eta at confidence 1-delta takes M at least log(2/delta)/(2 eta^2). For bounded approximate samples, choose per-sample tau at most tau_total/M and pay polynomial input-size and tau^-1 cost each sample.
claims.falsifier: Mis-calibration on blinded negative controls or clear departure from geometric conditional exchangeability; a failure of biology fit does not falsify the combinatorial family-115 theorem.
claims.next_gate: Run a preregistered negative-control/positive-control study with raw counts, donors, batches, spike-ins or technical replicates, comparing uniform, Poisson-factorial, and NB/capture-aware conditional nulls.

claims.statement: The reconstructed N77 network has infinitely many closed irreducible positive-recurrent classes in B+C=2 with pi_n(A at least n)=1, so the stationary family is not tight despite the shared positive ODE attractor. This is a classwise tightness obstruction only.
assumptions: Unit-rate N77 network and falling-factorial stochastic mass action as summarized in the pinned card.
claims.status: brief internally reconstructed carry-forward from supplied summary; full source proof/code packet absent and fixtures unreplayed
claims.novelty_boundary: No novelty claim; retained only to preserve the negative observation while avoiding overlap with parent probability work.
claims.costs: No new derivation or experiment in this pivot.
claims.falsifier: Any enabled reaction escaping the stated class or a stationary law placing mass below A=n.
claims.next_gate: None in this task.

unknowns: Independent proof validation and implementation replay for the family-115 exact sampler, bounded FPRAS, and bounded near-uniform sampler.
Whether a particular single-cell dataset is adequately modeled by independent geometric/NB-shape-1 counts with separable gene and cell odds.
Whether donor, batch, cell-type, capture, ambient-RNA, dropout, and data-selection effects have been controlled sufficiently for a fixed-margin randomization null.
Practical runtimes, peak memory, and sparse-input/output behavior at realistic gene-by-cell dimensions; polynomial theorem bounds have large/unspecified exponents.
Whether family-115 result priority or novelty claims survive external literature review.

ledger.exact_statement: As recorded in the pinned N51 source package, a coefficient-blind deterministic generator using unary n,B prints a polynomial-size list of n-tuples of integer square matrices whose prime-subfield reductions hit every family of at most B feasible affine pencils of order at most B over every coefficient field. With B=2s+1, the supplied reduction claims a defined invertible hit for each nonzero admissible size-s noncommutative rational formula and preserves every inverse occurrence in its original expression tree.
assumptions: Pencil feasibility means invertibility at some matrix evaluation over a coefficient-field extension.
For the rational-formula corollary, the formula is nonzero and has a nonempty original expression domain.
The source package reports internal proof/audit passes; the full generator was not executed and external correctness/priority are unresolved.
ledger.status: source-derived candidate; interface and supplied derivation reconstructed; not externally verified
ledger.novelty_boundary: The source-derived integer-list composition is not externally priority-cleared. This task reconstructs its stated interface and does not certify the generator or claim novelty.
ledger.costs: The source claims polynomial dense-output bit cost in n,B with impractical constants; it reports more than 4e62 tuples in an underlying n=B=1 example and says the full generator was not executed. Formula coefficient representation, formula evaluation, exact matrix/rank output, and physical acquisition are separate costs.
ledger.falsifier: A counterexample to the source theorem within its exact feasible-pencil or admissible-formula interface, or an independently verified construction failure, would refute the claim.
ledger.next_gate: External expert verification of the all-characteristic integer-list construction, complete generator execution at a nontrivial instance, and an acquisition/evaluation interface with explicit cost bounds.

ledger.exact_statement: Let X1,...,X5 range over strictly positive 2x2 continuous-time Markov transition kernels. The free rational formula Phi=s4(X1,X2,X3,X4)(I+X5)^(-1), where s4 is the degree-4 standard noncommutative polynomial, is nonzero over the free skew field and is defined at every such physical tuple, but Phi evaluates to the zero matrix for every such tuple. Therefore a universal nonzero-formula hit over unrestricted matrix substitutions does not guarantee a nonzero experiment in a fixed two-state pathway control family.
assumptions: The pathway state space is exactly two states and each intervention is represented by its 2x2 transition kernel.
Every pulse has positive rates and positive duration, so the second eigenvalue of each transition kernel lies in (0,1).
Matrix products encode sequential pulse composition.
ledger.status: internally reconstructed exact counterexample, conditional only on the stated two-state model
ledger.novelty_boundary: The Amitsur-Levitzki identity and two-state receptor models are established prior art. The new work product is the exact application-interface obstruction and its inverse-domain-preserving formula instance, not a new algebraic identity or biological claim.
ledger.costs: The physical model has two fitted rates per pulse condition. Estimating each 2x2 kernel requires preparing both starting states and classifying endpoints. The N51 substitution dimensions, arbitrary signed entries, exact formula-evaluation costs, and inverse-gate condition numbers have no physical encoding in the source. The illustrative order-response assay needs about 8,527 independent observations per order for 80% power at 5% under an ideal two-binomial approximation; this ignores overdispersion and misclassification.
ledger.falsifier: An exact rational 2x2 tuple with s4(X1,X2,X3,X4) nonzero and det(I+X5) nonzero would falsify the obstruction; the Amitsur-Levitzki theorem rules out such a tuple over commutative fields.
ledger.next_gate: For any enlarged pathway with D>2 resolved states, supply a deterministic encoding of an actual N51 hitting tuple into valid rate generators, calibrated positive singular-value margins at every inverse node, a final readout margin, and a frozen held-out comparison with an equally informed direct schedule-search baseline.

ledger.exact_statement: For the displayed two-state pulse kernels PA=[[9/10,1/10],[1/5,4/5]] and PB=[[7/10,3/10],[2/5,3/5]], an initial OFF state has active endpoint probability 33/100 for A-then-B and 31/100 for B-then-A.
assumptions: Row-vector state distributions and sequential multiplication p -> p PA PB or p -> p PB PA.
The displayed kernels are calibrated exactly and endpoint state classification is error-free for the ideal sample-size calculation.
ledger.status: exact model derivation plus finite rational arithmetic diagnostic; biological realization untested
ledger.novelty_boundary: This is an illustrative parameterized model prediction, not an experimentally established sequence effect for any named receptor.
ledger.costs: Two reversed sequence arms; approximately 8,527 independent endpoint observations per arm under the ideal normal-approximation 80%-power calculation, before batch, state-preparation, ligand, and measurement costs.
ledger.falsifier: In a blinded randomized assay with validated washout and calibrated state readout, the reversed-order difference falls outside the preregistered CTMC prediction interval or reverses sign under repeated independent batches.
ledger.next_gate: Acquire one receptor system's pulse-response kinetics, fit alpha and beta from single-pulse data, freeze the two-sequence prediction, and test on held-out randomized AB and BA protocols.

ledger.exact_statement: For every five-tuple A_i in Q^{dxd}, let m=d+1, E=[e_1-e_m,...,e_d-e_m], F=[I_d 0]-(1/m)1_d1_m^T, J=1_m1_m^T/m, K=1+max_i{||A_i||_{entry-1},||EA_iF||_{entry-1}}, t=1/(64mK), and P_i=J+E((1/2)I_d+tA_i)F. Then P_i is a strictly positive doubly stochastic m-by-m matrix with every entry >31/(64m); S=[1_m E] gives S^{-1}P_iS=diag(1,(1/2)I_d+tA_i), and A_i=t^{-1}(FP_iE-(1/2)I_d). For Phi=s4(X_1,...,X_4)(I+X_5)^{-1}, every inverse gate remains defined and S^{-1}Phi(P)S=diag(0,t^4s4(A_1,...,A_4)((3/2)I_d+tA_5)^{-1}). Hence every source hit with invertible Phi(A) produces a nonzero direct stochastic-kernel output. These P_i are also time-one kernels of dense positive CTMC generators log(P_i).
assumptions: All A_i are finite rational square matrices of the same dimension d.
The target rational formula is the stated s4 formula with its only inverse node (I+X_5)^{-1}.
For the N51 consequence, the selected integer tuple is a hit with invertible Phi(A), as claimed by the source interface; source correctness remains externally unverified.
For the CTMC statement, controls can in principle realize independently programmed dense generators and the model remains homogeneous during a unit-duration pulse.
ledger.status: internally reconstructed exact construction; one finite fixture exact-checked; physical control conditional
ledger.novelty_boundary: The construction is a direct internal derivation and is not priority-cleared. Amitsur-Levitzki, the N51 candidate, and Markov embeddability are prior art. No molecule is shown to implement the controls, and the N51 source generator is not externally verified.
ledger.costs: Exact rational work uses polynomial bit complexity in d and total input bit length L; five dense kernels contain 5(d+1)^2 entries. A conditional pulse implementation has 5(d+1)d off-diagonal rate channels and full transition readout requires 5(d+1)^2 start/end probabilities; direct s4 sequence measurement uses up to 24(d+1)^2 conditions before replicates.
ledger.falsifier: An exact rational counterexample to any displayed identity, positivity bound, or inverse-domain statement would refute the construction. For physical transfer, failure to implement/calibrate the five dense generators and to resolve the frozen nonzero output margin on held-out data refutes the proposed assay bridge for that tuple.
ledger.next_gate: Independently execute or verify an actual nontrivial N51 list instance, publish the selected tuple and its exact P_i, then test whether a measured pathway can realize the dense controls and transition readout within the computed precision budget.

ledger.exact_statement: Let H=max_{i,a,b}|(A_i)_{ab}|. The construction has K<=1+4d^4H and t>=1/[64(d+1)(1+4d^4H)]. For an integer N51 hit with s4(A) invertible, the lower zero-sum block Y of Phi(P) satisfies ||Y||_2>t^4/(2sqrt(d)). Thus the construction yields O(L+log d) bits of guaranteed raw signal precision when H<=2^L, but can require inverse-square endpoint-sampling cost t^{-8}poly(d), exponential in L. N51's polynomial entry-bit bound supplies no inverse-polynomial-in-input-size experimental margin, selected moderate-height hit, control encoding, or measured condition number. This is a worst-case interface limitation, not a claim that every source tuple has tiny signal.
assumptions: The N51 tuple entries are integers for the stated s4 norm lower bound.
An endpoint assay estimates bounded-variance transition probabilities and reads the direct signed formula output, rather than having exact rational entries supplied digitally.
N51 provides polynomial entry bit lengths but no stronger height or robustness guarantee in its stated interface.
ledger.status: derived analytic scale bound; actual N51 list-member heights and physical assay performance remain unmeasured
ledger.novelty_boundary: The scale conclusion follows from the explicit embedding and the source's stated bit-cost interface. It does not refute the abstract hitting-list theorem or assert an actual wet-lab failure.
ledger.costs: With entry magnitude H, t is inverse polynomial in H and d. For H exponential in L, t can be exponentially small in L; direct output suppression is t^4 and endpoint sampling scales as the inverse square of target precision. Exact digital evaluation avoids measurement only when the tuple and coefficients are already acquired, in which case the assay contributes no new model information.
ledger.falsifier: A source-level guarantee that every relevant selected hit has polynomial numerical height and a polynomial singular-value/output margin, or a validated equal-budget physical assay attaining the frozen precision, would remove this practical-margin objection for that restricted family.
ledger.next_gate: Materialize a specific N51 hit for a named formula and report H, t, inverse-node condition numbers, propagated output margin, actuator/readout map, and measured endpoint sample count before making a physical-use claim.

ledger.exact_statement: The four displayed integer 3-by-3 matrices in CYCLE2.md have s4(A)= [[1,-2,1],[4,-2,2],[-3,6,1]] with determinant 24; setting A_5=0 and applying the embedding yields five strictly positive doubly stochastic 4-by-4 kernels with K=10, t=1/2560, minimum entry 637/5120, and Phi(P)_{1,1}=1/64424509440000. The exact script verifies the basis, stochasticity, positivity, decoding, and raw output identities.
assumptions: Python standard-library Fraction arithmetic executes as provided.
This tuple is a hand-found exact witness and is not claimed to be a member of the N51 list.
ledger.status: finite exact computation, independently reproducible; not a general proof or biological result
ledger.novelty_boundary: The standard polynomial witness and exact stochastic embedding are mathematical; the fixture is not linked to a generated N51 member or a realized pathway.
ledger.costs: The script is a small exact rational computation. Its raw output entry is approximately 7.76e-14, illustrating that a valid positive embedding can have a very small readout signal despite four states.
ledger.falsifier: A failed assertion or independently computed different exact value in the saved finite check falsifies this fixture record.
ledger.next_gate: Use the same checker to inspect a materialized N51 hit; then determine whether a real four-state system supports the five required pulse kernels at the preregistered endpoint precision.

claims.statement: For a fixed finite-volume thermal network with C=C^T positive definite, K=K^T positive semidefinite, and matched port profiles b_i used both for heat-power injection and temperature measurement, H_ij(s)=b_i^T(K+sC)^(-1)b_j is symmetric under source/receiver exchange for every real s>0; its causal impulse response is symmetric at every lag. The same statement holds for the weak Fourier operator with positive volumetric heat capacity, symmetric positive conductivity, and reciprocal fixed boundary terms.
assumptions: linear Fourier diffusion
time-invariant coefficients and geometry
positive heat-capacity operator
symmetric reciprocal conductance/conductivity operator
matched conjugate input/output port profiles
calibrated source and sensor gains
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact theorem; standard self-adjoint resolvent reciprocity, no novelty or nature-level claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Generic diffusion reciprocity and transient thermal rectification are established. This is a task-specific matched-port reconstruction and experimental protocol; priority is not claimed.
costs: matched, spatially calibrated heating and temperature-sensing ports
pulse energy and waveform calibration
heat-capacity/contact characterization
ambient and parasitic loss accounting
finite-volume resolution and conditioning for numerical reconstruction
claims.falsifier: With time-invariant linear reciprocal material behavior and matched calibrated ports, a reproducible H_ij(t) != H_ji(t) beyond error bars falsifies at least one premise or the operator model.
claims.next_gate: Obtain the full 2025 Su et al. article and experimental protocol; identify its exact input, output, boundary conditions, initialization energy, and rectification metric before comparing its claim to this theorem.

claims.statement: For point ports in a fixed reciprocal RC network, the temperature semigroup E(t)=exp(-C^(-1)Kt) satisfies c_i E_ij(t)=c_j E_ji(t); hence equal initial-temperature pulses have cross-response ratio E_ij/E_ji=c_j/c_i, independent of time and conductance. Equal-energy heat impulses instead have equal swapped-port temperature responses. The symmetric contrast for equal-initial-DeltaT pulses is exactly (c_j-c_i)/(c_j+c_i).
assumptions: point-lumped ports
C diagonal with strictly positive node heat capacities
K symmetric reciprocal conductance matrix
same initial temperature increment in each swapped trial
same measured receiver nodes
claims.status: internally proved and exactly replayed on a two-node fixture; generic weighted semigroup identity is standard; experimental interface untested
claims.novelty_boundary: This is not a new heat-transfer phenomenon. It is a sharp normalization prediction distinguishing same-temperature initial conditions from equal-energy source-port transfer.
costs: independent node or patch heat-capacity measurements
matched location/area temperature sensing
repeatable same-DeltaT and equal-energy protocols
finite sensor/contact and boundary-loss calibration
claims.falsifier: For the same-DeltaT initial protocol, a time-varying cross-response ratio or a ratio inconsistent with independently measured c_j/c_i rejects the stated fixed reciprocal RC model; for equal-energy pulses, a nonzero matched-port difference rejects at least one model/calibration premise.
claims.next_gate: Run the paired initial-DeltaT/equal-energy pulse test on a graded thermal coupon with independently measured volumetric heat capacity and matched port profiles.

claims.statement: For a hydraulic graph consisting exactly of m pairwise edge-disjoint parallel corridors with corridor conductances g_i and additive corridor occlusion costs c_i, the exact minimum damage cost that reduces total conductance below G_* is min{sum_{i in I} c_i : sum_{i in I} g_i > sum_i g_i - G_*}. For rational inputs an exact 0/1 dynamic program computes this threshold in O(mW) time and O(W) memory after denominator clearing, where W=floor(L_g*(sum_i g_i-G_*))+1; this is pseudo-polynomial and the general minimum-knapsack dependence is NP-hard.
assumptions: the graph is exactly a parallel union of edge-disjoint series corridors
deleting any edge destroys its entire corridor
surviving corridor conductances remain fixed under damage
corridor occlusion costs are additive conservative lower bounds
linear passive hydraulic conductance model
claims.status: internally proved exact restricted-model theorem and exact rational DP; generic min-knapsack/path reasoning is standard; no physical validation or priority claim
claims.novelty_boundary: This sharpens the sufficient one-surviving-route condition in the independent fracture child report to a sharp aggregate parallel-corridor budget, but it is a standard reduced-network optimization and not a new continuum fracture result.
costs: conductance and fracture/occlusion lower bounds must be acquired per corridor
exact DP may be exponential in rational input bit length
pore geometry, uncertainty and held-out damage dominate physical cost
claims.falsifier: In the stated edge-deletion model, a subset with lost conductance above the strict threshold and cost below the computed optimum, or an exhaustive subset enumeration disagreeing with the exact DP, falsifies the calculation. Physical disagreement after graph assumptions are verified rejects the model transfer.
claims.next_gate: Use this budget on a small measured parallel-corridor microfluidic coupon, with edge conductance and occlusion-cost lower bounds independently measured.

ledger.overall_status: A precise capability boundary and falsifiable test are established for the model interface. No new material capability, validated experimental law, or priority claim is established.

claims.statement: For a finite, non-explosive CTMC with common initial law and transition rates q_theta(x,y)=theta*a(x,y) on a designated edge set, while all other rates are theta-independent, the complete path LLR is K*log(theta1/theta0)-(theta1-theta0)*A; its KL divergence is d_Pois(theta1||theta0)*E_theta1[A].
assumptions: Finite state space and no explosion on finite horizons
0 < theta0, theta1 < infinity and common transition support
Known, time-homogeneous baseline edge rates a(x,y)
Common initial law independent of the hypothesis
Complete path observation for the sufficiency statement
claims.status: internally proved conditional theorem; standard likelihood structure
claims.novelty_boundary: The likelihood factorization and data-processing step are standard. No priority claim; contribution is the explicit activity-normalized form for this sensor interface.

costs.activity: A_T=integral_0^T a(X_t)dt; assume A_T<=a_max*T for the horizon bound
costs.sufficient_statistic: current state, exact signal-transition count K_T, and integrated activity A_T
costs.precision: quantizing A_T to LLR error delta requires activity resolution <=2*delta/abs(theta1-theta0); K_T is unbounded absent a tail truncation
costs.acquisition: rate calibration and event/state sensing are not supplied by the theorem

claims.falsifier: A valid model within the stated assumptions whose complete-path LLR or relative entropy differs from the displayed formulas.
claims.next_gate: Extend the activity bound to hidden and controlled CTMC observations with charged policy and state information.

claims.statement: For a serial m-stage CTMC with hypothesis-independent forward rates k_i>0 and reset hazards mu0>mu1>0, endpoint success probabilities p_h=product_i k_i/(k_i+mu_h) satisfy p0>=p1^(mu0/mu1). At fixed m and p1, equal per-stage H1 success probabilities minimize p0; the finite-m optimum decreases to the power-law floor as m tends to infinity.
assumptions: One initial state, m serial forward transitions, and one absorbing reset outcome
At stage i the only outgoing transitions are forward at k_i and reset at mu_h
Forward rates do not depend on h; the reset hazard is the same at every stage within each hypothesis
Only terminal success/failure is used for the reported p_h
claims.status: internally proved conditional theorem; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Related multistage accuracy/speed/dissipation and first-passage/count analyses are established. This is a specific terminal-probability theorem at matched sensitivity; priority remains unverified.

costs.state_count: m+2 including reset and response terminals
costs.not_fixed: energy and rate calibration; at the equalized optimizer stage-event count and forward rate grow linearly in m

claims.falsifier: Within the stated CTMC interface, any rates and stage count yielding p0<p1^(mu0/mu1).
claims.next_gate: Generalize to multiple reset paths and determine sharp activity-constrained bounds.

claims.statement: If all signal-dependent CTMC rates depend on unknown gain gamma and input intensity u only through theta=gamma*u, then any rescaled pair (c*gamma,u/c) induces the same generator and path law; gamma and u are not separately identifiable from any trajectory statistic.
assumptions: Every transition rate is invariant under gamma*u-preserving rescaling
No independently calibrated gain or input measurement is supplied
claims.novelty_boundary: A basic structural identifiability gauge; no novelty claim.

costs.required_additional_information: independent gain/input calibration or a second transition channel with distinct parameter dependence

claims.falsifier: An observation law under the stated parameterization that changes when gamma*u is held fixed.
claims.next_gate: Quantify the minimum independent calibration needed when auxiliary channels are noisy.

claims.statement: For a known k-mode pure-death hidden CTMC with distinct positive decay rates and nonzero occupancy-times-effect amplitudes, 2k equally spaced exact terminal discrimination means identify unordered rate/amplitude pairs, but terminal delay data identify occupancy and per-mode effect only through their product.
assumptions: Known k and one absorbing baseline mode
Distinct positive decay rates and nonzero mode amplitudes
Terminal Bernoulli readouts at known delays; no hidden path observation
Reset baseline supplied or separately measured
claims.status: internally reconstructed conditional theorem; classical Prony component
claims.novelty_boundary: Prony reconstruction and hidden-Markov identifiability are established. This exact occupancy/effect confounding is scoped to the terminal-probability observation map; no novelty claim.

costs.delay_points: 2k exact scalar means, span (2k-1)*h, plus reset baseline
costs.computation: O(k^3) arithmetic and O(k^2) storage; noise stability depends on mode separation and amplitudes
costs.extra_observable: labeled occupancy or calibrated p_r is required to separate occupancy from effect

claims.falsifier: A terminal-delay-only estimator that uniquely recovers occupancy and state-specific effect on an open parameter set under the stated model.
claims.next_gate: General transient subgenerator; characterize similarity-class ambiguity and noisy observability.

claims.statement: For the N+1-state chain with forward rate theta from i to i+1 for i<N and reset rate rho from i>0 to 0, the stationary full-path KL rate is [1-(theta1/(theta1+rho))^N]*d_Pois(theta1||theta0); N raises active exposure with geometric diminishing returns. A detector using only X_T after one long run has positive limiting error because the stationary endpoint distributions have full support.
assumptions: N >= 1 and theta0, theta1, rho > 0
Forward events are the only theta-sensitive transitions
Reset rate is hypothesis-independent
Complete timed path for the KL-rate claim; only terminal state X_T for the endpoint-only counterexample
claims.status: internally proved exact model special case and counterexample; no nature or novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Stationary distribution and path-space KL specialization are elementary consequences of CTMC theory. The endpoint statement is limited to one terminal observation and does not rule out temporal accumulation.

costs.full_path: expected event count at most (theta1+rho)*T in the reset example; timestamps and labels cost extra precision/storage

claims.falsifier: An algebraic contradiction to the displayed stationary distribution or entropy rate under the stated generator.
claims.next_gate: Compare terminal and partial-time path readouts under explicit sampling intervals and event-record budgets.

claims.statement: For N iid Bernoulli event marks with common hypothesis-independent exponential event times, the all-pass terminal bit is a deterministic coarsening of the full mark path and has KL at most N*d_Ber(p0||p1), strictly less for N>=2 and p0!=p1. A finite stage-count CTMC with N(N+1)/2+2 states realizes the Neyman-Pearson threshold decision from N marks using one terminal bit at the same N jumps and mean time.
assumptions: Two known simple hypotheses; 0<p0,p1<1 and p0!=p1
Independent Bernoulli marks with the same p_h at every slot
Common hypothesis-independent Exp(lambda) event times
Fixed N and a terminal binary decision
claims.status: internally proved conditional comparison using data processing and Neyman-Pearson; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: The information ordering and threshold optimality are classical; the report reconstructs their exact finite-stage CTMC costs and matched readout interface. No priority claim.

costs.all_pass: 2N+1 reachable states; N jumps; mean elapsed time N/lambda; one terminal readout
costs.likelihood_counter: N(N+1)/2+2 reachable states; N jumps; mean elapsed time N/lambda; one terminal readout
costs.raw_marks: N external mark observations and N+1 count values; KL ceiling N*d_Ber(p0||p1)

claims.falsifier: A violation of data processing or of the Neyman-Pearson threshold result within the stated iid Bernoulli model.
claims.next_gate: Characterize the state-cardinality versus observation-cost frontier for explicitly specified finite-state transducers.

claims.statement: For two finite-state CTMCs with common transition support, the full-path KL is the initial-law KL plus the integral of occupancy-weighted row divergences. Every common readout channel has no larger KL, and equal-prior binary error is at least exp(-D_T)/4. Hidden strong lumping and one-lag generator aliasing give exact observational-equivalence counterexamples.
assumptions: Finite non-explosive CTMCs on a common finite state space
Common edge support and initial absolute continuity
A common hypothesis-independent readout channel
The endpoint error bound is for equal priors
claims.status: internally proved conditional general CTMC formula and elementary counterexamples; established mechanisms; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: The path likelihood, data-processing, and finite-state identifiability principles are established. Contributions are scoped formulas and exact counterexamples for explicit observation interfaces; external proof review and priority audit remain open.

costs.information: rate caps and common support are required for a finite rate ceiling
costs.records: continuous jump timestamps require explicit finite precision; sampled/hidden records lose information
costs.state_count: state count alone does not upper-bound path KL without rate restrictions
costs.calibration: generator, initial-law, and observation-channel calibration are outside the theorem

claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the rowwise path-KL identity, readout data-processing bound, or stated exact observational equivalences under the listed assumptions.

Initial occupancy of mode r is p_r
At a fixed delay, test input u emits a Bernoulli output with state-specific probability theta_{u,r}

claims.exact_statement: For two simple hypotheses with iid Bernoulli(p_h) event marks over N fixed slots, the full N-mark path has KL N*D(Ber(p0)||Ber(p1)). Any terminal readout Y that is a function or randomized post-processing of that path has no larger KL and no lower optimal decision risk. In the all-pass design, P_h(Y=1)=p_h^N and, for N>=2 and p0!=p1, D(Ber(p0^N)||Ber(p1^N)) is strictly smaller than the KL of the physical state path and of the full mark record.
assumptions: H in {0,1} is simple and p_h is known with 0<p_h<1 and p0!=p1
The N event marks are conditionally iid Bernoulli(p_h)
Event holding times are independent Exp(lambda) with the same lambda>0 under both hypotheses
The endpoint is a deterministic function of the path; the all-pass CTMC retains only the stage and sticky pass/fail flag
claims.status: conditional theorem proved in proof.md; derives from established KL chain rule, data processing, and Blackwell comparison; no new general information theorem claimed
claims.novelty_boundary: The model-specific stage formulas are reconstructed; data processing and Blackwell dominance are prior art.

claims.exact_statement: For N iid Bernoulli event marks under known simple hypotheses p0<p1, a likelihood-ratio threshold on the pass count K, with boundary randomization if needed, maximizes power among binary tests at any prescribed false-positive level. claims.statement: For a finite rooted tree with q=4 symmetric Potts edge channels and selected independent q-symmetric sensors represented as attached noisy edges ending in perfectly observed terminals, the max-ray weighted-flow capacity is exactly computed by S_v = sum_child Phi_lambda(S_w) + sum_local_sensor g(rho), where Phi_lambda(S)=lambda^2*S/sqrt(1+(1-lambda^4)*S^2) and g(rho)=rho^2/sqrt(1-rho^4), with stated zero/one endpoint conventions.

known edge and sensor parameters in [0,1]
nonnegative conserved flow allowed to terminate at sensor terminals
max over root-to-sensor path energy

ledger.title: Spatial state alias in a published adaptive-treatment assay
ledger.overall_status: finite_reconstruction; novelty_not_established; no_policy_test; no_cancer_transfer

claims.statement: Appold et al. report spatially tracked resistant-mutant confinement and escape under time-modulated treatment in a yeast assay, with resource-mediated spatial dynamics and a treatment-schedule boundary; tumor and biofilm transfer is described as a hypothesis.
claims.limitations: The reductionist yeast system does not validate the mechanism or a steering rule in cancer or biofilms.

claims.statement: At frame 145 (72.5 h), P2 and P3 have colony areas of 308770 and 322430 px2 and two-hour log-area rates of 0.002909 and 0.002623 per hour, while nearest tracked clone-front clearances are 76.3 and 549.0 um. Under the final article eligibility and escape rules, P2 has one later escape (clone 15, first breach at frame 150) and P3 has no eligible breach through frame 251.
claims.limitations: Post-hoc two-colony comparison; it does not estimate predictive accuracy, causal effects, or policy value. P3's zero events applies only to source-eligible tracks through the supplied horizon.

claims.statement: In the adaptive cohort, P2 clone 15 and P8 clone 18 reach the same measured breach distance (2.59 um) at different times relative to the preceding and next pulses. P2 contacts 4.5 h after the previous pulse ends and remains within 80 um through 125.5 h; P8 contacts 23 h after the previous pulse ends, one hour before the next pulse, and retreats beyond 80 um 7.5 h after contact. This supports a candidate hypothesis that post-contact fate depends on front-growth state and dosing latency.
claims.limitations: Only two post-frame-145 contact events are compared; P2/P8 differences may reflect clone or local-neighborhood state. The source article already studies reconfinement and treatment timing. No predictive or causal effect, novelty, or policy benefit is established.

claims.statement: Generic spatial competition, adaptive therapy, clone confinement, growth rebound as a confinement proxy, and schedule steering are prior art; no priority claim is made for those ideas.
claims.limitations: This bounded check does not prove global novelty or exhaust the cancer-evolution literature.

claims.statement: The Barber/Couce Figure 2B supplementary workbook has some ML ΔmutH percentages that reduce to 20/21 and 18/21 (or integer multiples), not integer multiples of 1/48, while Methods report 48 parallel populations outside regime L.
claims.limitations: Effective denominators or attrition are not resolved; this is not a data-error claim and is not evidence for the spatial finding.

claims.statement: No new mechanism, theorem, prospective diagnostic, treatment policy, cancer validation, or clinical recommendation is established by this work.
claims.limitations: A prospective held-out assay could change the status of the clearance-feature hypothesis.

claims.statement: A prospective assay can test whether local sensitive-front growth, clone clearance, and pulse-relative contact latency improve prediction of breach and retreat beyond the existing bulk-rebound state and full treatment history, then randomize pulse-restart latency at matched total exposure to test causality.
claims.limitations: Unperformed; action mapping, sample size, segmentation error, and attainable prediction gain remain unknown.

rejected_routes.route: Generic claim that spatial population structure changes resistance evolution or adaptive-therapy response
Generic growth-rebound feedback as a proxy for resistant-clone confinement
Generic same-primary-resistance phenotype paths imply different collateral responses
Cancer or patient policy inferred from the yeast assay

restart_gates: Independently replicate under the source assay and prospectively preregister the escape horizon and feature set.
Hold out independently executed plate/chamber runs; compare the bulk-rebound baseline with the same-history model plus clone clearance, clearance velocity, and local sensitive-front growth.
Charge imaging, fluorescence, segmentation, latency, missed observations, and prior-treatment history equally across feature-ablation baselines.
Only after predictive gain, test a preregistered geometry-informed policy against rebound feedback at matched cumulative treatment and population control.
If events or image quality are insufficient, preserve UNKNOWN; do not claim clinical or cross-system generality.

Also mu_{k,j}/d_k is the uniform average over |A|=k of (-1)^(k j-|A intersect J|) for fixed |J|=j, so L's diagonal is twice the probability that this sign is -1.

claims.exact_statement: At n=7, the original eight Jordan-Wigner attained seed vectors do not satisfy the candidate r=0 star upper inequality on all rays of their support cones: exact checks give three failures among 40 rays and 10200 principal minors. On alpha=e5+e6, the seed support is 62, the trace term is 8008, and the exact 8x8 gap determinant is negative.
assumptions: The all-n r=0 recoupling formula and exact Krawtchouk diagonals in r0_seed_cone_probe.py are correct.
The finite support is exactly the maximum over the eight listed attained psi_h seeds, not full canonical support.
claims.novelty_boundary: Refutes only the eight-seed sufficient comparator at these rays. This is not a legal channel, global canonical-support counterexample, or refutation of the factor-two claim.
claims.costs: Exact symbolic 8x8 matrices and exact cone-ray enumeration; 10200 principal minors.
claims.falsifier: An error in the exact r=0 recoupling formula, the seed moment formula, or the recorded negative determinant.
claims.next_gate: Use the full support h_7(alpha) or an attained state strong enough to compare against a rigorous star upper bound.

claims.exact_statement: For n=7 and alpha=e5+e6, all 255 exact principal minors of (80711/10)I-H_{alpha,0} are nonnegative. An explicitly recorded normalized rational Spin(15) pure spinor has s5+s6=6290353328/99460729>63/10. Since the trace term is 8008, lambda_max(H_{alpha,0})-8008<=63/10<s5+s6<=h_7(alpha), so the full-support star inequality holds for this one ray and block.
assumptions: The r=0 recoupling matrix in r0_seed_cone_probe.py represents the exact star block in the declared orthonormal basis.
The rational amplitude coordinates and exact Clifford-word moment replay in spin15_rational_seed.py are correct.
claims.novelty_boundary: Rescues one direction in one block and diagnoses one false finite-seed obstruction; no n-uniform, all-r, channel, or novelty claim.
claims.costs: 128 complex amplitudes with integer numerators, exact Clifford-word moment sums, and 255 exact principal minors of an 8x8 matrix.
claims.falsifier: A changed Clifford phase convention that invalidates the moment replay, a negative exact principal minor, or reversal of the exact rational support comparison.
claims.next_gate: Find exact attained support witnesses or an analytic h_7 lower bound for the two remaining augmented-seed rays; then prove the continuous-support r=0 inequality uniformly in n.

claims.exact_statement: After adding the rational pure spinor in C12-SPIN15-E5E6-R0-RAY-RESCUED to the original eight seeds, the exact n=7 r=0 support-cone test has 48 distinct rays and two remaining failures, with 12240 principal-minor checks.
assumptions: The state certificate and exact finite cone enumeration are correct.
The nine-vector support is only an attained-seed lower bound on h_7.
claims.novelty_boundary: The two failures are not canonical-support violations. An unpreserved random numerical search is explicitly not counted as evidence.
claims.costs: Exact 8x8 r=0 block checks across 48 rays; 12240 principal minors.
claims.falsifier: An error in the exact cone enumeration, state moments, or star block.
claims.next_gate: Do not treat this finite family as full support; obtain an exact state or analytic support control for these rays.

claims.exact_statement: The all-n claim that every Spin(2n+1)-covariant unital, trace-preserving, Hilbert-Schmidt-self-adjoint self-compatible spinor channel, allowing negative grade transfers, admits one full-domain canonical EB map Psi with Psi >= 2Phi-id remains unknown in this branch.
assumptions: The full ordinary-tensor star and canonical-support separation criterion from the inherited cycle 11 report are the target interface.
A finite seed support lower bound is not substituted for full canonical support.
No positive Hilbert-Schmidt-spectrum restriction is imposed on the transfer vector.
claims.novelty_boundary: The listed quantum weight-enumerator papers are related transform machinery only; no direct preemption, exact novelty clearance, external review, proof-assistant verification, or validation in nature is claimed.
claims.costs: No legal global counterexample or all-n proof was produced. Exact orbit-POVM discretization/readout cost remains uncharged.
claims.falsifier: A correct all-n proof of the positive-dual support criterion or a legal broadcaster plus complete global canonical-support upper bound strictly below its target.
claims.next_gate: Prove the r>=1 recoupling gap uniformly and independently resolve the r=0 continuous-support inequality; a proof of only one gate is incomplete.

ledger.topic: assay and prior-art boundary for physical DNA lesion partition versus post-division repair in 2C-like ESCs

claims.claim: Under D1(t)=p D* exp(-k1 t), D2(t)=(1-p) D* exp(-k2 t), and a positive shared multiplicative physical-assay gain, the log sister ratio is log(P1/P2)=logit(p)+(k2-k1)t; two distinct times identify partition log-odds and differential repair.
assumptions: The damage class is fixed and the immediate post-division pair burden is p:(1-p).
Repair is first-order with constant sister-specific rates during the short observation window.
The physical assay has positive signals, common gain within a pair, and calibrated/subtracted common additive background.
No new sister-specific damage is generated during the fitted window.
The two observations retain the identity of both daughters.
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary algebra, not a novel theorem. The 2026 ESC study already tracks paired live 53BP1 and endpoint sister-pair gamma-H2AX; Ferrand et al. already measure physical CPD segregation and early repair in paired daughters. This formula is only a model/design check.
claims.costs: A direct, named physical lesion measure at/near cytokinesis; if destructive, indexed sacrificial cohorts and cohort-level assumptions; pair/fate tracking, timing, background, cell-cycle, and attrition measurement.
claims.falsifier: Any admitted trajectory violating the log-linear sister-ratio law under the stated model, or a calibrated test showing no early physical asymmetry despite a resolvable model prediction, refutes the corresponding model claim.
claims.next_gate: A calibrated lesion-specific physical measurement at division in spontaneous 2C-like ESC daughters linked to both daughter fates; until then the biological proposition remains UNKNOWN.

claims.claim: At a single delayed time, partition p and differential repair are non-identifiable; a focus channel additionally cannot identify physical partition if daughter-specific focus loading is unknown.
assumptions: The first observation occurs at t>0 with no independently known differential repair rate.
For the focus confound, no independent physical assay or calibrated sister-specific focus efficiency is available.
claims.novelty_boundary: Exact model-specific non-identifiability, not a discovery about the published ESC system. Existing primary studies already show reporter dynamics and physical lesion asymmetry in distinct contexts.
claims.costs: One independent physical lesion channel, timing resolution, focus/background calibration, and complete lineage tracking.
claims.falsifier: A validated assay relation or independently measured repair-rate bound that uniquely recovers p would defeat the stated ambiguity.
claims.next_gate: Show that the direct physical assay is sister-resolved and calibratable at the required time resolution.

claims.claim: For independent pair asymmetry scores in [-1,1] from two arms, a Hoeffding sign test for a mean difference of at least Delta has error at most 2 exp(-n Delta^2/4); alpha=.05 and Delta=.20 require 369 informative pairs per arm.
assumptions: Informative mother divisions are independent within/across arms.
Each pair-level score lies in [-1,1].
The target arm contrast is at least the stated Delta.
claims.proof_path: Hoeffding's inequality, with the independent arm means subtracted.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard conservative sampling bound only; not a power estimate, empirical effect, or scientific advance.
claims.costs: At an assumed useful-pair yield q_div=.006, about 61,500 random divisions screened per arm in expectation; q_div is unknown and cannot be inferred from instantaneous 2C-like prevalence.
claims.falsifier: Clustering, informative tracking loss, unbounded score values, or an underestimated event-yield denominator invalidate the displayed design bound.
claims.next_gate: Estimate event yield, culture-level variance, tracking failure, and assay cost in a pilot before fixing biological sample size.

claims.claim: GSE289323 contains processed MERVL-GFP-positive and GFP-negative transcriptomic samples but no sister-pair/time-lapse damage trajectories needed to estimate the paired damage decomposition.
assumptions: The publicly indexed GEO record and its listed sample barcode files are the relevant public release.
claims.finite_check_path: GEO family SOFT metadata inspected via the public NCBI FTP record; barcode list counts inspected without downloading the large count matrices.
claims.novelty_boundary: A data-scope claim only; not a reanalysis of expression counts and not evidence for/against asymmetric damage inheritance.
claims.costs: No count matrix or focal time-lapse movie was downloaded; GEO metadata and barcode/feature files were inspected.
claims.falsifier: A public release containing sister labels and paired damage trajectories would change this limitation.
claims.next_gate: Obtain sister-resolved movies/source measurements from the focal study or generate a calibrated physical-lesion dataset.

claims.claim: The public Panagopoulos et al. source-data workbook contains an aggregated 3-category sister 53BP1 heterogeneity table: untreated 1/9/22 versus 4-Gy 7/28/19 (n=32 and 54). Pearson chi-square against a shared category law gives chi2(2,N=86)=9.468, p=0.008791, Cramers V=0.332.
assumptions: The workbook ED8i high/medium/low counts are interpreted as the stated 3x2 contingency table.
The Pearson test treats the listed sister pairs as independent; replicate labels are not present in the released sheet.
claims.novelty_boundary: Reproduces the published categorical contrast. It cannot estimate a paired log-ratio trajectory, partition intercept, repair slope, or rejuvenation mechanism.
claims.costs: Workbook is 957 KiB; raw imaging data are available on request according to the paper. No FASTQ or image movie was downloaded.
claims.falsifier: A misread count table or a test statistic failing to reproduce would falsify the numerical reproduction.
claims.next_gate: No further public-data claim; require raw sister-resolved image trajectories and loss records for mechanistic analysis.

prior_art_and_status.external_primary_system: Wang et al., Cell Research 2026, DOI 10.1038/s41422-026-01221-z. Figure 3 and Supplementary Fig. S3 inspected: live paired-sister 53BP1-Tudor reporter asymmetry, endpoint gamma-H2AX staining of tracked sister pairs, damage/fate association, and DDR perturbations. Comet assay is group-level/destructive.
measurement_prior_art: Ferrand et al. 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-56090-8: direct CPD measurement on sister chromatids and early-G1 daughter pairs; early repair negligible.
Lezaja et al. 2021, DOI 10.1038/s41467-021-23806-5: postmitotic RPA and 53BP1 mark distinct lesions and have different dynamics.
Panagopoulos et al. 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-08986-0: multigenerational PCNA/53BP1 tracking and sister heterogeneity; public data lack continuous trajectories.
prior_art_and_status.scientific_status: No new biological mechanism or novel theorem established. The broad ESC damage-asymmetry phenomenon is preempted; the partition-versus-repair ratio is an elementary conditional identity. Only direct lesion-class-specific physical burden at division in spontaneous 2C-like ESC pairs linked to both fates remains an unvalidated empirical question.
prior_art_and_status.next_observation_that_could_change_statu: A direct, calibrated physical lesion measure at/near cytokinesis in spontaneous 2C-like ESC daughter pairs, with complete sister identity, fate, cell-cycle, and attrition records.

ledger.statement: For a specified pair of K-state CTMC probe kernels with permutation-orbit gap gamma>0, unknown shared full-rank KxK categorical emission matrix E, supplied or certified pi_i>=p_*>0, conditionally iid reads during pure blocks, and a paid positive slow action with calibrated hold-plus-ramp no-change bounds, a finite-horizon confidence-spent doubling test (returning UNKNOWN on failed certification) has error at most alpha and uses O(K/(p_* gamma^2) kappa^-2 polylog) reads over O(K/(p_* gamma^2) log(K/alpha)) founders for covered kappa. This assumes the action/emission interface and does not validate a physical implementation.
ledger.novelty_boundary: Concentration, HMM identifiability and likelihood testing are established prior art. The fixed-pair construction is conditional on a paid near-freeze primitive with ramps budgeted; novelty/priority UNKNOWN. The kappa^-4 lower bound is only for the stated independent two-read pair law, not passive multi-time likelihoods. An optimal likelihood on the same active data is at least as informed; no strict advantage is shown.
ledger.costs: Fixed design uses m=O(K gamma^-2 log(K/alpha)) transitions per row; Nc=O(p_*^-1 log(K/alpha)) calibration founders; Nt=O((m+log(K/alpha))/p_*) probe founders; B=Nc+2Nt blocks; R_J=O(kappa^-2 log(BJ/alpha)) repeated reads/block. Charge R_j Delta and ramps per block, nominal probe, readout, calibration, founders, culture, exposure, viability/recovery and actuator. Must have q_ramp<alpha/(4B) and positive rho above hardware floor. Conservative witness at kappa=0.1 uses about 3.09e11 frames and assumes q_ramp=0; no physical advantage follows.
ledger.falsifier: Emission drift, non-independent/path-integrated reads, unbounded jump/ramp disturbance, zero or uncertified state occupancy, hardware slowdown floor, or gamma=0 invalidates the theorem's applicability.
ledger.next_gate: Find a named system with stable repeated emissions, independent native founders or a proved dependence substitute, and a finite protocol-wide one-sided transition bound including ramps at a positive hardware-feasible setting. Then compare active and passive likelihoods at matched walltime and detected-photon dose with all calibration/action costs.

ledger.statement: For the explicit three-state stationary cycle pair and E_kappa=kappa I+(1-kappa)11^T/3, the fixed passive two-read pair law has KL O(kappa^4), so fixed-error tests require Omega(kappa^-4) independent pairs even with known nuisance parameters.
ledger.novelty_boundary: Existing fixed pair-law baseline; not a universal lower bound for all passive trajectories or controls.
ledger.costs: Two reads per independent founder; Omega(kappa^-4) pairs for fixed error in this stated family.
ledger.falsifier: Failure of the exact J0-J1 identity or the small-kappa KL expansion for the stated family.

ledger.statement: For the specified two-world three-daughter CLE alias under direct semantic family labels, B-only fixed sampling is minimax among adaptive allocation policies; nine B founders are the smallest fixed n with minimax error at most 0.05, and every sequential policy with maximum error delta needs expected B count at least kl(1-delta,delta)/(0.5 log 3) in each world.

Sources do not provide a ramp-inclusive one-sided transition bound, invariant emissions across controls, independent-founder interface for this theorem, or equal-resource likelihood comparison. Applicability remains UNKNOWN.

claims.statement: For K states, known reporter W_kappa=kappa I+(1-kappa)U, uniform stationary start, and all legal candidate transition matrices doubly stochastic with Dobrushin coefficient <=r with 0<r<1; if r=0 the transcript laws are identical uniformly in kappa, any shared history-adaptive randomized action policy has full-transcript KL at most 8 K^3 n kappa^4 (r/(1-r))^2. Uniform stationary law is preserved by every action in both worlds
Reporter W_kappa is known to the tester and 0<kappa<=1/2
Every action kernel has a Dobrushin coefficient bounded by one fixed r<1 independent of kappa
No cadence-dependent wall-time or photon-price improvement is assumed

ledger.statement: For a specified pair of K-state CTMC probe matrices with permutation-orbit Frobenius gap gamma>0, unknown shared full-rank KxK column-stochastic emission matrix E with sigma_min(E)=kappa>0, fixed positive read duration Delta and conditionally independent outputs, and independent native founders with pi_i>=p_*>0, a calibrated positive-rate slow-read action can yield a finite-sample nearest-orbit test with error at most alpha using O(K/(p_* gamma^2) * kappa^-2 * polylog(K/(alpha p_* gamma))) reporter frames. All slow-block state-change probabilities, including ramps, must be union-bounded over the declared finite protocol, and the model order/candidate kernels are supplied.

ledger.falsifier: An algebraic or numerical counterexample to the exact pair-law difference or KL asymptotic for the stated family.
ledger.next_gate: Compare with any proposed legal action under an explicitly matched sensor/action budget; do not elevate to a universal passive lower bound.

ledger.statement: Selected reversible cryo-arrest protocols support repeated imaging in particular living-cell molecular assays, but do not establish a uniform scalar slowdown Q->rho Q for arbitrary cell-fate labels or stable emission matrix E.
ledger.novelty_boundary: Physical feasibility is established only for protocol-specific imaging targets; the theorem-to-biology bridge is not claimed.

claims.statement: For a fixed pair of supplied K-state probe kernels with permutation-orbit Frobenius gap Gamma>0, an unknown shared full-rank categorical reporter E, start occupancy floor p_*, and a uniform history- and start-state-conditional per-block disturbance envelope q_phys<=p_* min(1,Gamma)/768, the pre-read cohort can be used to certify unknown emission clusters and estimate the probe transition matrix up to permutation with error below Gamma/2 using O(kappa^-2) repeated-read frames up to fixed-pair factors and logarithms.
assumptions: Known K and supplied candidate kernels
Unknown common E with sigma_min(E)=kappa>0
Every initial-state mass is at least supplied or certified p_*>0
Same-state emissions are iid categorical and invariant across all blocks/actions
Every slow block has uniform conditional jump risk q_phys, including ramps and read backaction
Independent native founder episodes
Finite maximum frame cap; abstain if observable cluster certificate fails
claims.novelty: UNKNOWN; component tools are prior art and the composition has not been externally reviewed
claims.costs: For K=3, p_*=1/3, Gamma=.20900495, alpha=.05, kappa=.1, Delta=.01 s: N_t=294411, 588822 blocks, 308712308736 frames, 97.825 years held-read time excluding ramps and all setup/control/recovery costs; q_phys<=9.0714e-5, scalar rho<=1.7303e-9 if q_ramp=0 and Lambda=10/s.

claims.statement: For a known reporter W_kappa=kappa I+(1-kappa)U, uniform stationary initial law, and any adaptive policy over doubly stochastic candidate transition kernels with Dobrushin coefficient at most fixed r<1, full-transcript KL is at most 8 K^3 n kappa^4 (r/(1-r))^2, forcing Omega(kappa^-4) observations for fixed-error testing.
assumptions: Known K, emission W_kappa, candidate kernels, and uniform initial law
Common uniform stationary distribution
All legal action kernels are doubly stochastic and have coefficient bounded by r<1 independent of kappa
The same randomized history-dependent control policy is used in both worlds
Positive emissions with per-symbol lower bound from kappa<=1/2

claims.falsifier: Within the declared class, exhibit an action policy with fixed r<1 and a full-likelihood error guarantee using o(kappa^-4) outputs; a cadence with r approaching 1 is outside the claim.

ledger.exact_statement: For supplied finite-dimensional unital, trace-preserving, CPTP, Hilbert-Schmidt-selfadjoint, Hilbert-Schmidt-positive self-compatible Phi, any Hermitian contractions A,B satisfy ||[A,B]||_{2,tau} <= 10 (e_Phi(A)+e_Phi(B))^(1/4), where e_Phi(A)=<A,(I-Phi)A>_tau.
assumptions: Phi exact and finite dimensional
symmetric two-output broadcaster supplied
tau=Tr/d
A,B Hermitian operator-norm contractions
ledger.status: internally derived conditional lemma; not externally reviewed
ledger.novelty_boundary: Uses the pre-existing internal broadcast-tree commutator estimate and elementary positive-spectrum functional calculus; does not produce a common measurement or EB approximation.
ledger.costs: No dimension factor in the modulus. Uses exact powers of supplied Phi and tree lemma; no algorithmic implementation or precision bound claimed.
ledger.falsifier: Find a channel within the exact interface and Hermitian contractions violating the displayed bound, or invalidate the cited tree commutator lemma.
ledger.next_gate: Convert pointwise low-energy pairwise commutation into one common POVM with weighted joint variance controlled by mean Dirichlet energy, uniformly over all finite frames and dimensions.

ledger.exact_statement: For n-qubit observables {X_i,Z_i}_{i=1}^n with uniform weights, mean squared normalized-HS pairwise commutator is 2/n, while every common rank-one POVM has average pure-state variance at least 1/2.
assumptions: d=2^n
uniform prior on 2n Pauli observables
measurement ensemble barycenter I/d

ledger.next_gate: Retain the channel-energy profile in the dual frame; do not replace it by only mean pairwise commutator data.

assumptions: X,Y Hermitian matrices
u uniform in [0,h)

ledger.next_gate: Find a dimension-free refinement/iteration that yields a masa or POVM while controlling the full weighted frame loss.

assumptions: finite-dimensional matrix algebra
T unital CPTP in Heisenberg picture
one masa D controls the full operator unit ball

ledger.costs: Dimension-free norm conversion via normalized Schatten monotonicity. Minimal-projection outcome count d if D is a masa; no efficient construction claimed.

ledger.next_gate: Prove the full-ball range approximation under the relevant low-mode/channel assumptions, or establish the weaker all-frame joint-variance gate needed by N93.

ledger.exact_statement: For all finite weighted low-energy frames from admissible self-compatible channels, q((A_i,p_i)) <= omega(sum_i p_i e_Phi(A_i)) for one common POVM, with dimension- and frame-size-independent omega(t)->0 as t->0.
assumptions: exact supplied channel and broadcaster
all finite frame sizes and all dimensions
no minimum positive spectral gap
common POVM chosen for the whole frame
ledger.status: UNKNOWN; no proof and no qualifying counterexample found
ledger.novelty_boundary: Fixed-tuple normalized-HS almost-commuting results have tuple-size-dependent bounds; ultraproduct commutativity/lifting for preselected separable families does not supply a coordinate POVM uniform over an entire growing operator unit ball.

assumptions: G is explicit, simple, finite, undirected, and supplied as adjacency lists.
The target-degree array is supplied and satisfies the source's one-word and local-range conditions.
The source theorem and matching subroutine are correct as stated; this worker did not independently verify their proof.

The one-word f array, O(n+m log(n+2)) reduction, O(m log(n+2))-size matching instance, matching computation, witness checks, decoding, random bits, and output are within the source's word-RAM accounting.

Under the family-120 source guarantee, no-factor inputs always receive NO, while feasible inputs receive a valid witness with probability at least 2/3; thus NO on a feasible input is possible and is not an infeasibility certificate.
assumptions: One permitted contact per unordered site pair; no edge multiplicity or edge weight is required.
All chemical legality constraints relevant to the modeled decision are fully represented by this simple graph and exact degree targets, or have a separately proved encoding.
The family-120 theorem is true as source-reported.

ledger.task: Prime-dimensional Weyl self-compatibility versus factor-two entanglement-breaking domination

claims.statement: For prime d, the factor-two mode inequalities are feasible within the convex hull of the d+1 maximal-abelian line-dephasing channels and the depolarizing channel if and only if B(lambda)=sum_L max_{x in L\{0}} (2 lambda_x-1)_+ is at most 1.
claims.quantifiers: Any real Weyl-diagonal spectrum; necessary and sufficient only for this specified mixture ansatz.
claims.proof: Each nonzero phase-space mode lies on one unique projective line. A mixture has eigenvalue w_L on that line, so all inequalities hold iff w_L is at least the maximum clipped target on L and the sum of required weights is at most one.
claims.boundary: B>1 rules out the line-dephasing mixture only; it is not a separability or general EB obstruction.

claims.statement: There is an exact d=5 unital CPTP, Hilbert-Schmidt-self-adjoint Weyl-covariant channel with a two-output CPTP extension and line-cover budget B=(6294997/6303442)+(476808 sqrt(5)/3151721)>1.
claims.quantifiers: One fixed channel in dimension five; all its Weyl modes are specified by four exact Q(sqrt(5)) classes in FINAL_REPORT.md.
claims.proof_core: The class vector f is fixed by the normalized symplectic Fourier transform. The kernel X=f f^T/N is PSD, has diagonal q=f^2/N, and its compatibility transform is q again. Haapasalo's finite-Weyl criterion therefore yields a two-output extension. Exact mode classes give B-1=(953616 sqrt(5)-4445)/6303442>0.
claims.source: Haapasalo, Compatibility of covariant quantum channels with emphasis on Weyl symmetry, arXiv:1901.06113, Corollary 2, Eq. (22).
claims.falsifier: A wrong class Fourier equation, compatibility-kernel phase convention, eigenvalue formula, or line assignment would invalidate the example; the five Fourier equations and exact formulas are reproduced in FINAL_REPORT.md and d5_exact_repair_audit.py.
claims.limitation: This disproves a universal line-cover budget bound B<=1, not the factor-two EB lift itself.

claims.statement: The exact d=5 channel in WCL-2 admits one factor-two EB comparator whose Choi state is an explicit convex mixture of Weyl-twirled product states.
claims.quantifiers: One common comparator for all 25 Weyl modes of this fixed channel.
claims.construction: Six exact-normalized rational complex kets, with six positive rational weights summing exactly to one; the comparator Choi state is their mixture of Weyl twirls of |psi><psi| tensor |conj(psi)><conj(psi)|. The input decimals are parsed as exact rational numbers and weights are renormalized exactly.
claims.check: 80-digit outward-rounded interval calculation certifies all 24 nonidentity mode inequalities. Minimum direct gap mu_x-(2 lambda_x-1) exceeds 0.0236367126398862; minimum clipped gap mu_x-(2 lambda_x-1)_+ exceeds 0.0139661206985528.
claims.limitation: The exact algebraic and interval checks have not been formalized in a proof assistant or independently reviewed. No separability witness for non-domination was obtained or needed; this comparator proves domination for this candidate.
