supplied bistochastic Kraus family K_y with both normalization sums equal I
reference sigma central in the block algebra
likelihood ||H||_infinity<=theta
ledger.novelty_boundary: This is a supplied N92 internal proof, not an independent proof here. It does not represent every positive selfadjoint self-compatible map as an instrument-derived C*C.
ledger.costs: Kraus family, POVM effects, reference block structure and finite precision are supplied; no general instrument search or efficient decoder compiler is proved.
ledger.falsifier: A direct counterexample to the SOS identity or an explicit map in the stated class violating the EB residual bound.
ledger.next_gate: Find a representation or reduction from arbitrary N93-compatible maps to this class while preserving the promised residual.

ledger.statement: For a finite N-state family of Holevo capacity C and a full-domain permutation-invariant K-receiver channel with one-receiver marginal T, there is a full-domain EB channel Psi with max_x (1/2)||T(rho_x)-Psi(rho_x)||_1 <= (N/2)*sqrt(2C/K).
assumptions: finite-dimensional input and receiver spaces
finite family of N promised input states
C is the supremum of Holevo information over priors on that family
a full-domain CPTP K-receiver extension is permutation invariant and has common marginal T
EB decoder is allowed to depend on the family and K, and is required to be one full-domain CPTP map
ledger.novelty_boundary: Brandao-Harrow Theorem 1 proves a local-measurement de Finetti estimate with sqrt(2 ln(output_dimension)/K). This candidate sharpens the final proof entropy cap to the actual I(X:B^K) for a fixed HJW label measurement, retains a reference-marginal constraint, and converts one common measurement to trace loss using a randomized Helstrom-test POVM. It is an internal adaptation, not a theorem stated in the paper, and still has an N factor.
ledger.costs: The K-receiver extension is a physical channel output; a separable Choi state, POVM and EB map are existential finite-dimensional objects. No efficient search/compiler or proof-runtime bound is established. The Helstrom setting is a witness POVM, not an extra decoder side register.
ledger.falsifier: A finite exact counterexample to the constrained local-measurement de Finetti inequality or to the Choi inversion/randomized-Helstrom conversion in the stated interface.
ledger.next_gate: Prove a dimension- and cardinality-free control of the incompatible Helstrom-test complexity using bounded Holevo information and channel-origin extendibility, or produce a qualifying counterexample to the original target.

ledger.statement: If a full-domain two-output broadcaster has worst promised-state marginal half-trace error b on an N-state family of Holevo capacity C, then for each integer t>=0 there is one full-domain EB decoder with worst-state half-trace error at most t*b + (N/2)*sqrt(2C/2^t). Consequently b*log(N)->0 and bounded C suffice for EB error to vanish.
assumptions: finite-dimensional input/output system with same receiver space at each recursion step
two-output full-domain CPTP broadcaster
finite family of N states and uniformly bounded Holevo capacity C
recursive channel use is charged: 2^t receiver leaves and 2^t-1 broadcaster invocations
ledger.novelty_boundary: Combines the finite-family candidate BIA-C2-01 with binary tree iteration and a final output permutation twirl. It is dimension-free but family-size dependent, so it does not settle arbitrary bounded-capacity experiments.
ledger.costs: For error O(b), the sufficient choice is 2^t on the order of C*N^2/b^2; the proof consumes that many physical receiver outputs and channel calls. No side register or independent-cloning guarantee is claimed.
ledger.falsifier: A finite-channel counterexample violating the recursion triangle bound, Holevo data processing, or BIA-C2-01 under its hypotheses.
ledger.next_gate: Find a complexity measure of label-conditioned discrimination that is controlled by capacity and yields a uniform EB modulus independent of N.

ledger.statement: For every fixed 0<a<1 and 0<delta<1/2, there are commuting state families of Holevo capacity at most c(a)=(1/2)[(1+a)ln(1+a)+(1-a)ln(1-a)] with at least 2^{d(1-h_2(delta))}/(d+1) elements separated in half-trace distance by at least a*delta.
assumptions: even dimension d
balanced signs s in {+1,-1}^d
states rho_s=(I+a diag(s))/d
greedy constant-weight binary code with pairwise Hamming distance at least delta*d
ledger.novelty_boundary: This shows that capacity does not bound trace-packing cardinality; all states commute and are exactly broadcastable, so it is not a counterexample to broadcasting-implies-EB reconstruction.
ledger.costs: The family lives in dimension d and has exponential cardinality in d; no implementation or acquisition advantage is asserted.
ledger.falsifier: An exact violation of the relative-entropy upper bound, balanced-code packing bound, or trace-distance calculation.
ledger.next_gate: Use this commuting family as a control when seeking a noncommutativity-sensitive complexity bound.

ledger.statement: For any full-domain permutation-invariant K-receiver channel with local output dimension d, Chiribella Theorem 5 supplies a common full-domain EB marginal within diamond distance 2*d^2/K; after iterating a two-output broadcaster with error b, this yields EB half-trace error at most t*b+d^2/2^t.
assumptions: finite-dimensional local receiver space of dimension d
full-domain symmetric broadcast channel with permutation-invariant output
iteration produces K=2^t receivers and common marginal T^t
ledger.novelty_boundary: The bound is a cited finite de Finetti theorem for arbitrary permutation-invariant output. The Bose-supported d/K theorem is not used; permutation twirling does not imply Bose support.
ledger.costs: The K-receiver channel is a physical extension. The common measure-and-prepare approximation is existential; no postselection or success probability occurs. It gives a sufficient condition b*log(d)->0, not a capacity-only theorem.
ledger.falsifier: A contradiction to Chiribella Theorem 5 or a mismatch between its diamond-norm normalization and the stated half-trace marginal consequence.
ledger.next_gate: Seek a new capacity-sensitive extension bound that improves the local dimension d^2 without assuming Bose-symmetric support.

ledger.statement: The general implication from uniformly bounded Holevo capacity and vanishing two-receiver broadcast error to uniform EB reconstruction remains unresolved by this cycle; no qualifying counterexample was constructed.
assumptions: family dimension and cardinality may grow
full-domain CPTP broadcaster with each promised-state marginal error tending to zero
uniform Holevo capacity bound
one full-domain EB decoder must work uniformly on the whole family
ledger.novelty_boundary: Finite-family and dimension-dependent sufficient conditions are established as above, but neither controls all growing-dimension, growing-cardinality bounded-capacity families. N61 has divergent capacity; N93's bounded-capacity controls do not have vanishing broadcast error.
ledger.costs: Any resolution must charge the full broadcaster output, all physical receiver systems, and a single common EB decoder; no label-dependent side register is allowed.
ledger.falsifier: A proof uniform in both dimension and family cardinality, or an explicit sequence satisfying bounded capacity, vanishing broadcast error, and a positive global EB lower bound.
ledger.next_gate: Derive an incompatibility-sensitive information bound eliminating the N factor, or construct a channel-origin symmetric counterexample with all stated costs visible.

ledger.status_note: This is an internal research ledger. Internal derivations and finite computations do not establish novelty, physical validation, or product-level efficiency.

claims.exact_statement: For a connected finite detailed-balance Arrhenius network with fixed symmetric conductances c_e^0, rates k_{i->j}=c_e^0 g_i(t), signed currents j=C_0 B^T q, and p_dot=-B j, the integrated finite-horizon edge flux satisfies Phi=C_0 B^T L_0^dagger[p(0)-p(T)]. Consequently, a periodic state has zero integrated edge current.
assumptions: No chemostat cycle affinity or nonconservative edge force
Fixed barriers/conductances
Connected graph
Finite state space
Incidence convention is + at source and - at target
claims.status: Established prior art; internally reconstructed as an equivalent Laplacian form of Rahav-Horowitz-Jarzynski Eq. 4/11. Not a novelty claim.
claims.proof_path: CYCLE2_REPORT.md, section 'RHJ prior art and finite-cycle endpoint identity'; local source_RHJ_2008.txt; source_RHJ_2008.pdf
claims.novelty_boundary: RHJ already gives the integrated-current decomposition and fixed-barrier no-pumping theorem. The pseudoinverse formula only changes representation and handles nonperiodic endpoints explicitly.
claims.costs: No physical controller cost is needed for this mathematical identity; it says nothing about work needed to vary wells.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample within the stated state-potential fixed-conductance model would refute the derivation; first audit sign convention and graph connectivity.
claims.next_gate: Independent algebra review and explicit comparison of V rows to C_0 B^T L_0^dagger with RHJ's edge orientation/gauge.

claims.exact_statement: For c_e(t)=c_e^0[1+epsilon_e(t)] on a connected detailed-balance graph, the actual integrated flux obeys Phi=C_0 B^T L_0^dagger[p(0)-p(T)]+P r, where r_e=integral c_e^0 epsilon_e(q_i-q_j)dt and P=I-C_0B^T L_0^dagger B is an idempotent projection onto ker(B). For a periodic N-unicycle, J_C=R_C^{-1} sum_e integral epsilon_e(q_i-q_j)dt and |J_C|/T<=2 eta g_max/R_C when |epsilon_e|<=eta.
assumptions: Arrhenius conductance form and zero instantaneous cycle affinity
Connected simple ring for scalar cycle-current formula
p is a periodic distribution for the leakage bound
g_i(t)>0 with finite g_max
R_C=sum_e 1/c_e^0
claims.status: Exact conditional derivation, internally reconstructed. The graph projection is a Hodge/Laplacian representation of known stochastic-pump flow structure; priority not established.
claims.proof_path: CYCLE2_REPORT.md, section 'Exact cycle-space leakage identity and small-gate law'
claims.novelty_boundary: RHJ's general path-integral identity already covers driven currents. The quantitative perturbation envelope is a candidate extension/application, not an asserted new theorem in the literature.
claims.costs: epsilon is a dimensionless conductance change. It is not actuator work; rates alone do not price barrier modulation.
claims.falsifier: Numerically compare exact integrated fluxes to the projection identity on random connected graphs; a single mismatch under the stated convention refutes the formula.
claims.next_gate: Derive graph-general constants and independently audit whether the bound can be sharpened under periodic admissibility constraints.

claims.exact_statement: For a fixed periodic well waveform with baseline periodic state p_0 and conductance perturbations |epsilon_e|<=eta, the first-order optimum over independent signed edge controls is eta/R_C times integral sum_e |q_i^0-q_j^0|dt, attained by epsilon_e(t)=eta sign(q_i^0-q_j^0). If the baseline propagator contracts zero-sum vectors in l1 as M exp[-lambda(t-s)] and Lambda_0 bounds baseline escape rates, then for a simple ring |J_C-J_lin|<=4 M g_max Lambda_0 T eta^2/(R_C lambda).
assumptions: Periodic baseline and perturbed states exist
Small relative conductance modulation
Independent edge controls with no slew/bandwidth limits for the linear optimum
Uniform exponential mixing assumption on the fixed-barrier baseline propagator
Simple ring, degree two, finite g_max and Lambda_0
claims.status: Conditional derivation; constants are internally derived and numerically instantiated. Novelty is not externally verified.
claims.proof_path: CYCLE2_REPORT.md, equations (4)-(5), parameterized mixing-gap audit; sharp_ring.py and adversarial_controls.py
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a feed-forward linear-response allocation law plus a perturbation remainder, not a global nonlinear optimum and not a work-efficiency result.
claims.costs: The law charges only conductance amplitude. Gate energy, bandwidth, controller, and measurement costs are absent. At the worked parameter set the rigorous remainder bound is loose (0.01954 cycle-count units at d=0.1).
claims.falsifier: Under a certified baseline mixing gap, direct integration violating the remainder bound refutes the constants; constrained-control optimization below the formula is expected if gates have bandwidth/cost limits.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof audit; then solve an actuator-constrained periodic optimal-control problem and charge measured work.

claims.exact_statement: For the specified three-state rotating-well/traveling-barrier ring with A=beta DeltaE, d=beta DeltaB, c_0=nu exp(-beta B_0), and equal phase dwell tau, each frozen phase satisfies detailed balance. As tau tends to zero, the averaged clockwise/reverse rates are u=c_0[e^d+e^{-A}(1+e^{-d})]/3 and w=c_0[e^{-d}+e^{-A}(1+e^d)]/3; the per-edge current is J_inf=(u-w)/3=2c_0(1-e^{-A})sinh(d)/9. The state-well work rate tends to 2c_0 A(1-e^{-A})cosh(d)/3, hence W_well/J_C tends to 3A coth(d) k_BT per internal ring completion.
assumptions: Three states oriented 0->1->2->0
Equal attempt frequencies and equal dwell time
Wells and barriers rotate as listed in CYCLE2_REPORT.md
Piecewise-constant local-detailed-balance Arrhenius rates
Fast-switching limit tau->0
Work includes well-energy changes only
claims.status: Internal analytic model result; exact finite-period calculations corroborate the limit. Not a product-level or total-energy result.
claims.proof_path: CYCLE2_REPORT.md, sections 'Explicit three-state periodic witness' and 'Work law'; sharp_ring.py; crosscheck_sharp_rk4.py
claims.novelty_boundary: The time-dependent ratchet mechanism is established prior art. The explicit rate/work law is a scoped construction, not an asserted general catalytic theorem.
claims.costs: Well-energy work is computed; barrier actuator, clock, controller, and sensing costs are unpriced. J_C is internal ring circulation, not a chemically identified product current.
claims.falsifier: Direct ODE integration failing to converge to the formulas as tau decreases, or a nonzero current under either one-parameter-only control, refutes this model implementation.
claims.next_gate: Map a real chemical cycle's stoichiometry/reservoirs and calibrate both well and transition-state response plus actuator energy.

claims.exact_statement: The fast-limit averaged uniform three-state unicycle has physical traffic T=u+w and affinity A_eff=3 ln(u/w), and exactly satisfies J=(T/3)tanh(A_eff/6), the Yang-Dill equal-traffic bound. In the finite-period simulation at A=4,d=0.1,B_0=0.5,tau=0.02, the exact internal cycle rate is 0.01325831426697 s^-1 per site, well work is 0.09577731855816 k_BT per site per period, fixed-barrier well-only and fixed-well barrier-only controls have zero current to numerical precision, and mirrored barrier phase reverses current.
assumptions: Unicycle steady state for the ETP comparison
Physical edge traffic T=sum_e tau_e, distinct from bare rate sum K
Uniform rates/distribution in the fast-limit equality case
Finite-period values computed by exact small-matrix exponential with independent RK4 check
claims.status: ETP is an established external theorem; equality/application is internally reconstructed. Numerical witness is finite computation only.
claims.proof_path: CYCLE2_REPORT.md, finite-period table; sharp_ring.py; adversarial_controls.py; crosscheck_sharp_rk4.py
claims.novelty_boundary: No new equal-traffic bound is claimed. Time-order reversal alone does not reverse the high-frequency average; mirroring barrier phase relative to wells does.
claims.costs: Static comparator can be matched on cycle current and traffic using a chemostat affinity. Its fuel work is not commensurate with the pump's total work until barrier-control work is included.
claims.falsifier: The listed matrix/RK4 outputs or no-pumping controls can be falsified by rerunning the scripts or independent high-precision integration.
claims.next_gate: Validate the ETP convention with edge traffic and affinity definitions in any applied catalytic network; measure product-specific currents and actuator power.

claims.exact_statement: A periodic catalyst with nonzero chemostat cycle affinity can sustain stationary baseline turnover at fixed parameters. The closed detailed-balance no-pumping theorem constrains only the pumped/excess current in its domain; it cannot be applied to total catalytic product flux when the RHJ stationary-current term is nonzero.
assumptions: Local detailed balance includes reservoir chemical potentials/stoichiometry
Nonzero total cycle affinity is held by chemostats
Current decomposition includes the RHJ stationary contribution
claims.status: Established distinction from RHJ Eq. 4 and standard local detailed balance; chemistry application remains network-specific.
claims.proof_path: CYCLE2_REPORT.md, paragraphs on chemical affinity and model boundaries
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a scope clarification, not a new theorem.
claims.costs: The affinity entails chemical free-energy input; a complete comparison also charges controller work and product separation/feed conditions.
claims.falsifier: A claimed zero total steady current under fixed parameters with nonzero affinity would conflict with the model's stationary master equation and must be checked against stoichiometry and detailed balance.
claims.next_gate: Build the applied state-transition graph with explicit species stoichiometry, feed/product chemical potentials, and separate baseline versus driven excess currents.

claims.exact_statement: Whether any admissible periodic well/barrier waveform can approach the full pointwise 2 g_max/R_C leakage-current ceiling is unresolved. The current explicit symmetric fast-limit family reaches one third of that ceiling as A grows, and no global periodic-control optimality proof is available.
assumptions: Triangle or simple unicycle leakage model as specified
Periodic p(t) must solve the controlled master equation
No proof or exhaustive waveform search was completed
claims.status: UNKNOWN; explicit family gives a lower construction, but global attainability is not established.
claims.proof_path: CYCLE2_REPORT.md, sharpness paragraph and equations (3)-(4); sharp_ring.py
claims.novelty_boundary: No sharpness claim is made; algebraic integrand saturation is insufficient because p(t) is constrained by dynamics and periodicity.
claims.costs: A physically meaningful optimum also needs a gate work/bandwidth model and controller cost.
claims.falsifier: An explicit admissible periodic protocol with ratio approaching one would refute any conjectured strict fraction; a proof of a stricter dynamic bound would resolve the other direction.
claims.next_gate: Formulate the three-state periodic optimal-control problem with bounded g, epsilon, switching bandwidth, and work cost; either construct a saturating sequence or prove a stricter attainable bound.

claims.exact_statement: For the stated two-stage open mass-action CRN, the two candidate rate tables have identical pointwise full-state CLE drift and covariance at every source and every deterministic nonnegative feed waveform. The exact tables also have equal M0, M1, M2 per feed action, while M3 differs by -6 under F0 and -12 under F1. This follows because the rate difference is 2 epsilon_a alpha_k, with alpha=(1,-3,3,-1), whose k^0,k^1,k^2 moments vanish and k^3 moment is -6, and each jump vector is affine in k.
assumptions: Finite species state vector includes catalyst, clamped feed, and all reporter/product coordinates
Reaction jumps have the stated affine form b_{i,a}+k u_i

The policy is Bayes-optimal among the two-step causal policies in this two-action menu.

Each stage product category is read before the next pulse

ledger.task: Biomolecular design frontier audit focused on inverse folding and kinetic RNA switches

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For a fixed sequence, condition, and decision window T, suppose the ligand-free conformational trajectory X(t) is independent of ligand until first binding; binding is conditionally Poisson with hazard c r(X(t)); and a binding event commits the regulatory output through the decision. With A_T = integral_0^T r(X(t))dt, capture is exactly R(c)=1-E[exp(-c A_T)]. The full hidden folding network affects this output only through the law of A_T.
claims.status: conditional_theorem; internally reconstructed from a standard conditional-hazard identity; no external review; novelty unknown
claims.novelty_boundary: No priority claimed for the conditional-hazard/Laplace identity or for kinetic control of riboswitches; exact application novelty has not been established.
claims.costs: No molecule counts needed for the algebraic identity; acquiring the exposure law requires complete independent single-molecule trajectories in the specified condition and decision window, plus separate ligand-binding calibration if r(X) is not directly measured. Cellular readout requires additional reporter validation.
claims.falsifier: With measured per-transcript exposure and calibrated binding hazard, capture readout differs from 1-E[exp(-c A_T)] beyond measurement and model uncertainty under the stipulated absorbing-capture regime.
claims.next_gate: Test on a transcriptional pbuE or ZTP construct where binding commitment and state-resolved exposure can be measured in the same assay window; explicitly test for unbinding before decision.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For any finite panel of m distinct positive ligand concentrations and any allowed exposure interval with positive length, there are two distinct exposure distributions on that interval that match all m exact dose-response measurements but disagree at any selected additional distinct concentration. Therefore finite-dose output data alone cannot distribution-freely certify the entire off-grid dose-response curve without extra shape or kinetic assumptions.
claims.status: conditional_theorem; internally reconstructed using standard Chebyshev-system/finite-moment reasoning; novelty unknown
claims.novelty_boundary: This is an information limit for the exposure-law model, not evidence that existing parametric fits fail on a particular riboswitch or that every constructed law is sequence-realizable.
claims.costs: The counterexample is algebraic and has no sequence synthesis or computational cost; avoiding the ambiguity requires direct trajectory data, a validated finite-dimensional kinetic model, or a restriction on candidate exposure distributions.
claims.falsifier: The claim is falsified if the specified finite dose panel plus the stated exposure-support constraint uniquely determines every admissible exposure distribution; the Chebyshev construction predicts it does not.
claims.next_gate: Compare off-grid predictions from a Hill fit, a prespecified CTMC fit, and the exposure-law bounds on a held-out dose series.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: If A_1,...,A_n are independent complete observations from the exposure distribution G, then R_hat_n(c)=1-n^{-1}sum_i exp(-c A_i) obeys Pr(sup_{c>=0}|R_hat_n(c)-R(c)|>eps)<=2exp(-2n eps^2). For K candidate sequences, n>=ceil(log(2K/delta)/(2eps^2)) trajectories per sequence gives a simultaneous 1-delta curve certificate and selecting by a specified monotone response objective loses at most 2eps versus the best candidate in the panel.
claims.status: conditional_algorithm; DKW theorem is established mathematics; biomolecular interface is internally derived; not externally reviewed; novelty unknown
claims.novelty_boundary: The statistical confidence bound is standard; no claim that single-molecule dose-curve reconstruction is novel. Bounded search found established smFRET and CTMC analyses but did not establish absence of this exact all-dose DKW certificate in prior work.
claims.costs: Sufficient trajectory counts: K=16, delta=.05, eps=.1 requires 324 complete trajectories per construct (5,184 total); eps=.05 requires 1,293 each (20,688 total). Multiply per independently measured condition/window. These are conservative sufficient counts, not an optimality result. Reporter validation, imaging, labels, photobleaching losses, and kinetic calibration are additional.
claims.falsifier: The confidence guarantee fails if trajectories are dependent, incomplete/censored without correction, or the state-to-exposure measurement error is unbounded; model transfer fails if binding is reversible before decision or output is not determined by first capture.
claims.next_gate: Run a small matched-expression-platform panel with the same aptamer, measure full cotranscriptional competent-state trajectories, and validate one withheld concentration and readthrough output independently.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For a specified equilibrium ensemble partitioned into target basin A and all off-target conformations B, p(A)=1/(1+exp(-DeltaF/(kBT))) where DeltaF=F_B-F_A; p(A)>=1-delta iff DeltaF>=kBT log((1-delta)/delta). Without an upper bound on omitted off-target partition mass, finite queried decoys cannot certify a positive target-occupancy lower bound.
claims.status: conditional_theorem and scoped no-go; standard equilibrium identity plus internally explicit omitted-mass construction; not novelty
claims.novelty_boundary: Boltzmann occupancy and landscape-aware/negative design are established; report only makes the omitted-state certification condition explicit. It does not certify physical accuracy of any force field or decoy generator.
claims.costs: At 298 K, the 95% basin occupancy threshold is 1.74 kcal/mol in free-energy gap; for one target state versus 100 equal-mass off-target states, the per-state energy gap must be 4.46 kcal/mol (6.46 kcal/mol if each basin free energy may err by 1 kcal/mol). Full landscape enumeration can cost thousands of CPU-hours in the cited Rosetta study; no landscape computation was run here.
claims.falsifier: Under the specified equilibrium ensemble and basin partition, direct population measurements disagree with the free-energy odds identity; the omitted-mass no-go would be falsified only by additional restrictions that bound the unseen partition mass.
claims.next_gate: Use published matched designs to compare target-only score, minimum-decoy gap, and estimated ensemble mass against assay data, then prospectively measure a small NMR-resolved panel if the data support the premise.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: A finite panel of off-target assays cannot certify universal absence of binding without a rule restricting unassayed contexts. If instead off-target contexts are iid from a declared distribution Q, true cross-binding prevalence is p, and each true cross-binder is detected with probability at least s, then after n independent contexts with zero detections, a one-sided 1-alpha upper bound is p<=min(1,(1-alpha^(1/n))/s).
claims.status: distribution-free finite-panel no-go plus conditional prevalence bound; internally derived standard binomial argument; recent experimental motivation is source-reported in a bioRxiv preprint; not novelty
claims.novelty_boundary: Finite assays support only the named construct, assay, threshold, and concentration unless Q, iid/exchangeable sampling, and a sensitivity floor are justified. Odin-Multi is a September 2026 preprint; S2 is one experimentally discriminating lead against a named one-residue pMHC variant, not a proteome-wide specificity certificate.
claims.costs: At 95% confidence and sensitivity floor s=.9, 332 distinct iid off-target contexts with zero hits are needed to bound prevalence below 1%; replicates of the same context do not count as independent draws from Q. The Odin-Multi M4A campaign reports 1,700 design trajectories versus 203 target-only; median-time extrapolation is about 1,681 versus 68 V100 GPU-hours, excluding AF3 and lab costs. Its tetramer panel used 500 pooled designs, a 2e6-cell input, and individually followed 20 clones; the source reports no monetary prices.
claims.falsifier: The panel no-go would fail only if the off-target universe is fully enumerated or a validated structural/probabilistic rule constrains every untested context. The prevalence bound fails if contexts are not iid/exchangeable from Q or assay sensitivity is below s.
claims.next_gate: Predeclare the biological off-target sampling frame, binding threshold, and assay sensitivity calibration, then test a blind iid or explicitly challenge-enriched context panel and report panel PASS/FAIL plus UNKNOWN outside the justified scope.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For a fixed binary mutation-by-context equilibrium cycle, the four Boltzmann weights identify the effective coupling J_eff=-RT log(W11 W00/(W10 W01)), but do not identify whether it arises from a direct mutation-context energy term or from a latent two-state conformational mediator: every strictly positive 2x2 weight matrix admits both representations. Separately, a predictor that omits a context variable and receives the same input for two targets separated by binding-energy delta has worst-case absolute error at least |delta|/2.
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact identifiability no-go; cycle identity is established; PDZ3 extension maps are source-reported experiments; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: A thermodynamic cycle measures coupling but does not reveal a unique molecular path; latent-state nonidentifiability is a standard mixture/representation fact. Recent PSD-95 PDZ3 maps motivate the interface but do not make the algebra new.
claims.costs: A focused discriminator has 4 protein variants x 2 extension contexts x 2 ligand lengths = 16 binding conditions before replicates and stability controls; NMR relaxation for WT and the distal I341 mutant adds labeled samples and instrument time. Dollar costs are lab-specific and unreported. No new measurement was performed.
claims.falsifier: The path non-identifiability claim would fail if equilibrium cycle endpoints uniquely determined the direct-contact versus hidden-conformation mechanism under the stated unconstrained model class. The core-only error bound would fail if one predictor output could approximate two scalar targets separated by delta with worst error below |delta|/2.
claims.next_gate: Read Supplementary Data 3 to freeze the exact I341 amino-acid substitution and numeric eta; then compare short canonical versus full CRIPT ligands, extension present/absent, F337 direct-contact control, and NMR relaxation.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For N candidate sequences with arbitrary noiseless scalar assay labels and a unique active sequence z, any randomized adaptive method making B<N distinct-sequence queries and then one recommendation has exact minimax success (B+1)/N over the class f_z(x)=1{x=z}; this is a distribution-free no-go only when no sequence prior or restricted hypothesis class is supplied.
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact minimax theorem; standard query-complexity result; not a novelty claim or empirical model of typical protein/RNA landscapes
claims.novelty_boundary: Realistic sequence priors, homolog alignments, physics, structures, pretrained models, and restricted local landscapes are outside the adversarial hidden-hit class; the bound does not disprove low-label design with those inputs.
claims.costs: Counts unique genotypes, not reads or replicate wells. For N=2^20 and B=1,000, success is at most 0.0955%; 95% requires 996,147 distinct queries. Real noisy assays cost more.
claims.falsifier: The exact minimax value is contradicted by an algorithm whose worst-case success exceeds (B+1)/N under the exact arbitrary-label interface and unique-hit class.
claims.next_gate: State the actual prior/hypothesis class and compare its assay/query cost against equally informed active-learning and physical-model baselines.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For K sites with q_i alleles at site i and an exact noiseless scalar landscape containing arbitrary interactions on at most d distinct sites, identifying every coefficient requires and is achieved by D_d=sum_{|S|<=d} product_{i in S}(q_i-1) distinct genotype labels. This identifies the assumed low-order model but does not guarantee that a real landscape has no higher-order effects.
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact rank theorem; standard factorial-design/Mobius inversion result; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: The count is a model-identification requirement, not a bound for ranking one prespecified sequence. Higher-order terms, assay noise, synthesis bias, and transfer across conditions remain open.
claims.costs: For eight binary edits and d=3, 93 unique genotypes identify the cubic model; a proposed additional 16 blind high-order variants is a pilot choice, giving 109 sequences or 218 genotype-replicate outcomes at two replicates per condition. Statistical power and dollar/read costs are unmeasured.
claims.falsifier: The exact count is contradicted if fewer than D_d labels can identify every coefficient in the declared full degree-d function class, or if the proposed design matrix is rank deficient despite D_d rows.
claims.next_gate: Run a frozen 8-edit local cubic fit and 16-sequence blind high-order challenge with replicate variance measured in advance; compare against additive, pairwise, and matched-random controls.

ledger.task: Cycle 2 biomolecular design: reversible RNA-switch rate acquisition and robust sequence ranking

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For a time-homogeneous U<->C<->B CTMC with rates U->C=alpha, C->U=beta, C->B=c*kon, B->C=koff, initialized in U, let S=alpha+beta+c*kon+koff, D=alpha*c*kon+alpha*koff+beta*koff, and r±=(S±sqrt(S^2-4D))/2. For c>0 and distinct roots, P(B at t)=alpha*c*kon/D * [1-(r+ exp(-r- t)-r- exp(-r+ t))/(r+-r-)]; repeated-root value is its continuous limit and at c=0 it is zero.
claims.status: conditional_theorem; exact finite-state model identity internally derived
claims.novelty_boundary: Closed-form CTMC calculations are standard, and reversible ligand/folding models in riboswitches are prior art; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: Needs calibrated sequence-specific alpha, beta, kon, koff, concentration c, and decision time t; constant-size closed-form evaluation after acquisition.
claims.falsifier: Non-exponential state dwell times, non-linear concentration dependence, additional bound or folding states, or history-dependent rates invalidate the three-state response interface.
claims.next_gate: Fit state-resolved dwell paths under fixed transcription conditions and validate the full response at a withheld dose/time.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For two U<->C<->B birth-death CTMCs initialized in the same ordered state, if alpha_A>=alpha_B, beta_A<=beta_B, kon_A>=kon_B, and koff_A<=koff_B, then P_A(B at t)>=P_B(B at t) for every common c>=0 and t>=0. The same result holds under a shared nonnegative time-varying ligand schedule c(t).
claims.status: conditional_theorem; internally reconstructed application of standard birth-death stochastic monotonicity
claims.novelty_boundary: The comparison argument is standard; this is a task-specific all-dose/all-time sequence-ranking consequence. Priority is unresolved.
claims.costs: Requires simultaneous rate intervals for each prespecified sequence; no reporter grid over dose and time is required after the model is acquired. Model validation assays and state-resolving trajectory acquisition remain necessary.
claims.falsifier: A held-out bound-state or regulatory response outside the interval prediction band under validated CTMC assumptions rejects use of the fitted model. A rate tradeoff alone does not falsify the theorem; it makes the candidates incomparable.
claims.next_gate: Test two to four same-aptamer expression-platform variants with state-resolved trajectories and a preregistered held-out decision condition.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For each of K frozen sequences at a fixed calibrated concentration c_star>0, observe m_U, m_C, and m_B independent complete dwell episodes. U and B sojourns have exponential rates alpha and koff. C sojourns have exponential total rate rho=beta+c_star*kon, with C->B exit probability r=c_star*kon/rho independent of duration. Exact chi-square intervals for exponential rates and a Clopper-Pearson interval for r, transformed via gamma=rho*r and beta=rho*(1-r), give simultaneous rate coverage >=1-delta by allocating eta=delta/(4K) to each of four primitive intervals per sequence. A pair is robustly ranked when its rate intervals are separated in the favorable componentwise order; otherwise the all-domain ranking is UNKNOWN.
claims.status: conditional_algorithm; exact fixed-look marginal intervals internally reconstructed from standard exponential/binomial inference
claims.novelty_boundary: The inference distributions and Bonferroni correction are standard; no claim of a new statistical method.
claims.costs: At a fixed look with m episodes per source state and K sequences, 3*K*m completed dwell episodes are required; expected planned dwell duration per sequence j is m/alpha_j + m/(beta_j+c_star*kon_j) + m/koff_j. Add construct synthesis/QC, state preparation, FRET calibration, camera frames, censoring losses, concentration calibration, and held-out output assays. Repeated optional looks require alpha spending.
claims.falsifier: Confidence coverage is not certified if dwell episodes are not independent exponential samples, exit labels are misclassified, data are censored without a valid likelihood, or concentration is miscalibrated.
claims.next_gate: Acquire a fixed-look pilot, evaluate dwell diagnostics and rate intervals, and report pairwise rank only after simultaneous separation.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: With alpha=beta=1 s^-1 for both candidates and c=1 micromolar, candidate A (kon=2 micromolar^-1 s^-1,koff=10 s^-1) has P_A(B_t)=t^2+O(t^3) and stationary bound probability 1/11; candidate B (kon=1 micromolar^-1 s^-1,koff=1 s^-1) has P_B(B_t)=t^2/2+O(t^3) and stationary bound probability 1/3. Their exact response curves cross near t=0.273165 s.
claims.status: exact_model_counterexample; numerical root is a finite computation from the closed form
claims.novelty_boundary: Synthetic counterexample demonstrating why tradeoff pairs cannot be totally ordered; it is not an empirical biological observation.
claims.costs: Constant-size evaluation and one-dimensional root solve; no wet-lab cost for the mathematical example.
claims.falsifier: The stated probabilities and crossing are directly checkable from the exact finite-state formula; no empirical claim is made.
claims.next_gate: Keep non-separated or tradeoff candidates incomparable globally, or choose using a prespecified concentration/time response objective.

work_boundaries.prior_art: Beisel-Smolke and Lin-Thirumalai provide primary reversible riboswitch kinetic models; Keilson-Kester establish birth-death monotonicity. The present report claims no novelty or priority.
unperformed: No single-molecule trajectory or reporter measurement was collected.
No external proof review, novelty search, or biological validation was completed.

claims.statement: For a sequence-frozen DENV translational RNA sensor, all 59 independently sampled genotype/context pairs from the pre-registered equal-serotype cluster distribution D, and four full-length genome sentinels (one per serotype), meet the simultaneous functional thresholds F_ON/F_OFF >= 10, F_ON >= 0.25 F_constitutive, and F_OFF <= 0.05 F_constitutive at 60 minutes in every cell-free reaction point of a pre-registered 3-temperature x 3-magnesium grid. If all 59 independent D draws pass, the exact one-sided 95% upper confidence bound on the D failure probability is 4.95%.
assumptions: The sensor sequence and analysis code are frozen before access to the 59 held-out sequence/context pairs.
D is a precisely documented distribution over phylogenetic-cluster representatives, weighted equally across DENV serotypes; the result does not generalize beyond D.
The condition grid is fixed before candidate results are observed, and constitutive reporter controls remain measurable throughout the grid.
Each context draw is independently sampled from D; assay uncertainty is propagated using independent reaction preparations, not repeated time points.
Target concentration is fixed at the published challenge scale (10^13 copies/reaction); this does not establish clinical limit of detection.
claims.novelty_boundary: Pan-DENV sequence coverage, up-to-three-mismatch tolerance, thermodynamic/structure-aware design, and kinetic effects are prior art. Potential increment is a blinded joint sequence-context by reaction-condition certificate, including full-length genome sentinels; priority is unverified.

costs.runtime: Must be measured with pinned software and hardware; estimate not available.

claims.falsifier: A blinded test context or any full-length serotype genome falls below the pre-registered response threshold in any environmental condition. The decisive first test is the paired 36-nt trigger versus flanked/full-length genomic RNA comparison at the low-magnesium/high-structure corner.
claims.next_gate: Resolve the distribution frame from the primary DENV genome corpus; run a variance-estimating pilot; design and freeze a candidate sequence; confirm the held-out finite panel has not leaked into design; then execute the blinded assay.

ledger.exact_statement: For any p in (0,1) and horizon T>0, the two-state reversible continuous-time Markov generators q(U,B)=a p and q(B,U)=a(1-p), a>0, all have stationary bound fraction p and identical equilibrium free-energy difference, while P(B at T | X_0=U)=p(1-exp(-aT)) ranges from 0 to p as a varies. Thus equilibrium energies alone do not determine a nontrivial finite-time response bound uniformly over detailed-balance kinetics.
assumptions: Two-state reversible CTMC
Finite positive horizon T
Transition rates are not supplied by the equilibrium energy landscape
ledger.novelty_boundary: The mathematical rate-scaling fact and finite-time two-state relaxation are standard; no novelty or priority claim. Primary riboswitch papers already distinguish affinity/equilibrium from rates and transcription timing.

costs.equilibrium_only: Requires energies or KD but cannot identify absolute response times
costs.kinetic_prediction: Requires absolute association/dissociation/folding rates and transcription decision-time or pause distribution

ledger.falsifier: No-go falsifier would require an additional supplied restriction linking equilibrium energies to a uniformly bounded kinetic timescale; none is part of the stated interface.
ledger.next_gate: For a named riboswitch, acquire same-condition rates and transcription timing, then test the finite-window prediction against direct transcript readthrough/termination.

ledger.exact_statement: Under a constant concentration c and a conditional first-capture hazard k_on*c while an unbound ligand-free trajectory is binding competent, the capture probability by decision is p(c)=1-E[exp(-k_on*c*A)], where A is the integrated competent-state exposure up to the actual transcription decision. For K prespecified sequences with n independent complete paths per sequence and known k_on,j, the empirical Laplace dose curves satisfy simultaneous coverage over all c>=0 and all sequences with probability at least 1-delta using half-width eps=sqrt(log(2K/delta)/(2n)).
assumptions: Until first capture, the concentration-c ligand-free conformational path has the same law as the measured path
Capture hazard is k_on,j*c on competent unbound states and zero elsewhere
Capture is absorbing for the output being predicted
k_on,j is known
For each fixed sequence, exposure traces are iid and complete through transcription decision
K sequences were prespecified
ledger.novelty_boundary: The conditional Poisson/Laplace identity and DKW inequality are standard mathematical tools. Bounded primary-literature search found no riboswitch paper using ligand-free per-path exposure to predict the full dose curve this way; priority is unverified.

costs.exposure: N_complete=K*ceil(log(2K/delta)/(2 eps^2)) complete ligand-free single-molecule transcription traces; at frame interval dt and horizon T, approximately N_complete*ceil(T/dt) frames
costs.rate: Acquire same-condition k_on for each sequence unless a validated common value is supplied; acquire k_off to test capture commitment
costs.measurement: State classification calibration and temporal-resolution/censoring bounds are additional systematic-error costs

ledger.falsifier: A held-out ligand concentration with measured capture/output outside the simultaneous band after certified rate, censoring, state-classification and exposure-discretization errors rejects the one-state absorbing first-capture model.
ledger.next_gate: Acquire complete trajectories for a small fixed sequence screen, freeze bands before measuring outcomes at held-out concentrations, compare with KD-only and a full multistate CTMC fit.

ledger.exact_statement: The integrated exposure A alone does not determine bound-at-decision probability when ligand dissociates: for early and late competent windows of equal duration T/2 with first-capture rate lambda and dissociation rate mu>0, P_late(bound at T)=exp(mu*T/2)*P_early(bound at T)>P_early(bound at T), despite identical A=T/2.
assumptions: Competence occupies either [0,T/2] or [T/2,T]
Association rate lambda while competent
Bound ligand dissociates at rate mu>0
No rebinding after dissociation outside the competent interval
ledger.novelty_boundary: A model counterexample, not a biological discovery. It demonstrates that the path-exposure theorem predicts first capture only unless irreversibility/commitment is established.

costs.needed_for_endpoint_prediction: Acquire k_off and state-specific post-binding/transcription-transition rates, or directly measure endpoint outcomes

claims.statement: K pure starts are minimal for identifying all K(K-1) off-diagonal switching rates and K net-growth rates from t=0 composition and log-total derivatives alone, for an unrestricted open rate family.

unknown parameters are all off-diagonal q_ij and all r_i, with no known sparsity or parameter sharing
each tested initial condition yields K-1 independent composition slopes and one total-count slope

claims.statement: K starts are not necessary from full continuous exact count trajectories: in the two-state model, a single pure-start trajectory from e_1 with q_12=a>0 identifies a, b, r_1, and r_2; more generally a cyclic initial state with full Krylov rank yields a full-span state curve and identifies A.
assumptions: exact noiseless absolute count trajectory and its derivatives
known initial state and fixed autonomous matrix A
for the two-state construction, a>0 so the second state becomes populated
for the general statement, the initial vector is cyclic for A
claims.status: internally proved structural counterexample to unconditional K-start minimality; finite-data conditioning UNKNOWN
claims.novelty_boundary: This refutes only unconditional minimality; the standard cyclic-vector observability condition and structural exact-data scope are not a biological or practical acquisition claim.
claims.costs: Continuous exact trajectory and derivatives are an idealization; state-spanning can be ill-conditioned, particularly when transition rates are small or states are rarely occupied.
claims.falsifier: The explicit two-state formulas fail if applied to an exact trajectory satisfying a>0 and x_2(t)>0; with noisy finite data, the issue is estimator error rather than structural injectivity.
claims.next_gate: Quantify conditioning and sample cost before using fewer sorted starting populations.

nonnegative initial counts and Metzler A_u
joint confidence region actually contains the unknown action matrices with stated coverage
uniform switching-exit cap Lambda and net-growth cap R for the continuous-time path margin

numerical matrix exponentials are outward-certified
objective and unsafe events are defined on phenotype compositions/mean counts
claims.status: internally reconstructed conservative certificate algorithm; no efficient-complexity or biological validation claim

claims.next_gate: Implement interval arithmetic on a small benchmark and compare its safe schedules and false-rejection rate with exact worst-case search over synthetic compact parameter sets.

claims.exact_statement: There exist two binary-offspring branching models with the same per-daughter fate probabilities P(S)=p and the same mean number 2p of S daughters, but different clonal extinction probabilities. Specifically, for p>1/2, common-fate sisters give q=(1-p)/p and independent sisters give q=((1-p)/p)^2.
assumptions: Each S cell divides into exactly two daughters.
F is terminal and contributes no S offspring.
Successive parent-cell offspring vectors are iid within each named model (Galton-Watson assumption).
p is fixed, with p>1/2 for the displayed nontrivial extinction roots.
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_exact_model_counterexample; standard Galton-Watson fixed-point mechanism; no novelty or external proof claim
claims.novelty_boundary: The two generating functions and fixed-point equations are elementary standard branching-process reasoning. The counterexample is scoped; it does not claim the underlying theory is new. CLiNC already models the joint daughter-state distribution.
claims.costs: No data or computation required for the exact calculation. Biological inference would require sister-resolved lineage acquisition, clone tracking, and validation.
claims.falsifier: The mathematical statement is falsified only by an algebraic error or violation of stated offspring laws; biological relevance is falsified for a proposed assay if the observed offspring laws are effectively independent and transition-only predictions remain calibrated on held-out clones.
claims.next_gate: Acquire sister-resolved data under a regeneration/depletion intervention and compare transition-only versus joint-offspring models on held-out organoids.

claims.exact_statement: If at most H at-risk parent divisions occur, at most b daughters are produced per division, and each daughter has conditional unsafe-fate probability at most epsilon, then without any independence assumption the probability of any unsafe daughter is at most min(1,H*b*epsilon). For one b=2 division with identical marginal unsafe probability epsilon, the probability at least one daughter is unsafe lies sharply in [epsilon,min(1,2*epsilon)].
assumptions: H is a deterministic upper bound on at-risk parent divisions over the horizon.
The conditional per-daughter unsafe probability bound epsilon holds under the intervention and all relevant safe histories.
Each parent produces at most b daughters.
State classifications and lineage observations are valid.
claims.status: internally derived finite-horizon union-bound certificate; conservative; not a biological guarantee
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard union bound and Fréchet bounds; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: Must acquire a defensible division-count cap H and a one-sided upper confidence bound for epsilon; imaging, barcoding, fate classification, and clone/organoid-level replication are charged.
claims.falsifier: Any intervention-matched conditional per-daughter rate above epsilon or any lineage horizon exceeding H invalidates the certificate premises.
claims.next_gate: Pre-register eta and estimate H and epsilon_U from sister-resolved perturbation data; otherwise retain UNKNOWN.

claims.exact_statement: The published human cerebral-organoid assay provides a relevant experimental interface for testing lineage-aware regeneration models: barcodes identify broad clone-size heterogeneity, and puromycin depletion of WT cells can be compensated by a minority of resistant cells under reported conditions.
assumptions: This is a source-reported result in the named in-vitro organoid setting.
The result is not generalized to in-vivo regeneration or human treatment.
claims.status: externally reported primary biological result; not independently reproduced in this lane
claims.novelty_boundary: Existing primary study; used as assay context only.
claims.costs: The proposed extension requires barcoding, organoid differentiation replicates, live paired-daughter imaging or assay, single-cell fate classification, and held-out evaluation.
claims.falsifier: The cited study's assay is not a falsifier; the proposed model relevance fails if joint offspring law does not improve held-out predictions beyond a calibrated transition-only model.
claims.next_gate: Run the preregistered paired-sister assay under vehicle and depletion/rescue conditions.

claims.exact_statement: For b exchangeable daughter unsafe indicators with marginal epsilon, the sharp one-division probability of at least one unsafe daughter is in [epsilon, min(1,b*epsilon)].
assumptions: b is a fixed number of daughter slots
sister indicators are exchangeable
each indicator has marginal epsilon
claims.status: internally derived exact Frechet/first-moment bound; standard; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary sharp dependence bounds; not a new branching theorem.
claims.costs: No computation. Empirical use requires paired daughter fate classification.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample satisfying the stated fixed-b exchangeable law and marginal would falsify the algebraic claim.
claims.next_gate: Estimate the count of unsafe daughters per division rather than only the pooled single-cell marginal.

claims.exact_statement: If a full b-ary safe progenitor tree is forced through T divisions and every daughter has conditional unsafe marginal epsilon given the full prior all-safe history, then the sharp probability of no unsafe fate lies between max(0,1-b*epsilon)^H and (1-epsilon)^H, H=(b^T-1)/(b-1).
assumptions: Each safe parent divides once per generation
exactly b daughter slots per division
conditional marginal epsilon holds after every prior all-safe history
unsafe fate is a first-hit failure
T is finite
claims.status: internally derived sharp finite-horizon bound under conditional-history interface; not biological validation
claims.novelty_boundary: Repeated sharp one-family Fréchet bounds plus chain rule; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: Need a safe-path division cap/tree-depth horizon and conditional fate marginals; full-tree experiment cost grows with potential lineage count H.
claims.falsifier: Violation of the conditional marginal, exact full-tree, or offspring-cap assumptions invalidates the formula as a biological bound.
claims.next_gate: For a capped real system, measure safe quiescence/death and replace the full-tree assumption with its actual at-risk division bound.

claims.exact_statement: Under a one-type Galton-Watson process with exchangeable within-family offspring count K in {0,...,b}, mean mu=bp, and independent parent-family offspring vectors, the sharp T-generation survival interval over all admissible offspring laws is 1-G_max^T(0) <= P(Z_T>0) <= 1-G_min^T(0), where G_max(z)=1-p+p*z^b and G_min is the nearest-integer mean law on floor(mu),ceil(mu).
assumptions: One regenerative cell type
offspring count cap b
per-daughter regenerative marginal p
within-family exchangeability
independent offspring vectors across parents
fixed or generation-wise admissible mean mu
finite T
claims.status: internally derived via standard PGF recursion and convex order; sharp under stated assumptions; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard Galton-Watson/convex-order result; lineage literature already represents joint offspring laws. No novelty or priority claim.
claims.costs: Empirical prediction requires the family-level offspring count law, not only state transition marginals; sequencing, imaging, and clone-level replication are charged.
claims.falsifier: The algebraic statement is falsified by a law satisfying its constraints but outside the recursively computed interval; biological use fails if inter-parent dependence or density feedback is material and omitted.
claims.next_gate: Fit the offspring PGF and test held-out clone persistence under the intervention; include clone-level latent effects if parent families are dependent.

claims.exact_statement: For b=3, two exchangeable offspring-count laws (1,3,3,1)/8 and (1,9,3,3)/16 over K=0,1,2,3 have the same per-daughter marginal 1/2 and pairwise covariance zero, but different P(K=0) and hence different one-generation clone persistence.
assumptions: Daughter labels are exchangeable conditional on K
K is sampled from the displayed law
claims.status: internally checked exact finite counterexample; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Finite combinatorial witness illustrating why pairwise covariance is insufficient for b>=3.
claims.costs: No data or code. Empirical identification requires at least the family offspring-count histogram.
claims.falsifier: Direct arithmetic: a failed equality of means/pair moments or unequal exchangeability would falsify this witness.
claims.next_gate: When b>=3, acquire the full offspring-count histogram or PGF rather than only sister-pair correlations.

remaining_control_implication.statement: Ratio-matched synthetic fate controllers should be compared under different fate-resolution timing because identical daughter marginals need not imply identical clone reliability. A recombinase branching platform makes this a plausible assay, but no literature result located here demonstrates independent control of sister dependence at fixed marginals.
remaining_control_implication.status: proposed experimental stress test; not demonstrated actuator and not a novelty claim

claims.exact_statement: There exist two controlled three-daughter branching models with exactly identical CLE drift b(x,a) and covariance A(x,a) at every full observable state and for every action, yet opposite action rankings for safe founder reach. The laws nu1=(1,3,3,1)/8, nu2=(1,9,3,3)/16, and nu2rev=(3,3,9,1)/16 all have E[K]=3/2 and E[K^2]=3, so with a common division rate lambda the actionwise fields are b=lambda*r*(1/2,3/2) and A=lambda*r*diag(1,3). Swapping nu2 and nu2rev across the B action changes P(K=3) from 3/16 to 1/16 while preserving all fields.
assumptions: The full observable state is the R and U cell-count vector (and may include clone-labelled counts); only R cells divide.
At each action a, each R parent is replaced at the same unknown common rate lambda in both worlds by three exchangeable daughters with offspring count K from the action-specific law.
Offspring draws are independent across parent events; the three laws have the same first and second raw jump moments.
Safe reach for one generation is K=3 and unsafe-any is K<3.
claims.status: internally derived exact controlled CLE-equivalence counterexample; verified with exact rational arithmetic; no biological validation or novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Uses the existing Cycle 2 b=3 pairwise-independent offspring laws and standard CLE jump-moment formulas; Cycle 3 is a controlled coefficient-equality application, not a new branching theorem.
claims.costs: No data needed for the construction. Biological application requires randomized founder clones, full sister outcome histograms, division-time/rate tracking, and semantically valid endpoint assays.
claims.falsifier: An algebraic contradiction under the listed offspring laws would falsify the construction; biological relevance is falsified if no feasible intervention pair matches division rate and first two offspring moments while separating the higher-order family law.
claims.next_gate: Demonstrate two feasible schedules with matched division rate, E[K], and E[K^2] but separated higher-order K law; then validate on held-out randomized lineages.

claims.exact_statement: For the strict CLE-equivalent models in CLG3-1, if W-plus uses reporter sensitivity/false-positive rates 0.9/0.1 and W-minus uses 0.1/0.9, and the B offspring law in W-minus is the coordinatewise complement of W-plus, then every observed daughter-label vector has exactly the same law in both worlds. The common division rate is the same under both actions and in both worlds, so event times match and all finite/multigeneration lineage transcripts remain identical under any adaptive policy although the safe-reach action ranking reverses; worst-case ranking error is at least 1/2.
assumptions: W-minus uses the mirrored offspring law for each action relative to W-plus.
W-plus reporter sensitivity/false-positive rates are 0.9/0.1 and W-minus rates are 0.1/0.9.
Reporter emissions are not externally calibrated or semantically anchored.
All observed event times and censoring are retained; the common division rate lambda is identical between worlds and actions.
claims.status: internally derived exact observational-equivalence proof; not biological validation
claims.novelty_boundary: A model-specific construction using standard hidden-state label symmetry; no new general HMM identifiability theorem is claimed.
claims.costs: No finite sample count resolves an exact alias. A gold-standard endpoint/emission calibration or an orthogonal functional endpoint is required.
claims.falsifier: A calibrated semantic anchor or an observed variable with different conditional laws in the two models invalidates the stated observation interface and can distinguish the worlds.
claims.next_gate: Use action- and context-matched gold-standard R/U references to bound the emission matrix orientation and error.

claims.exact_statement: For two randomized independent-founder arms with directly observed binary safe-reach endpoint and true mean gap Delta, Hoeffding gives ranking error at most exp(-n Delta^2); for the strict witness gap Delta=1/16 and alpha=0.05, n=767 founders per action suffices. With known independent per-daughter sensitivity 0.9/false-positive rate 0.1, the product deconvolution score has range width 405/256 and n=1920 founders per action suffices for the same true endpoint ranking.
assumptions: Founder clones are the independent sampling units.
Assignment is randomized, endpoints are bounded and correctly classified, and the action-specific population/context is fixed.
The ranking gap is positive and known for the bound; there is no unmodeled interference.
For the noisy-label bound, reporter errors are independent across daughters conditional on their true fates and the calibrated per-daughter channel has sensitivity 0.9 and false-positive rate 0.1.
claims.status: internally derived concentration bound and arithmetic check; not a biological power calculation
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard Hoeffding bounds; no statistical-method novelty is claimed.
claims.costs: Counts independent founder clones; donor/organoid blocks, lineage imaging, reporter calibration, exposure measurement, and censoring follow-up are additional costs.
claims.falsifier: Dependence between purported independent founders, action-specific reporter drift, or misclassified endpoints invalidates the nominal bound.
claims.next_gate: Pilot donor-level dependence, endpoint noise, and event rates before assigning an organoid-scale sample budget.

claims.exact_statement: Known or calibrated binary endpoint emissions with positive contrast permit inversion p=(q-f)/(s-f); if s-f is bounded below by kappa0 and treatment/calibration proportions each have error at most gamma<=kappa0/4, plug-in probability error is at most 4 gamma/kappa0.
assumptions: A gold-standard semantic R/U reference is available for calibration.
The same calibration channel applies to treated observations, or calibration is stratified by every action/type/context affecting emissions.
The emission contrast satisfies s-f>=kappa0>0.
claims.status: internally derived deterministic inversion/error bound from Hoeffding-calibrated proportions
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary confusion-matrix inversion and concentration; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: Requires n_cal >= ceil(log(4/alpha_cal)/(2 gamma^2)) gold-standard examples for each of R and U, plus the treated founder sample and any needed action/type/context strata.
claims.falsifier: Unknown semantic orientation, contrast near zero, or emission drift outside calibrated strata prevents the bound from applying.
claims.next_gate: Measure action- and phenotype-stratified confusion rates with orthogonal truth labels.

claims.exact_statement: For an exchangeable three-daughter law K in {0,1,2,3}, once normalization and E[K], E[K^2] are fixed, one scalar such as P(K=3) or E[K(K-1)(K-2)] determines the remaining one-dimensional offspring-count family. In the witness, this statistic separates nu1, nu2, and nu2rev despite identical first and second moments.
assumptions: The daughter outcomes are exchangeable, so their joint law is determined by the count law of K.
The support is exactly contained in {0,1,2,3}.
The first two count moments are known or tested equivalent.
claims.status: internally derived finite-dimensional linear-algebra fact; standard and no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Specific finite-support moment identification; no new moment-problem theorem is claimed.
claims.costs: Requires paired/triple daughter fate classification per founder division; aggregate single-cell marginals or pair covariance are insufficient.

claims.next_gate: Estimate the full daughter-count histogram in matched-moment, held-out action arms.

claims.claim: As hidden switching becomes arbitrarily fast, both mechanisms have the same action-averaged burst law, so any fixed finite snapshot experiment loses uniform separation; an unbounded-rate controller must permit UNKNOWN.

ledger.exact_statement: For a two-state homogeneous CTMC with X_0=0, rates alpha>0 and beta>0, and horizon T>0, fixing z in (0,1) leaves a continuum of strictly positive rate pairs alpha_lambda=lambda*z/(1-exp(-lambda*T)), beta_lambda=lambda-alpha_lambda for lambda> -log(1-z)/T that all have P(X_T=1)=z but have distinct and strictly increasing expected integrated occupancy I(lambda)=z*(T/(1-exp(-lambda*T))-1/lambda). If two randomized interventions swap two such rate pairs between them, endpoint-only observations of one state per independent founder have identical distributions in both worlds while the intervention maximizing expected integrated occupancy reverses. Any policy then has worst-case regret at least half the occupancy gap. For two specified worlds, one calibrated nondifferential binary observation at an intermediate time tau and n independent founders per arm has sign-test error at most exp(-n*d(tau)^2), where d is the observed-probability gap; a finite grid minimizing the resulting cost provides an executable sufficient design.
assumptions: binary time-homogeneous CTMC with fixed positive rates within each intervention arm
all founders start in verified state 0
interventions are randomized at the independent founder-lineage level
no interference, state-dependent division/death, censoring, or shared-well dependence
the objective is expected integrated state-1 occupancy over a fixed horizon
reporter sensitivity and specificity are known and nondifferential across arms and times
ledger.status: conditional theorem internally derived; numeric design finite-grid computation; biological validity and novelty/priority UNKNOWN
ledger.novelty_boundary: Does not claim that lineage-based cell-state inference, kin-correlation analysis, CTMC estimation, active timepoint selection, experimental design, or robust POMDP control is new. KCA can infer reversible networks from pedigree correlations and endpoint labels; multi-time population methods and tree-HMM methods use richer channels than the one-founder-endpoint interface here; ICML 2026 already studies active measurement-time selection for measure-valued trajectories, and Bayesian optimal perturbation time design exists for haematopoiesis. The scoped contribution is the explicit action-reversing path-reward alias, minimax endpoint-only regret statement, and finite-grid sensing certificate for this two-state model. No full priority review was done.

The candidate biological model is rejected for a selected system if direct tracks show non-exponential/non-Markov dwell times, state-dependent division/death or censoring changes the observed process, reporter error is arm-dependent/uncalibrated, or replicated data reject the predicted endpoint equality and intermediate separation. In the numeric example the predicted midpoint-grid readout is p_fast=0.4400941 versus p_slow=0.1370682 at tau=0.21215T, while both terminal probabilities are 0.5.
ledger.next_gate: Extend the time selector to confidence sets of rates and reporter channels by maximizing worst-case separation across action-reversing model pairs per acquisition cost; return UNKNOWN if every time has zero robust separation. claims.name: Full-K one-lag global identification
claims.statement: For K>=3, one unrestricted finite-time endpoint matrix, even from all K pure starts with exact fractions and absolute totals, does not globally identify all switching rates and net growth rates.
claims.proof: Three-state irreducible circulant cycle: fix s=u+v and shift d=u-v by 4*pi/(sqrt(3)*tau); shared Fourier eigenvectors and eigenvalue imaginary shifts +/-2*pi/tau give identical exp(tau Q) for distinct positive rate pairs. For K>3, block-diagonal embedding refutes the full allowed class.
claims.finite_check: At tau=1, pairs (5,5) and (8.6275987285,1.3724012715) have max endpoint matrix difference 2.34e-15 and max generator difference 3.6276.
claims.limits: For K>3 the embedded example is reducible; no claim is made for every larger-K irreducible subclass or for parameter boxes that provably exclude aliases.

claims.name: Two-state exact endpoint recovery
claims.statement: For K=2, exact M(tau)=exp(tau A) identifies any admissible 2x2 Metzler A; its spectrum is real and A is recovered by the principal logarithm.
claims.proof: A 2x2 Metzler matrix has discriminant (a-d)^2+4bc>=0; the real exponential is injective on its eigenvalues, with the repeated/Jordan case also uniquely inverted.

claims.name: No-alias recovery for general K
claims.statement: If tau*||A||_1<pi, K linearly independent known initial mixtures recover M and the principal logarithm recovers A; then q_{i->j}=A_{ji} and r_i=sum_j A_{ji}.
claims.sufficient_bound: If |r_i|<=R and sum_{j!=i}q_{i->j}<=Lambda for all i, ||A||_1<=R+2*Lambda.

claims.name: Number of independent initial conditions
claims.statement: K linearly independent known initial mixtures are necessary for a uniform all-rates guarantee; K pure starts are sufficient only with an injectivity/no-alias condition.
claims.counterexample: With fewer than K pure starts, a source state can be made unreachable from all observed starts; changing its outgoing rates leaves all observed endpoint columns unchanged.

claims.name: Absolute totals separate switching from net growth
claims.statement: Fraction-only endpoints can alias switching and relative growth even with all pure starts; absolute endpoint totals recover the column scales needed to form M.
claims.counterexample: At tau=1, one-way rate q=1,r=(0,0) and q'=e-1,r'=(e-2,-1) have identical fractions from both pure starts but different total from state-1 start.

claims.name: Finite-time first-order rate error
claims.statement: For ||A||_1<=B, R_tau=exp(B*tau)-1-B*tau, and entrywise endpoint error <=epsilon_M, the estimator (Mhat-I)/tau has off-diagonal rate error <=(epsilon_M+R_tau)/tau; net-growth error <=(K*epsilon_M+R_tau)/tau.
claims.finite_check: Cycle script verifies the observed max off-diagonal error is below the analytic finite-tau remainder bound for its test instance.

claims.name: Bounded-well sample complexity
claims.statement: For A0 actions, K pure starts, n independent wells per action/start, unbiased normalized count coordinates in [0,C], probability of any endpoint mean coordinate error above epsilon_M is at most 2*A0*K^2*exp(-2*n*epsilon_M^2/C^2).
claims.limitation: The expected-count ODE alone supplies no concentration law. Unbounded branching counts require a specified tail/variance/likelihood model; clipping bias must be added.

claims.name: Finite-action robust reach-avoid
claims.statement: For state-level CTMC reach-avoid by horizon H and a coordinate confidence radius epsilon_q on off-diagonal rates, action value differs from its center by at most 2*H*(K-1)*epsilon_q; maximizing lower bounds is a finite-action maximin rule.
claims.limitation: The mean-count ODE does not define lineage branching/extinction probabilities. Population reach-avoid needs an explicit branching and censoring model.

acquisition_oracle_geometry_conditioning.exact_sampler_model: Given an exact iid sampler for p and an evaluable chi, n output samples require n p draws, n chi evaluations, O(nk) output-coordinate arithmetic, and O(k) streaming memory. The comparison Gaussian needs k normal variates once q mean/covariance normalization is supplied. The W2 theorem is distributional and supplies no explicit sample-to-Gaussian coupling algorithm.
acquisition_oracle_geometry_conditioning.density_support_oracle: No sampler is supplied. Hit-and-run or another sampler must separately charge density/line-restriction integration, warm-start ratio M, convex-body geometry, and finite-precision error. KLS improves a conductance premise but such sampling consequences are prior art and not a novel result here.
acquisition_oracle_geometry_conditioning.normalization_conditioning: Center and whiten q. If output covariance Sigma_q is supplied and lambda_min(Sigma_q)>0, whitening gives G8( Sigma_q^(-1/2)(chi-Echi),p ) <= lambda_min(Sigma_q)^(-2) G8(chi,p). Reduce to the covariance support rank when q is singular. Estimating/certifying the mean and covariance has additional data/sample costs not included in the theorem.
acquisition_oracle_geometry_conditioning.moment_acquisition: G8 must have an analytic or certified upper bound; a finite empirical moment estimate alone does not certify it absent tail assumptions. Compact support and a bound on chi derivatives/images are needed for concrete ranges.
acquisition_oracle_geometry_conditioning.finite_precision: If each transformed summand has deterministic Euclidean error <= delta_chi, normalized-sum error is <= sqrt(n) delta_chi. If X error <= delta_x and chi is L_chi-Lipschitz on support, error is <= sqrt(n)L_chi delta_x. To reserve epsilon_num take delta_chi<=epsilon_num/sqrt(n), delta_x<=epsilon_num/(L_chi sqrt(n)); bit depth also requires support/output ranges and arithmetic model. Constants C0 and C_* are non-effective in the sources, so no numerical n threshold or end-to-end bit complexity follows.

claims.exact_statement: For every even N=2m with even m>=4 and every 0<epsilon<1, two connected 2m-cycles can have all vertex degrees 2, the same m unit-conductance and m epsilon-conductance edges, and the same opposite source/sink vertices, while their effective conductances are G_A=(1+epsilon)/m and G_B=4 epsilon/[m(1+epsilon)], respectively. Their ratio (1+epsilon)^2/(4 epsilon) is unbounded as epsilon approaches zero. Therefore local degree and edge-conductance histograms alone do not determine or uniformly lower-bound boundary throughput in this reversible linear-response hopping model.
assumptions: Finite undirected graph with fixed topology and positive symmetric edge conductances.
Reversible hopping and linear response near equilibrium, so effective conductance is given by the Dirichlet principle.
Conductance is measured between fixed opposite vertices of the cycle; no alternate bulk or surface path is included.
claims.status: internally_proved_exact_finite_network_result; standard effective-resistance mathematics; no novelty claim and no catalyst validation

claims.costs: The mathematical example has O(N) vertices and edges and uses no fitted data. A physical transfer requires operando spectroscopy, Faradaic/O2 balance, proton-sensitive impedance or flux measurement, catalyst ECSA/state, and sufficiently long AIMD or validated reactive-MD trajectories with uncertainty and autocorrelation accounting. Full-cell voltage is needed for device input work.
claims.falsifier: An arithmetic error in the path resistances or a violation of the fixed reversible linear-response interface would invalidate the proposition as stated. For the proposed experimental extension, if connectivity/time-correlation adds no held-out predictive value beyond matched local coordination and barrier marginals, that extension is rejected.
