ledger.exact_statement: Fix n,s>=1. For every admissible noncommutative rational formula Phi over Q of tree size <=s, there is an exact black-box protocol using only n,s and at most one query per trial to an oracle Eval_Phi(X) that returns UNDEFINED on any original-tree inverse-domain failure, else the complete exact rational D-by-D value matrix. The protocol samples one parameter triple uniformly from {1,...,G'}^3, where G'=2^ceil(log2 G), G=1+3(s+2)B M^3, B=2s+1, Delta=2(n+1)^3 B, M is the least power of two >B Delta, D=M^2/2; it constructs X_i=Z_0^-1 Z_i when Z_0 is nonsingular and accepts exactly when Eval_Phi(X) is defined and invertible. For every operationally nonzero Phi, per-trial acceptance probability is >1/2; for every operationally zero Phi, acceptance probability is 0. After r independent trials, a nonzero Phi is accepted with probability >=1-2^-r. A trial uses 3 log2(G') random bits, candidate input length O((n+s+1)^36 log(n+s+1)), per-entry query-coordinate height O((n+s+1)^15 log(n+s+1)), D=O((n+s+1)^10), and can be implemented in O((n+s+1)^96 log^3(n+s+1)) bit operations with elementary arithmetic and a conservative Cramer-rule implementation. Formula oracle time and response length are additional charged costs and have no bound in n,s alone because rational leaf constants have no height bound.
assumptions: The formula is promised admissible in the operational sense of the pinned source.
The size bound s and variable count n are supplied in unary.
The evaluation oracle uses exact rational matrix semantics and respects every inverse occurrence in the original tree.

If the oracle returns matrix values, the protocol can test exact rational nonsingularity; a bit-only alternative must itself provide a correct defined-and-invertible predicate and its computation cost is charged.
The source's internal algebraic proof of the universal list construction is accepted; this report reconstructs rather than independently certifies that proof.
ledger.novelty_boundary: The success-probability claim is a direct Schwartz-Zippel corollary of the pinned paper's parameter-grid degree estimate, not a new universal hitting-list theorem. Existing randomized black-box rational identity testing is prior art; no priority claim is made. Companion single-point theorems cover division-free formulas only. Astra N51 is an unreviewed internal all-field integer-list candidate and not independent validation.

costs.random_bits: 3 log2(G')=O(log(n+s+1)) per trial, with G'=next power of two >= G
costs.query_input_bits: O((n+s+1)^36 log(n+s+1)) per attempted nonsingular-normalizer tuple
costs.coordinate_height_bits: O((n+s+1)^15 log(n+s+1)) per rational matrix entry encoding
costs.sampler_bit_time: O((n+s+1)^96 log^3(n+s+1)) per trial under classical integer arithmetic and the stated coarse Cramer implementation
costs.oracle_response: Exact full D-by-D rational matrix or UNDEFINED; actual response length L and oracle evaluation cost C_Phi(X) are charged separately; no bound in n,s alone
costs.precision: Exact only; no finite-precision robustness claim

ledger.falsifier: For a valid nonzero admissible formula, exhibit that the product determinant polynomial P_Phi used in §§3-5 can be identically zero or has degree >=G/2, or that some grid triple with P_Phi nonzero fails to give a defined invertible rational evaluation. A source-proof error in Proposition 3.2, Proposition 4.2, or Proposition 5.1 would also invalidate the corollary.

Binary endpoint phases A,B at zero energy and target AB at -0.10 eV/atom produce a stable target in the panel; an omitted A2B phase at composition x_B=1/3 and energy -0.30 eV/atom yields a mass-balanced mixture at x_B=1/2 with energy -0.225 eV/atom, rendering AB unstable.
assumptions: No lower energy bound or exhaustive enumeration is supplied for omitted phases.
ledger.novelty_boundary: Elementary but load-bearing scope boundary; GNoME and the 2026 seven-facet preprint also state discoveries are relative to known/declared phase sets and that structure search remains unresolved.

claims.exact_statement: For a finite complete competitor universe Omega, target upper bound U_t, and certified independent lower bounds L_z on every competing phase, let H_L(x_t)=min{sum_z lambda_z L_z: lambda>=0, sum lambda=1, sum lambda x_z=x_t}. The target is stable for every allowed interval completion iff U_t<=H_L(x_t). By LP strong duality this is equivalent to an affine plane ell with ell(x_t)>=U_t and ell(x_z)<=L_z for every competitor z.
assumptions: Omega contains every admissible competing phase, including omitted structures and same-composition polymorphs.
All energies and compositions use the same per-atom thermodynamic convention, target fidelity, temperature, and pressure.
Energy uncertainty is an independent box with target upper bound U_t and competitor lower bounds L_z.
The target composition is a feasible convex combination of competitor compositions; LP arithmetic/rounding is certified.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard robust LP and convex-hull duality applied to a complete finite phase universe; not a new hull algorithm. If the LP fails, an unstable completion exists inside the supplied independent interval box, so any stronger claim needs extra information.

costs.acquisition: Must supply certified lower bounds for all competing phases or complete enumeration; this can dominate DFT/structure-search cost.
costs.runtime: One hull LP plus a primal/dual witness; polynomial in encoded finite input, excluding structure generation and energy acquisition.
costs.nature_boundary: A PBE certificate concerns PBE; experimental claims require matched Gibbs-energy intervals and model-error coverage.

claims.falsifier: A phase in Omega has energy below its claimed L_z, or a checked LP primal/dual witness violates the asserted inequalities.

claims.exact_statement: Freeze a support plane ell with ell(x_t)>=U_t and an audit law Q over omitted phase IDs. For the alternative class where the target is unstable by at least eta and Q({z:E_z<=ell(x_z)-eta})>=rho, independent Q draws with exact energy queries or deterministic error epsilon<eta miss all detectable plane violations with probability at most (1-rho)^m. Thus m>=ceil(log(delta)/log(1-rho)) bounds false global-stable output by delta.
assumptions: The plane and Q are frozen before an independent audit; Q's support and candidate generator are declared.
Every alternative in scope has energy-depth eta and bad-set probability at least rho; this is an extra premise, not implied by instability.
Each queried energy has deterministic error at most epsilon<eta, or a separately justified detection probability is supplied.
The target energy is bounded by U_t<=ell(x_t); only alternatives satisfying the stated depth and coverage conditions are protected.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard independent-sampling miss bound applied to a plane-violation set. Does not prove a realistic materials Q has positive rho, and does not cover instability gaps below eta.

costs.DFT: m candidate-generation/relaxation/high-fidelity energy evaluations; actual core-hours and failure rates must be recorded.
costs.synthesis: With per-attempt detection floor p_min, miss bound is (1-rho*p_min)^m; charge each attempt and characterization. Failed synthesis is censored.
costs.sample_size: m=ceil(log(delta)/log(1-rho)); e.g. rho=0.01 and delta=0.05 requires 299 independent queries.

claims.falsifier: A fully enumerated blind benchmark finds Q(bad set)<rho, a claimed low phase below the detection margin is missed above delta, or measured query error violates epsilon.
claims.next_gate: Pre-register and validate rho, eta, and oracle error on a frozen, fully enumerated chemical benchmark before any global-certification claim.

claims.exact_statement: For N known IDs with exact query answers, a null with no destabilizer and an alternative that changes exactly one uniformly random ID to a deep destabilizer have transcript total variation m/N after m distinct adaptive queries. The equal-prior minimax testing error is exactly (1-m/N)/2. If stable-null certification probability is at least 1-alpha, average false-stable probability is at least (1-m/N)(1-alpha); alpha=0 and false-stable target delta require m>= (1-delta)N.
assumptions: Finite known ID universe, exact answers, and alternatives differ from the null only at the hidden ID.
Hidden ID is uniform for the average-case statement; the one-sided certificate bound averages over this prior.
No structural lower bound or informative prior over candidate IDs is supplied.
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary oracle indistinguishability bound, not materials-specific discovery evidence. It applies equally to CAL/GNoME when given identical oracle information and no valid prior/lower-bound service.

claims.exact_statement: A denominator-M grid of normalized compositions over q elements contains binom(M+q-1,q-1) points; with S candidate structures per composition it has S*binom(M+q-1,q-1) IDs. Under a global L-Lipschitz phase-family residual and instability depth eta, an eta/(2L)-net detects a plane violation of depth at least eta/2 in every family; with family weight w_min and composition density q_min, a random radius-eta/(2L) hit has mass at least w_min*q_min*c_q*(eta/(2L))^(q-1), where c_q is a domain ball-volume lower bound.
assumptions: Phase structure families have globally Lipschitz energy residuals across the simplex; isolated stoichiometric phases may violate this premise.
A deterministic net covers every family, or the random audit law has family-weight and density lower bounds.
For sampled eta/2-depth violations, query error is below eta/2.
claims.novelty_boundary: Simplex counting and Lipschitz covering argument; scientific utility depends on measuring family coverage, smoothness, and structural completeness.

The laws of the complete coefficient maps on a square coupon of side w have total-variation distance at most w/L. For N independent coupons, total variation is at most min(1,Nw/L), and every estimator has worst-case expected operator-norm error at least ((K-1)^2/(4(K+1)))*(1-Nw/L)_+.
assumptions: Continuum scalar steady diffusion equation -div(a grad u)=0 in two dimensions.
Perfectly bonded ideal alternating layers; no interface resistance or non-Fourier effects.
Uniform random phase on the period 2L; coupons are independent draws from one of the two ensembles.
Each coupon observation is a function of its complete coefficient restriction to a square of side w; w<=L.

claims.exact_statement: Let ell>0, K>1, gamma=1-1/K, and let each of M=nN disjoint cells independently have conductivity K with unknown probability p in [1/4,3/4] and conductivity 1 otherwise. A width-n*ell coupon's exact two-terminal DtN map has conductance G=[ell(n-gamma B)]^(-1), where B is the number of K-cells, so the coupon responses jointly contain exactly the information in M iid Bernoulli(p) observations. With D_K=gamma/(1-3gamma/4)^2, the minimax expected absolute error for A_hom(p)=(1-gamma*p)^(-1) lies between D_K/(82*sqrt(M)) and D_K/(2*sqrt(M)). For 0<epsilon<=D_K/64 and 0<delta<=1/8, M >= D_K^2/(2 epsilon^2)*log(2/delta) is sufficient and M > 3D_K^2/(1024 epsilon^2)*log(1/(4delta)) is necessary for confidence 1-delta. Thus the sample law is Theta(D_K^2 epsilon^(-2) log(1/delta)) up to universal factors. If resistance error is bounded by eta_R<gamma*ell/2, each B is decoded exactly; coupon width and count trade through nN>=M_min.
assumptions: One-dimensional scalar steady conduction with perfectly bonded cells of known length ell and exact phase conductivities 1 and K.
Cell phases are iid Bernoulli(p); coupons consist of disjoint aligned blocks, so coupon observations are independent.
The unknown p belongs to the supplied interval [1/4,3/4]; K, ell, coupon alignment and the resistance-error bound are supplied/calibrated.
The observation is the complete two-terminal DtN map or its scalar resistance with worst-case error less than gamma*ell/2.

It does not falsify the conditional minimax proof.

claims.exact_statement: Under Fischer-Neukamm's differentiable scale-ell spectral-gap hypotheses and a case-by-case R-periodized law agreeing with the original coefficient law on central balls of radius R/4, the periodic RVE tensor has stretched-exponential random fluctuation scale (R/ell)^(-d/2). Its no-extra-small-scale-regularity bias is C_b(R/ell)^(-(d wedge 4)/2) times the stated critical logarithm; with their condition (R), the power improves to d wedge 4. This yields the stated sufficient single-coupon and median-of-means width/count recipes after charging tensor-response error. Separately, for iid uniformly elliptic discrete lattice edge conductances in d>=2, Gloria-Neukamm-Otto Theorem 2 gives RMSE at most C(d,K)[N^(-1/2)s^(-d/2)+s^(-d)(log s)^d] for N independent periodic RVEs.
assumptions: Fischer-Neukamm bound requires their differentiable spectral-gap inequality, monotone uniformly elliptic operator assumptions, and an R-periodized ensemble whose existence is proved case-by-case; discrete-valued sharp binary fields are not automatically covered by the derivative-form inequality.
The iid bound is for a discrete uniformly elliptic lattice network, iid edge law, periodic RVE ensemble and torus-cell interface. An open crop does not supply seam conductances automatically.
The full-DtN-to-periodic-cell variational identity assumes exact continuum response; finite boundary bases require charged calibration and response-error bounds.

claims.claim: For C with (Cu)_i=q1*u_i+q2*u_(i+1), q1,q2>0 and unequal, H0=C^T C has a geometric zero mode and ideal bulk gap Delta=(q2-q1)^2. Adding endpoint penalty kappa lifts the mode at first order with coefficient equal to the normalized zero mode endpoint weight rho.

no prestress
unit masses or stated generalized-coordinate norm
only the specified positive-semidefinite endpoint penalty
q1 and q2 positive and unequal

claims.argument: A local boundary support term changes the low mode eigenvalue and edge compliance while leaving bulk winding unchanged. Material hinge stiffness, prestress, clamping and finite-size overlap also vary independently of the index.

Standard eigenspace perturbation controls mode rotation when kappa norm(P) is small relative to the gap.

claims.claim: For a quasistatically equilibrated reversible passive material with a single-valued Helmholtz free energy, arbitrary internal coordinates, ideal unilateral frictionless contact, and all controlled coordinates/ports included, a closed complete-state cycle has zero net all-port work.
claims.proof: At equilibrium, dPsi=P dot dq+sum_j lambda_j dg_j. Complementarity and sustained ideal contact imply lambda_j dg_j=0 almost everywhere. Thus delta W_all,on=dPsi, and integration over a complete-state closed cycle gives zero.
assumptions: quasistatic equilibrium at every point
single-valued stored Helmholtz free energy for the complete system
complete internal state and contact/slider geometry return to the initial state
all external mechanical work ports are included
unilateral contact is ideal, frictionless, non-adhesive, and no finite-power impact occurs
claims.falsifier: Synchronized all-port raw data show closed-state net work outside propagated uncertainty while independently confirming reversible equilibrium, no omitted ports, and complete state return.
claims.costs: Analytical proof is O(number of generalized coordinates plus active contact constraints); physical validation requires calibrated force/torque and displacement/rotation histories at every port, state/contact observation, and uncertainty propagation.

claims.claim: Passive viscoelastic or frictional systems cannot deliver net work on a cycle returning their complete internal state; all-port work input equals nonnegative dissipation.
claims.proof: For an isothermal passive system, delta W_all,on=dPsi+delta D with delta D>=0. On a complete-state cycle W_all,on=D>=0; output work is therefore nonpositive.
assumptions: passive constitutive evolution
nonnegative dissipation
complete state return
all reservoirs and actuators counted

claims.claim: The Shaat-Park 2023 source-free reversible cycle satisfies its stated Eq. (31) and yields nonzero net work with zero free-energy change.
evidence: Eq. (31), p. 14: delta W=dPsi for each reversible isothermal process; prose says the proposed passive solids always satisfy it.
Closed cycle returns to the stated zero-stress/reference state, so integral dPsi=0.
§4.1.2 and Fig. 5 report W approximately 16.6 kJ/m^3 for the favorable cycle and about -16 kJ/m^3 for another.
Eq. (32), p. 15, splits work into a potential differential and delta w_cn, which the authors state cannot be obtained from potential energy.
claims.resolution: At least one premise must be dropped: work is omitted at an actuator port; the constitutive contribution is active/non-equilibrium and not an equilibrium free-energy differential; the complete state is not closed; or the claimed cycle work is a modeling/accounting error.

claims.claim: The 2023 paper proves the rigid slider used to modulate circle profile contributes zero cycle work because endpoint stress is unchanged.
evidence: Appendix A.1 states that the slider mechanism is needed and moves rigidly up/down at states 3 and 4.
The paper infers zero energy contribution from unchanged stress state at the switch endpoints.
No slider actuator force/torque versus travel trace or integral is reported; the FEA energy check is described for deformation processes separately.
claims.valid_omitted_port: Generalized actuator work W_slider,on=sum_s integral F_s,specimen da_s, including all slider motions. Endpoint stress equality does not evaluate this path integral.
claims.qualification: The paper does not establish that slider work is nonzero; it also does not establish that it is zero. A measured nonzero value would explain output as externally driven work, while a rigorously zero value leaves the constitutive/Eq. (31) contradiction unresolved.

claims.claim: The reported approximately 16.6 kJ/m^3 cycle output is validated by public raw all-port physical data.
claims.evidence: The paper reports finite-element calculations and plotted increments (Appendix A.1 states N=40000); no raw all-port history for slider force/travel is available in the cited manuscript.
claims.falsifier: For the claimed output W_boundary,on=-16.6 kJ/m^3, measure W_slider,on and every other input port. A passive closed cycle requires W_slider,on+W_other,on=16.6 kJ/m^3+D, within uncertainty. Output with all measured input below that bound falsifies the source-free passive account; matching slider input identifies the drive.

claims.claim: Odd elasticity with nonzero closed-cycle work is already associated in primary literature with nonconservative/active interactions.
claims.evidence: Scheibner et al. state odd moduli are forbidden by energy conservation, derive cycle work proportional to enclosed strain-space area, and describe active bond forces.

claims.claim: A passive-component mechanical metamaterial can exhibit driven odd response when an external mechanical drive is explicitly applied.
claims.evidence: Rahimi and Park use periodically driven chiral gears, frictional tooth-wall contact, and detachment/recontact; the paper identifies the periodic mechanical loading as the input energy source.
claims.scope_limit: This is driven odd elasticity, not source-free equilibrium pumping; source is a 2026 arXiv preprint and reports FE simulations.

raw_channels: all boundary force and displacement histories
all boundary moment and rotation/spin histories
specimen-side slider force/torque and travel at every profile switch
all electrical, thermal, or chemical input ports
decisive_measurement.criterion: For reversible equilibrium, DeltaPsi=D=0 and R=0 within uncertainty. For passive dissipation D>=0 and all-port input equals D. A boundary output of 16.6 kJ/m^3 requires at least that much net positive slider/other input plus dissipation.

costs.source_computation: The primary paper uses a 4x4 lattice and 40000 increments per cycle. An auditable rerun adds slider degrees of freedom and exports force-travel, boundary work, internal energy, contact dissipation, and residual at each increment.
costs.physical_test: Requires an aluminum 4x4 sample and profiled sliders; translation/rotation stage; calibrated boundary load/torque and specimen-side slider sensors; DIC/contact observation; calibration coupons; repeats in both orientations; and propagated uncertainty. Dollar cost is unknown because fabrication and instrumentation choices are unspecified.
costs.evidence_limit: No physical all-port data or raw slider trace was located in the primary manuscript; no empirical result is claimed here.

ledger.exact_statement: For a finite square two-dimensional nearest-neighbor Ising torus with Hamiltonian E(σ)=-J sum_<x,y> σ_x σ_y-H sum_x σ_x, J>0, H>0, all-minus initial state, low-temperature limit β→∞, fixed volume large enough to contain the critical droplet without wraparound, and standard Glauber dynamics, away from critical-size degeneracies 2J/H∈N, the critical side is ℓ=floor(2J/H)+1 and the critical saddle is an ℓ×(ℓ−1) droplet plus one protuberance. Its energy above all-minus is Γ=8Jℓ−2H(ℓ²−ℓ+1), which sets the established exponential scale of metastable escape.
assumptions: finite periodic square lattice
nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising coupling
uniform positive field
β→∞ with fixed finite volume
volume fits critical droplet and excludes torus wrapping
standard single-spin Glauber rates
nondegenerate field 2J/H not an integer for unique simple shape statement
ledger.novelty_boundary: Classical Ising metastability result; no novelty claimed. Application to real materials is not established.

costs.model: Finite state space grows exponentially in lattice area for exact enumeration; direct KMC waiting time scales exponentially in βΓ.
costs.data: Requires repeated first-passage observations if used as a measurement design.
costs.energy: J,H,Γ are model energies; physical work and compute joules are unreported.

ledger.falsifier: Within the stated model, a low-temperature critical path or escape exponent inconsistent with the critical droplet barrier falsifies the parameter, volume, or rate assumptions; for a material, mismatch falsifies the material-to-Ising mapping, not the theorem.
ledger.next_gate: Reconstruct the exact theorem statements and boundary conditions from the full Neves–Schonmann text and check exceptional-field cases before using a degenerate field.

ledger.exact_statement: For the square-lattice Ising model with J=1, the standard hard Glauber rate W_hard=(1+exp(βΔE))^−1 and factorized soft rate W_soft=(1+exp(βΔE_J))^−1(1+exp(βΔE_H))^−1 both satisfy detailed balance for the same Hamiltonian, but Park et al. report Γ_soft=Γ_hard+2H for 0<H<4 in the low-temperature nucleation regime. At H=3/2, ℓ=2, Γ_hard=7, Γ_soft=10, and reported prefactors are 3/8 and 1/8 in the paper's time convention.
assumptions: square-lattice Ising model
J=1 units
uniform positive field 0<H<4
low-temperature single-droplet nucleation
nonconserved single-spin-flip dynamics
specified hard or factorized soft rates
for the worked prefactor example 1<H<2 and H=3/2
ledger.novelty_boundary: Published 2004 result; not new. It refutes only the universal inference that Gibbs equilibrium or the static saddle energy alone determines kinetics within the named model family.

costs.simulation: Published check used L=24 and 2000 escape runs, or 6000 for fields at/above 4; source gives no wall-time or joule accounting.
costs.measurement: Requires independent nucleation trajectories over multiple temperatures at a fixed field; calibration costs for an actual material are unknown.
costs.compute: Brute-force updates scale with L² per sweep and exponentially long waiting time; rare-event acceleration has separate estimator costs.
costs.energy: No physical energy-per-sample or compute-energy measurement is available.

ledger.falsifier: At J=1,H=3/2, after confirming single-droplet conditions, fit log mean lifetime versus β: hard predicts slope 7 and soft predicts slope 10. Persistent disagreement rejects the corresponding kinetic rule or shared model assumptions.
ledger.next_gate: Independently replay the full-lattice absorbing-chain/kinetic-Monte-Carlo comparison and validate one calibrated material system before claiming physical transfer.

ledger.exact_statement: If first-nucleation times are independent exponential samples with mean A exp(βΓ), with temperature-independent A at two inverse temperatures β1,β2, then for M observations at each temperature, the log-mean slope estimator has exact variance 2 ψ1(M)/(β2−β1)^2. For large M, resolving an exponent gap 2H at z standard errors requires approximately M≥z²/[2H²(β2−β1)²] samples per temperature.
assumptions: independent exponential first-passage times
same prefactor A across the temperature window
single-droplet regime
no significant finite-temperature curvature
large-M normal approximation for the stated sample inequality
ledger.novelty_boundary: Elementary conditional sampling calculation, not a new metastability theorem or a validated experiment.

costs.data: M independent resets and event-time measurements per temperature and field; total exposure is about M times the sum of mean waiting times.
costs.compute: Direct kinetic Monte Carlo requires exponentially long waiting times in βΓ; actual wall time is unknown.
costs.energy: Laboratory and compute joules were not measured and remain unknown.

ledger.falsifier: The design assumptions fail if waiting-time data are not exponential, the fitted prefactor varies materially with temperature, or multiple nuclei appear before growth completes.

ledger.exact_statement: The Ising critical-droplet and hard/soft rate results do not by themselves imply a nucleation barrier, switching rate, or design recommendation for a real material with different order parameters, disorder, strain, transport, or transition-state kinetics.
assumptions: no specific material or measured kinetic data supplied

ledger.novelty_boundary: No physical-material claim is made. Yao–Jack's disordered-Ising findings are simulation results and do not certify a general reaction coordinate.

ledger.exact_statement: For a fixed finite connected undirected graph G=(V,E), disjoint nonempty A,B, state energies E_x, symmetric fixed prefactors a_e>0, and edge transition levels S_e, define μ_β(x)=exp(-βE_x), q_β(x,y)=a_e exp(-β(S_e-E_x)), and γ(S)=min over A-to-B paths of max edge S_e. The chain is reversible with conductance c_β(e)=a_e exp(-βS_e), and lim_{β→∞} -β^{-1}log cap_β(A,B)=γ(S). With E_A=min_{x∈A}E_x, lim_{β→∞}-β^{-1}log(cap_β(A,B)/μ_β(A))=γ(S)-E_A.
assumptions: fixed finite connected graph as β tends to infinity
positive symmetric edge prefactors independent of β
Arrhenius transition rates with a shared edge transition level in both directions
capacity defined by the reversible Dirichlet principle
ledger.novelty_boundary: Cirillo-Nardi-Sohier's general rare-transition communication-height and escape-exponent theory already includes transition costs. The present path/cut proof is an explicit reversible Arrhenius specialization; no priority claim is made.

costs.input: Full finite graph, state energies, and edge transition levels or conductances are required.
costs.compute: Bottleneck-path exponent can be computed by threshold connectivity in O(|E| log |E|); many-body state graph size can be exponential.
costs.physical_energy: No lab work, material sample energy, or compute joules were measured.

ledger.falsifier: A counterexample satisfying the finite reversible Arrhenius assumptions with a capacity exponent different from the minimum bottleneck edge level would falsify the theorem; the proof's path/cut bounds rule this out under its assumptions.
ledger.next_gate: Validate that a measured or simulated nucleation model has a fixed finite reversible Arrhenius graph and independently acquired transition levels.

ledger.exact_statement: On the three-state path 0-1-2 with energies (0,1,-1), unit edge prefactors, and A={0}, B={2}, edge levels (1,1) and (1,1+δ) yield identical Gibbs families, state-energy landscapes, state saddle, and transition topology but escape exponents 1 and 1+δ. Any exponent prediction based only on the shared static input has worst-case absolute error at least δ/2. Since δ can be arbitrarily large absent a kinetic bound, static data have no finite uniform exponent-error guarantee.
assumptions: same finite state graph and state energies for both models
detailed-balance Arrhenius edge rates as defined in PN-C2-01
δ>0 is not bounded by the supplied static information
ledger.novelty_boundary: The general fact that transition costs affect metastability is established prior art. This is an elementary sharp minimax witness isolating non-identifiability from Gibbs weights and state saddles; it is not claimed as a novel metastability theorem.

costs.input_missing: A static-only estimator omits edge transition levels or equivalent kinetic conductances.
costs.data: No physical data required for the mathematical counterexample.

ledger.falsifier: The exact mean hitting-time formula for this three-state chain or a Gibbs/state-saddle-only estimator with a uniform finite error bound over all δ would contradict the claim.
ledger.next_gate: Measure edge hazards or supply a justified finite interval for kinetic barriers; otherwise report the exponent as unidentifiable.

ledger.exact_statement: For a finite reversible CTMC with known state masses μ and correct graph, if directed edge counts N_e over fixed cumulative occupation exposure t_e are Poisson(t_e q_e), exact Garwood intervals with Bonferroni allocation α/|E| give simultaneous edge-rate coverage at least 1-α. Mapping to conductance intervals and using monotonicity of Dirichlet capacity yields a 1-α interval [cap(c^-)/μ(A), cap(c^+)/μ(A)] for the finite-temperature capacity-normalized rate. If known Arrhenius prefactors permit transforming rate intervals into edge-level intervals, the minimum-bottleneck-path functional yields a simultaneous confidence interval for the asymptotic exponent.
assumptions: finite reversible CTMC with correctly enumerated transition graph
known equilibrium masses μ for the finite-temperature rate interval
known cumulative occupation exposure in each source state and correctly labeled directed transitions
Poisson edge-count model is correct
known edge prefactors are additionally required for single-temperature asymptotic barrier transformation
ledger.novelty_boundary: Garwood intervals, Bonferroni coverage, and capacity monotonicity are standard ingredients. Their composition into this stated graph-rate interface is a conditional construction; novelty and priority have not been searched exhaustively or established.

costs.data: Requires state-labeled transition counts and occupation exposures on relevant edges; rare-event exposure scales as 1/q_e and can grow exponentially with β times the edge barrier.
costs.equilibrium: Known μ(A) or aggregated state masses may require exhaustive enumeration or umbrella sampling; that acquisition cost is not included in the edge-count interval.
costs.compute: Two finite weighted-Laplacian Dirichlet solves; dense worst-case O(|V|^3), sparse methods depend on graph conditioning.

ledger.falsifier: Under valid fixed-exposure CTMC sampling, repeated coverage trials below nominal coverage or a held-out rate outside its interval beyond sampling coverage would falsify at least one count, graph, reversibility, mass, or interval-propagation assumption.
ledger.next_gate: Implement the interval calculation on a specified graph and compare predictions against independent held-out first-passage or forward-flux samples.

ledger.exact_statement: For a preregistered nucleation coarse state z=(n,j), where n is largest stable-phase cluster size and j a candidate nucleation location, edge-hazard capacity estimation gives an exact reduced-chain rate interval only if the projection is Markov-sufficient (strong lumpability suffices) and reversible. Committor concentration and lag-transition checks are necessary falsification gates for this proposed reduction; failure requires more coordinates or the microscopic state graph.

strong lumpability or another proof of Markov sufficiency
reversible aggregated generator and known aggregated equilibrium masses
independently acquired transition-hazard data
ledger.novelty_boundary: Yao-Jack's RFIM simulations already motivate location-augmented reaction coordinates and show residual shape-fluctuation deviations. This graph-capacity estimator is a conditional proposed interface; no claim of general physical adequacy or methodological priority is made.

claims.exact_statement: Let U(x,y) be C2 and scalar, with a unique smooth equilibrium minimizer y*(x) for each controlled deformation x and positive-definite U_yy. The reduced equilibrium response f(x)=+/- grad F(x), F(x)=U(x,y*(x)), has symmetric tangent K_eff=U_xx-U_xy U_yy^{-1} U_yx and zero work on every closed quasistatic x-cycle. The same conclusion holds for differentiable equilibrium Helmholtz free energy and for frictionless contact when all internal coordinates are included in a single-valued constrained energy minimization.
assumptions: all internal mechanical/contact states are included in y
the material is in equilibrium at each x and returns to the same full state
a scalar stored energy or equilibrium free energy exists
the reduced state is unique and smooth for the displayed tangent formula; nonsmooth contact transitions retain a single-valued reduced potential
no externally powered, chemical, thermal-gradient, or other work port is omitted
source_pointers: Derivation is included in the report; it follows from the envelope theorem and the Schur complement of the Hessian of U.
The 2023 target paper itself states reversible isothermal delta W=d psi in PDF p.13, lines 1491-1510.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard reciprocity/thermodynamic integrability result; no novelty or priority claim. It excludes only source-free equilibrated models within the listed assumptions, not all passive viscoelastic or driven systems.

costs.theorem: No oracle or computation; model requires the complete internal state and potential.
costs.physical_test: Two-coordinate actuation, all boundary force/torque sensing, internal-state/contact imaging, and synchronized work integration.

claims.next_gate: Independently audit force/coordinate conjugacy and all ports in the target finite-element model, then test a specimen under repeated cycles.

Under those stated premises, integration forces the cycle work to be zero; the claimed nonzero value cannot follow unless a premise, state-closure assertion, or work accounting is changed.
assumptions: the paper's Eq. (31) applies to each increment of the claimed cycle
psi is a state function and the final full state equals the initial state
delta W is the same cumulative external work used in the later closed-cycle claim
source_pointers: PDF pp. 13-14, lines 1491-1538: Eq. (31), state-function closure, and claimed nonzero work.
PDF pp. 23-25, lines 2640-2712: FE energy balance claim, zero endpoint energy/displacements, and accumulated-work calculation.

claims.exact_statement: For a postulated constant two-coordinate constitutive matrix K and a closed strain path of oriented area A, signed work is W=(K21-K12)A=2 kappa A, where kappa=(K21-K12)/2. A repeatable powered device with work-like drive delivering W_out per cycle of period T must receive drive work at least W_out plus dissipative losses each cycle; therefore P_drive >= W_out/T + P_loss. Thermal drive must be compared through available free energy (exergy), not raw heat. Without replenishment, a finite available-free-energy reservoir B obeys N W_out <= B over N cycles, before losses.
assumptions: linear constant constitutive response over the tested range
x_1 and x_2 are conjugate deformation/load coordinates
the full device is in a periodic steady state for the powered bound
the source term in P_drive is work-like energy; heat-driven cycles require an exergy balance
W_out is positive delivered mechanical work and P_loss is separately measured
source_pointers: Nature Communications 2021 paper derives odd-modulus work proportional to strain-space area and reports a piezoelectric/circuit-driven metamaterial.
Rahimi and Park 2026 preprint uses periodic driving of chiral gears and reports an effective odd shear modulus.
claims.novelty_boundary: Area-work identity and first-law accounting are standard. They are used here as an explicit cost equation for comparing powered dynamic structures with claimed source-free materials.

costs.measurement: Integrate load-cell force times displacement, torque times angle, electrical voltage times current, and chemical work ports over each period. For heat-driven cycles, meter heat and reservoir temperatures to compute available exergy.
costs.uncertainty: For exact displacement samples, force error epsilon_f, path length L, maximum sample step h, and force Lipschitz bound M_f, left-Riemann work error is at most epsilon_f L + M_f h L/2; other sensor and synchronization errors must be added.

claims.falsifier: A calibrated, closed, periodic device output exceeding the sum of all measured replenished input work and any reduction in stored free energy would contradict the full-system energy balance or indicate an unmeasured port.
claims.next_gate: Measure all mechanical and nonmechanical input ports on the driven specimen and report net useful output, heat, cycle time, reset cost, and cycle drift.

claims.exact_statement: For a complete passive system coupled to one heat bath at fixed temperature T, with every work port counted and no other exergy input, a process returning the complete state or its full distribution obeys W_on = T Sigma >= 0. Here W_on is net work into the complete system and Sigma is total entropy production. For a noncyclic process, W_out <= F_initial - F_final.
assumptions: First law Delta U=Q+W_on, with Q entering and W_on positive inward.
Single reservoir at T and Clausius relation Delta S=Q/T+Sigma, Sigma>=0.
System includes material, hidden contact/phase/spin coordinates, actuators/controllers, and stores claimed as passive.
All mechanical, electrical, magnetic, chemical, actuator, and other work/exergy inputs are counted.
For stochastic systems, entropy/free energy refer to the complete state distribution.
source_pointers: Delta F=Delta U-T Delta S=W_on-T Sigma; for a full-state cycle Delta F=0.
Standard first/second-law derivation; no novelty or priority claim.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard thermodynamic passivity bound. A single port may deliver positive work if another counted port supplies it; finite output is allowed when available free energy decreases.

claims.exact_statement: Ideal frictionless unilateral contact with gap g(q,s)>=0 and compressive multiplier lambda>=0 is not an energy source. At fixed geometry, an active quasistatic branch has g=0 and g_dot=0, hence ideal contact power lambda*g_dot=0; an open branch has lambda=0. If the gap depends on slider coordinate s, that slider is an additional work port. Hysteretic switching requires accounting for dissipation or hidden-state change.
assumptions: Ideal normal complementarity contact, no adhesion, frictional drive, or hidden active control.
Admissible quasistatic motion respects active contact constraints.
Any profile coordinate s is counted with its conjugate actuator work.
source_pointers: Contact-power derivation in report.
Shaat and Park, printed pp. 6-7 and 23: normal contact and profile-switching mechanism.

claims.exact_statement_assumptions: For M independent monovalent (+e,-e) pairs on an odd periodic d-dimensional lattice, let physical coordinates be x+=u+v and x-=u-v. In each coordinate, symmetric u jumps of +/- one site occur at rate a and symmetric v jumps of +/- one site at rate b, with a,b>0; pair events are allowed regardless of pair separation. At zero field this process is irreducible and reversible with a parameter-independent uniform equilibrium law. Each ion's complete marginal path law is the same continuous-time nearest-neighbour walk whenever a+b=lambda is held fixed, with D+=D-=a0^2 lambda. Yet at density nu=M/V, sigma=4 beta e^2 a0^2 b nu and sigma_NE=2 beta e^2 a0^2(a+b)nu, so sigma/sigma_NE=2b/(a+b). Thus identical one-ion path marginals and equilibrium law permit sigma arbitrarily close to 0 or 2 sigma_NE. The concerted event is a toy kinetic coupling, not a short-range interaction model.
claims.status: exact internally proved conditional model theorem; independent review, scientific novelty/priority, and nature validation unresolved

claims.exact_statement_assumptions: For two independent periodic one-dimensional channels of L sites and spacing a, with N hard-core ions of charge +q in one channel and N ions of charge -q in the other, each particle-vacancy exchange occurring at rate gamma per active nearest-neighbor bond, let V=2 A L a and F be the total number of unlike neighboring occupancy pairs over the two channels. The finite product-canonical process is irreducible and reversible. Under stationarity, the total unwrapped charge displacement Q_t is a martingale with predictable bracket q^2 a^2 gamma integral_0^t F(eta_s) ds. Since E_pi F=4N(L-N)/(L-1), the one-dimensional EH conductivity is exactly sigma_L=beta q^2 a gamma N(L-N)/(A L(L-1)); if N/L tends to rho in (0,1), sigma tends to beta q^2 a gamma rho(1-rho)/A. The model-specific observable integral F is unbiased and conductivity-identifying when gamma and the other parameters are supplied.

claims.exact_statement_assumptions: For the preceding model, start R independent trajectories from the product canonical stationary distribution, each of duration t. claims.exact_statement: Let w(x)=1/[4*cosh(x/2)^2], x=(E-mu)/(k_B*T), and let a measurable transport profile phi satisfy 0<=phi<=1. Define A=integral(phi*w), B=integral(x*phi*w), C=integral(x^2*phi*w), and a_lat=kappa_l/(Sigma_max*k_B^2*T)>0 for a fixed positive lattice thermal conductivity and a uniform pointwise cap Sigma_max. Then normalized PF=B^2/A and ZT=B^2/[A*(C+a_lat)-B^2]. For each admissible profile with A>0 there is an interval J, including a half-line at an extreme first moment, with the same A and B and with C_J<=C. Therefore the supremum of ZT over all profiles satisfying normalized PF>=p0 equals the supremum over saturated interval profiles phi=1_J, for every feasible p0>0. This is a global two-endpoint reduction of the full maximum-ZT-at-minimum-power-factor design problem within the stated moment model.

ledger.evidence_convention: Source-reported literature, internally reconstructed model results, finite computations, and nature-level evidence are distinguished. No nature-level profile or material result was acquired.

claims.exact_statement: For fixed-sign branch B>0, let A,B,C,a lie in the literal box [A_lo,A_hi] x [B_lo,B_hi] x [C_lo,C_hi] x [a_lo,a_hi], with A_lo>0, a_lo>0, B_lo>0, and denominator positive throughout. For PF=B^2/A and ZT=B^2/[A(C+a)-B^2], the exact infima over the box are PF_lower=B_lo^2/A_hi and ZT_lower=B_lo^2/[A_hi(C_hi+a_hi)-B_lo^2]. If the uncertainty radii are profile-independent, the supremum of ZT_lower subject to PF_lower>=p0 over measurable 0<=phi<=1 equals the supremum over saturated energy intervals, including limiting half-lines. The same interval reduction holds when radii depend on center moments A,B only.
assumptions: Single-temperature near-equilibrium Boltzmann/RTA moment model with w(x)=1/[4 cosh(x/2)^2].
Uniform pointwise cap Sigma_max is supplied and the normalized transport profile is measurable with 0<=phi<=1.
The normalized lattice leak a is positive and independent of changes to phi; its uncertainty is represented by the supplied interval.
The B uncertainty interval stays on one sign branch; reflection x->-x handles the opposite sign.
The rectangular moment/leak set is the stated adversarial set. It can conservatively include physically infeasible combinations because A,B,C share one spectrum.
The uncertainty radii do not vary with profile beyond possible dependence on A,B.
claims.proof_path: work/agents/materials_energy/thermoelectric/CYCLE2_REPORT.md, section 'Interface and exact robust certificate'; base equal-moment rearrangement is reconstructed in work/agents/materials_energy/thermoelectric/FINAL_REPORT.md, section 'Conditional Pareto theorem'.
claims.novelty_boundary: The corner evaluation is generic monotonicity and the interval shape is already central in bounded-transport and Landauer thermoelectric optimization. Ding's article text directly reports a boxcar optimal transmission for arbitrary density-of-modes bounds M(x) and lattice conductance parameter beta. The present robust PF-floor equality is an equal-moment/rearrangement extension; no priority claim is made. Supplementary source proofs were not fully reconstructed in this cycle.
costs: Acquire a simultaneous uncertainty region for A, B, C, and lattice leakage a, including covariance and calibration/systematic floors.
Measure or infer energy-resolved transport and the supplied transport cap; charge temperature control, energy resolution, sample preparation, and computation.
Measure kappa_l independently or report uncertainty induced by subtracting kappa_e from total kappa; charge every device heat path, including contacts, radiation, and parasitic conduction.
Charge feature resolution, filter fabrication, yield, interface resistance, profile drift, gates/control work, and any change in lattice conduction.
The finite endpoint search scales quadratically in number of energy-grid bins after cumulative moments are tabulated; the theorem itself does not require that discretization.
claims.falsifier: A verified tuple in the stated rectangular set with positive denominator whose PF or ZT falls below the displayed corner value falsifies the corner formula. A noninterval profile with the same A,B and the same profile-independent uncertainty bounds but greater worst-case ZT falsifies the interval reduction. If measurement radii depend on profile, the claim does not apply.
claims.next_gate: Acquire a named sample/device, energy-resolved transport distribution and cap, joint A/B/C covariance or confidence set, and an independent interval for kappa_l; then compare matched-A,B interval-filter and noninterval profiles including all contact and parasitic channels.

claims.exact_statement: For a fixed candidate with center moments A,B,C,a and deterministic moment/leak radii e_A,e_B,e_C,e_a on the positive-B branch, robust PF>=p0 and robust ZT>=z0 are equivalent to (B-e_B)^2>=p0(A+e_A) and (1+z0)(B-e_B)^2>=z0(A+e_A)(C+a+e_C+e_a), assuming positive robust denominator. Under e_i=q_i s_i/sqrt(n_i) with specified simultaneous-coverage multipliers q_i and noise scales s_i, minimizing acquisition energy sum_i u_i n_i over positive integer n_i subject to these inequalities is the exact conditional discrete measurement-allocation problem. In the small-error regime with PF slack, the continuous local relaxation with target-margin budget sum_i g_i e_i<=tau and cost sum_i alpha_i/e_i^2 has interior optimum e_i=tau*(alpha_i/g_i)^(1/3)/sum_j alpha_j^(1/3)g_j^(2/3), with minimum local cost [sum_j alpha_j^(1/3)g_j^(2/3)]^3/tau^2 and g=(z0(C+a),2(1+z0)B,z0 A,z0 A).
assumptions: Measurement intervals jointly cover the true parameter tuple at the stated confidence level; q_i are selected by an explicitly valid joint procedure or multiplicity adjustment.
Independent repeat model e_i=q_i s_i/sqrt(n_i) is appropriate over the sample and temperature range.
The closed-form allocation is a first-order local approximation, PF remains slack, and the optimum lies in the interior without systematic error floors or precision caps.
Acquisition energy per repeat u_i and the local cost coefficient alpha_i are supplied.
claims.novelty_boundary: Threshold algebra and local Lagrange allocation are generic robust-estimation/design mathematics, not a new thermoelectric measurement principle. The cited studies support the importance and real cost of uncertainty characterization, not the proposed noise law for a specific sample.
costs: Instrument and sample energy/time per acquisition, calibration, repeated specimens, joint confidence construction, and computational effort.
Systematic bias floors and drift prevent arbitrarily tight intervals and must be estimated independently.
Filter/gate/control operating work and fabrication energy are outside the local statistical allocation unless added to its cost function.
claims.falsifier: For supplied q_i,s_i,u_i and a declared simultaneous-coverage/error model, any allocation whose true covered parameters violate the claimed robust PF or ZT threshold falsifies the certificate implementation or coverage assumptions. A lower-cost integer allocation than a separately certified global optimum would falsify that optimizer; no global numerical optimizer is claimed here.
claims.next_gate: Measure the joint covariance and bias floor for the four channels on an actual material/device, then solve and verify the exact nonlinear allocation program against equal-total-energy allocation and the laboratory's existing standard protocol.

claims.exact_statement: There is no universal measurement-channel allocation or robust material-design policy derivable from the current task record: neither the joint uncertainty set, the confidence level, nor the precision-versus-time/energy/fabrication costs of A, B, C, and a were supplied. Two admissible positive cost vectors with opposite relative channel costs can reverse which channel receives the marginal measurement effort, so a data-independent ranking is not identifiable.
assumptions: The permitted measurement channels enter at least one active robust margin with positive sensitivity.
No acquisition noise/cost model beyond the generic task interface has been supplied.
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a nonidentifiability result about the missing inputs, not a claim that optimal measurement design is impossible once those inputs are measured.
costs: Any actionable policy must charge parameter estimation, confidence, systematic error, instrument energy, specimen acquisition, filter fabrication, and device operating work.
Realization of an ideal boxcar may change lattice conductivity and complete-device heat paths; these couplings are not represented by fixed a.
claims.falsifier: A supplied named material with validated joint uncertainty and cost functions would remove the missing-input premise and permit a numerical policy; it would not make a universal policy possible across arbitrary cost models.
claims.next_gate: Request no further abstract optimization. Resume with acquired material/device uncertainty and cost curves, and compare against a same-data center-ZT baseline subject to the same robust PF floor.

finite_computation.result: Center-ZT objective under robust PF floor chooses [1.76,6.30] with center ZT 5.1130242 and worst-box ZT 2.6056070. Worst-box objective chooses [1.46,5.18] with center ZT 4.8517173 and worst-box ZT 2.6984216. The latter raises the grid worst-case value about 3.6% and lowers center ZT about 5.1%. The radii are hypothetical and no confidence level is assigned.

claims.statement: For a fixed finite broadcast tree with K leaves, an individual pulled-back outcome effect is computed recursively by E_(a,b)=B*(E_a tensor E_b) using only d-by-d effects, in O(K) dense broadcaster-adjoint contractions.
assumptions: finite-dimensional broadcaster B:M_d->M_(d^2)
tree and local leaf effects are explicitly specified
B or B* is evaluable from a finite-bit dense descriptor
claims.limitations: Does not produce the exponentially long list of all tree effects.

claims.statement: The complete tree outcome z can be sampled under an input density sigma with probability Tr(E_z sigma) using a recursive left-marginal sampler and a d-by-d conditional right-root state chi=Tr_L[(E_a tensor I)B(sigma)]; at sigma=I/d the law is tau(E_z).
assumptions: the exact dense descriptor permits evaluating B(sigma), its marginal Phi(sigma), partial traces, and B* contractions
finite-precision sampling is allowed with inverse-polynomial total-variation error
claims.limitations: A device-only black box or arbitrary exact-real input does not give the same classical runtime guarantee.

claims.statement: For canonical effects E_z, with p_z=tau(E_z) and trace-one rho_z=E_z/Tr(E_z), the normalized-HS transfer map is d^2 E_p[|rho_z><rho_z|_tau]; on traceless space the sampled summand using rho_z-I/d has norm at most d and variance proxy at most dI.
assumptions: effects sum to I
sampling distribution is p_z=tau(E_z)
tau=Tr/d
claims.limitations: Using E_z/tau(E_z) as a state would be misnormalized by a factor d.

assumptions: the output format accepts a circuit/tree plus classical postprocessing
the dense broadcaster descriptor is finite-bit or available as an exact channel primitive

claims.statement: For any two fixed affine two-state Markov occupancy maps F_A(x)=a_A x+b_A and F_B(x)=a_B x+b_B, the endpoint occupancy contrast F_B(F_A(x))-F_A(F_B(x))=(a_B-1)b_A+(1-a_A)b_B is independent of the initial occupancy x. A common terminal observation channel maps this to an outcome-law contrast proportional to the hidden occupancy contrast, including common read transitions and backgrounds.
assumptions: Hidden state is exactly two-state and transition dynamics are Markovian at the declared state resolution
The A/B waveform maps are stable and identical in their AB and BA uses
Terminal read conditional laws L0,L1 are common across order arms
The endpoint statistic or total-variation separation has a nonzero state read contrast
claims.novelty: UNKNOWN. Affine pulse-order algebra and force-dependent HJ HMM analyses are prior art; no priority claim is made for this endpoint formulation.
claims.costs: One independent molecule per endpoint record in the conservative design. Pairing independent bounded [0,1] outcomes across arms gives n>=8 log(2/alpha)/g^2 per order arm for both errors <=alpha. Add pilot, blank, force telemetry, and molecule-capture costs; those are not sourced.
claims.falsifier: A two-state affine map counterexample with initial-state-dependent AB-BA occupancy contrast, or a stable common-read controlled experiment whose endpoint law violates proportionality to that contrast.
claims.next_gate: Acquire time-tagged force and photon records under randomized AB/BA loops; estimate ramp maps, state-read contrast, background, and force-history dependence.

claims.statement: When an A loop consists of fixed pre/post ramp Markov maps around an A plateau of duration s, while a B loop duration is fixed, the order contrast is C0+C1 exp(-lambda_A s). Three equally spaced duration contrasts D0,D1,D2 with nonzero curvature satisfy (D2-D1)/(D1-D0)=exp(-lambda_A tau), so lambda_A is identified without knowing initial occupancy, equilibrium occupancies, fixed ramp maps, or terminal emission amplitude.
assumptions: Two-state homogeneous CTMC at each plateau force, with lambda_A=k01(A)+k10(A)
Pre/post A ramp waveforms do not change with plateau duration or sequence position
B loop is fixed across the three durations
Terminal channel is common and has nonzero contrast
Duration curvature coefficient C1 is nonzero and signs can be oriented
claims.novelty: UNKNOWN. Three-point exponential ratio/Prony system identification is classical; the possible contribution is the force-loop endpoint interface under common unknown readout, which has not had a priority search.
claims.costs: Six treatment arms (three durations by two orders); finite Hoeffding rate inversion can require tens of millions of independent endpoint records per arm at the illustrative HJ-scale contrast. HMM full traces may dominate.
claims.falsifier: Held-out same-molecule duration contrasts that fail a single exponential with fixed ramp maps, or force-loop curvature C1 too small to resolve at declared costs.
claims.next_gate: Compare full photon-likelihood estimates against the endpoint ratio at equal photon dose and force time; require two-state residual checks and report UNKNOWN under kinetic-class sign cancellation.

claims.statement: A force intervention with different stationary occupancies at A and B can create an O(kappa) endpoint output gap under a weak kappa reporter and hence O(kappa^2) endpoint KL, while the c4 full-transcript lower bound is O(kappa^4) only for fixed-uniform-stationary doubly stochastic action kernels. An explicit two-state pair has passive C-only laws equal and nonzero AB/BA contrast under active forces.
assumptions: Same common C generator and same initial law in candidate worlds
The alternative A/B inputs have pi_A != pi_B; the null does not
A weak known binary reporter has contrast kappa
Endpoint outputs across randomized molecules are independent at the superpopulation level
claims.novelty: The exponent separation follows from leaving the lower-bound action class; this is not a counterexample to its theorem or an external novelty claim.
claims.costs: For the explicit witness, the order-arm gap is about 0.2398*kappa and the conservative paired-difference Hoeffding count is about 514*kappa^-2 at alpha=0.05. At kappa=0.1 this is about 51,400 records per arm; the c4 lower-bound constant is weak at that point.
claims.falsifier: A proposed physical control whose stationary law is in fact common across force levels, or a measured endpoint channel with no detectable order contrast at the stated exposure cost.
claims.next_gate: Quantify whether force-dependent equilibrium shifts and terminal photon contrast are large enough in the actual HJ geometry; compare with full-likelihood active acquisition.

claims.statement: In the no-ramp two-state contiguous AB/BA model with sA+sB=T fixed, the absolute hidden occupancy order gap is |piB-piA|(1-exp(-lambdaA*sA))(1-exp(-lambdaB*sB)); its unique maximum equates lambdaA/(exp(lambdaA*sA)-1) and lambdaB/(exp(lambdaB*sB)-1). For a fixed bounded read gap, this minimizes the distribution-free Hoeffding endpoint bound within this schedule family.
assumptions: Two-state homogeneous CTMC at A and B
No ramps, or ramp overhead independent of the dwell split for this stated formula
Contiguous AB/BA comparison with fixed total plateau dwell
Known rates for selecting the optimum, with any pilot cost charged separately
A common terminal bounded read channel across order arms
claims.novelty: UNKNOWN. The optimization is elementary within the restricted model and is not a global optimal-control or photon-information result.
claims.costs: Synthetic T=2 s scenario at rates 0.5 and 2 per second lowers a bounded-read per-arm Hoeffding count from 709 to 629; actual ramp calibration and pilot molecule costs are unknown.
claims.falsifier: A within-model split with larger endpoint gap at the same total dwell, or an empirical calibrated-ramp design whose optimum is incorrectly predicted by the no-ramp equation.
claims.next_gate: Use calibrated loop affine maps and a pilot-funded design to compare the best-split endpoint statistic with full photon-arrival CTMC/HMM likelihood under identical photon, molecule, force-time, and blank budgets.

claims.statement: A physically proposed HJ assay uses existing optical-tweezer/smFRET hardware to apply repeated force loops in the dark, return to one common read force C, and collect a short terminal FRET read after randomized AB or BA. This is a proposed acquisition protocol, not a reported or validated experiment.
assumptions: Piezo force trajectories can be measured and repeated at required timescales
Confocal excitation is shuttered during loops and tracks the molecule as in the source setup
The force order does not irreversibly change the construct or its terminal dye channel
A low-dose common endpoint read has usable conditional state contrast
claims.novelty: UNKNOWN. Force-pulse protocols, HJ force-smFRET, and HMM kinetic fits exist. The proposed combination of dark pulse loops and common endpoint randomized order has not been priority-cleared.
claims.costs: Charge three independent cost streams: founder count per endpoint arm, waveform wall time/force calibration, and photons/background blanking. Source photon rates and ramp settling are absent, so absolute time, laser dose, and expected photons are UNKNOWN.
claims.falsifier: AB/BA terminal contrast disappears under common force/read calibration, or its apparent effect is reproduced by no-tether/fluorophore controls or force-path differences.
claims.next_gate: Pilot exact waveform repeatability, background, photon arrivals, dye-history controls, and full-likelihood matched comparator before any claim of practical information gain.

claims.statement: For positive absolutely continuous states satisfying dx_i/dt=(a_i u(t)-d_i(t))x_i+r_i(t), with common measurable u>=0, finite integral, and integrable r_i/x_i, the pairwise log-ratio change equals (a_i-a_j) integral(u) - integral(d_i-d_j) + integral(r_i/x_i-r_j/x_j). claims.proof: Added moves e_A, e_B-e_C, e_D generate the kernel of K=(0,1,1,0) and their binomials generate <a-1,b-c,d-1>. The unit activity vector detailed-balances every pair; product-Poisson(1) conditioned on B+C=2 is finite. B,C are bounded, immigration is bounded, and the total rate of A-increasing jumps is at most linear in A with jumps bounded by three. A linear pure-birth comparison and the fact that downward jumps cannot occur more often than accumulated births plus the initial population give nonexplosion. Irreducibility plus the invariant probability gives positive recurrence.

claims.claim: For every enabled reaction y->y', F(x-y+y')-F(x) <= log(M(x)/x_under_y), where F(x)=min_{z<=x} log((x-z)!) and M(x)=max_{z<=x} x_under_z over available complexes.
assumptions: Finite complex/reaction set.
Falling-factorial stochastic mass-action propensities and availability y<=x.
The reaction target y' is in the complex set, so it is available at x-y+y'.
claims.proof: At the post-jump state z=x-y+y', the target y' is available and z-y'=x-y, so F(z)<=log((x-y)!). Also F(x)=log(x!)-log(M(x)); subtracting gives the inequality exactly.
limitations: The original N76 derivation/code packet was not supplied; this identity was independently reconstructed from the summary.
The supplied summary's finite verification counts were not replayed.

claims.claim: For a finite weakly reversible network with fixed positive rate constants, E[exp(F(X_{j+1})-F(X_j))|X_j] <= C_rate, hence P(max_{j<=N}F(X_j)>=F(X_0)+N log C_rate+u)<=exp(-u).
assumptions: Each complex has an outgoing reaction, as holds for a finite weakly reversible network.
All reaction rate constants are fixed and strictly positive.
The embedded reaction-event chain is considered up to its successive jumps.
claims.proof: Use the N76 exact jump inequality termwise in the next-reaction expectation. A source attaining M(x) contributes at least kappa_min M(x) to total rate q(x), giving C_rate=(sum_r kappa_r)/kappa_min. Doob's maximal inequality applies to exp(F(X_j)-F(X_0)-j log C_rate).
limitations: This is an upper-growth envelope per reaction event, not negative drift to a finite set.
It does not control holding times E_j/q(X_j), so it proves neither physical-time nonexplosion nor positive recurrence.

claims.claim: For the all-rate-one network 2C->A+B+C->3A+2B->2C and 2C<->2C+D, each Gamma_n={(n,0,2,d),(n+1,1,1,d),(n+3,2,0,d):d>=0}, n>=0, is closed, irreducible, nonexplosive, and positive recurrent.
assumptions: Falling-factorial stochastic mass-action propensities x_under_y with all constants equal to one.
State space N_0^4.
claims.proof: The phase rates are 2, n+1, and 2(n+1)(n+2)(n+3); in the first phase D has birth rate 2 and death rate 2d. The explicit invariant probability in the report satisfies global balance. Phase transitions are bounded for fixed n and D births are dominated by a rate-2 Poisson process, so the chain is nonexplosive. Irreducibility plus an invariant probability gives positive recurrence.
limitations: The source-reported 216 fixtures and original balance logs were not supplied or replayed.
The explicit Gamma_n family was reconstructed directly; this does not assert that the displayed classes exhaust every communicating class of the network.

claims.claim: The family of stationary laws pi_n on Gamma_n is not tight although all pi_n are positive recurrent, all classes lie in the same linear stoichiometric plane B+C=2, and each Gamma_n contains the positive state (n+1,1,1,1).
claims.proof: Every state in Gamma_n has A>=n. A compact subset of R_+^4 has bounded A-coordinate, hence pi_n(K)=0 for all sufficiently large n.
assumptions: Same network and rate convention as N77_classwise_positive_recurrence.
Tightness is tested on N_0^4 with its discrete topology or on the ambient Euclidean state space; compact sets have bounded A.
limitations: This refutes uniform tightness across the displayed classes only; it does not refute componentwise recurrence or existence of a tight stationary mixture on the full state space.
Historical novelty and priority are not established.

claims.claim: The strongly endotactic network 0->2A+B->4A+4B->A is transient for every fixed positive rate-constant choice under stochastic mass action.
claims.proof: The source constructs a positive-probability finite access path to (a,0), then an infinite sequence of cycles increasing A by one. At level n the required reactions beat competing reactions with probabilities 1-O(n^-2); summable failure probabilities imply a positive infinite-product success probability.
evidence: Anderson, Cappelletti, Kim, Nguyen, Tier structure of strongly endotactic reaction networks, Example 3.1: https://arxiv.org/html/1808.05328v2#S3
limitations: This network is not weakly reversible, so it does not refute arbitrary-dimensional weakly reversible positive recurrence.
The source has one prose occurrence of 4A+4B->0 inconsistent with the displayed network 4A+4B->A; the reconstruction follows the displayed network and cycle calculation.

claims.claim: The strongly endotactic network 0->2A->4A+B->6A+4B->3A is explosive with positive probability for every initial condition and every fixed positive rate choice.
claims.proof: The final three reactions can repeat with a positive infinite-product probability, increasing A by one per cycle; desired propensities grow with orders n^2, n^4, and n^6, while competitors have lower order, and the expected holding times along the selected path are summable.
evidence: Anderson, Cappelletti, Kim, Nguyen, Tier structure of strongly endotactic reaction networks, Example 3.2: https://arxiv.org/html/1808.05328v2#S3
limitations: This network is not weakly reversible; it refutes transfer from broad deterministic endotactic permanence to stochastic nonexplosion, not the restricted weakly reversible target.

claims.claim: Wiuf and Xu prove positive recurrence with exponential ergodicity on each positive irreducible class for one-dimensional weakly reversible mass-action SRNs under their stated H2-H3 hypotheses; their broader theorem covers one-dimensional endotactic systems whose state space consists of closed communicating classes.
assumptions: Stoichiometric dimension one (H2).
Both positive and negative reaction directions (H3) for the infinite-class theorem.
Mass-action availability condition; species that never change can be removed/absorbed into rates as described by the source.
evidence: Wiuf and Xu, Classification and threshold dynamics of stochastic reaction networks, Theorem 4.8 and Corollary 4.10: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.07954
limitations: This is a one-dimensional result and does not give a general higher-dimensional theorem.

claims.claim: Every bimolecular weakly reversible stochastic mass-action system is nonexplosive, as a corollary of the source theorem for second-order endotactic systems.
assumptions: Every reactant complex has total molecularity at most two.
Stochastic mass-action kinetics.
evidence: Chuang Xu, Non-explosivity of endotactic stochastic reaction systems, https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.05340
limitations: Nonexplosion alone does not establish positive recurrence on infinite classes.

claims.claim: Anderson et al. Theorem 7.2 proves each closed irreducible component of a strongly endotactic mass-action network is positive recurrent after adjoining specified high-order drains for every species; optional lower-order reactions are allowed.
assumptions: For each species S_i, a nonempty family of added reactions a S_i -> sum_j r'_j S_j with a>=m-1 and sum_j r'_j<=a-1, where m is maximum source molecularity of the base network.
Optional added reactions have source molecularity at most m-2.
The source's strict molecularity ordering condition on the drains.
claims.proof: The source establishes a proper physical-time Lyapunov function with generator drift at most -1 outside a finite set, then applies a Foster-Lyapunov criterion that includes nonexplosion and finite expected hitting time.
evidence: Anderson, Cappelletti, Kim, Nguyen, Tier structure of strongly endotactic reaction networks, Theorems 7.2-7.3 and Corollary 7.1: https://arxiv.org/html/1808.05328v2#S7
limitations: The added drains are a substantive network restriction; this theorem is not a recurrence theorem for all strongly or weakly reversible networks.

claims.claim: N35's stopped finite-horizon exit bound does not imply infinite-time survival, nonexplosion after exit, recurrence, or stationary tightness. In its A<->B fixed-volume example at rates one, the finite irreducible birth-death chain visits the zero-species endpoints infinitely often despite deterministic convergence to 1/2.
limitations: The N35 finite-horizon probability theorem remains valid on its supplied buffered initial condition, polytope, rate envelope, and time horizon.

claims.claim: No source or reconstruction here proves positive recurrence for every arbitrary-dimensional weakly reversible stochastic mass-action network, nor derives such a theorem from N76's embedded-chain exponential upper-growth bound.
claims.missing_lemma: For each closed class Gamma, prove nonexplosion and a proper physical-time Foster-Lyapunov drift/finite expected return, or build a recurrence-preserving event-chain coarse graining with explicit accumulated holding-time bounds. A uniform tightness claim additionally needs bounds uniform over the hidden class parameter.
evidence: N76 source card records general weakly reversible positive recurrence as not proved.
The cited positive-recurrence results require one-dimensionality or added drains.
N77 refutes only the cross-class uniform-tightness strengthening.

claims.claim: The four-pair reversible detailed-balanced completion 2C<->A+B+C, A+B+C<->3A+2B, 3A+2B<->2C, and 2C<->2C+D has closed irreducible classes Gamma_n={(n,0,2,d),(n+1,1,1,d),(n+3,2,0,d):d>=0} for every n>=0, with the same unbounded pathwise invariant H=A-B(B+1)/2 on B+C=2.
assumptions: All effective directional stochastic mass-action constants equal one.
State space is N_0^4 and propensities use falling factorials.
The displayed pairs include both directions of each reaction.
claims.proof: On B+C=2, the enabled main-network edges cycle among population phases (n,0,2), (n+1,1,1), and (n+3,2,0); each direction preserves H. The D pair changes only D and is enabled at phase (n,0,2), where it supplies immigration rate 2 and death rate 2d. These transitions connect the three phases and all d values, and no transition leaves Gamma_n.
limitations: Historical novelty or priority is not established.
The source-reported N77 fixture logs were not replayed; this class proof is reconstructed directly from the reversible network.

claims.claim: Each Gamma_n is nonexplosive and positive recurrent, and its detailed-balanced stationary law is product-Poisson(1) restricted and normalized on Gamma_n; the family of these laws is not tight because A>=n on Gamma_n.
assumptions: The reversible network and unit rates stated above.
Tightness is on the count state space embedded in R^4.
claims.proof: For a fixed n, phase rates are bounded; D-births are bounded by rate 2 and D-deaths cannot increase D, which proves nonexplosion. Product-Poisson(1) satisfies detailed balance edge by edge because (1/x!)x_under_y=1/(x-y)!. Its restriction to the closed irreducible Gamma_n is a normalizable invariant probability. Since every state there has A>=n, any compact set with A<=M receives zero mass for n>M.
evidence: Anderson, Craciun, Kurtz, Product-form stationary distributions for deficiency zero chemical reaction networks, https://arxiv.org/abs/0803.3042
limitations: The escaping stationary family is across distinct closed communicating classes in one deterministic stoichiometric fiber.

claims.claim: Within the fiber B+C=2, the Gamma_n for n>=0 contain all states with H>=0 and are closed irreducible classes, but they do not exhaust the fiber: for every d>=0, (0,1,1,d), (0,2,0,d), (1,2,0,d), and (2,2,0,d) are additional absorbing singleton classes.
claims.proof: At the first listed state the A+B+C source lacks A; at the other three states the 3A+2B source lacks three A. The 2C exchange lacks two C in all four profiles. No reaction is enabled, and D is inert there. Every remaining state in the fiber has H>=0 and matches exactly one of the three Gamma_n profiles.
limitations: This is an exhaustive classification only inside B+C=2, not of the full N_0^4 state space.

claims.claim: For the reversible candidate the reaction lattice L equals S intersect Z^4 equals ker_Z(0,1,1,0), so the lattice is saturated.
claims.proof: The rank is three, every reaction vector lies in ker_Z(0,1,1,0), and the minor of the stoichiometric matrix on rows A,B,D and columns nu1,nu2,nu4 equals -1. The rank-three column lattice is therefore primitive and equals the integer kernel.
evidence: Exact SymPy calculation recorded in the task execution: rank 3, minor -1, nu1+nu2+nu3=0, nu2-nu1=e_A.
limitations: Saturation only removes distinct lattice cosets inside the real stoichiometric class; it does not imply reaction-enabled connectivity.

claims.claim: Lattice saturation does not imply one CTMC communicating class per deterministic integer fiber: (0,0,2,0) and (1,0,2,0) differ by e_A=nu2-nu1 in L but belong to distinct closed classes Gamma_0 and Gamma_1.
claims.proof: The two states have B+C=2 and lattice difference e_A. H is preserved along every enabled reaction in that fiber, taking value 0 at the first state and 1 at the second; Gamma_0 and Gamma_1 are closed by the exact phase analysis.
limitations: This disproves the saturation-only connectivity gate; it does not disprove stronger reaction-aware Markov-basis conditions.

claims.claim: For K=(0,1,1,0), the primitive move binomials of the candidate reaction vectors do not generate the toric ideal I_K=<a-1,b-c,d-1>; hence the reaction-vector moves are not a Markov basis for the B+C fibers.
claims.proof: After cancelling shared catalyst factors, the move binomials are c-ab, c-a^2b, a^3b^2-c^2, and 1-d. They all vanish at (a,b,c,d)=(0,1,0,1), while a-1 and b-c do not. Thus their ideal is strictly smaller than I_K. The source-complex reaction binomial ideal is also strict, with generators c^2-abc, abc-a^3b^2, a^3b^2-c^2, and c^2-c^2d.
evidence: Diaconis and Sturmfels, Algebraic Algorithms for Sampling from Conditional Distributions, https://statistics.stanford.edu/technical-reports/algebraic-algorithms-sampling-conditional-distributions
limitations: The reaction graph is still more restrictive than the primitive move graph whenever source complexes contain extra common catalysts.

claims.claim: If the reaction lattice is saturated and the network contains positive-rate reversible catalyst-free reactions u^-<->u^+ for every move in a Markov basis of that lattice, then every nonempty integer stoichiometric fiber is one irreducible CTMC class.
assumptions: Finite move set is a Markov basis for the integer conservation matrix defining the fiber.
Each basis move is implemented by its primitive source/target complexes with no extra common catalyst.
Every directional rate constant is strictly positive.
claims.proof: The Markov-basis theorem gives a path between any two nonnegative states in the same fiber using basis moves while staying nonnegative. Catalyst-free reversible complexes make every such feasible move an enabled reaction. Positive rates make each edge have positive probability, so the reaction graph is connected and the CTMC class is irreducible.
evidence: P. Diaconis and B. Sturmfels, Algebraic Algorithms for Sampling from Conditional Distributions, Stanford technical report: https://statistics.stanford.edu/technical-reports/algebraic-algorithms-sampling-conditional-distributions
limitations: It proves connectivity only; it does not prove nonexplosion, positive recurrence, or any quantitative stationary tail bound.

claims.claim: Adding unit-rate reversible pairs empty<->A, B<->C, and empty<->D supplies a catalyst-free Markov basis for ker_Z(0,1,1,0) and connects the entire B+C=2 fiber.
claims.proof: The three primitive moves e_A, e_B-e_C, and e_D connect any two nonnegative states with B+C fixed by adjusting A, then D, then the B/C split. Their binomials 1-a, b-c, and 1-d generate I_K.
limitations: This modifies the reaction network and is not asserted to be chemically or biologically natural.
Connectivity alone does not provide a stationary law or prove tail bounds.

claims.claim: A saturated Markov-basis condition does not yield uniform stationary tightness across changing rates: for empty<->X with birth rate theta and death propensity x, the sole fiber is N_0 and the unique stationary law Pois(theta), which escapes as theta tends to infinity.
claims.proof: The moves +/-1 connect the fiber and generate the toric ideal for the zero-row conservation matrix. For every finite M, Pois(theta){0,...,M} tends to zero as theta tends to infinity, so the family is not tight.
limitations: This varies the rates between models; for one fixed positive recurrent irreducible class, the invariant probability is unique and individually tight.
