claims.exact_statement: For a finite-state, time-inhomogeneous Markov chain X_1,...,X_n with initial law mu, transition kernels K_t, and bounded additive observable S=sum_t f_t(X_t), define q_i=sum_{j=i}^n K_{i+1:j} f_j, c_i=osc(q_i), and V_n=Var_mu(q_1)+sum_{i=2}^n Var_{K_i(X_{i-1},.)}(q_i). With c=max_i c_i, P(S-E S >= s and V_n<=v) <= exp(-s^2/[2(v+cs/3)]). A two-sided event incurs factor 2. The deterministic v_* formed by replacing each transition-conditioned variance by its maximum over predecessor states dominates V_n pathwise.
assumptions: finite state spaces
known transition kernels or certified upper bounds for the quantities used
bounded real observables
arbitrary initial law
no stationarity or reversibility requirement
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_standard_specialization; correctness follows from the Doob decomposition and Freedman; no independent proof review
claims.novelty_boundary: Doob martingale plus Freedman is standard. Kontorovich-Ramanan explicitly cover inhomogeneous Markov chains. The dynamic-program formulas are a useful specialization, not a supported novelty claim.
claims.costs: For sparse finite transition tables, backward q recursion and statewise conditional-variance evaluation are linear in total listed transition entries. Exact Dobrushin coefficients can cost quadratically in the number of transition rows. Unknown kernels, state truncation, and estimation errors are not free.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the displayed Doob-difference or conditional-variance identity under the stated Markov interface; none found.
claims.next_gate: Use only if a concrete kinetic model makes v_* materially smaller than the range-only proxy and competitive with available spectral Bernstein bounds.

claims.exact_statement: For delta_t=sup_{x,x'} ||K_t(x,.)-K_t(x',.)||_TV with TV=sup_A |P(A)-Q(A)| and b_t=osc(f_t), c_i=osc(q_i) <= sum_{j=i}^n b_j product_{k=i+1}^j delta_k. Thus P(|S-E S|>=s) <= 2 exp(-2s^2/sum_i cbar_i^2), where cbar_i is the displayed influence sum.
assumptions: finite-state time-inhomogeneous Markov chain
certified per-step Dobrushin coefficients
bounded additive observables
claims.novelty_boundary: The inhomogeneous-chain coverage and mixing-coefficient method are prior art. The product profile is the direct Markov specialization and does not support priority.
claims.costs: Requires supplied/acquired bounds on every delta_t and observable oscillation. Exact dense row-pair TV computation has quadratic row cost; certified upper bounds avoid that cost.
claims.falsifier: A failure of osc(K_t g)<=delta_t osc(g) or of product contraction under the stated TV convention; none found.
claims.next_gate: Compare the bound against spectral-gap Bernstein when reversibility is available; do not claim novelty without a structured application and exact prior-art proof comparison.

claims.exact_statement: For the stationary binary chain P(X_{t+1}=X_t)=(1+rho)/2 and f_t(x)=x, the Dobrushin-Azuma squared-width proxy is asymptotic to 4n/(1-rho)^2, while Var(sum_t X_t)=n+2 sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(n-k)rho^k is asymptotic to n(1+rho)/(1-rho); the exact Doob conditional-variance sum equals this variance and is order n/(1-rho) for n much larger than the mixing time.
assumptions: stationary uniform initial law
n(1-rho) tends large
claims.novelty_boundary: Illustrates loss in range-only Azuma; homogeneous reversible spectral Bernstein is established prior art and already addresses this scaling.
claims.costs: None beyond symbolic calculation; no experiment or simulation performed.
claims.falsifier: Direct covariance or Doob-variance computation disagreeing with the displayed exact formulas; none found.
claims.next_gate: Only use as a diagnostic for a nonstationary/local-variance application where spectral theory does not already dominate.

claims.exact_statement: For independent uniform signs U_1,...,U_m and X_a=product_{j:a_j=1}U_j indexed by nonzero a in F_2^m, the N=2^m-1 variables are pairwise independent, Var(sum_a X_a)=N, yet P(sum_a X_a=N)>=1/(N+1). Hence bounded marginals and pairwise covariance alone do not imply a universal variance-proxy sub-Gaussian tail P(|T-E T|>=t)<=2 exp(-t^2/[C Var(T)]) for any fixed C.
assumptions: U_j independent Rademacher signs
claims.status: explicit finite construction; algebraic proof included
claims.novelty_boundary: Classical pairwise-independent character construction used here as a scope obstruction, not a new result.
claims.costs: No computational cost; construction has N=2^m-1 variables and an m-bit latent source.
claims.falsifier: Checking pairwise character orthogonality or the all-plus latent event; both identities are exact.

claims.exact_statement: For a two-state continuous-time Markov environment with transition rates alpha for 1->2 and beta for 2->1, and mode-dependent constant escape hazards lambda_1, lambda_2, the mean escape times from the two modes are m_1=(alpha+beta+lambda_2)/(alpha*lambda_2+beta*lambda_1+lambda_1*lambda_2) and m_2=(alpha+beta+lambda_1)/(alpha*lambda_2+beta*lambda_1+lambda_1*lambda_2). Under alpha=beta=c*exp(-s*N), lambda_i=a_i*exp(-b_i*N), fixed a_i,c>0 and 0<b_1<b_2, lim_(N->infinity) N^(-1)log E_2[tau]=median(b_1,s,b_2). For s<b_1, b_1<s<b_2, s>b_2, respectively, E_2[tau] is asymptotic to (2/a_1)exp(b_1*N), (1/c)exp(s*N), (1/a_2)exp(b_2*N).
assumptions: The environment is exactly a two-state CTMC with the stated rates.
Conditional on the current environment, killing/escape has a constant exponential hazard and does not affect environment transitions.
The environment and killing clocks are conditionally independent given the current mode.
For the asymptotic statement, exponents are fixed, 0<b_1<b_2, and prefactors are positive constants independent of N; the sharper equivalences exclude s=b_1 and s=b_2.
claims.novelty_boundary: The exact 2x2 killed-generator calculation is elementary, and fluctuating barriers, environmental modulation of extinction, and multiscale rare-transition Markov chains are established. No priority claim is made. A source-level comparison is required before attributing novelty to the median-exponent phase diagram or its application.

costs.mathematical: Constant-size linear algebra once alpha, beta, lambda_1, lambda_2 are supplied.
costs.acquisition: No hidden-state, hazard, or barrier acquisition is included. Experimental state-labeling, rate estimation, reporter calibration, censoring, and rare exits must be charged.
costs.direct_experiment: For exponential observations, about 100 completed independent exits per condition give roughly 10% relative standard error before censoring and parameter-estimation error. Expected waiting time is exponential in N.

claims.falsifier: After independently estimating mode-conditioned hazards and environmental transition rates, observed survival curves fail the exact two-state phase-type survival law, or a controlled barrier series fails the predicted slopes while within-mode exponential hazards remain empirically adequate.
claims.next_gate: Compare full derivations in fluctuating-barrier escape and multiscale Markov-chain literature. If not already covered, test whether a biologically grounded non-Markovian or multi-mode extension yields a genuinely new theorem and remains identifiable from data.

claims.exact_statement: In the model above with b_1=1, b_2=4, s=2, a_1=a_2=c=1 and initial mode 2, E[tau] is asymptotic to exp(2*N), while replacing the modulated hazard by its stationary average predicts asymptotic mean 2*exp(N). Thus stationary hazard averaging can be exponentially wrong when switching is on an intermediate rare-event scale.
assumptions: The exact two-mode killed-chain assumptions in claim two_mode_killed_chain_exact_mte_and_barrier_switch_crossover hold.
The initial environment is mode 2 and the environment is symmetric, so its stationary mode weights are 1/2,1/2.
claims.novelty_boundary: The general warning that environmental correlations alter escape/extinction times is established. This is a transparent exact counterexample for the supplied averaging rule, not a new general theorem.

costs.calculation: Direct substitution in the exact mean formula.
costs.measurement: Mode occupancy alone is insufficient; transition rates and conditional escape hazards are needed.

claims.falsifier: A recalculation under the stated parameters that yields a different asymptotic exponent; or empirical evidence that the event hazard does not obey the stated conditional exponential model.
claims.next_gate: Use the example as a control in a frequency-sweep assay and compare equal-information stationary-average and environment-aware predictors.

claims.claim: Poincare near-extremality plus only the displayed field, energy, Sylvester, and commutator hypotheses implies a cap-independent scale-integrated MI bound.
claims.evidence: The rate-2 Laplace law eta(dy)=exp(-2|y|)dy has P(eta)=1. With smooth psi=0 on y<=0 and psi(y)=y-c on y>=2, set a_j=1-1/j, c_j=(E exp(2 a_j psi))^(-1/2), R_j=[c_j exp(a_j psi)], and Hhat_j=[a_j psi']. Then E tr R_j^2=1, E|D R_j|^2->1, the Sylvester equation holds exactly, and all commutators vanish. X_j=R_j(Y)^2 has Pareto tail exponent beta_j=1/a_j->1 and E[X_j 1_{X_j>=K}]->1 for every fixed K. Binary output-event tests yield, for h0<H<=L, liminf_j integral I(Y;Z_T)dT/T^2 >= (p0/8) log(H/h0), where p0=P(|G|>=sqrt(2))>0. Taking H=L/2 disproves a universal bound independent of L. A smooth strengthened example uses eta_delta=Law((Laplace(rate 2)+N(0,delta))/sqrt(p_delta)), where p_delta is its exact best Poincare constant; tensorization and convergence of compact-test quotients prove p_delta->1, so the rescaled law has P=1 exactly. Explicit convolution tail bounds preserve size-biased tail escape and the reciprocal tail envelope, giving the same MI lower bound without exact Pareto tails.
claims.qualification: This refutes the abstract replacement using only (7.1)-(7.2), not a stronger lemma imposing full provenance from the critical eigenfunction/tensor hierarchy. Smoothness is also met by the convolution-rescaled sequence; it still does not satisfy the source near-unit LSI provenance.

claims.claim: A reciprocal upper tail P(X_j>u)<=1/u for u>=1 together with size-biased tail escape E[X_j 1_{X_j>=K}]->1 for every fixed K forces a cap-growing scale-integrated MI lower bound in the scalar covariance Gaussian channel.
claims.evidence: For each fixed h0<H<=L and x>=H exp(H/4), set T=h/x and A_h={|Z|>=sqrt(h)}. The conditional event probability is at least p0=P(|G|>=sqrt(2)); the marginal probability is at most 3 exp(-h/4). Binary data processing gives conditional KL >= p0 h/8 for h>=h0. Integrating dT/T^2=x dh/h^2 yields liminf_j J_j(L)>= (p0/8) log(H/h0). The proof uses no Pareto asymptotics.
claims.qualification: Quantifiers are fixed L,H before j->infinity; choose H=L/2 only after that limit.

claims.claim: The smooth scalar tail field cannot be completed to the Family 093 Proposition 5.1 hierarchy by simply taking the natural eigenfield w_j proportional to R_j and rescaling its amplitude.
claims.evidence: Condition (5.2) forces I_j=E w_j^2->0 in one dimension: if I_j stays bounded below, some fixed c makes the identity rank-one projection admissible and it captures all the w_j energy. Then (5.3) has rank bound C_epsilon I_j<1, so its projection is zero and requires E b_j^2<=epsilon. At fixed s=1/8, the source decomposition gives b_j=y+s Dlog eta_j-s omega_j. On 1<=y<=2, Dlog eta_j->-2 and omega_j=w_j (or 0) tends to zero after the forced amplitude rescaling; hence b_j->y-1/4 and eta_j([1,2]) tends to positive Laplace mass, so E b_j^2 is bounded below. The smooth test does have an approximate eigenfield and its tail prediction calculation gives m_j(r)->e^-r, but this projection/outlier pair blocks the natural 1D hierarchy attempt.
claims.qualification: This is a one-dimensional candidate-specific obstruction; it does not rule out a higher-dimensional realization with diffuse w and source-generated b fields.

claims.claim: A normalized field with size-biased tail escape at every fixed threshold cannot satisfy Family 093 Proposition 3.9/7.2 near-unit LSI provenance when its derivative energy tends to one.
claims.evidence: For X_j=R_j^2 with EX_j=1 and E[X_j 1_{X_j>=K}]->1, Ent(X_j)>=log(K) E[X_j 1_{X_j>=K}]-1/e. Letting j->infinity and then K arbitrarily large forces Ent(X_j)->infinity. Source LSI instead gives Ent(R_j^2)<=2 RLSI(eta_j) E|DR_j|^2<=2 lambda_j^(-1) E|DR_j|^2->2. For matrix fields apply LSI to ||R_j||HS/sqrt(E tr(R_j^2)). The smooth scalar candidate also misses Proposition 5.1 conditions (5.2)-(5.3) under any rescaling of its natural one-dimensional eigenfield.
claims.qualification: This excludes the tail-escape falsifier from full source provenance; it does not prove the covariance-only replacement for other source-generated fields.

claims.claim: The specific covariance-only information step needed by N75 may hold for fields generated by the full Family 093 critical construction, with additional source-specific constraints.
claims.evidence: The counterexample is not shown to arise from the source's §§5-6 eigenfunction/tensor hierarchy. The displayed hypotheses alone are insufficient, so any proof must use further structure or any corrected theorem must state it explicitly. The current falsifier cannot satisfy the full source sequence: Proposition 3.9 supplies the additional near-unit LSI, which the tail-escape profile violates by an explicit entropy divergence. The actual covariance-only estimate for hierarchy-generated fields remains unproved and unfalsified.

claims.claim: The Family 093 LSI proof uses posterior likelihood LSI, Gaussian score identity, and an integrated spectral multiplier to obtain 9/4.
claims.qualification: Primary source reconstructed locally; no external proof validation claimed.

limits: The direct rate-2 Laplace model and its smooth Gaussian-convolution/rescaling version refute only the displayed Poincare-plus-field interface, not Family 093 Proposition 7.2 with its LSI assumption.

ledger.task: Quantitative stationary-law comparison and uniqueness for interacting single-site resampling systems
ledger.overall_status: finite theorem reconstructed; established comparison mechanism; novelty unsupported

claims.exact_statement: For finite V, binary replacement dynamics with site rates lambda_i>0, suppose q_i and qtilde_i have a common influence matrix C with TV(q_i(.|eta),q_i(.|zeta)) and TV(qtilde_i(.|eta),qtilde_i(.|zeta)) each at most sum_j C_ij 1[eta_j!=zeta_j]. If both processes use the same rates, delta_i=sup_eta TV(q_i(.|eta),qtilde_i(.|eta)), and spectral radius rho(C)<1, then both have unique stationary laws mu,mutilde and there is a coupling with p_i=P(X_i!=Y_i) satisfying p <= (I-C)^(-1) delta. Therefore TV(mu_S,mutilde_S) <= sum_{i in S}[(I-C)^(-1)delta]_i and |mu f-mutilde f| <= sum_i osc_i(f)[(I-C)^(-1)delta]_i.
assumptions: finite site set and finite spin space {0,1}
single-site replacement dynamics with positive site rates
a common, uniformly valid influence matrix for both kernels
same update rates in the compared systems
rho(C)<1
claims.novelty_boundary: The finite-volume result is a direct specialization of Dobrushin comparison / general invariant-Markov-kernel comparison. No novelty claim is made.
claims.falsifier: A discrepancy coupling violating the stationary coordinate inequality under the displayed common-clock and influence assumptions; none identified.

claims.exact_statement: For a countable-site finite-range Feller replacement process with rates uniformly bounded above and below, if positive weights bounded above and below satisfy Cw<=alpha w for alpha<1, common-clock coupling contracts the weighted sup discrepancy at rate at least lambda_min(1-alpha). The process has a unique invariant law. For a second process with the same clocks and common C, the stationary coupling obeys p<=sum_{n>=0} C^n delta.
assumptions: countable product of finite spin spaces
finite-range measurable replacement kernels and standard well-posed Feller graphical construction
uniform positive lower and finite upper bounds on update rates
weights with 0<w_min<=w_i<=w_max<infinity and Cw<=alpha w, alpha<1
same clocks for the paired-process comparison
claims.novelty_boundary: Uniform Dobrushin coupling uniqueness is established machinery. The exact nonreversible generator presentation was not searched exhaustively and is not claimed as new.
claims.falsifier: A violation of local cylinder convergence or invariant-law uniqueness under the finite-range Feller and strict weighted contraction assumptions; none found.

claims.exact_statement: For a finite region Lambda and two frozen exterior boundaries b,bprime, if C_LambdaLambda bounds internal influences and C_LambdaB bounds boundary influences, then p_Lambda <= (I-C_LambdaLambda)^(-1) C_LambdaB 1[b!=bprime], and local-observable differences are bounded by summing coordinate disagreement times oscillations.
assumptions: finite volume
same internal update clocks
rho(C_LambdaLambda)<1
boundary influences uniformly bounded by C_LambdaB
claims.novelty_boundary: Classical Dobrushin boundary comparison; no novelty claim.

claims.exact_statement: For q1(1|x2)=1/5+(3/5)x2 and q2(1|x1)=1/10+(1/5)x1, the local kernels are unchanged (delta=0) and rho(C)=sqrt(3/25)<1, but the stationary joint moment r is (lambda1*7/55+lambda2*39/440)/(lambda1+lambda2). Thus r=19/176 at rates (1,1) and r=151/1320 at (2,1); comparing only kernel perturbations is invalid when clocks differ.
assumptions: two binary sites
strictly positive replacement probabilities
noncompatible, non-Gibbs local conditionals
claims.novelty_boundary: A scope counterexample, not a new phenomenon claim.
claims.falsifier: Directly recomputing the two stationarity equations for marginals and the x1*x2 equation; all displayed values are exact fractions.

claims.exact_statement: The weighted contraction condition is sufficient, not necessary. At low temperature the two-dimensional ferromagnetic Ising model has spontaneous magnetization and distinct plus/minus infinite-volume states, even though each finite-volume positive-rate heat-bath chain has a unique stationary law.
assumptions: infinite two-dimensional nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model at sufficiently low temperature
finite-volume comparison uses strictly positive heat-bath updates
claims.novelty_boundary: Classical low-temperature phase coexistence, included to delimit the contraction theorem.

prior_art.source: Patrick Rebeschini and Ramon van Handel, Comparison Theorems for Gibbs Measures, Journal of Statistical Physics 157 (2014), 234-281
prior_art.relevance: Theorem 2.4 gives a local-update Dobrushin comparison bound; Proposition 3.2 gives a general comparison principle for invariant measures of Markov kernels using Wasserstein influence matrices. A finite CTMC stationary law is invariant under its associated random-scan update kernel.

prior_art.source: R. L. Dobrushin, The problem of uniqueness of a Gibbsian random field and the problem of phase transitions, Functional Analysis and Its Applications 2 (1968), 302-312
prior_art.relevance: Classical uniqueness and phase-transition boundary for Gibbs random fields.

prior_art.source: Robert B. Griffiths, Peierls Proof of Spontaneous Magnetization in a Two-Dimensional Ising Ferromagnet, Physical Review 136 (1964), A437-A439

costs: Computing exact worst-case influence coefficients may require enumeration over all local boundaries; supplied analytic upper bounds are preferable.
The resolvent sums directed influence paths and can be expensive or loose if represented densely.
The comparison is conditional on certified C and delta values; they are not acquired for free.
limitations: The exact dynamics are single-site replacement/resampling processes; general spin-flip or jump IPS need a separate coupling drift bound.
Finite-volume uniqueness does not imply infinite-volume uniqueness or boundary independence.
The contraction condition is sufficient and failure of it proves neither coexistence nor slow mixing.

No code, simulation, external proof review, or exhaustive novelty search was performed.

claims.claim: Initial-temperature Green kernels obey eta(x)G_T(x,y,t)=eta(y)G_T(y,x,t); equal initial temperature jumps can look asymmetric when heat capacities differ, while equal energy impulses give symmetric responses.
The 2022 primary paper defines two-terminal reciprocity by swapping boundary temperatures and requiring cross-paired time-averaged terminal heat fluxes to reverse sign (published Eq. 4).
claims.evidence: Li et al., Nat Commun 13, 167 (2022), DOI 10.1038/s41467-021-27903-3. This is a direct terminal-observable prior under the paper's mass-conserving time-modulated harmonic-steady-state assumptions, not the exact all-time fixed-LTI body-source theorem.

claims.claim: The 2015 transformation-thermotics diode uses explicitly temperature-dependent conductivity/geometry switches and reports rectification up to 30 for a numerical parameter set.
claims.evidence: Li et al., PRL 115, 195503 (2015), arXiv:1505.00971, Eqs. 2-4; therefore outside a fixed linear operator.

claims.claim: The 2017 two-slab transient rectifier relies on nonlinear temperature-dependent conductivity or thermal capacitance; transient rectification can exceed steady-state behavior under some conditions.
claims.evidence: Herrera, Luo & Go, J Heat Transfer 139, 091301 (2017), DOI 10.1115/1.4036339. A later primary article reports hot-boundary-temperature impulse from uniform cold initial state and linearized k(T); publisher PDF blocked in this audit.

claims.claim: The exact source, receiver, normalization, observable, and equation defining nonreciprocity in Su et al. (2025) are unknown from the accessible indexed material; no source-definition error can be asserted.
claims.evidence: Su et al., Int J Heat Mass Transfer 239, 126570 (2025), DOI 10.1016/j.ijheatmasstransfer.2024.126570. Indexed record mentions Dirac heat source/Green function, swapped source/receiver framing, transient spatial asymmetry and steady symmetry; full text inaccessible (403).

counterexample.description: Equal initial temperature impulses are not unweighted reciprocal when C varies.
counterexample.interpretation: The 4:1 asymmetry is the unequal energy of equal-Delta-T jumps, not a violation of matched-port reciprocity.

ledger.discriminating_experiment: At one fixed sample and geometry, compare same-joule localized source pulses with paired temperature readouts, then repeat with equal initial Delta-T and with swapped Dirichlet terminal temperatures/conjugate flux readout. Record source energy, temperature field, terminal fluxes, initial state, contact/ambient losses, source shape, actuator energy. Equal-Delta-T-only asymmetry is predicted by unequal capacity; a reproducible inequality under normalized matched power/temperature or boundary temperature/flux ports would challenge the fixed reciprocal model.
ledger.costs: Two directional runs per port pair; calibrated power, temperature and heat-flux sensing; baseline reset; calorimetric accounting; source-profile calibration; model fitting. No numeric costs available.

ledger.task: Hard falsification of classwise nonexplosion/positive recurrence for finite time-homogeneous integer mass-action endotactic networks
ledger.overall_status: All-endotactic classwise claim refuted by a published strongly endotactic explosive class; new finite-cap arithmetic is internally reconstructed and externally unreviewed.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For the finite diagram 0->2A->4A+B->6A+4B->3A with any fixed positive time-homogeneous rate constants and stochastic mass-action propensities kappa_r x_under_y, Gamma={(a,b) in N0^2:a>=3} is a closed irreducible class. From every state in Gamma the minimal CTMC explodes with positive probability.
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md: the closure/irreducibility proof gives enabled pump and decrement macros; the infinite prescribed cycle from (n,0) has factors p1_n,p2_n,p3_n=1-O(n^-2), while conditional holding-time means sum as O(n^-2+n^-4+n^-6). Thus the channel-choice event has positive probability and its elapsed time is finite almost surely.
source_pointers: Anderson-Cappelletti-Kim-Nguyen, Definition 3.2 and Example 3.2, arXiv HTML lines 140-151 and 198-209; same falling-factorial CTMC convention at lines 121-133.
Xu, On the Regularity of Reaction Systems, arXiv v2 lines 110-115 restates the same witness and its stochastic explosion.
claims.novelty_boundary: The underlying strongly endotactic transient/explosive counterexamples are established prior work. The closed-class description and finite-cap estimate are independent reconstructions; no novelty or priority claim is made.
claims.costs: Four reactions, two species, fixed positive rates. The highest reactant molecularity is ten. Exact arithmetic for a finite prefix and a rational angular sweep is local CPU only; no experiment or SSA trajectory was acquired.
claims.falsifier: A proof that the prescribed event has zero probability or infinite conditional clock would invalidate this reconstruction; the primary source independently gives the same positive-product/summable-time proof. A generator-level model with measured propensities departing from the stated factorial law is a different model.
claims.next_gate: Independent review of the class macro argument and finite-cap conditional-time inequality; for any physical use, specify and measure a staged or resource-limited implementation and recheck its generator.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For unit rates and V=1, starting at (3,0), the prescribed runaway event has probability P_infty>0. The exact product through levels 3,...,99 and exact telescoping tail competitor-ratio sum from n=100 give the certified rational bound P_infty>0.346709327029.
claims.proof_path: check_endotactic_explosion.py computes the exact rational prefix and tail sum 27506776741/1260593928000; log(1+q)<=q and exp(-Q)>=1-Q give the product lower bound. CHECK_OUTPUT.json contains the exact numerator/denominator and decimal display.
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a scoped exact numerical sharpening of a known existence proof. Novelty is unknown and unclaimed.
claims.costs: One Python exact-rational run; no stochastic simulation. Prefix product is 97 cycles (291 intended jumps); the remaining tail is bounded analytically.
claims.falsifier: An arithmetic error in any rational propensity, prefix factor, or telescoping tail identity; rerunning the included script and parsing CHECK_OUTPUT.json reproduces the calculation.
claims.next_gate: A fresh exact-algebra audit by a reviewer, followed by a confidence-calibrated finite-cap simulation only if the idealized model is of practical interest.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For the unit-rate, V=1 network, modify the CTMC by blocking any reaction leaving D_M={(a,b):a+b<=M}. This is a finite-state nonexplosive CTMC. For every M>=107, the probability of hitting (M-7,0) by time T=44401/43200 is at least 0.1733546635 under the specified hard-cap convention.
claims.proof_path: Along each selected pump cycle beginning at (n,0), the maximum total count is n+8; the cap therefore leaves the selected route to N=M-7 intact. Route probability is bounded below by the exact P_infty lower bound. Conditional route time has mean at most S=44401/86400; Markov's inequality at 2S gives conditional probability at least 1/2 of reaching N by T.
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a model-specific finite-size consequence of a known runaway path; it is not a claim about natural chemistry or priority.
claims.costs: The cap adds an explicit boundary rule; the lower bound assumes all outward jumps are blocked and all interior propensities remain unmodified. Only rational arithmetic was run.
claims.falsifier: In a capped simulation or physical emulation matching the generator and boundary rule, a statistically reliable hit probability below this bound at the stated start, M, and horizon contradicts the ideal model assumptions or the derivation.
claims.next_gate: If pursued empirically, calibrate all propensities, exact count capacity, and time-homogeneity, then compare event-path and uncapped-rate records against a direct Gillespie implementation.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: Under standard volume-scaled stochastic mass action lambda_r^V(z)=kappa_r V^(1-|y_r|)z_under_y, for every fixed V>0 the same class and prescribed route remain explosive with positive probability. The conditional route time is bounded by S_V=V/(2kappa_1)+V^4/(72kappa_2)+V^9/(86400kappa_3). For fixed starting count n=3, the probability of the first selected cycle is Theta(V^-17) as V tends to infinity with rate constants fixed.
claims.proof_path: Scale each desired and competing stage rate by V^(1-|y|). The asymptotic n-orders at fixed V are unchanged, so the infinite product and inverse-rate series remain finite. At n=3 and large V, stage success factors scale as V^-2, V^-5, and V^-10. This bounds the canonical runaway path probability, not the total explosion probability.
claims.novelty_boundary: The finite-volume continuation is an internal extension of the known witness. It does not claim a thermodynamic-limit explosion probability or a fixed-concentration counterexample.
claims.costs: Volume scaling is an explicit model convention. S_V is an analytic conditional-clock bound; no data were acquired.
claims.falsifier: Changing the volume convention changes the displayed factors and requires recomputation. The assertion is falsified if any fixed-V canonical stage factor is zero or if the inverse desired-rate sum diverges.
claims.next_gate: Analyze total explosion probability and first-passage scaling under an explicit physical cutoff; do not infer those from the canonical path alone.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: Xu's Theorem 3.6 gives a sufficient nonexplosion condition: there is u>0 such that every reaction with u dot (y'-y)>0 has propensity O(||x||_1). Xu also states all second-order endotactic mass-action systems are nonexplosive. Anderson-Cappelletti-Kim-Nguyen's Theorem 7.2 gives positive recurrence on each closed irreducible class after adding its specified high-order species drains to a strongly endotactic network. These are sufficient neighboring classes, not maximal or necessary-and-sufficient characterizations.
claims.proof_path: See FINAL_REPORT.md section 'Volume scaling and physical boundary' and primary source theorem statements. Xu uses a positive linear Lyapunov function for regularity; Anderson et al. prove a proper Foster-Lyapunov drift after drain additions.
source_pointers: Xu Theorem 3.6, lines 150-164; abstract and scope at lines 34-37.
Anderson et al. Corollary 7.1 and Theorem 7.2, arXiv HTML lines 1116-1153.
claims.novelty_boundary: Both theorem families are established primary literature; they are not consequences of N33/N76 and are not newly claimed here.
claims.costs: The drain theorem changes the network by adding reactions; the nonexplosion condition requires checking a positive direction and growth bounds. Neither condition alone gives a broad unmodified all-endotactic recurrence theorem.
claims.falsifier: A mismatch between the stated source theorem assumptions and the report summary; see the cited primary theorem ranges.
claims.next_gate: For a positive recurrence theorem, test the exact added-drain hypotheses or supply a new classwise physical-time Foster function. No maximal valid class is claimed.

claims.exact_statement: For same source support, generator/SDE unconfoundability follows if there exists at least one source y whose positive drift-covariance cones are disjoint; requiring disjointness at every source is incorrect. The published Theorem 3.3(2) states the latter universal condition, while Theorem 5.15 and its proof establish confoundability iff every source intersection is nonempty.
assumptions: Finite mass-action reaction networks on the same species set
Strictly positive rate constants
Faul-Hoessly-Xia local Langevin/SDE uniqueness and generator-law hypotheses
claims.status: source-reported published statement plus internally reconstructed correction and exact counterexample; no external author correction checked
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a correction of a published quantifier statement derived from the paper's own confoundability theorem and proof; no novelty or author intent claim.
claims.costs: No experimental or computational cost; exact symbolic argument.
claims.falsifier: Find positive rates for the explicit 0->A,A->0 versus 0->2A,A->0 networks yielding identical drift and covariance on an open interval; coefficient equations show this would require alpha=2 alpha'=4 alpha'.
claims.next_gate: Independent expert verification and check for an author-posted correction/erratum.

claims.exact_statement: For a fixed linear sensor H and known controlled full initial concentration x, equality of the observed local drift and covariance response fields on an open set is equivalent to equality of sourcewise projected coefficient vectors. Positive rate vectors matching those fields exist iff all projected source cones intersect; hence one empty projected intersection rules out local-response confounding.
assumptions: Finite networks with mass-action monomials and positive rates
Known linear readout H
Known full state at each controlled initial intervention, though only HX is measured as output
Response notion is conditional local first and second characteristics, not Markov generator or full partial-output path law
claims.status: internally reconstructed conditional theorem; proof included; external correctness and priority unresolved
claims.novelty_boundary: The source paper explicitly leaves partial observation as future work; related deterministic few-species identifiability exists for restricted network classes. This projection argument is short and priority is unverified.
claims.costs: Requires candidate reaction graphs, H, controlled known full initial concentrations, source-cone LP checks, and local drift/covariance measurements.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample where all projected source coefficients match on an open set but the stated local response fields differ, or where one projected source cone is disjoint yet positive-rate response fields match on an open set.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof review; extend or delimit against arbitrary partial-output path-law equivalence and unknown hidden initial concentrations.

claims.exact_statement: Given m distinct source monomials and an admissible open concentration box, m rational setpoints can be selected with invertible monomial evaluation matrix W. Pointwise local-response errors at most eta yield source coefficient error at most sqrt(m)||W^{-1}||_2 eta. If source coefficient sets under supplied positive compact rate boxes are separated by delta, nearest-set classification is correct when sqrt(m)||W^{-1}||_2 eta < delta/2.
assumptions: Same projected local-response setting as claim projected-source-cone-local-response
Admissible concentration set contains a nonempty open box
Finite distinct source exponent set known from candidate networks
Rates constrained to compact intervals bounded away from zero for a positive uniform margin
Local response estimates have a certified deterministic error bound
claims.status: internally proved algorithmic consequence; no empirical estimator or finite-window error bound implemented
claims.novelty_boundary: Uses polynomial interpolation and compact-set separation; no claim that generic finite-design or optimal experimental-design literature is exhausted.
claims.costs: m interventions and local-response estimates; exact rank search and dense O(m^3) matrix solve; error amplification ||W^{-1}|| and margin delta; sensor-panel search may cost 2^n LP checks.
claims.falsifier: Failure of the coefficient error bound under exact W, or a bounded-rate pair with disjoint projected cones but zero distance between their compact coefficient sets.
claims.next_gate: Use cycle-2 stopped-increment bounds with a well-conditioned intervention matrix, then validate real reset/readout/interlock assumptions.

claims.exact_statement: For N={B->A+B,A->0} versus N'={B->2A+B,A->0}, observing A alone while setting a=1 and intervening at b=1,2 isolates source-B local characteristics (k,k) versus (2 lambda,4 lambda), which cannot coincide for positive rates. If all rates are in [1,2], the two source coefficient sets have Euclidean gap 2, and pointwise response error eta<1/2 suffices for the two-setting contrast classifier. The matched ODE baseline can be confounded by k=2 lambda and mu=mu'.
assumptions: Langevin approximation is valid over short observation windows
B is a controlled concentration and is unchanged by the catalytic reactions
Only A is output-measured; full initial setpoint is known
Rates are positive; robust margin uses dimensionless rate box [1,2]
Estimated local drift/variance pair has per-setting Euclidean error below 1/2
claims.status: exact symbolic model calculation; experimental execution and nature-level validation absent
claims.novelty_boundary: Illustrative application of the conditional projected-cone theorem; not an empirical biological finding or priority claim.
claims.costs: Finite instantiation: 2 setpoints, 6,000,000 independent starts per point, h=1e-4, 12,000,000 resets total, at least 24,000,000 scalar endpoint reads, continuous A-channel stop monitoring, A reset and B setpoint error at most 1e-6, gain error at most 1e-6, and per-read additive residual at most 5e-7. These are assumed bounds, not measured hardware facts.
claims.falsifier: Validated local-response estimates within eta<1/2 that place both candidate source-B coefficients in overlapping sets, contrary to exact separation; or failure of the Langevin response prediction in the physical system.
claims.next_gate: Compare the finite variance-slope test against a robust stopped-CIR likelihood and ODE-only baseline after validating instrument/monitor bounds.

claims.exact_statement: For a C2 diffusion on compact K stopped/held at first exit, with bounded drift/diffusion, independent repeated starts whose reset errors are at most rho, calibrated linear sensor gain error epsilon_H, and arbitrary adversarial endpoint-increment readout residual norm at most nu, the estimators (Rh)^-1 sum Y_r and (Rh)^-1 sum Y_rY_r^T satisfy the displayed high-probability bounds beta_a+s_a and beta_Q+s_Q. The beta terms explicitly include reset and setpoint uncertainty, sensor-gain error, finite-window generator bias, stop-exit probability, drift-square/cross terms, and readout residual; s terms are coordinatewise Bernstein bounds. The data analysis uses endpoint H increments only; an invariant set or implementable stop interlock is a separate operating assumption/cost.
assumptions: C2 coefficients on a neighborhood of K; uniform bounds B,S and generator/Lipschitz bounds on K and over any setpoint uncertainty box
All replicate reset choices are fixed before the runs or randomized independently of path data; fresh diffusion increments are independent conditional on the fixed reset list
Stopped process is held at the first exit and the stopping/censoring rule can actually be implemented
Known nominal linear H and operator calibration bound epsilon_H; endpoint residual differences are deterministically bounded by nu, with no zero-mean or independence assumption
Finite-window local response is the conditional mean/covariance of the stated diffusion model, not an empirical claim about a chemical system
claims.status: internally derived conditional finite-sample theorem with proof sketch and explicit constants; not externally reviewed or experimentally validated
claims.novelty_boundary: Generic concentration, stopped-Ito bias, and moment estimation are standard tools. The proposed contribution is only the explicit combination for the projected Langevin source-response interface; priority is unverified, and moment-based error-guaranteed inference for stochastic reaction networks with unobserved species already exists for the CME model.
claims.costs: R independent resets per setpoint; two endpoint readings per run plus safety monitoring/interlock cost; setpoint/reset precision rho/rho_u; gain calibration epsilon_H; endpoint residual nu; known bounded coefficients and stop probability; matrix dimension and Bernstein sample size. No experimental cost or data were acquired.
claims.falsifier: A verified counterexample to any of the stated stopped-process bias/concentration inequalities under their assumptions, or an admissible model/reset/noise instance violating the displayed bound.
claims.next_gate: Independent stochastic-analysis proof review and measurement of real reset/readout/interlock bounds; compare to a same-data model-aware likelihood.

claims.exact_statement: For N={B->A+B at rate k, A->0 at rate mu} and Nprime={B->2A+B at rate lambda, A->0 at rate muprime}, with only A read, controlled B setpoints 1 and 2, all four rates in [1,2], h=1e-4, K_A=[0.5,2.5], A reset/setpoint uncertainties 1e-6, gain error 1e-6, endpoint residual at most 5e-7 each, and the stated B,S,Lipschitz/generator bounds, the stopped-increment variance-slope threshold at 3 using R=6,000,000 starts per setpoint has error probability at most 0.05 uniformly over each network rate box. The true nominal variance slope is in [1,2] for N and [4,8] for Nprime; the finite bound gives slope estimation error below 0.8395.
assumptions: The observed one-dimensional A Langevin diffusion is valid over each short window and the B control is constant
The A-channel interlock stops/holds the process on K_A; monitor threshold uncertainty is included in the stated reset/location bound
Fresh independent starts, rate boxes supplied, two fixed setpoints, bounded sensor calibration/readout/reset/setpoint errors as stated
All constants have the concentration/time units used by the displayed SDE; no natural-system validation
claims.status: explicit internally calculated finite-data discrimination theorem for a conditional model; no experiment or simulation performed
claims.novelty_boundary: Illustrative application of the sourcewise projected-characteristic result. A specialized shifted-CIR likelihood uses the same endpoint increments and has an exact transition law; no statistical advantage or novelty priority is claimed.
claims.costs: 12,000,000 trajectories total, h=1e-4 each; at least 24,000,000 scalar endpoint readings, continuous A-channel safety monitoring/interlock, 12,000,000 resets, 1e-6 reset/setpoint/gain envelope and 5e-7 per-endpoint residual envelope. No hardware or physical data costs measured.
claims.falsifier: Within the model and stated boxes, finding an allowed rate tuple with q(2)-q(1) outside [1,2] or [4,8], or violating the computed beta/statistical bounds. In a real system, failure to reproduce the contrast with validated noise bounds falsifies the model-to-data bridge.
claims.next_gate: Run a matched finite-data benchmark against robust/exact stopped-CIR likelihood and an ODE-only baseline; first validate instrument and monitor bounds.

claims.exact_statement: At fixed B=b, the A-only Langevin SDE in N becomes a CIR diffusion after Z=A+kb/mu, and in Nprime after Zprime=A+4 lambda b/muprime. Thus an exact scaled noncentral-chi-square endpoint transition density is available in the un-stopped model. It is a same-channel/same-setpoint model-informed likelihood control; with bounded adversarial readout it must be robustified over compatible latent increments, and with stopping it must use the stopped transition kernel or censoring atom.
assumptions: Fixed b during each replicate
The candidate SDE equations and rates are correct
Known-readout likelihood claims assume a known stochastic readout law; bounded adversarial noise is treated as an interval nuisance
The exact un-stopped CIR kernel approximates the stopped experiment only up to the explicitly bounded exit probability
claims.status: internal algebraic reduction; no likelihood optimizer or power comparison run
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a model-specific existing statistical control, not a new CIR theorem. It blocks claims that the sourcewise variance statistic is more efficient than equally informed model-based inference; minimax superiority was not evaluated.
claims.costs: Likelihood evaluation/profile over the same rate boxes and per-run reset/setpoint nuisance bounds; for stopped trajectories solve/evaluate the one-dimensional stopped transition kernel; no computation time was benchmarked.
claims.falsifier: An error in the shift-to-CIR algebra or transition parameter mapping; a direct comparison may show the robust likelihood impractical, but no such comparison is currently available.
claims.next_gate: Derive/implement the stopped-CIR robust likelihood and compare worst-case finite-sample error and compute against the moment rule.

claims.statement: For a rational recognizable series with state dimension r and all reduced realization numerators/denominators at most 2^H, evaluated on a jointly strictly upper-triangular rational tuple of dimension D whose entry heights are at most 2^B, every output entry has denominator dividing Q*=Q_lambda Q_gamma (Q_A Q_X)^(D-1), with log2 Q* <= 2rH+(D-1)(nr^2H+nD^2B). A deterministic per-entry rounded exact oracle with at least 2 log2 Q*+2 fractional bits can be reconstructed exactly by continued fractions, preserving an adaptive exact learner transcript subject to a charged rational-query-generation interface.
assumptions: The target has a rational linear realization of dimension r
Every input tuple is jointly strictly upper triangular
All realization and query rational-entry heights are bounded as supplied parameters
The exact learner's adaptive query generation and bit complexity are explicitly charged
claims.status: INTERNALLY_DERIVED_CYCLE2_CANDIDATE; PRIMARY PRIOR ART NOT CLEARED
claims.novelty_boundary: Rational reconstruction is classical. The local contribution is the explicit denominator bound for this finite nilpotent evaluation and its transcript/precision accounting. It is not a numerical stability theorem for arbitrary characteristic-zero series and does not validate L01.

claims.statement: For f_w(u)=1[u=w], w in [n]^d, minimal Hankel rank is d+1. One exact full-matrix rational query of dimension d+1 identifies w under sum_i X_i^T X_i <= I with polynomial input/output bit costs. Under the reconstructed adaptive full-matrix Gaussian oracle with fixed variance sigma^2 and the same per-query excitation cap, any zero-vs-hidden-word test with both errors <=delta has expected total query dimension and returned scalar entries at least 2 sigma^2 n^d kl(1-delta,delta).

The exact input and output are rational and exact
For the noisy interface every returned matrix entry receives independent Gaussian noise of variance sigma^2
Each query obeys the aggregate per-call excitation constraint
C is expected total query dimension under the zero target
The test must distinguish zero from every hidden word with both errors <= delta < 1/2

The output law or next-bit conditional evaluator is polynomial-time evaluable at required precision
Training access is ordinary passive trajectories only
The process may include the clocked parity automaton construction

claims.claim: For rho=2^-n, P_b has uniform fair X_1..X_n and terminal Y=b deterministically only when X=0^n, otherwise Y is fair. The shared teacher Q is uniform on all n+1 bits. Both worlds have KL(P_b||Q)=rho ln 2, TV(P_b,Q)=rho/2, and TV(P_0,P_1)=rho. Both sources have O(n) clock/flag states with probabilities in {0,1/2,1}; Q is positive and exactly evaluable.
claims.uniform_target_lower_bound: TV(P_0^m,P_1^m)=1-(1-rho)^m<=m rho. For m<=2^(n-2), equal-prior testing success is at most 5/8. A conditional predictor within 1/3 TV at h*=0^n would test b with success >=2/3, contradiction. Thus Omega(2^n)=Omega(1/zeta_n) complete P trajectories are necessary even with unlimited exact Q queries.

costs.passive_data: Each P trajectory has n+1 symbols; the lower bound is Omega(n 2^n) observed symbols.
costs.teacher: Any number of calls is uninformative because every Q answer is identical in the two worlds; a conditional Q call is O(1), full word probability output is O(n) bits.
costs.conditional_control: One chosen-prefix conditional sample from P at h*=0^n returns b deterministically; prefix specification costs n bits.

claims.claim: At cut t<=n, only prefix 0^t has nonzero conditional TV from Q; its P mass is 2^-t and conditional TV is 2^-(n-t+1). Therefore E_P[TV(P(.|H_t),Q(.|H_t))^2]=2^(-2n+t-2)<=2^-n/4=zeta_n/(4 ln 2). For every bounded future task the squared conditional-mean error is at most this value, simultaneously over tasks at that cut.
claims.consequence: The constant-state recurrence for Q itself satisfies this pair's actual-path O(zeta_n) loss whenever C>=1/(4 ln 2). The lower bound only refutes the stronger uniform-over-prefixes target; it does not refute the A06 canonical objective.

claims.statement: From N=L+q independent noiseless reset paths, row-rank recovery over F_2 recovers s under P_s with failure below 2^{-q-1}; under Q_L the N by L sample matrix has rank L except with probability below 2^{-q}. A rank-only classifier and a held-out adaptive parity test have the error bounds stated in the report.
assumptions: Independent resets produce independent length-L prefixes.
The learner sees every binary output bit exactly and knows the parity-clock class promise.
All linear algebra is over F_2; no numeric noise is present.
claims.status: INTERNALLY_DERIVED_ELEMENTARY_THEOREM; ALGORITHM IS STANDARD PARITY LEARNING
claims.novelty_boundary: No algorithmic novelty or priority claim. This is ordinary noiseless parity learning embedded in a clocked finite-state process class.
claims.costs: N paths of L bits; feature descriptor L bits; O(N L^2) bit operations; O(L^2) streaming memory. A held-out validation block adds t paths and Lt bits.
claims.falsifier: A violated union bound for rank failure or a counterexample to the unique nonzero null vector when the observed row rank is L-1.

claims.statement: Under a uniform prior on nonzero masks, N<=L-2 raw rows leave at least three equally likely nonzero nullspace candidates, so exact mask recovery success is at most 1/3. For class testing against the uniform mixture over P_s, total variation from Q_L^N is below 2^{N-L+1} for N<=L-1; thus constant-confidence classification requires L-O(1) paths.
assumptions: The prior over nonzero s is uniform for the average-case recovery statement.
The class-test lower bound compares Q_L^N with the uniform mixture over P_s^N and uses equal prior probabilities.
Observed paths are independent resets.
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary rank/posterior and likelihood-ratio argument; no priority claim.
claims.costs: Applies to any estimator/classifier with the stated raw sample interface, including arbitrary adaptive post-processing.
claims.falsifier: A likelihood-ratio or rank-deficiency probability calculation error.

claims.statement: Under independent bit flips of rate epsilon, the first-L output law is 2^{-L}(1+rho_s chi_s), rho_s=(1-2 epsilon)^wt(s), so TV from Q_L is |rho_s|/2 and a known-direction threshold test has a Hoeffding sample upper bound O(rho_s^{-2} log(1/delta)).
assumptions: Each of the first L observed bits is independently passed through a binary symmetric channel with crossover epsilon.
The fair tail is not used.
The known-s feature is evaluated exactly after channel noise.
claims.novelty_boundary: Fourier multiplier calculation only; no efficient noisy unknown-direction recovery claim.
claims.costs: A dense s and fixed positive epsilon attenuate even the known-feature expectation gap exponentially in L.
claims.falsifier: An incorrect BSC action on the character chi_s or a wrong total-variation calculation.

claims.statement: The adaptive parity constructions here neither establish nor refute the Astra L01 cyclic-grid learner because L01's stated interface is an exact full matrix-output oracle for proper recognizable series, whereas the positive theorem here uses reset paths and the auxiliary query construction uses scalar expectations of bounded path tests.
assumptions: The local source-derived Astra card L01-cyclic-grid and blocker B-EXACT-ORACLE-INTERFACE are accurately summarized.
No bridge between matrix-output, scalar-expectation, and passive-sample interfaces is assumed.
claims.novelty_boundary: Interface accounting only; navigation card is not independent proof validation.
claims.costs: L01 charges full matrix dimensions and outputs; this report separately charges reset paths, scalar answers, precision, local bit operations, and memory.
claims.falsifier: A mismatch between the L01 source card's stated query interface and the local summary or discovery of a valid bridge theorem that transfers guarantees between these access models.

ledger.task: Adaptive conditional feature acquisition beyond supplied parity
ledger.overall_status: internal proof for structured rank-2 case; general conditional-sample TV learning open problem closed by Liu-Moitra STOC 2025; exact worst-history feature identification is not implied by constant-TV learning

claims.claim: With A_i=A_{i-1}1{X_i=s_i}, X_i fair, and Z_i|A_i distributed as Ber(3/4) if alive and Ber(1/4) if dead, every cut has at most two distinct future rows, hence rank at most 2. A clocked HMM lift uses at most 8T+1 states; emitting transition weights are 1/8 or 3/8, with deterministic termination allowed.
claims.supplied_structure: T, the pair alphabet, clocked prefix-match template, and marker noise 1/4; no secret s or candidate predictive-feature dictionary is supplied.
claims.proof: PROOFS_CYCLE2.md section 1

claims.claim: Independent chosen-prefix full-suffix conditional samples recover s exactly with failure at most delta using m=ceil(2(1-2eta)^(-2)log(2T/delta)) calls per bit. The statistic R=(-1)^X(Z-1/2) has conditional mean plus or minus (1-2eta)/2.
assumptions: Fresh independent suffix per call
Exact observed symbols
Known eta or certified upper bound below 1/2

resources.returned_suffixes: m*T*(T+1)/2 pair symbols = m*T*(T+1) bits; all suffix symbols charged
resources.communication: m*T^2 pair symbols = 2*m*T^2 raw bits, excluding framing
resources.memory: O(T+log m) bits with streamed responses; plus O(T) pair symbols if buffering a suffix
resources.runtime: O(m*T^2) bit operations including all I/O and prefix encoding
resources.precision: No numerical oracle output; exact half-integer arithmetic; T-bit feature output

claims.proof: PROOFS_CYCLE2.md section 2

claims.claim: For two words differing only in s_T, exact one-path TV is (1-2eta)*2^(-(T-1)). Any estimator on N iid passive paths has average last-bit error at least [1-N*(1-2eta)*2^(-(T-1))]/2; success >=2/3 requires N>=2^(T-1)/(3*(1-2eta)). At eta=1/4 this is 2^T/3.
claims.scope: Exact rare-history feature identification, not constant-TV distribution approximation.
claims.proof: PROOFS_CYCLE2.md section 3

claims.claim: Along a successful run, the exact queried history ((s_1,1),...,(s_{k-1},1)) has mass ((1-eta)/2)^(k-1), or (3/8)^(k-1) for eta=1/4. Passive rejection costs the inverse expected resets. Conditional-call count is therefore not an equal-cost passive sample count.
claims.proof: CYCLE2_REPORT.md and PROOFS_CYCLE2.md section 2

claims.claim: Kakade et al. COLT 2023 Open Problem 1 asks for efficient chosen-prefix conditional-sample learning of any low-rank law. Liu and Moitra STOC 2025 Theorem 1.3 resolves arbitrary-rank distribution learning in TV with poly(S,|Omega|,T,1/epsilon) conditional queries/time and an efficiently samplable output.
claims.scope: Does not imply exact rare-history feature recovery at polynomial T: neighboring words have TV only (1-2eta)*2^(-(T-1)); a generic TV guarantee must take epsilon below half this gap. This is not a lower bound against a specialized algorithm.

claims.claim: At equal response-symbol budget, m calls per level return m*T*(T+1)/2 pair symbols, matched by floor(m*(T+1)/2) passive paths. An oracle-known-s control uses T side-information bits and can score the same conditional validation responses. Passive and conditional validation samples cannot be literally paired because the interfaces return different conditional laws. GF(2) nullspace on X has no information because X is iid uniform independent of s.

ledger.novelty_boundary: No novelty claim. Explicit feature-identification witness and passive lower bound for a structured rank-two class. Arbitrary-rank conditional-sample TV learning is covered by Liu-Moitra STOC 2025.

ledger.scope: Exact active identification of finite deterministic controlled input-output behavior; no biological validation claimed.

claims.claim: For two deterministic Mealy machines with at most n states each and different response functions from their initial states, a distinguishing intervention word exists with length at most n^2.
claims.basis: A shortest distinguishing path in the product machine cannot revisit a product state; the product has at most n^2 states.
limits: Requires finite deterministic machines and exact outputs.

claims.claim: Adaptive pairwise version-space elimination identifies the exact intervention-to-output response function within at most M_n-1 experiments, each of length at most n^2, where M_n=sum_{k=1}^n k^(k|A|+1)|Y|^(k|A|).
claims.basis: Enumerate every labeled machine up to n states, quotient duplicate response functions, run a shortest separating word for a disagreeing pair, and retain only candidates consistent with each full trace.
limits: Worst-case experiment, compute, and memory bounds are exponential/astronomical; no efficiency claim.

claims.claim: The response function determines the reachable minimal predictive state quotient q~r iff every future intervention word produces the same output word from q and r.
claims.basis: Residual response maps define the quotient; any merged non-equivalent pair has a distinguishing continuation.
limits: This is behavioral predictive state, not molecular state, a causal DAG, or a mechanistic invariant.

claims.claim: Without a known finite state cap, no finite set of finite-horizon experiments certifies the entire unbounded intervention-response function.
claims.basis: For tests of maximum length H, an all-zero one-state machine and an H+1-delay chain can agree on every completed experiment and differ on a longer word.
limits: Does not rule out approximate or distribution-specific prediction.

claims.claim: Moore's finite-state experimental framework is deterministic and black-box; it explicitly notes that scientific systems can be continuous or probabilistic, limiting direct application to biology.

He and Geng's active causal intervention design targets orientation within an observational Markov-equivalence class under faithfulness and no latent variables; it does not by itself acquire the supplied graph/class or a predictive state machine.

A primary HCMV single-cell study reports temporal infection trajectories and perturbations that stall, delay, accelerate, or alter progression, motivating dynamic predictive targets but not validating finite-state acquisition.

The cell-control application is a proposed idealized use case; deterministic transitions, exact repeated reset, finite response bins, and a known state cap are not established for ordinary cell assays.
claims.basis: Biological interpretation of the formal interface and limitations discussed in REPORT.md.

not_claimed: Novelty or priority of the finite-state theorem.
Recovery of a causal graph, hidden molecular state, or biological invariant.
Exact finite-state acquisition on existing Perturb-seq data.

ledger.exact_statement: For the class f_w(u)=1[u=w], w in [n]^d, over Q, the minimal Hankel rank is d+1. A single exact full-matrix query of dimension d+1 can identify w with polynomial input and output bit cost while satisfying sum_i X_i^T X_i <= I. In the adaptive full-matrix Gaussian oracle of the N25 card, any zero-vs-hidden-word test with both errors <= delta and per-query excitation cap E=1 has expected total query dimension C >= 2 sigma^2 n^d kl(1-delta,delta); expected returned-entry count is at least C.
assumptions: n >= 2 and d >= 1
full matrix output, independent Gaussian noise with variance sigma^2 in every real entry
each query tuple satisfies sum_i X_i^T X_i <= I
C is expected sum of query matrix dimensions under the zero target
the noisy learner distinguishes zero from every f_w with both errors at most delta < 1/2
ledger.novelty_boundary: This is a strict interface counterexample to naive exact-to-noisy transfer for a finite hidden-word subclass. It does not refute L01 or prove priority; exact weighted-automaton learning, noisy spectral learning, tolerance-based active automata, and adaptive Gaussian sensing all have prior art.

ledger.title: Sufficient predictive compression under finite samples

interface.source: n iid categorical observations from an unknown fixed law on K symbols, or a fixed controlled dynamical system
interface.target: predict the next symbol/future block under the same law, or predict action-conditioned tests under the same system
interface.shift_case: target representation may have an unknown binary alignment bit; only unlabeled target representations are available

claims.claim: The K-symbol histogram is sufficient for the unknown iid categorical law, and every posterior predictive future-block law under any prior depends on the sample only through the histogram.
assumptions: iid sampling
same law for future observations
finite alphabet K

cost.precision: exact integer counts and rational output under rational prior

claims.claim: The empirical categorical predictor has expected one-step TV error at most (1/2)sqrt((K-1)/n).
assumptions: iid sampling
same source law
claims.scope: expectation guarantee, not a high-probability guarantee

claims.claim: Any exact summary of length-n histories that must preserve next-symbol predictions for every process over a K-symbol alphabet must be injective on K^n histories, requiring at least n log2(K) bits.
assumptions: all possible processes are in scope
exact next-symbol prediction
claims.scope: does not rule out compression for a fixed structured process

claims.claim: Every environment represented by a finite POMDP has a linear PSR whose number of tests is at most the state count of a minimal POMDP.
claims.evidence: Littman, Sutton, Singh (2001), Theorem 1, PDF pp. 6-10
claims.scope: representation from supplied POMDP; no finite-sample acquisition theorem. Paper identifies action-conditioned PSR learning as open work.

claims.claim: With a hidden target encoder flip, source labels and unlabeled target marginals have identical observable laws in two worlds with opposite target rules; every learner, including one retaining raw source data and receiving infinitely many unlabeled target samples, has error at least 1/2 in one world.
claims.status: proved in report by two-world construction
assumptions: binary uniform latent variable
source encoding identity
unknown target identity-or-flip encoder
no target labels or cross-domain alignment pairs

cost.unlabeled_target_samples: no finite or infinite number distinguishes the two worlds

claims.scope: strict unknown-alignment no-go; do not generalize to known transforms or invariant-label shift models

claims.claim: Covariate shift by itself does not guarantee successful domain adaptation without further distribution-similarity or shared low-error-classifier assumptions; the cited lower bounds apply without target labels.
claims.evidence: Ben-David, Lu, Luu, Pal (2010), AISTATS/PMLR 9:129-136
claims.scope: domain-adaptation hypotheses and access model from the paper

claims.claim: Ruan, Dubois, Maddison characterize idealized optimal representations under their assumptions via task discriminability and support matching, and prove a no-free-lunch result for source-only representation learning in their stated setting.
claims.evidence: Ruan, Dubois, Maddison (ICLR 2022), Theorem 1 §3.2 and Proposition 1 / Appendix Proposition 4 §B.3
claims.scope: discrete spaces and idealized population-risk model with stated generalized covariate-shift and Bayes-image assumptions

unresolved: Finite-sample PSR acquisition with explicit coverage, identifiability, conditioning, precision, and runtime bounds.
A nontrivial prediction guarantee for the actual target representation interface, if any is supplied.
Novelty or priority of the elementary two-world hidden-alignment construction.

ledger.topic: stationary three-state cycle assay with unknown shared emissions

claims.statement: For independent stationary replicate pairs (Y0,Yh) from a common time-invariant column-stochastic 3x3 emission matrix E with certified sigma_min(E)>=sigma_floor>0, H0:d=0 gives population pair skew S=C-C^T=0, while H1:d=4pi/(sqrt(3)tau), s in [s_min,s_max], s_min>d, gives ||S||_F >= (2sqrt(2)/3) sigma_floor^2 exp(-3 s_max h/2)|sin(2pi h/tau)|. The threshold test ||S_hat||_F>=Delta/2, using the empirical pair skew, has each testing error at most alpha for n=ceil((2sqrt(2)+4sqrt(ln(1/alpha)))^2/Delta_*^2) independent pairs at h*=tau/(2pi) atan(4pi/(3s_max tau)), where Delta_*=(2sqrt(2)/3)sigma_floor^2 exp(-atan(x)/x)x/sqrt(1+x^2), x=4pi/(3s_max tau).
assumptions: The hidden three-state cycle is initialized in its uniform stationary law.
The same emission matrix E is used at both pair endpoints and under both hypotheses.
The assay supplies independent reset pairs; overlapping observations from one path are not treated as iid.
tau, s_min, s_max are known and sigma_min(E)>=sigma_floor is certified.
The test uses only lag-h pair asymmetry, not a same-lineage three-time likelihood.
claims.novelty_boundary: Scoped statistical construction for the supplied three-state cycle; no novelty or priority claim.
claims.costs: n independent stationary resets, 2n emission records, and n*h_* cumulative replicate exposure; add calibration and any endpoint-control arm separately.
claims.falsifier: A mistake in the hidden semigroup/skew norm, the emission congruence bound, the bounded-difference constant, or the stated sample-size algebra.
claims.next_gate: Derive the joint three-time likelihood if the same lineage is observed at 0,h,tau; otherwise keep the theorem restricted to independent pair arms.

claims.statement: For E_kappa=kappa I+(1-kappa)11^T/3 and one stationary lag-h pair, the exact chi-square divergence Xi=chi^2(p1||p0) is 4r^2(1-cos(phi))^2/[3(1+2r)] + r^2/(1-r)[2(1-cos(phi))^2/3+2sin(phi)^2], r=kappa^2 exp(-3sh/2), phi=2pi h/tau. Any test with both errors at most alpha<1/2 from n independent pairs must satisfy n>=ln(1+4(1-2alpha)^2)/ln(1+Xi). Independent known-state emission calibration and independent lag-tau alias pairs add zero divergence when shared identically under both hypotheses. At h=tau, Xi=0; at kappa=0, Xi=0 for every h.
assumptions: The same s is used under H0 and H1, with any fixed s in the admissible interval.
The 3-state emitter E_kappa is common under both hypotheses and 0<=kappa<=1.
Process samples are independent lag-h pairs; any lag-tau control arm is a separate independent arm.
Calibration probes emissions from known hidden states independently of the transition dynamics.
claims.novelty_boundary: An explicit two-point lower bound for this finite-state assay, not a general HMM minimax theorem.
claims.costs: The lower bound counts only informative lag-h pairs. Calibration emissions and separate endpoint-alias pairs still count toward total assay cost even though their likelihood ratio is one.
claims.falsifier: An error in the nine-cell observed pair laws, chi-square summation, product tensorization, or the total-variation/chi-square inequality.
claims.next_gate: For a shared path read at 0,h,tau, recompute the joint law and divergence; pairwise alias marginals alone do not establish that triple data are uninformative.

claims.statement: With m_E independent known-state emission standards per hidden state, the empirical 3x3 E satisfies max-entry error<=eta with probability at least 1-18 exp(-2m_E eta^2), yielding the valid lower confidence bound sigma_min(E)>=sigma_min(E_hat)-3eta. A margin promise sigma_min(E)>=sigma_floor+6eta makes the floor certify with probability at least 1-alpha_cal when m_E=ceil(ln(18/alpha_cal)/(2eta^2)). For E_kappa, eta=kappa/12 certifies sigma_floor=kappa/2 using ceil(72 kappa^-2 ln(18/alpha_cal)) standards per hidden state.
assumptions: Each known hidden state can be prepared or reliably labeled for calibration.
Emission samples are independent and use the same stationary assay sensor channel.
A 6eta slack between true sigma_min(E) and the floor to be certified is available.
claims.novelty_boundary: Hoeffding plus Weyl calibration accounting; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: 3m_E labeled-state emission records, plus preparation/sorting/verification of each standard; allocate alpha_cal separately from testing alpha.
claims.falsifier: A failure of the coordinatewise Hoeffding union bound, Frobenius/operator norm conversion, or Weyl singular-value perturbation step.
claims.next_gate: Replace ideal known-state standards with the actual assay's state-label error and preparation cost model, or retain sigma_floor as an explicit external certificate.

claims.statement: For any passive-sample budget B and any estimator of the worst-history conditional transition probability, there are two stationary 2-state binary HMMs with common A-to-B transition epsilon, theta in {1/4,3/4}, deterministic full-rank emissions, full-rank transitions, and hidden-chain absolute spectral gap at least 1/4 such that max_theta E_theta[|theta_hat-theta|] >= (1-4 B epsilon)/4 when 4 B epsilon <= 1. The guarantee also covers arbitrary adaptive post-hoc observable selection from the same data.
assumptions: The learner receives at most B emitted symbols from one or more stationary reset episodes.
No intervention changes hidden transitions and no exact conditional-probability oracle is supplied.
The scored target is the conditional probability P(Y_{t+1}=1 | Y_t=1), under absolute loss.
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary missing-context/coverage lower bound; no novelty or priority claim. It is narrower than an average-risk or fixed-horizon total-variation impossibility.
claims.costs: All observed output symbols, across all reset episodes, count toward B. Post-hoc computation is unrestricted. Active interventions or conditional oracles are outside the interface.
claims.falsifier: A proof audit finding a violated stationary-marginal union bound, an estimator whose output law on the all-zero transcript depends on theta beyond that transcript, or an arithmetic error in the triangle-inequality risk bound.
claims.next_gate: For a positive theorem, state an explicit lower bound on relevant context mass or provide a costed active policy guaranteeing visits; then compare worst-history and stationary-average losses separately.

claims.statement: The 2-state construction satisfies the rank assumptions in Hsu-Kakade-Zhang (positive stationary initial support and full-rank transition/emission matrices), while sigma_min(P_{2,1})=Theta(epsilon). The paper's finite-horizon spectral guarantee depends on inverse singular values of O and P_{2,1}; its separate conditional-KL guarantee is history-averaged and adds strict positivity assumptions that deterministic emissions violate.
assumptions: Hsu-Kakade-Zhang 2012 source statements are read at Condition 1, Theorem 6, Condition 3, and Theorem 7.
P_{2,1} uses rows for the second observation and columns for the first.
claims.novelty_boundary: A consistency/conditioning comparison, not a new spectral-learning theorem and not a refutation of Hsu-Kakade-Zhang.
claims.costs: Spectral learners use the same raw observation budget in the comparison. Their rank and singular-value promises must be charged as model conditions; the lower bound covers any estimator given those observations.
claims.falsifier: The source theorem has been misread, the pair-probability matrix formula or determinant is incorrect, or the claimed Theta(epsilon) singular-value scaling fails for either fixed theta value.
claims.next_gate: If benchmarking implementations, feed the same reset tuples and report both joint-law error and conditional error on the rare context; record numerical regularization and initialization.

claims.statement: For every fixed policy with loss in [0,1], |R_Q(pi)-R_P(pi)| <= TV(P,Q); hence joint TV(P,Q)<=rho gives robust target risk <= source risk + rho.
claims.evidence: Bounded-function variational characterization of total variation; proof in REPORT.md.
claims.scope: TV is over the full joint feature-label law. A marginal-only feature divergence does not imply this claim without conditional-label structure.
claims.costs: No density-ratio estimation, target samples, or target labels are used; rho is a supplied valid upper bound.

claims.statement: For a finite M-policy class and n iid fully labeled source examples, empirical risk minimization has target robust risk <= best source risk + 2 sqrt(log(2M/alpha)/(2n)) + rho with probability >=1-alpha.
claims.evidence: Uniform two-sided Hoeffding bound over the finite class and the TV transfer lemma; derivation in REPORT.md.
claims.scope: The bound does not imply an adaptive-acquisition advantage when the baseline may optimize over the same policy class and transcript.

claims.statement: For uniform independent bits (Z0,A,B), Y=A when Z0=0 and Y=B when Z0=1, an ERM over 16 branch-conditioned policies queries exactly two features and has robust target risk <= sqrt(log(16/alpha)/(2n))+rho; every fixed feature subset of size at most two has robust risk at least 1/4. claims.evidence: Conditional Bayes-error lower bound, finite-class one-sided Hoeffding bound, and a TV reweighting adversary for the concrete static rule; full proof and accounting in REPORT.md.
claims.scope: Advantage is over nonadaptive fixed-subset feature acquisition under a two-query deployment cap. It is not an advantage over adaptive robust ERM with the same policy class.

claims.statement: A feature-marginal TV budget alone cannot bound target classification risk without an assumption on conditional label laws.

claims.scope: Exact even when feature marginals are identical.

claims.statement: For a finite family rho_e=P_e/Q_e with finite rational exponent supports and strictly positive rational coefficients, the common positive denominator D=product_f Q_f lifts channel e to P_e product_(f!=e) Q_f. Its source height is h_D(w)+h_Pe(w)-h_Qe(w). Therefore the standard essential-source endotactic criterion is equivalent before and after lifting, provided neutral channels are excluded before maximizing and every active top tie is tested.
assumptions: Every P_e and Q_e has a finite nonempty support in Q^d and all coefficients are positive rational numbers; no numerator or denominator vanishes on R^d_{>0}.
Each channel has one fixed reaction vector nu_e; if coefficients vary in time, they are measurable and lie in one common compact positive interval.
The endotactic test is the essential-source condition: for each w, remove e with w dot nu_e=0, maximize source order over the remaining channels, and require every maximizer to satisfy w dot nu_e<0.
claims.novelty_boundary: Common denominator multiplication and support-function additivity are elementary; the report makes no historical novelty claim. In two species, the permanence consequence reduces to established endotactic power-law permanence after time change. The finite direct LP-cell recognizer is a transparent exponential exact formulation, not a demonstrated advantage over lifted-graph MILP.

ledger.exact_statement: For a nonnegative absolutely continuous active-enzyme abundance satisfying dE/dt=p-gamma*E, E(0)=E0, with measurable envelopes 0<=p<=pbar, gamma>=gamma_lower>=0 and catalytic turnover kcat<=kbar, the abundance is bounded by Ebar(t)=E0 exp(-Gamma(t))+integral_0^t pbar(s) exp(-(Gamma(t)-Gamma(s))) ds, Gamma(t)=integral_0^t gamma_lower. A forward flux v_j<=chi*kbar*E therefore satisfies integral_0^T v_j<=integral_0^T chi*kbar*Ebar. Thermodynamic gate chi is zero only when the measured Gibbs interval robustly forbids forward flux; uncertain direction retains chi=1.
assumptions: measurable locally integrable parameter envelopes
specific synthesis p and dilution/degradation gamma share consistent biomass basis
forward flux obeys v<=kcat*E
TFA directionality used only with a declared strict Gibbs margin

claims.statement: Let integer-complex reactions y_r->y'_r have jumps nu_r, molecular intensities V k_r(t) phi^V_{y_r}(X^V_{t-}), and a compact positive safe polytope Q in a stoichiometric class with proper relative facets g_i(x)=a_i^T x+b_i>=0. Let predictable allocations satisfy k_t in a nonempty compact coupled set K(X^V_{t-}) subset product_r[0,kbar_r], and suppose for each facet i there are theta_i,eta_i,ell_i>0 such that sup_{x in Q, 0<=g_i(x)<=ell_i, k in K(x)} sum_r k_r x^{y_r}(exp(-theta_i a_i^T nu_r)-1) <= -eta_i. With D_i=sum_r kbar_r E_{y_r}(U)|exp(-theta_i a_i^T nu_r)-1|, any certified C_i>=max(0,sup_{x in Q,k in K(x)} H_i), c_i=theta_i ell_i, V_0=max(1,max_i ceil(2D_i/eta_i)), and any finite activity bound Lambda_Q>=sup_{x in Q,k in K(x)}sum_r k_r x^{y_r}, every compatible initial lattice point X_0^V in Q and every predictable admissible allocation obey, for V>=V_0 and finite T, P(tau_Q<=T) <= sum_i exp(-theta_i V g_i(X_0^V)) + T sum_i (V C_i+D_i)exp(-c_i V). The result is a conditional candidate theorem: it follows from the exact molecular generator, the uniform falling-factorial correction, and a stopped exponential-potential/Dynkin argument; it does not imply infinite-time survival or stochastic permanence.
assumptions: Each reaction has integer nonnegative molecular complexes and uses the stated falling-factorial mass-action convention; factorial divisors are absorbed into k_r.
Q is compact, lies in the strictly positive orthant and in the supplied affine stoichiometric class; all remaining inequalities are proper relative facets and coordinate bounds U are supplied.
K(x) is nonempty compact and contained in the per-reaction box [0,kbar]; the control is predictable, including any dependence on time, past history, or independent randomness.
The coupled exponential-generator collar inequality is globally certified for every facet and every feasible allocation, not merely sampled on trajectories.
The initial count is on the required integer reaction-lattice/coset and belongs to Q; the result's volume threshold uses the exact finite-volume correction D_i.

claims.statement: For locally Lipschitz dissipative ecological equations x_i'=x_i f_i(z), y'=g(z), assume (A3a) every missing-species invasion rate is nonzero for every boundary ergodic measure, (A3b) signs for a missing species are constant across ergodic measures with the same species support, and the invasion graph is acyclic. If each -i community has positive invasion rate for its absent species i, Hofbauer-Schreiber Corollary 1 implies robust permanence. A twice continuously differentiable system with a boundary subcommunity at which every missing species has a negative invasion rate is not permanent (their Remark 3).

acyclic invasion graph
