claims.statement: In the cyclic May-Leonard competitive Lotka-Volterra system x1'=x1(1-x1-beta x2-alpha x3), x2'=x2(1-alpha x1-x2-beta x3), x3'=x3(1-beta x1-alpha x2-x3), take alpha=0.8 and beta=1.3. At each single-species equilibrium one absent strain invades at rate 1-alpha=+0.2 while the other has rate 1-beta=-0.3, yet the boundary supports an attracting heteroclinic cycle and the system is not permanent. Thus singleton invasion information without invasion-graph acyclicity is insufficient.

claims.falsifier: A correctly specified autonomous unicycle with measured stationary traffic and affinity violating the inequality beyond uncertainty.

claims.exact_statement: Under tight coupling with one fuel input and one work output per net cycle, dimensionless fuel affinity A_f, dimensionless load l in [0,A_f], and a maintained bare-rate cap K, output power satisfies P_out(l)<=k_B*T*(K/N^2)*l*tanh((A_f-l)/(2N)). This pointwise envelope does not identify the efficiency at maximum power of a fixed catalyst without its load-dependent rate law.
assumptions: All assumptions of CT1
No slippage, side cycles, or uncoupled fuel consumption
The load work and fuel input refer to the same tightly coupled net cycle
K remains capped by the same value at the operating load
claims.novelty_boundary: Pointwise result follows directly from CT1 under tight coupling. The envelope maximizer is not a universal or device-specific EMP claim; EMP load sharing is established model-dependent prior art.
costs: Measure chemical input, product output, force or torque, displacement, temperature, and the load-dependent transition rates.
Quantify futile cycles, reverse steps, slippage, and barrier-control energy before reporting efficiency.
Any barrier tuning or active rate control must be included in the engineering cost ledger.
claims.falsifier: A tightly coupled model satisfying the assumptions with output power above the pointwise envelope at the same A_f, l, N, and K.
claims.next_gate: For a named device, characterize the full load-dependent rate law and test tight coupling before predicting any efficiency-at-maximum-power value.

claims.exact_statement: Affinity alone cannot upper-bound current: multiplying all forward and backward rates by c>0 leaves A and the stationary distribution unchanged while multiplying J by c. Barrier changes that multiply both directions on an edge preserve that edge rate ratio and can alter current without changing the cycle affinity.
assumptions: Autonomous unicycle with positive rates
Barrier perturbations act symmetrically on forward and backward rates of the affected edge
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary scaling counterexample and interpretation of established barrier-control results; not a novelty claim.
costs: A meaningful turnover prediction must acquire or bound rate constants/traffic in addition to affinity.
Barrier interventions require separate calibration of their effects on each directional rate and control work.
claims.falsifier: None within the stated rate-rescaling operation; it is an algebraic identity. A physical intervention failing to rescale rates as assumed does not refute the mathematical counterexample.
claims.next_gate: Reject claims that infer work, efficiency, or current from barrier amplitude alone unless a separate calibrated kinetic and thermodynamic model is supplied.

claims.exact_statement: In a multicycle system, a measured product current and its nominal cycle affinity do not determine total dissipation or thermodynamic efficiency when independent futile fuel-consuming cycles are unobserved.
assumptions: At least two cycle currents can operate; one contributes product and another consumes fuel without product
Total entropy production includes all cycle affinities and currents
claims.novelty_boundary: Follows from standard cycle decomposition and the product-chain counterexample; no novelty claim.
costs: Measure all coupled cycle fluxes, fuel consumption, product output, and work to estimate efficiency.
Resolve branches, slippage pathways, and futile loops; hidden cycle states can invalidate a unicyclic reduction.
claims.falsifier: The counterexample is structural; it is blocked only by independently establishing a genuinely single-cycle, tightly coupled device with no other fuel-consuming path.
claims.next_gate: Use cycle-resolved fluxes and full reservoir accounting before interpreting product turnover as thermodynamic efficiency.

claims.exact_statement: The finite random-rate diagnostic sampled 1000 positive rate vectors at each of 15 (N,A) choices for N in {2,3,4,5,7} and A in {0.2,1,4}, normalized K=1, found no sampled current above (1), and reproduced the uniform equality case to floating precision.
assumptions: Diagnostic code and Python floating-point arithmetic as recorded in finite_check.py
Fixed random seed 20261008
claims.novelty_boundary: Finite deterministic sample only; neither a theorem proof nor evidence of priority/external validation.
costs: 1000 sampled stationary linear solves per (N,A) pair; Python standard library only.
claims.falsifier: The recorded output or code replay differs, or a sampled point exceeds the bound; the latter would signal a proof/model/implementation issue requiring investigation.
claims.next_gate: Retain only as a reproducibility check; the analytical proof is the basis for the theorem claim.

claims.exact_statement: The reviewed pinned Astra records N34, N35, N76, and N77 do not provide the CT1 unicycle current-versus-affinity-and-bare-rate-sum theorem; their claims concern reaction recognition/certification, finite-horizon molecular-jump safety, event-chain growth, and stationary tightness, respectively.
assumptions: Pinned Astra commit 8ede33c2f09a8abe07b430892b3ac4bb71c27c83
Review limited to the relevant indexed cards and supplied source mappings
claims.novelty_boundary: A limited audit of adjacent cards does not establish novelty against the broader literature.
costs: Source-retrieval and card-review effort is recorded in the parent chemistry workspace; no external tool or experiment was run for these cards.
claims.falsifier: A pinned card or proof range stating the same current-affinity-bare-rate-sum result under matching assumptions.
claims.next_gate: Use only as an Astra boundary check; broader priority review remains open.

ledger.overall_status: A useful finite-resource kernel boundary is reconstructed for an ideal continuous spatial clock. The recent apparatus is a source-reported spectroscopy demonstration, not a demonstrated stabilized or alias-free clock. The kernel theorem is internal model mathematics; no new physical capability or priority claim is established.
ledger.target: Test whether spatially gated continuous atom transport removes a measurement bottleneck after temporal response, atom flux, and a strongest zero-dead-time control are charged.

claims.exact_statement: For the ideal normalized rectangular per-atom phase response z_t=tau^{-1} integral_t^{t+tau} y(s) ds, averaging over a uniform continuum of atom start times t in [0,T-tau] gives aggregate kernel k_T(s)=|[0,T-tau] intersect [s-tau,s]|/[tau(T-tau)]. It is flat on the interior [tau,T-tau] and has boundary ramps of width tau. Its per-atom frequency response is exp(i pi f tau) sinc(pi f tau), with exact zeros at every nonzero f=k/tau.
claims.status: internally derived exact result for the stated ideal phase-averaging interface; it is not the measured Rabi sensitivity function of the apparatus
assumptions: Known constant transit time tau and uniform spatial/temporal atom-start density over the stated interval.
Linearized phase response is a rectangular average; actual Rabi excitation probabilities, velocity spread, spatial magnetic-field profile, and contrast inhomogeneity are not included.
Atom outcomes are combined with equal weights for the aggregate-kernel formula.
claims.novelty_boundary: Rectangular-window Fourier zeros and Fubini aggregation are elementary model consequences, not a claim of novel metrology. The contribution is a scoped boundary against inferring alias-free readout from continuous delivery alone.
costs: Transit time tau=L/v and its calibration uncertainty.
Atom flux, arrival-time/occupancy record, and edge handling over the measurement interval.
Empirical Rabi sensitivity-function identification, LO-noise PSD, contrast, and state/readout noise.
claims.physical_falsifier: For the actual moving-lattice apparatus, measure the complex response to weak LO frequency-modulation tones. A response incompatible with the measured per-atom sensitivity function or absence of its predicted conditioning/null structure refutes transfer of the rectangular model; it does not refute the aggregate-kernel identity.
claims.next_gate: Measure the actual atom-resolved sensitivity function and repeat the transfer-function experiment with a matched, gapless two-ensemble interleaved clock at the same isotope, LO, interrogation time, total atom flux, contrast, and readout.

claims.exact_statement: For a stationary Poisson stream of atoms entering a zone with dwell time tau at rate r, the in-zone occupancy at a fixed interior time is Poisson(r tau), so the empty-zone probability is exp(-r tau) and occupancy coefficient of variation is 1/sqrt(r tau). The expected number of arrival gaps longer than tau across duration T is approximately r T exp(-r tau), up to boundary effects; this is a Markov bound on the probability of any such uncovered interval.
claims.status: internally derived exact Poisson occupancy result plus a long-record expected-gap approximation; Poisson arrivals are not asserted for the published lattice conveyor
assumptions: Stationary homogeneous Poisson arrival process, independent of the LO and atom outcome noise.
Each atom contributes sensitivity on exactly one interval of length tau.
Long-record gap-rate approximation ignores start/end correction terms.
claims.novelty_boundary: The occupancy identities are standard Poisson-process consequences. They show that mean continuous delivery does not by itself guarantee gap-free or uniform sensitivity under a stochastic arrival model.
costs: Required flux depends logarithmically on total observation time and desired gap probability.
No-gap coverage and pointwise sensitivity flatness are different constraints; at r tau=18, pointwise occupancy CV is about 24%.
Empirical arrival Fano factor and spatial occupancy must be measured before using the Poisson model.
claims.physical_falsifier: Time-tag atom arrivals/occupancy. A non-Poisson record outside the assumed model invalidates its numerical gap bound; an observed gap rate materially above r T exp(-r tau) after boundary correction falsifies the stated Poisson approximation.
claims.next_gate: Obtain the source's atom arrival/occupancy record and evaluate the measured sensitivity-weighted coverage, not merely the mean loading rate.

claims.exact_statement: In an ideal independent-atom mid-fringe phase readout with contrast C, per-atom interrogation duration tau, and N detections, frequency Fisher information is 4 pi^2 C^2 tau^2 N, yielding sd(nu_hat) >= 1/(2 pi C tau sqrt(N)). A spatial conveyor and a gapless interleaved two-ensemble clock with equal N, tau, C, per-atom response kernel, and readout noise have identical QPN/readout floors in this model.
claims.status: internally derived benchmark model; not an observed clock stability or an exact formula for the source's Rabi line
assumptions: Ideal local mid-fringe phase likelihood with independent Bernoulli outcomes.
Known contrast C, calibrated interrogation time tau, and identical effective phase kernels across architectures.
Equal total detected atoms N and equal total averaging time; LO noise and dead-time costs must be compared separately.
claims.novelty_boundary: The QPN formula is standard. It denies an automatic precision gain from continuous transport against a strongest already gapless interleaved control; spatial transport may still improve hardware throughput or synchronization overhead.
costs: Atoms per second and total detected atoms.
Per-atom clock exposure tau and total atom-time N tau.
Contrast, atom preparation and readout photons, laser/transport/magnetic-field power, LO PSD, and calibration uncertainty.
claims.physical_falsifier: At equal atom flux, duration, interrogation response, and readout, a reproducible Allan-deviation advantage over the two-ensemble control would falsify the equal-resource no-automatic-gain conclusion's physical transfer; a null difference supports architecture-only benefit within that tested band.
claims.next_gate: Run both clock architectures on the same LO with matched total Sr atoms, measured transit/readout costs, injected common LO spectrum, and preregistered Allan-deviation bands.

claims.exact_statement: Under tau=0.75 s, r=24 s^-1, T=86400 s, and C=1, a Poisson arrival fixture has mean in-zone occupancy 18, fixed-time empty probability exp(-18), expected long-gap count scale 0.032/day, occupancy CV 23.6%, N=2,073,600, ideal mid-fringe QPN/readout frequency SD about 0.147 mHz, and first rectangular-kernel zero 1.33 Hz.
claims.status: reproducible illustrative calculation; none of these flux/noise figures is reported for the spatial-clock apparatus
assumptions: Uses the stated ideal Poisson and mid-fringe phase models.
claims.novelty_boundary: A feasibility-scale calculation only; it is not a source-data replay, engineered design, or instrument prediction.
costs: Flux 24 atoms/s; 18 atoms simultaneously in the 0.75-s zone; 2,073,600 detected atoms per day; contrast assumed unity.
claims.physical_falsifier: Measured flux, contrast, atom correlations, or LO/readout spectra that differ from the illustrative assumptions make the numerical prediction inapplicable.
claims.next_gate: Replace every fixture value with measured values and include preparation/readout throughput, transport energy, calibration uncertainty, and LO PSD.

source_boundary.primary_spatial_platform: Nishida et al., Nature Communications 17, 7662 (2026), https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-76017-1. Source-reported 88Sr moving-lattice transport at 16 mm/s through a 12-mm interaction region, localized magnetic clock coupling, and a 1.2-Hz-wide spectrum. This is spectroscopy and continuous delivery, not a demonstrated stabilized clock or measured alias-free Allan deviation.
source_boundary.strong_control_prior_art: Zero-Dead-Time Strontium Lattice Clock with a Stability at 10^-19 Level, Phys. Rev. Lett. (2026), DOI 10.1103/zbpb-6qxb; source-reported interleaved ensembles and 2.9e-19 at 20,000 s. It is a strong architecture control but a different isotope/device, so it is not an equal-resource same-apparatus trial.
source_boundary.external_validation: No independent replication or specialist review.

validation.source_status: primary article abstract and source search excerpts inspected; source-reported facts only
validation.kernel_derivation: closed analytically for ideal rectangular phase averaging
validation.numerical_fixture: saved in code/resource_fixture.py; not a physical experiment
validation.measured_atom_flux_or_arrival_process: not available in the material inspected
validation.clock_lock_or_Allan_deviation_for_spatia: not demonstrated in the inspected source description

ledger.overall_verdict: Principled rejection of a universal intrinsic selectivity-overpotential-turnover law; retain only conditional transport, conservation, and whole-cell energy relations. Catalyst-specific Pareto frontiers remain unknown.

claims.exact_statement: There is no universal monotone relation between product Faradaic selectivity and local cathodic overpotential across electrochemical catalysts. In the two-pathway model j_i=n_i F k_i^0 exp(beta_i eta) C_s^{m_i}, beta_i=alpha_i n_{e,i}F/(RT), target FE odds obey ln(FE_t/(1-FE_t))=ln(n_t k_t^0/(n_s k_s^0))+(beta_t-beta_s)eta+(m_t-m_s)ln(C_s). Setting beta_t=beta_s and m_t=m_s makes FE_t exactly independent of eta and the common reactant concentration.
assumptions: Steady-state Faradaic current only; no capacitive current in the FE denominator.
The two named products account for all Faradaic current.
Both pathways use the same measured surface reactant concentration C_s and have the displayed power-law rate forms.
The claim rejects universality; it does not assert that selectivity is potential-independent in any specific real catalyst.
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_counterexample; no universal law is rejected within the stated model interface
claims.novelty_boundary: The algebraic counterexample is elementary and not claimed as a novel theorem. Source studies support configuration dependence, not a universal inference across catalysts.
claims.costs: For application to a material, acquire local product-specific rate curves, local reactant/pH, catalyst state, and steady FE; an electrode potential alone is insufficient.
claims.falsifier: The explicit equal-slope/equal-order parameter instance falsifies any theorem claimed to hold over this model class. A catalyst-specific relation requires testing on held-out potentials and transport conditions.
claims.next_gate: Freeze a model fit on a small equipotential Cu coupon, then test sector-resolved FE and partial currents on larger electrodes at changed collector pitch and flow.

claims.exact_statement: For first-order target kinetics r=k_0 exp(alpha n_e F eta/(RT)) C_s coupled to steady planar transport k_m(C_b-C_s)=r, j=n_p F r obeys j=j_lim k/(k_m+k), j_lim=n_p F k_m C_b, and the apparent Tafel slope is b_app=(2.303 RT/(alpha n_e F))/(1-j/j_lim).
assumptions: Steady planar boundary layer with one dissolved limiting reactant.
First-order surface kinetics in C_s and a cathodic Tafel regime.
Constant k_m, temperature, active catalyst state, and no other substrate source or inhibition.
n_e is the electron count in the potential-sensitive elementary step; n_p is the full product electron stoichiometry.
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a Koutecky-Levich/series-rate correction and not claimed as new. It is an explanatory model, not a substitute for porous-electrode transport measurements.
claims.costs: Measure a transport-limited current under the same geometry and feed. Near j_lim, uncertainty in j_lim sharply amplifies corrected intrinsic-current uncertainty.
claims.falsifier: Within the stated single-reaction model, measured j(eta) that violates the relation after independently measuring k_m, C_b, and kinetic parameters falsifies the model assumptions or implementation.
claims.next_gate: Measure product-specific local Tafel curves below and near the limiting current at two independently measured k_m values.

claims.exact_statement: If product t consumes nu_t molecules of a limiting reactant per molecule and its FE is defined against total steady Faradaic current, then j_t <= n_t F J_X,max/nu_t and j_total <= n_t F J_X,max/(nu_t FE_t).
assumptions: The maximum reactant supply J_X,max is measured per geometric electrode area under operating conditions.
No uncounted source or reservoir supplies the reactant.
Steady-state product rate and total Faradaic current use the same sampling interval.
All reactant replenishment from gas, dissolved feed, and carbonate/bicarbonate is included in J_X,max when relevant.
claims.novelty_boundary: Direct material balance; not claimed as novel. The unresolved experimental quantity is the effective maximum flux in porous or buffer-fed electrodes.
claims.costs: Needs calibrated inlet/outlet flow and composition, product assay, total current, carbonate crossover, and gas/liquid mass balance.
claims.falsifier: A sustained target molar production rate above J_X,max/nu_t with a complete, calibrated reactant balance falsifies the claimed flux bound or its measurement assumptions.
claims.next_gate: Acquire J_X,max and carbon balance in the same GDE used for FE measurements, rather than infer it from bulk dissolved CO2 alone.

claims.exact_statement: At steady full-cell voltage V_cell, total current density j, electrode area A, product electron stoichiometry n_i, and product FE_i=n_i F dot(n_i)/(jA), stack electrical energy per mole of product is w_i=n_i F V_cell/FE_i. Between two designs with unchanged product thermodynamics and no auxiliaries, energy per mole improves exactly when FE_i,2/FE_i,1 > V_cell,2/V_cell,1.
assumptions: The measured voltage is the full cell voltage over the same interval as FE and product rate.
Product FE accounts for total Faradaic charge and product losses/crossover are measured correctly.
Auxiliary power, feed conditioning, heating, pumping, separation, and recycle are excluded from this stack-only identity.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard Faraday and power accounting; not claimed as a new result. Its practical use is to compare FE gain against full-cell voltage cost consistently.
claims.costs: Requires two-electrode cell voltage, product-specific calibrated flow/concentration, total current, and a declared system-energy boundary.
claims.falsifier: A complete steady-state charge/product/voltage balance that violates w_i=n_i F V_cell/FE_i falsifies the measurement definitions or accounting boundary.
claims.next_gate: Report full-cell V and product FE together for each operating point; add pump, gas, heat, and separation power before system-level energy claims.

claims.exact_statement: For a thin resistive catalyst sheet with uniform normal current density j, thickness t, and resistivity rho, one-edge collection over length L gives a maximum in-plane voltage drop rho j L^2/(2t). Equipotential conductors at pitch s give a between-conductor maximum drop rho j s^2/(8t), hence the ideal maximum-drop ratio is s^2/(4L^2).
assumptions: Quasi-steady one-dimensional sheet conduction with uniform current source.
Constant sheet resistivity and thickness.
Perfectly equipotential edge/wires and no current redistribution feedback.
claims.status: internally_derived_conditional_sheet_model; direction supported by source-reported spatial model/experiment
claims.novelty_boundary: The scaling follows Ohm's law and is not claimed as new. Real current varies with potential; the cited authors solve a nonlinear field numerically.
claims.costs: Measure in-plane sheet resistance and current distribution; large cells require high-current hardware, spatial voltage taps, and segmented product sampling.
claims.falsifier: A constant-resistivity uniform-current sheet with measured geometry violating the derived ratio falsifies the sheet model or measurement. A real electrode can deviate if its current is nonuniform.
claims.next_gate: Test the s^2 reduction with 4-, 10-, and 20-mm collector pitches and held-out sector FE.

claims.exact_statement: Recent primary studies report device- and microenvironment-dependent co-variation of potential/cell voltage, partial current, Faradaic selectivity, and transport; these source-reported observations show that empirical trends are configuration-specific but do not certify a universal law.
assumptions: Published measurement definitions and experimental controls are as reported by each source.
Values are not independently reproduced in this research track.
claims.novelty_boundary: No new experimental finding, reproduction, or priority claim is made. HCGDE 50-cm2 trials were single experiments and non-isothermal numerical details need supplement-level recheck before reproduction.
claims.costs: Reproduction needs electrochemical cell hardware, matched cathodes, gas/liquid product analytics, local potential/pH probes, and replicate/stability runs.
claims.falsifier: Direct replication under the published controls fails to reproduce the reported current, FE, and voltage changes within the reported experimental variability.
claims.next_gate: Run a replicated segmented-cell intervention with matched catalyst, flow, local potential, pH/CO2, and source-resolved energy accounting.

ledger.overall_status: NO_NEW_THEORETICAL_CAPABILITY_ESTABLISHED; SOURCE_SCOPED_RESULTS_AND_REANALYSIS_ONLY

children: mito_turnover: mitochondrial mtDNA turnover and finite-copy damage threshold
tissue_repair: aged Paneth-cell niche renewal and αKG regeneration

claims.exact_statement: Sereda et al. report that age-related CMA decline alters senescent-cell secretomes, suppresses macrophage CMA/phagocytosis/survival, and is associated with persistent senescence and slower wound repair; systemic CA77.1 lowers several senescence markers in aged mice and disease readouts in a bleomycin model.
claims.scope: Published cell, mouse and human-lung observations under the paper's specific protocols; no independent replication in this task.
claims.measurement_boundary: KFERQ-Dendra reports CMA cargo delivery; SA-β-gal, p21, HMGB1 and gene scores are proxies; bead fluorescence is bead uptake; wound size and fibrosis are tissue-level endpoints. No joint in-vivo clearance/birth-rate observation was made here.
claims.novelty_boundary: Biological mechanism is published. No new aging mechanism, clinical outcome or priority claim is asserted.
claims.next_gate: Compartment-restricted manipulation with lineage-resolved senescent-target birth, macrophage survival and target uptake measured in the same tissue and animals.

claims.exact_statement: Descriptive extraction of Sereda et al. Fig. 4 source data gives Fig. 4h means of 14.6267 (control secretome/no CA), 2.6143 (CMA-deficient secretome/no CA), and 6.3909 (CMA-deficient secretome/CA); the CA mean closes 31.44% of the no-CA gap. Fig. 4e group means are 53.47% versus 2.94% efferocytosis for control versus CMA-deficient macrophages with untreated fibroblasts, and 45.13% versus 2.58% with senescent fibroblasts; the paper reports ANOVA variance shares 98.22% macrophage genotype, 0.8562% fibroblast state and 0.7214% interaction.
assumptions: Workbook labels and reported group assignments are correctly transcribed.
Fig. 4e has n=3 independent experiments; descriptive means are reported without a new inferential test.
Fig. 4h fields are nested within three independent experiments; fields are not treated as independent biological replicates.
claims.scope_limit: Fig. 4e measures efferocytosis of staurosporine-killed targets; Fig. 4h measures IgG-bead uptake. Neither is a living senescent-cell clearance rate or tissue-repair probability.
claims.novelty_boundary: A descriptive reanalysis of the source data; not a new mechanism, theory, independent replication, or causal intervention result.
claims.falsifier: A correctly parsed source workbook with group labels or values inconsistent with the extractor output.

claims.exact_statement: A proposal to bypass macrophage CMA decline by blocking CD47/SIRPα/QPCT-L is already covered in relevant part by Schloesser et al., who report that checkpoint-axis or QPCT/L interference reverses senescent-cell-mediated suppression of bystander efferocytosis; CD47 loss alone did not induce engulfment of senescent cells.
claims.scope_limit: This blocks a generic checkpoint-bypass novelty claim but does not show that every tissue or senescent-cell type is fully cleared.
claims.next_gate: Only reconsider with a distinct, measured macrophage survival or lineage-resolution mechanism not covered by this checkpoint work.

claims.exact_statement: Under an exchangeable genotype-blind N-copy Moran model, the probability that a neutral k-copy allele reaches m copies before loss is k/m; mutation-supply weighting yields a conditional source-parameter accounting identity, while turnover rescales finite-horizon event time and selection may reverse its effect.
assumptions: Fixed copy number, neutral equal replication/removal, no mutation after focal origin for the threshold result, no cell division or selection.
Mutation-supply calculation uses an infinite-sites neutral origin model and does not equate threshold crossing to cell dysfunction.
claims.novelty_boundary: Neutral drift variance, time-rescaling and exact finite-population threshold analysis are prior art. No new mitochondrial mechanism is claimed.

claims.exact_statement: In a stationary one-crypt source model, a candidate Paneth-production route obeys 0.15 D p c <= P/tau_P; pooled equal-crypt renewal fraction q and calibrated threshold tau bound the crypt coverage pi by max(0,(q-tau)/(1-tau)) <= pi <= min(1,q/tau). These are conditional accounting/identifiability statements, not biological estimates.
assumptions: Stationary mature Paneth-cell pool and replacement flux P/tau_P.
The source's approximately 0.15 asymmetric division fraction applies to the modeled +3/+4 ISC division flux D.
Equal crypt weighting and calibrated local threshold tau for the coverage inequality.
claims.novelty_boundary: Mass-balance and probability bounds are standard; focal organelle-age/αKG mechanism is published primary work. D, P, residence time, output c and functional threshold are not jointly measured.

claims.exact_statement: Recent CMA and glutamine-flux MuSC studies report aged-cell interventions and acute transplantation/regeneration readouts, but the inspected primary evidence does not provide repeated-injury reserve trajectories or joint single-cell lineage/fate rates needed to validate a reserve-preserving intervention model.
claims.novelty_boundary: A generic stem-pool branching model or metabolic flux allocation restatement is not claimed as new.

claims.exact_statement: This branch establishes no new quantitative aging-control capability, causal cell-clearance law, validated regeneration intervention, or human clinical result.

charged: Two Luna Max child audits; one child for mitochondrial copy turnover and one for intestinal tissue repair.
Primary article and selective supplement/source-data inspection for macrophage CMA and muscle-stem-cell metabolism.
One small source-data workbook download and descriptive extraction with a reproducible Python script.
not_performed: Wet-lab work, animal work, lineages, flow/imaging acquisition, tracer experiments or pharmacokinetics.
Systematic review, external expert review, independent replication or clinical work.

Macrophage death and per-cell uptake measured jointly with source-cell fate in the same tissue and time window.
Whether tissue-marker decline reflects physical cell clearance, marker-state change, or multiple sources.
Repeated-injury muscle stem-cell reserve response to glutamine/lipid/CMA interventions.
Numerical acquisition cost, throughput, sample size and power for the compartment-specific tests.
Novelty and priority beyond the bounded primary-source audit.

ledger.topic: mitochondrial turnover, mtDNA heteroplasmy and neutral threshold crossing

claims.claim: Under a fixed-N, genotype-blind Moran replacement model, a focal neutral mtDNA allele initially at k copies reaches an m-copy threshold before loss with exact probability k/m.
assumptions: N mtDNA copies remain constant.
Each replacement attempt chooses the parent and removed copy independently and uniformly.
The focal allele has no replication, degradation, or mitophagy selection.
No recurrent mutation at the focal allele occurs after its single-origin start.
The stopping boundaries are allele loss at 0 and threshold attainment at m.
claims.novelty_boundary: Exact harmonic solution of the classical neutral Moran chain; the mitochondrial threshold application is not claimed as a new theorem or priority result.
claims.costs: Requires N, initial copy count k and threshold m; an experiment must detect single-copy heteroplasmy and acquire enough independent lineages.
claims.falsifier: Observed event-count-normalized threshold hitting differs from k/m after confirming constant N and neutral replacement in the stated model.
claims.next_gate: Measure genotype-conditioned replication/removal and single-cell threshold trajectories in a nondividing preparation.

claims.claim: In the neutral model, changing the total replacement rate from N*rho1 to N*rho2 with rho2>rho1 leaves the embedded chain unchanged and can only increase the probability of reaching a threshold by a fixed calendar time; the eventual hit-before-loss probability remains k/m.
assumptions: All transition rates are multiplied by the same turnover factor rho.
The transition kernel and threshold remain fixed as rho changes.
No selection, copy-number feedback, cell division, or intervention-induced change in event probabilities occurs.
claims.novelty_boundary: Classical Poisson time-change of a Moran chain; no novelty claim. Broad turnover-driven variance/time-rescaling is prior art.
claims.costs: Finite-time probability requires N, rho, horizon T, starting k and threshold m; the supplied code uses standard-library uniformization.
claims.falsifier: At matched event kernel and independently measured N, higher rho lowers fixed-age threshold-hit probability, or event-count-normalized probabilities differ.
claims.next_gate: Use a neutral marker and pulse-chase turnover in a matched-copy-number model system; separately test pathogenic alleles.

claims.claim: For an infinite-sites model with mutation-label rate mu per mtDNA replication and rho homeostatic turnover cycles/year, the expected number of labels born in a duration T that eventually reach an m-copy threshold is N*rho*mu*T/m. For m approximately N*h*, the leading N dependence cancels.
assumptions: Each turnover cycle comprises N replication/replacement events.
Every new label is unique and selectively neutral.
Each label's carrier count follows a neutral Moran marginal after its single-copy origin.
A label's success is defined by eventually hitting m before extinction, including after the mutation-birth interval.
The result counts labels, not cells or disease events.
claims.novelty_boundary: Composition of mutation supply N*rho*mu with classical neutral threshold-hit probability 1/m; standard population-genetic cancellation is likely prior art. Not presented as new biology or a disease-risk prediction.
claims.costs: Requires mutation probability per replicated genome, genome length or functional target spectrum, N, turnover cycles/year and threshold. Allele-selection and functional-consequence acquisition are not supplied by the arithmetic.
claims.falsifier: In a neutral infinite-sites model, empirical expected successful-label counts per mutation-birth interval depart from N*rho*mu*T/m beyond finite-time/censoring corrections.
claims.next_gate: Compare finite-time CTMC predictions to lineage-resolved single-cell DNA data with independently calibrated turnover and functional target annotations.

claims.claim: With mutant replication fitness 1-s and uniform removal, 0<s<1, the exact expected change in mutant count per replacement attempt is -s*k*(N-k)/(N*(N-s*k)), so increasing turnover accelerates loss in this selected countermodel.
assumptions: Wild-type fitness is 1 and mutant fitness is 1-s.
The reproducing parent is fitness weighted and the removed copy is uniform.
N remains fixed and s is constant.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard selected-Moran drift identity. It is a counterexample to overgeneralization, not a fitted estimate of mitochondrial selection.
claims.costs: Requires allele-specific fitness/replication or clearance bias s, not bulk mitophagy flux.
claims.falsifier: The conditional drift is not negative for interior k under the stated fitness-weighted birth/uniform-death kernel.
claims.next_gate: Measure mtDNA genotype-conditioned replication and clearance for each allele class before making a turnover intervention prediction.

claims.claim: Human somatic clone work reports a mutation rate near 5.0e-8 alterations per bp replication, about 750 mtDNA copies per cell in its model translation, and inferred homeostatic turnover rates 6.5-11.5 cycles/year for the reported cell types; high-VAF truncating mutations are constrained.
assumptions: Values are transcribed from An et al. 2024 and their model definitions.
The rates are inferred in specific sampled tissue types and are not universal constants.
The mutation rate is reported per bp replication and is not a direct clinical risk rate.
claims.novelty_boundary: Source-reported observations/estimates only; no raw data reanalysis or external validation performed here.
claims.costs: Source analyzed 2,096 clones from three cell types and 31 donors; the parameter translation adds the stated model assumptions and threshold.
claims.falsifier: Source erratum or correction changes the reported estimates or their turnover units.
claims.next_gate: Replicate direct turnover and single-cell mtDNA measurements in the specific tissue/condition of interest.

claims.claim: The broad proposal that more mitophagy/turnover alone is a new rejuvenation mechanism is preempted and underidentified: published work already derives neutral heteroplasmy variance laws, network-state modulation, selective organelle-level QC models, human turnover/mutation estimates, and exact Moran threshold-time inference.
assumptions: The cited primary studies are accurately characterized in sources/NOTES.md.
Search is bounded and cannot establish exhaustive priority.
No biological experiment or expert priority review was performed.
claims.novelty_boundary: Bounded search supports rejection of the generic candidate; it is not an exhaustive priority determination.
claims.costs: Primary papers searched/opened selectively; no supplement/raw-data reproduction, broad systematic review, or biological experiment.
claims.falsifier: A materially distinct mechanism or theorem plus direct primary evidence not covered by these works and with a decisive new prediction.
claims.next_gate: Pursue only if genotype-specific turnover/selection and a tissue-specific functional threshold can be independently measured.

ledger.scientific_status: No novel aging mechanism, biological validation, or externally cleared priority claim. The defensible artifact is an exact conditional Moran derivation, finite-horizon calculation, source-unit translation, and explicit selection counterexample.
ledger.next_observation_that_could_change_statu: For an isogenic nondividing preparation, acquire error-corrected single-cell mtDNA counts, copy number, homeostatic turnover and allele-specific replication/removal under a turnover perturbation; compare finite-time and event-count-normalized threshold crossing against the neutral and selected models.

ledger.status_summary: No new biological result or priority claim. A source-reported mechanism was reconstructed into conditional mass-balance and identifiability statements; synthetic checks establish only exact arithmetic.

claims.exact_statement: Andersson et al. (2025) report that a subset of mouse Lgr5-high ISCs enriched for old mitochondria is metabolically distinct, has elevated alpha-ketoglutarate, and is biased toward Paneth-cell emergence; in aged mice, dm-alphaKG increases EdU-positive Paneth cells, newly made EdU-positive Paneth cells show lower Notum transcript, and a separate prophylactic dm-alphaKG cohort has improved 5-FU recovery readouts.
assumptions: Applies to the species, ages, doses, and protocols reported in the primary paper.
claims.status: source-reported primary study; not independently replicated or externally validated here
claims.proof_path: sources/NOTES.md; primary article DOI 10.1038/s42255-025-01325-7, PMC lines 203-219, 253-257, 367-378
claims.novelty_boundary: The biological mechanism is published prior art. No new biological discovery is claimed.
claims.costs: Published work used aged mice, repeated intraperitoneal dm-alphaKG, EdU, flow/qPCR/tissue assays and an acute 5-FU cohort; exact costs are not reported here.
claims.falsifier: For the named protocol, fail to reproduce the treatment-associated EdU-positive Paneth increase, lower Notum in renewed cells, or improved tissue recovery using prespecified and matched assays.
claims.next_gate: Per-crypt paired replication with calibrated lineage, Notum/Wnt and injury/recovery measures.

claims.exact_statement: In a stationary one-crypt model with P mature Paneth cells, mean residence time tau_P, D relevant ISC divisions per day, asymmetry probability a, and expected c Paneth-cell output conditional on biased daughter commitment probability p, the candidate route's production cannot exceed total Paneth birth flux: a D p c <= P/tau_P; hence p <= P/(a D c tau_P).
assumptions: Steady Paneth count and replacement flux P/tau_P.
The measured asymmetric fraction a applies to the exact relevant division flux D.
Candidate route output is a subset of all Paneth births; c includes downstream amplification and maturation probability.
Cells are counted once at mature Paneth fate; no unmodelled non-steady accumulation.
claims.status: conditional mathematical result; internally reconstructed algebra, not a biological rate estimate
claims.novelty_boundary: A model mass balance, not a novel theorem about tissue biology; source paper itself states deterministic differentiation would overproduce Paneth cells.
claims.costs: To evaluate p requires position-specific D, crypt-level P, residence-time distribution and lineage output c. None is jointly measured in the focal study.
claims.falsifier: Under the assumed steady-state interface, measured a,D,P,tau_P,c that violate the inequality falsify the model assumptions or measurement mapping.
claims.next_gate: Acquire lineage-resolved +3/+4 division and fate data, with Paneth birth/death tracking in the same age/treatment condition.

claims.exact_statement: For equal-sized crypts with renewal fractions R_i in [0,1], pooled mean q=E[R_i], and an independently specified functional threshold tau, the fraction pi of crypts with R_i >= tau is bounded in closure by max(0,(q-tau)/(1-tau)) <= pi <= min(1,q/tau). The interval can be wide, including [0,1] at q=tau=1/2.
assumptions: Equal crypt weighting; R_i is a valid per-crypt fraction in [0,1].
Functional support is represented by a local threshold R_i >= tau.
The threshold is external/calibrated; it is not inferred from the pooled measurement.
claims.status: conditional mathematical result; exact bound proved; threshold model uncalibrated
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard probability bound applied to a tissue-repair interface; not claimed as novel mathematics or measured crypt behavior.
claims.costs: Per-crypt EdU counts, Paneth counts and a local functional readout are needed; cell-weighted pooled means are insufficient when crypt sizes differ.
claims.falsifier: A calibrated threshold and per-crypt data that imply a narrower coverage interval than the bound under its stated assumptions would indicate a model or computation error.
claims.next_gate: Measure the joint distribution of per-crypt renewal, Notum/Wnt output, and crypt recovery after injury.

claims.exact_statement: Under a constant-hazard replacement model, a pooled EdU fraction fbar over window T equals E[1-exp(-lambda_i T)] and does not identify E[lambda_i] or the distribution of crypt rates; Jensen supplies only E[lambda_i] >= -log(1-fbar)/T.
assumptions: EdU positivity represents at least one replacement event during T.
Conditional replacement follows a constant Poisson hazard, label detection is complete, and each crypt's rate is fixed during T.
claims.status: conditional mathematical result; exact synthetic heterogeneity example computed
claims.novelty_boundary: Jensen/Laplace-transform fact, not novel mathematics or an estimate of the source study.
claims.costs: Rate distributions require multiple labeling windows, pulse-chase or lineage data; EdU uptake, dilution and cell loss must be measured.
claims.falsifier: A measured rate distribution under the stated Poisson model that does not reproduce the pooled EdU fraction falsifies that model or its label mapping.
claims.next_gate: Collect at least two EdU pulse/chase windows plus crypt-level lineage observations.

claims.exact_statement: The published treatment-level association between dm-alphaKG, Paneth renewal/Notum readouts and 5-FU recovery does not identify the proportion of dm-alphaKG's recovery effect mediated by Paneth renewal or Notum reduction, because the readouts were in separate cohorts and the focal injury experiment did not selectively intervene on that mediator.
assumptions: Mediation refers to the specific causal path ISC alphaKG/TET activity -> new low-Notum Paneth cells -> local Wnt/ISC restoration -> repair.
A direct dm-alphaKG path and other systemic effects remain admissible explanations.
claims.status: nonidentifiability demonstrated for the reported aggregate design; not evidence against the proposed mechanism
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard causal-inference limitation; Pentinmikko et al. independently established Paneth-Notum/Wnt involvement under a different intervention.
claims.costs: Mechanism blockade/clamp adds aged-mouse groups, lineage and local tissue assays; sample-size and dose costs unknown.
claims.falsifier: A randomized, selective mediator-block experiment with adequate target engagement showing complete loss of dm-alphaKG's recovery benefit would support necessity; preserved benefit would refute necessity of this route.
claims.next_gate: Factorial dm-alphaKG x selective ISC-to-PC or Paneth-Notum perturbation, with matched 5-FU, per-crypt target engagement and recovery.
